We study a simple example of this type, identifying an explicit phase transition and giving a qualitative description of the equilibrium states for all real \(t\). (joint work with Dylan Bansard-Tresse and Reza Mohammadpour).

e62e71dd0d24aaaf.title: On the Wilson-Fisher Fixed Point in the Limit of Integer Spacetime Dimensions
e62e71dd0d24aaaf.speaker: Bernardo Zan
e62e71dd0d24aaaf.abstract:
The Wilson–Fisher (WF) fixed point, a scalar field theory with a quartic interaction in $d = 4 - \epsilon$ dimensions, is the textbook example of a weakly coupled CFT. The epsilon expansion accurately reproduces the critical exponents of the $d = 3$ and the $d = 2$ Ising model. This has led to the common view that WF defines a continuous family of CFTs in non-integer dimensions, interpolating between the free theory at $d=4$ and the Ising model at $d = 3$ and $d = 2$. In this talk I will look at what happens to the WF CFT when the number of dimensions approaches an integer value. Identifying the $d\to 2$ limit of WF as the $2d$ Ising CFT raises some issues, related to the fact that the $d=2$ CFT has infinitely many conserved currents that the $d>2$ theory does not have. I will propose a scenario, inspired by some exactly solved two-dimensional models, where the $d\to 2$ limit of WF contains the $d=2$ Ising CFT as a subsector, but contains more operators which do not completely decouple from the Ising subsector. I will explain why this makes the task of obtaining a $d= 2 + \epsilon$ expansion for the Ising model harder.

e7d50b8c5e8d381a.title: Homogenized Transformers
e7d50b8c5e8d381a.speaker: Hugo Koubbi
e7d50b8c5e8d381a.abstract:
The GdT OT-PDE-ML is a research seminar organized by the ParMA team. It brings together researchers to discuss recent theoretical and numerical developments at the crossroads of Optimal Transport theory, Partial Differential Equations and Machine Learning.
Abstract: We study a random model of deep multi-head self-attention in which the weights are resampled independently across layers and heads, as at initialization of training. Viewing depth as a time variable, the residual stream defines a discrete-time interacting particle system on the unit sphere. We prove that, under suitable joint scalings of the depth, the residual step size, and the number of heads, this dynamics admits a nontrivial homogenized limit.Depending on the scaling, the limit is either deterministic or stochastic with common noise; in the mean-field regime, the latter leads to a stochastic nonlinear Fokker–Planck equation for the conditional law of a representative token. In the Gaussian setting, the limiting drift vanishes, making the homogenized dynamics explicit enough to study representation collapse. This yields quantitative trade-offs between dimension, context length, and temperature, and identifies regimes in which clustering can be mitigated.

e93d9ae563910eea.title: Le principe d'incertitude fort sur les groupes abéliens finis
e93d9ae563910eea.speaker: Emma Weschler
e93d9ae563910eea.abstract:
En mécanique quantique, le principe d'incertitude d'Heisenberg stipule qu'on ne peut connaître simultanément avec précision la position et la vitesse d'une particule. Cette célèbre inégalité relie en réalité une fonction et sa transformée de Fourier.
En 1989, motivés par des applications en traitement du signal, Donoho et Stark donnent un nouveau principe d'incertitude, non plus pour des fonctions définies sur les réels mais sur un groupe abélien fini. Ce dernier a ensuite été significativement amélioré : en 2006, Tao prouve ce qu'on peut appeler un principe d'incertitude fort pour des fonctions définies sur Z/pZ, où p est premier.
Plus récemment, en 2021, Garcia, Karaali et Katz généralisent ce principe aux corps finis, pour des fonctions vérifiant une certaine condition de symétrie qu'on détaillera.
Dans cet exposé, on présentera une généralisation du principe d'incertitude fort pour des groupes abéliens finis quelconques et nous verrons ce que donne l'étude de ce dernier sur les groupes cycliques.

eab425cd42dc1e8f.title: AI for Math: From Group Theory to Discrete Holography
eab425cd42dc1e8f.speaker: Fedor Levkovich-Maslyuk
eab425cd42dc1e8f.abstract: I will describe how one can use modern machine learning methods to attack open problems in group theory. I will show how ideas from AI, pure math, integrability, string theory and quantum information meet here in a highly productive way. I will focus on much-studied Cayley graphs of permutation groups, which are often very hard to explore due to their enormous size. I will describe how a modern ML approach overcomes this challenge and provides efficient pathfinding on these huge graphs. The outcome is a large set of new results and conjectures that in particular sharpen famous bounds on the diameters of these graphs. These results also hint at the existence of a novel, discrete string-like duality for this setting. It provides a realisation of the paradigm "complexity = volume" from AdS/CFT holography, and may potentially be applicable to a wider range of AI tasks. Lastly I will outline some new results for combinatorics of quantum periods and how this could help in improving these ML approaches. Based on arXiv:2509.19162, 2603.22195 and work to appear. Our code is publicly available as the CayleyPy library.

ead7e14f1ce2d23b.title: How to Encode World Knowledge?
ead7e14f1ce2d23b.speaker: Guy Gilboa
ead7e14f1ce2d23b.abstract:
Foundation models are a key platform which implicitly encodes world knowledge. In this talk we first focus on vision-language models, such as CLIP, and investigate their geometric behavior and logic behind the high-dimensional feature encoding. For instance, we find that as image or text become more rare and distinct they are encoded further from the center of the embedding. We explain why InfoNCE loss leads to that behavior. We also find out empirically that each modality can be well modeled statistically as admitting a multivariate Gaussian distribution. This finding is then proved formally, where we show InfoNCE asymptotically induces Gaussian statistics. Finally, we connect two major image foundation models – encoders and generators, through a universal normal embedding hypothesis. A surprising consequence of this hypothesis is demonstrated, where generative diffusion « noise » contains semantic data which can be accessed by linear probing for either classification or editing. This talk is based on 6 recent papers in the group published at ICML 2025, ICLR 2026 and CVPR 2026.

ed8633e232e3c95b.title: Good complexifications of nonnegatively curved manifolds
ed8633e232e3c95b.speaker: Ethan Peng
ed8633e232e3c95b.abstract: A closed manifold M admits a good complexification if it is diffeomorphic to the set of real points of a real affine variety X such that the embedding X(R) -> X(C) is a homotopy equivalence. We will give examples of such closed manifolds, including classical ones (spheres, RP2, homogeneous spaces, Cheeger manifolds), as well as a class of closed Riemannian manifolds with non-negative sectional curvature constructed by B. Totaro using plumbing techniques. We will also discuss topological constraints on closed manifolds admitting a good complexification, such as the classical non-negativity of its Euler characteristic, and vanishing of some Betti numbers and Pontryagin numbers as proved by Totaro. An effort will be made to explain how the curvature constraints interplay with the algebro-geometric aspects. If time permits, we will also discuss how good complexifications pass to quotients by nice group actions, giving ways to "algebraicize" various familiar manifolds.

eef32bcaae0bd0d8.title: "Quantum'' rational numbers, q-deformed Coxeter friezes, and the cross-ratio
eef32bcaae0bd0d8.speaker: Valentin OVSIENKO
eef32bcaae0bd0d8.abstract:
The classical cross-ratio ``crosses'' both classical and modern mathematics, linking geometry with combinatorics, dynamics, and mathematical physics. It provides natural coordinates on many moduli spaces. In this talk, I will introduce a new q-deformed, or ``quantum'' cross-ratio: a PSL(2,Z)-invariant of ordered quadruples of distinct points on the rational projective line. The construction is based on the theory of q-deformed rational numbers developed jointly with Sophie Morier-Genoud. I will discuss several properties of this new invariant, with its close connection to q-deformed Coxeter frieze patterns taking centre stage.
This talk will take place in hybrid mode at the Institut Henri Poincaré.
eef32bcaae0bd0d8.organizer: J. Alev, D. Hernandez, B. Keller, Th. Levasseur, et S. Morier-Genoud.

eef507ba4813d3bf.title: Murphy’s law in non-abelian Hodge theory
eef507ba4813d3bf.speaker: Gregorio Baldi
eef507ba4813d3bf.abstract: We discuss explicit examples of non-integral variations of Q-Hodge structures. Our approach leverages Fenchel–Nielsen-type parameterizations, due to Kabaya and Maskit, of the Teichmüller component of relative character varieties. Additionally, we discuss various Diophantine results concerning the OK,S -integral points of such character varieties, and give a new proof of Beauville’s classical theorem on families of elliptic curves. If time permits, pathological behaviors of the Hodge locus of non-integral QVHS will also be presented.
eef507ba4813d3bf.organizer: O. Biquard, I. Itenberg, S. Shen, T.-D. Tô

ef67103dfc4fc979.title: Ondes internes et viscosité
ef67103dfc4fc979.speaker: Malo Jézéquel
ef67103dfc4fc979.abstract: Je discuterai dans cet exposé du phénomène de concentration géométrique des ondes internes en présence de viscosité. Après avoir présenté un peu de contexte, j'expliquerai comment on peut étudier le régime de basse viscosité en remplaçant le domaine sur lequel le problème est originellement posé (un domaine borné de R2) par une autre surface dans C2. Il s'agit d'un travail en commun avec Jian Wang.

f034597a0e4253b5.title: Weight functions on the Berkovich affine line over any non-Archimedean field
f034597a0e4253b5.speaker: Michael Maex
f034597a0e4253b5.abstract:
The theory of weight functions by Mustaţă-Nicaise on Berkovich spaces hints at an intrinsic approach to studying skeleta without the limitations of the usual tools from algebraic geometry, i.e., semistable reduction or resolution of singularities. In this talk we discuss how Mustaţă-Nicaise's construction can be generalised to define weight functions intrinsically on any quasi-smooth Berkovich space as a sort of normalised log-discrepancy of a canonical form.
Next, we turn our attention to computing weight functions on the Berkovich affine line over any non-Archimedean field K. This question reduces to the entirely value-theoretic problem of describing the integral log differentials $\Omega^{\log}_{L^\circ / K^\circ}$ for a simple extension of real valued fields $L / K$ , which we describe using the data in MacLane-Vaquié chains.
We find that on the affine line, weight functions are completely determined by the integral piecewise linear (Z-PL) structure the affine line and vice versa, yielding new insight into the Z-PL structure.
Finally, we discuss how this can be used to define and compute the essential skeleton of certain Berkovich spaces.

f1541130f606c978.title: Exact curve counting on the once-punctured torus
f1541130f606c978.speaker: Mingkun Liu
f1541130f606c978.abstract: Two closed curves on a surface are said to have the same topological type if they lie in the same mapping class group orbit. Mirzakhani first showed that, on a hyperbolic surface, the number of closed geodesics of a given topological type of length at most L is asymptotically proportional to L^{6g-6}. In this talk, we will focus on the case of the once-punctured torus. Rather than using hyperbolic length, we will count curves according to their word length. In this setting, it turns out that exact counting formulas can be obtained. This is joint work with Filippo Baroni and David Fisac.

f4e64a7a842867c4.title: Percolation de premier passage brochette
f4e64a7a842867c4.speaker: Maxime Marivain
f4e64a7a842867c4.abstract:
Nous étudions un nouveau modèle de percolation de premier passage, appelé percolation de premier passage brochette, dans lequel les temps de passage associés aux arêtes situées sur une même droite sont égaux. Nous établissons tout d'abord un théorème de convergence point à point, où la constante de temps est identifiée. En particulier, nous étudions le cas où cette constante de temps est nulle et mettons en évidence l'existence d'une grande variété de comportements possibles.
Nous démontrons ensuite un théorème de forme, montrant que la forme limite est le diamant L^1. Nous étendons ensuite l'analyse en établissant un théorème de convergence point à point dans le cadre où les temps de passage peuvent prendre la valeur infinie. Enfin, nous nous intéressons à la déviation transversale maximale des géodésiques par rapport à la ligne droite. Nous démontrons l'existence de géodésiques sous des hypothèses faibles et déterminons l'ordre de grandeur de leur déviation par rapport à la ligne droite en fonction du comportement de la distribution des temps de passage au voisinage de son infimum.

f50fc35646665436.title: On the undefinability of C*-tensor norms
f50fc35646665436.speaker: Isaac Goldbring
f50fc35646665436.abstract:
Both the minimal and maximal tensor product norms on a pair of C*-algebras are defined in an "extrinsic" way in terms of representations of the C*-algebras involved. One might wonder if there could be an intrinsic definition of these norm. For example, one might wonder if either the minimal or maximal tensor norm on a sum of simple tensors could be calculated by some sort of formula using norms of *-polynomials of the elements appearing in the simple tensors. In this talk, I explain how to use model theory to formulate a precise version of this latter question. We then discuss two variants of the question: the global version (where such a formula should hold for all C*-algebras, perhaps relative to some elementary class) and, time permitting, the local version (where such a formula should hold only for the pair of C*-algebras involved). I will explain that the answer to the global questions for both the maximal and minimal tensor product norms is negative in general, while in the local case, we give some examples where the answer is negative. The latter examples use the quantum complexity results MIP*=RE and MIP^co=coRE. The work presented in this talk is joint with Thomas Sinclair.
No prior knowledge of C*-algebra theory will be assumed.

f564968cf9d1737e.title: Positivité et sommes de carrés
f564968cf9d1737e.abstract: En 1927, Artin résout le 17ème problème de Hilbert en montrant que tout polynôme réel qui ne prend que des valeurs positives est une somme de carrés de fractions rationnelles. Mais combien de carrés sont nécessaires ? Cette question quantitative sera le fil conducteur de l’exposé. Je l’aborderai dans le cadre classique des polynômes réels, ainsi que dans des variantes arithmétiques et analytiques, en présentant quelques problèmes ouverts et des développements récents.

f995fffb74480dc2.title: Kneser Graphs: Variations on a Theme
f995fffb74480dc2.speaker: Matej Stehlik
f995fffb74480dc2.abstract:
Kneser graphs are a classical family of graphs that play a central role in graph colouring. In 1978, Lovasz determined their chromatic number using topological methods. Schrijver later strengthened this result by identifying vertex-critical induced subgraphs of Kneser graphs, now known as Schrijver graphs.
The talk will survey several recent developments involving these graph families, including constructions of edge-critical subgraphs of Schrijver graphs, a common generalisation of Kneser and Schrijver graphs, and a new family of vertex-critical graphs for which the standard topological lower bounds on the chromatic number are not tight.
The talk is based on joint work with Carmen Arana, Penny Haxell, and Tomas Kaiser.

f9a8885d047de507.title: Algebraic Hodge-Generic Points and the Period Conjecture
f9a8885d047de507.speaker: Gregorio Baldi
f9a8885d047de507.abstract: Let f:X\to S be a quasi-projective family of varieties defined over Qbar. We prove that the points of S(Qbar) that are Hodge generic for the variation of Hodge structures associated to f are analytically dense in S. More generally, motivated by the Grothendieck period conjecture and under a large-monodromy assumption, we establish the density of algebraic points at which the periods of the fibre satisfy no unexpected relations of degree at most delta. The main technical input is a new result on relations among solutions of G-operators, based on height estimates of Bombieri and André. This is a joint work with Gal Binyamini and David Urbanik.

rec.title: Defects in skein theory
rec.speaker: Juan Ramón Gómez García
rec.abstract:
Skein theory forms a once-extended categorified TQFT that assigns skein algebras to surfaces and skein modules to 3-manifolds.
These algebras and modules are defined in terms of generators of topological flavor, namely a certain class of graphs embedded in the 3-manifold,
modulo the relations induced by evaluating (locally) these graphs in an underlying ribbon category. In this talk I will explain how this picture
can be extended to stratified manifolds with strata of codimension 1 and 2 (called defects). Using the appropriate algebraic structures,
we can define evaluation functors around defects, yielding notions of stratified skein modules and algebras. Examples of these structures
are provided by the formalism of parabolic restriction. As an application, we use an interpolating version of parabolic defects to construct
a categorification of the Turaev coproduct in the HOMFLY skein algebra.

rec.title: 2-catégories de fusion graduées par les 3-groupes et invariants quantiques homotopiques
rec.speaker: Matthew Cellot
rec.abstract:
À la fin du XXe siècle, les travaux remarquables de Jones, Drinfeld,
Witten et Kontsevich ont permis la construction de nouveaux invariants de
variétés, appelés invariants quantiques, obtenus notamment à partir de certains
groupes quantiques. L’un des premiers succès dans cette direction est l’invariant
de Turaev-Viro-Barrett-Westbury des 3-variétés, défini comme une somme d’états
à partir de la donnée d’une catégorie de fusion. Plus récemment, Douglas et
Reutter ont construit des invariants de 4-variétés par somme d’états, en utilisant
des 2-catégories de fusion.
Cet exposé porte sur les invariants quantiques homotopiques, c’est-à-dire les
invariants quantiques de variétés munies d’une structure supplémentaire codée
par une application vers un espace topologique. Plus précisément, nous
généralisons la construction de Douglas-Reutter pour obtenir des invariants des
3-fibrés plats sur les 4-variétés ou, de manière équivalente, des 4-variétés
munies d’une classe d’homotopie d’applications vers un 3-type d’homotopie.
Les structures algébriques utiles pour cette construction sont les 2-catégories
de fusion graduées par les 3-groupes, où le 3-groupe modélise le 3-type
d’homotopie. Dans ce cadre, les applications vers un 3-type d’homotopie sont
codées par des triangulations coloriées. En démontrant une généralisation
coloriée du théorème de Pachner, nous obtenons que ces invariants sont
indépendants de la triangulation choisie.
rec.series_name: Séminaire de Géométrie et Dynamique de Cergy-Pontoise

rec.title: Formes normales et structures géométriques sur les variétés de Hopf
rec.speaker: Paul Boureau
rec.abstract:
Nous montrerons comment la dynamique holomorphe contractante définissant
une variété de Hopf permet de construire naturellement une géométrie localement homogène.
La théorie de Poincaré–Dulac et les polynômes sous-résonnants conduisent à l’existence
d’une (G,Cn)(G,\mathbb C^n)-structure sur toute variété de Hopf de dimension au moins deux.
Nous étudierons également la rigidité, la non-unicité et la classification de ces structures.
rec.series_name: Séminaire de Géométrie et Dynamique de Cergy-Pontoise

rec.title: Mass in almost Kähler geometry
rec.speaker: Partha Ghosh
rec.abstract:
In this talk, I present an explicit formula for the ADM mass of asymptotically
locally Euclidean (ALE) almost Kähler manifolds. The formula expresses the mass in terms of
the total Hermitian scalar curvature and topological data associated with the underlying almost
complex structure, extending a result of Hein and LeBrun in the Kähler ALE case. The proof is
based on a spin-c adaptation of Witten’s proof of the positive mass conjecture in the spin case
and is therefore distinct from previous complex-geometric methods. In dimension 4, I show that
one can prove a positive mass theorem and a Penrose-type inequality for asymptotically Euclidean
(AE) almost Kähler manifolds using this formula.

rec.title: Diffuse Interface Models and their Sharp Interface Limits
rec.speaker: Helmut Abels
rec.abstract:
CANCELED – For personal reasons, Helmut Abels has unfortunately been forced to cancel his seminar. – CANCELED
Speaker: Helmut Abels (Universität Regensburg)
Interfaces separating two or more species or components of a material are omnipresent in applications in the sciences. Nowadays there are two main classes of models to describe interfaces, both from a theoretical and practical point of view: In classical so-called « sharp interface models » the species or components under consideration fill disjoint domains that are separated by lower dimensional surfaces of a certain regularity. On the other hand in « diffuse interface models » a partial mixing of the species or components on a small length scale is taken into account, which leads to an interfacial layer of small but positive thickness. This has the advantage that the interfaces do not need to be resolved explicitly and singularities in the interfaces can be described consistently.
In the first part of the talk we will give an overview of some basic diffuse interface models with applications to material sciences. Moreover, we will discuss some analytic results on the relation between diffuse and sharp interface models, when the interfacial thickness of the diffuse interface tends to zero. The analysis is based on formally matched asymptotic expansions (in a rigorous manner) together with uniform estimates for the linearized operator. In this part we will focus on the Allen-Cahn equation as basic model.
In the second part we will discuss a Navier-Stokes/Allen-Cahn system, which describes the flow of two macroscopically immiscible viscous incompressible fluid, separated by a diffuse interface. We will present some recent results on novel higher-order estimates for the sharp interface limit of this system. With the aid of a suitable weight taking the distance to the interface and the interfacial thickness into account we obtain optimal regularity estimates, which are uniformy in the interfacial thickness. This enables to improve previous convergence results in two space dimensions significantly and extend results to three space dimensions. This is a joint-work with Mingwen Fei, Yadong Liu, and Maximilian Moser.

rec.title: Dynamique des tourbillons visqueux dans un demi-plan
rec.speaker: Thierry Gallay
rec.abstract:
ANNULÉ – En raison de la fermeture du campus Pierre-et-Marie Curie le séminaire est ANNULÉ.
Speaker: Thierry Gallay (Université Grenoble Alpes)
Le but de cet exposé est de définir un cadre mathématique permettant de décrire les interactions entre tourbillons et parois pour des écoulements plans à grand nombre de Reynolds. Les phénomènes typiques que l’on souhaite étudier à terme sont le mouvement auto-induit (pour un tourbillon isolé) et l’effet de rebond (pour une paire de tourbillons).
Dans la première partie, à caractère tout à fait élémentaire, on explique comment résoudre les équations de Navier-Stokes incompressibles dans un demi-plan en exploitant l’équation d’évolution pour le tourbillon du fluide. Si l’on suppose que la vitesse s’annule sur la paroi, le tourbillon vérifie une condition au bord non linéaire et non locale qui est difficilement utilisable en pratique. On peut toutefois la remplacer par une condition intégrale permettant une formulation élégante du système, lequel se résout alors par un simple argument de point fixe dans un cadre fonctionnel approprié.
Dans la seconde partie, en cohérence avec l’objectif affiché, on suppose que la donnée initiale est une collection finie de tourbillons ponctuels, dont les circulations peuvent être arbitrairement grandes. Ce cas ne peut pas être traité comme précédemment par un simple argument de point fixe, mais on peut tout de même montrer l’existence et l’unicité de la solution en utilisant une décomposition appropriée, qui permet de traiter la partie la plus singulière de la solution dans le plan tout entier où l’on dispose d’outils plus affûtés. En fonction du temps disponible, on présentera également quelques résultats concernant le comportement asymptotique en temps de la solution, ses propriétés de localisation, ou la question difficile de la limite non visqueuse.
Cet exposé repose entièrement sur un travail en collaboration avec Anne-Laure Dalibard.
Thierry Gallay (Université Grenoble Alpes)

rec.title: Un degré de différentiabilité peut tout changer
rec.speaker: Hélène Eynard-Bontemps
rec.abstract:
Par lisse, certains entendent de classe $C^1$, d’autres $C^\infty$, alors que pour l’analyse élémentaire, la mécanique Newtonienne ou les questions de courbure, $C^2$ semble plus naturel… Les mathématiques regorgent d’exemples de problèmes ou de techniques qui sont extrêmement sensibles à la régularité dans laquelle on travaille, souvent pour des raisons profondes et intéressantes. J’illustrerai cette affirmation à l’aide d’exemples tirés de la dynamique unidimensionnelle (qui s’intéresse aux difféomorphismes de l’intervalle et du cercle) mais aux origines bien géométriques : le célèbre théorème de Denjoy et le bijou moins connu qu’est le lemme de Nancy Kopell.

rec.title: David Bessis – La chute de l’économie du théorème

rec.abstract:
Si les machines démontrent les théorèmes, que reste-t-il aux humains ? En quelques mois, les progrès des modèles d’IA ont fait entrer la recherche mathématique mondiale dans une crise sans précédent, remettant à la fois en cause ses critères de valeur, son organisation pratique et son image publique. En dépit de sa nouveauté radicale, la crise actuelle nous confronte à des questions anciennes, jamais résolues, dont les mathématicien(ne)s ont longtemps cru qu’elles étaient purement théoriques : que sont les mathématiques ? Comment créent-elles de la valeur ? Quel rôle jouent-elles dans la cognition humaine ?

rec.title: How to Encode World Knowledge?
rec.speaker: Guy Gilboa
rec.abstract:
Foundation models are a key platform which implicitly encodes world knowledge. In this talk we first focus on vision-language models, such as CLIP, and investigate their geometric behavior and logic behind the high-dimensional feature encoding. For instance, we find that as image or text become more rare and distinct they are encoded further from the center of the embedding. We explain why InfoNCE loss leads to that behavior. We also find out empirically that each modality can be well modeled statistically as admitting a multivariate Gaussian distribution. This finding is then proved formally, where we show InfoNCE asymptotically induces Gaussian statistics. Finally, we connect two major image foundation models – encoders and generators, through a universal normal embedding hypothesis. A surprising consequence of this hypothesis is demonstrated, where generative diffusion « noise » contains semantic data which can be accessed by linear probing for either classification or editing. This talk is based on 6 recent papers in the group published at ICML 2025, ICLR 2026 and CVPR 2026.

rec.title: Automath! À qui appartiennent les mathématiques ? Maths + IA Controversy Workshop
rec.abstract:
À qui appartiennent les mathématiques ? En deux ans à peine, les mathématiques semblent être passées du statut de frontière de l’IA à celui de territoire de l’IA, du statut d’idéal cognitif servant à tester les capacités de raisonnement des modèles d’IA, à celui d’infrastructure de connaissance, productive et mobilisable de façon en partie automatisée. C’est en tous cas le message envoyé par OpenAI (e.g. Contre-exemple à la conjecture d’Erdős), Anthropic (e.g. Contre-exemple à la conjecture jacobienne), Google DeepMind (e.g. AlphaProof) ou encore la DARPA avec le programme ExpMath. Si le moment se veut historique, la suite n’est pas écrite pour autant. La communauté mathématique se prépare et s’interroge : À quel endroit faut-il résister ? Et à quel autre faudrait-il plutôt s’adapter ? À quelles conditions ? Comment souhaitons-nous voir se dessiner les trajectoires de l’IA et de la recherche mathématiques ? L’équipe Inria SIRA, le LFPC et le collectif Automath invitent la communauté mathématique élargie à se saisir collectivement de ces enjeux lors d’une journée de workshop (ai4sciencecontroversy.com)
Comme en témoigne la Déclaration de Leiden [1.] ou le formule Terence Tao dans une publication récente [2.] : « How should the mathematical community respond to the advent of modern AI technologies, and their real and/or claimed capabilities to perform mathematical tasks? (…) It is a metamathematical question. »

rec.abstract:

Tout d’abord nous rappellerons quelques résultats déterministes classiques autour de ce problème. Puis nous étudierons ce problème sous un angle probabiliste en nous demandant où se situent les racines du polynôme dérivé lorsque les racines du polynôme initial ont été tirées de manière indépendante et identiquement distribuée dans le plan complexe. Pour finir, nous étudierons ce problème sous un angle d’analyse en expliquant comment ce dernier peut mener à l’étude d’une équation aux dérivées partielles non linéaire et non locale obtenue après passage à une limite champ moyen

rec.title: Équations diophantiennes et cohomologie galoisienne
rec.abstract:
Le point de départ de cet exposé est d’expliquer comment classifier les surcorps non-commutatifs d’un corps K (par exemple, R a un surcorps non-commutatif donné par le corps des quaternions H, qui est de dimension 4 sur R).
L’idée clé derrière cette classification est la notion de « descente galoisienne » : informellement, elle consiste à dire que les objets définis sur un corps K viennent d’objets définis sur la clôture algébrique de K qui sont munis d’une action d’un certain groupe qu’on appelle le groupe de Galois absolu de K.
La classification de tels objets fait naturellement intervenir des groupes de cohomologie associés à ce groupe de Galois absolu, appelés groupes de cohomologie galoisienne. Ces groupes sont intimement liés aux propriétés diophantiennes du corps K : si certaines équations homogènes sur K avec beaucoup de variables ont des solutions, alors ces groupes de cohomologie ont tendance à s’annuler à partir d’un certain degré.
Pour rendre compte de ce phénomène, Lang a introduit la notion de corps C_i et a conjecturé que les corps C_i avaient une cohomologie triviale en degré > i. Cette conjecture est ouverte pour i>2 et on sait que sa réciproque est fausse. Si le temps le permet, je parlerai des conjectures de Kato et Kuzumaki qui raffinent la propriété C_i pour tenter d’avoir une condition diophantienne qui caractérise l’annulation de la cohomologie du corps en degré >i.

rec.title: Automath! On the Origin of False Proofs by Means of Bugs in Proof Assistants, Yannick Foster
rec.abstract:
Proof assistants have entered mainstream mathematical discourse so fast that now they are almost silently accepted as the ultimate guardians of correct proofs. Both the recent forced Euler blowup result by Buckmaster and Alpöge and the solution to the Navier-Stokes problem announced by OpenAI come with proofs verified in the Lean proof assistant, with code almost entirely written using LLMs. Only six months ago an experiment led by Tristan Stérin showed that LLMs are effective at finding bugs in proof assistants: several bugs were found both in Lean and the Rocq proof assistant. As a demonstration, Ramana Kumar has published a proof of the Collatz Conjecture in Lean, making use of a bug. These experiments have been followed by a flurry of bugs in Lean and Rocq found by Daniel Selsam at OpenAI. In this talk, I will discuss the tension between proof assistants as guardians for LLM-coded proofs and as vulnerable target for LLM-guided bug search. In this talk I will discuss what a false proof is, what a bug in a proof assistant is, and give a genealogy of bugs that have been found this year, focusing on what features of proof assistants they usually occur in. I will conclude with some thoughts on how we can have and increase trust in results developed in proof assistants.

rec.title: Aicha Ben Dhia (CFM) et Théo Leblanc (Ceremade)
rec.abstract:
Aicha Ben Dhia (CFM): Prédire les futures vagues de chaleur grâce à un simple ajustement statistique
Résumé : Pour savoir à quels types de phénomènes météorologiques extrêmes nous devrons faire face avec la hausse des températures, on s’appuie généralement sur des modèles de circulation générale. Ces modèles climatiques sont l’outil le plus complet et le plus fiable pour décrire la complexité des phénomènes climatiques. Mais cette complexité a des inconvénients importants : ces modèles sont très lourds en calcul, lents à exécuter et exigent un haut niveau d’expertise pour être manipulés. Au Resilience Lab, nous avons adopté une approche radicalement différente et construit des prédictions simples en extrapolant des séries temporelles de température. Nous parvenons ainsi à estimer la probabilité d’atteindre 50 °C à Paris dans les années à venir, ainsi que dans plusieurs autres endroits du monde. Nous réalisons plusieurs étapes de vérification pour tester la « robustesse » de ces résultats.
Théo Leblanc (Ceremade) : Introduction aux séries temporelles et à leur estimation statistique
Résumé : Dans cet exposé nous introduirons les principaux concepts nécessaires à la modélisation des séries temporelles, avec un intérêt particulier pour les processus AutoRégressifs (AR). Nous présenterons différentes méthodes d’estimation des paramètres caractérisant ces processus, ainsi que les principales composantes et propriétés des séries temporelles. Nous aborderons notamment les outils permettant d’estimer et d’analyser les dépendances temporelles présentes dans les données.

rec.title: Xenia Flamm, raconte-moi le spectre réel (de variétés de caractères) !
rec.abstract:
Le spectre réel est un outil de la géométrie algébrique réelle qui permet de compactifier les ensembles semi-algébriques en ajoutant, à l’infini, leurs k-points, pour tout corps k ordonné non-archimédien. J’en présenterai la construction ainsi que les principales propriétés.
Dans une deuxième partie, nous nous intéresserons aux variétés de caractères, c’est-à-dire des espaces de modules de représentations d’un groupe de type fini dans un groupe semi-algébrique G. Ces espaces permettent notamment de décrire de nombreuses structures géométriques sur les variétés. Nous verrons comment le spectre réel permet d’étudier leurs dégénérescences : les points à l’infini peuvent être interprétés comme des représentations à valeurs dans G(k), où k est un corps ordonné non-archimédien. À travers quelques exemples, j’expliquerai en quel sens ces dégénérescences peuvent être vues comme des structures géométriques « non-archimédiennes ».

rec.title: Théorie de Morse, pantalons et jupes
rec.abstract:
Lorsque l’on tient un pantalon droit, on observe qu’il possède un trou en haut et deux en bas. Le bord supérieur du pantalon est donc un cercle tandis que le bord inférieur est composé de deux cercles : les deux bords sont différents. En imposant que les deux bords soient simplement connexes on obtient une jupe (qui n’est rien d’autre qu’un cylindre). Tous les pantalons de dimension au moins 6 ayant 2 bords connexes sont en fait des jupes.
Dans cet exposé j’introduirai plusieurs outils de la théorie de Morse (points critiques, lemme de Morse, fonctions de Morse) et je définirai alors l’homologie de Morse. J’énoncerai ensuite comme application le théorème de h-cobordisme qui formalise mon affirmation sur les pantalons de grande dimension et donnerai selon le temps restant les idées de la preuve.

rec.title: Surfaces Browniennes et Explorations Métriques
rec.abstract:
Les surfaces browniennes sont des surfaces aléatoires continues qui apparaissent comme limites de grandes surfaces discrètes choisies au hasard. Elles constituent aujourd’hui des modèles fondamentaux de géométrie aléatoire.
Dans cet exposé, je présenterai ces objets et quelques-unes de leurs propriétés fondamentales. Nous reviendrons sur plusieurs résultats marquants de la théorie, en partant des modèles discrets dont ces surfaces émergent. On verra notamment comment certains processus stochastiques apparaissent naturellement lorsqu’on explore ces surfaces à partir d’un point, et comment ils permettent de mettre en évidence certaines propriétés de Markov spatiales.
Aucun prérequis particulier n’est nécessaire : l’objectif sera surtout de donner une intuition des objets et des méthodes, plutôt que d’entrer dans les détails techniques.

rec.title: Dynamics on the space of amenable subgroups
rec.speaker: Anna Cascioli
rec.abstract: Every countable group acts by homeomorphisms on its space of subgroups. The dynamics of this action, and in particular its restriction to the space of amenable subgroups, encode algebraic and geometric properties of the group. In this talk, I will explain how these dynamics can be used to characterize C*-simplicity, a property of groups that arises naturally in the study of unitary representations.

rec.title: FAMED triangulations will live forever
rec.speaker: Antonin Guilloux
rec.abstract:
I will present a joint work with Fathi Ben Aribi and Ka Ho Wong around volume conjectures. Roughly, a volume conjecture describes a link between the semiclassical limit of a quantum invariant of a triangulated hyperbolic knot complement and the hyperbolic geometry of its complement. There are several flavors and we will focus of a version by Andersen and Kashaev.
Recently, arguments by Fathi and Ka Ho reduce essentially this conjecture to a combinatorial property of the triangulation, called FAMED. I will explain this condition and how to extensively test this condition, and a path toward a proof of the volume conjecture.

rec.title: Height pairing over arithmetic function fields
rec.speaker: Juan Felipe Castro-Cardenas
rec.abstract:
Since the foundational work of Néron and Tate in the 60s, various conjectural definitions of the height pairing for homologically trivial algebraic cycles on smooth, projective varieties over a number field, or more general global fields, have been proposed by Belinson, Bloch, Gillet-Soulé and Schneider, among others. The related concept of height functions on sub-varieties was extensively developed by Faltings and, in the early 2000s, extended by Moriwaki to varieties defined over finitely generated extensions of $\mathbb{Q}$, also called arithmetic function fields. More recently, Bruno Kahn has used algebraic intersection theory to give a geometric construction of a ``refined" height pairing over the function field of a smooth, projective variety $B$, taking its values in $\textrm{Pic}(B)$.
In this talk, I will present an Arakelov-geometric analogue of this construction over an arithmetic function field $K$, taking its values in the arithmetic Picard group of a normal arithmetic variety whose function field is $K$. The construction is in two parts: first, Kahn's definitions are extended and adapted to arithmetic varieties using the intersection theory on regular schemes of Gillet-Soulé, and then the Archimedean term is added by considering generalized Green currents satisfying some ``admissibility" conditions, inspired by the original work of Arakelov. If time allows, I will discuss the connection with Moriwaki's work and with the work of Brosnan and Pearlstein on the degeneration of the Archimedean height pairing.

rec.title: Finiteness and density problems for (positive) integral points on Mordell–Schinzel surfaces
rec.speaker: Robin Zhang
rec.abstract: In 1952, Mordell erroneously claimed that the surface $xyz = G(x,y)$ has infinitely many integral points for any $G \in \mathbb{Z}[x,y]$. I will discuss a classification for finiteness and Zariski density of (positive) integral points on these log K3 surfaces when the coefficients of $G$ are non-negative. This combines a dynamical argument proposed by Mordell, the theory of generalized cluster algebras, and the Killing–Cartan classification of semisimple Lie algebras. This talk is partially based on joint work with Antoine de Saint Germain.

rec.title: The Hecke orbit conjecture and $p$-adic monodromy of Tate-linear varieties
rec.speaker: Livia Grammatica
rec.abstract: If $A$ is a $g$-dimensional principally polarized abelian variety over $\mathbb{C}$, it is not hard to show that the Hecke orbit of $A$ (the set of principally polarized abelian varieties which are isogenous to $A$) is dense in $\mathcal{A}_g(\mathbb{C})$. This fails in positive characteristic because Hecke orbits are confined to Newton strata, the loci of $\mathcal{A}_g$ where the Newton polygon of the abelian variety is constant. The Hecke orbit conjecture, now a theorem of Chai-Oort, thus asks whether Hecke orbits are dense in their respective Newton strata over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$. In the first part of the talk, we will explain Chai's strategy for proving the Hecke orbit conjecture, and we will present the recent results in $p$-adic monodromy that led to a proof, by D'Addezio and van Hoften, of the Hecke orbit conjecture for all Shimura varieties of Hodge type. In the second part we present a refinement of these $p$-adic monodromy techniques, with an application to the rigidity of Tate-linear varieties, which are central objects in Chai's work.

rec.title: On the undefinability of C*-tensor norms
rec.speaker: Isaac Goldbring
rec.abstract:
Both the minimal and maximal tensor product norms on a pair of C*-algebras are defined in an "extrinsic" way in terms of representations of the C*-algebras involved. One might wonder if there could be an intrinsic definition of these norm. For example, one might wonder if either the minimal or maximal tensor norm on a sum of simple tensors could be calculated by some sort of formula using norms of *-polynomials of the elements appearing in the simple tensors. In this talk, I explain how to use model theory to formulate a precise version of this latter question. We then discuss two variants of the question: the global version (where such a formula should hold for all C*-algebras, perhaps relative to some elementary class) and, time permitting, the local version (where such a formula should hold only for the pair of C*-algebras involved). I will explain that the answer to the global questions for both the maximal and minimal tensor product norms is negative in general, while in the local case, we give some examples where the answer is negative. The latter examples use the quantum complexity results MIP*=RE and MIP^co=coRE. The work presented in this talk is joint with Thomas Sinclair.
No prior knowledge of C*-algebra theory will be assumed.

rec.title: On supercuspidal representations in the l-adic cohomology of some local Shimura varieties
rec.speaker: Yoichi Mieda
rec.abstract: A local Shimura variety is a p-adic analogue of a Shimura variety. Its l-adic cohomology is expected to be related to the local Langlands correspondence. In the Lubin-Tate case, a supercuspidal representation appears only in the middle degree. In the GSp(4) case, a supercuspidal representation appears only in the degrees 3,4, and it appears in the degree 4 if and only if its L-parameter has non-trivial SL(2)-part. In this talk, I will explain my recent results in this direction for more general cases.

rec.title: Système d’Euler biparti pour les points de Drinfeld–Heegner
rec.speaker: Yichao Tian
rec.abstract:
Le système d’Euler biparti classique associé aux points
de Heegner a été introduit par Howard, basé sur des travaux pionniers
de Bertolini et Darmon. Il est un outil puissant pour l’étude de
l’arithmétique des courbes elliptiques sur le corps des nombres
rationnels.
Dans cet exposé, on expliquera un analogue de ce système d’Euler
biparti pour les points de Drinfeld–Heegner sur les courbes de
Laumon–Rapoport–Stuhler, qui sont des analogues des courbes de
Shimura sur un corps global de fonctions (i.e. le corps de fonctions
d’une courbe projective lisse sur un corps fini). Ces résultats
pourraient avoir des applications à l’étude des groupes de Selmer
des courbes elliptiques non isotriviales sur de tels corps. Comme un
ingrédient technique de la démonstration, on obtient également un
analogue du lemme d’Ihara classique pour les courbes de
Laumon–Rapoport–Stuhler.

rec.series_name: Séminaire Groupes Réductifs et Formes Automorphes
rec.organizer: Farrell Brumley, Yichao Tian

rec.title: Diameters and box spaces
rec.speaker: Alain Valette
rec.abstract:
Le séminaire d'algèbres d'opérateurs aura lieu à l'IHP le temps du trimestre "algèbres d'opérateurs : approximation, ridigité et dynamique"
Résumé : Consider a sequence $(X_k)_{k>0}$ of finite, connected, d-regular graphs with size going to infinity. It is known that, if $(X_k)_{k>0}$ is an expanding sequence, then the diameter of $X_k$ is exactly logarithmic in the number of vertices of $X_k$. On the opposite, for $0<\alpha \leq 1$, say that $(X_k)_{k>0}$ has property $D_\alpha$ if the diameter of $X_k$ grows at least like $|X_k|^\alpha$: this is a strong form of non-expansion. For a finitely generated, residually finite group $G$, let $(N_k)_{k>0}$ be a filtration of $G$. The box space associated with $(N_k)_{k>0}$ is the sequence of finite Cayley graphs $(Cay(G/N_k,S))_{k>0}$ where $S$ is a fixed finite generating set of $G$. It turns out that property $D_\alpha$ for a box space is related to interesting algebraic properties of $G$, and we will survey results by Breuillard-Tointon, Khukhro-Valette, and Guo-Tointon. Now, assuming that $G$ can be realized as a subgroup of $GL_n(A)$, where $A$ is a unital, commutative ring, we have filtrations given by congruence subgroups, giving rise to arithmetic box spaces. Sometimes the growth of the diameter is more constrained on arithmetic box spaces then on general box spaces, i.e. non-arithmeticity can be detected purely metrically. We will illustrate this with lamplighter groups $L_F:=F\wr\Z$, where $F$ is a finite abelian group. This is joint work with Etienne Grezet.
rec.location_text: IHP, Amphi Darboux
rec.organizer: Matthieu Joseph, Omar Mohsen

rec.title: Skein and Hall algebras of decorated marked surfaces
rec.speaker: Shunsuke KANO
rec.abstract:
The skein algebra of a surface S is defined using isotopy classes of curves in the thickened surface SxI, where I is the unit interval, subject to local relations involving crossings and their smoothings. Qiu pioneered the use of decorated marked surfaces as a geometric framework for studying the derived category of the Ginzburg dg algebra associated with a triangulation of a marked surface. In this talk, I will introduce the skein algebra of a triangulated decorated marked surface and discuss its connections with the derived Hall algebra of the perfectly valued derived category of the corresponding Ginzburg dg algebra. This is a report on ongoing joint work with Denis Lyskov.
This talk will take place in hybrid mode at the Instiut Henri Poincaré.

rec.title: Sur les points fixes des sous-groupes de Moy-Prasad dans les représentations admissibles irréductibles de groupes réductifs p-adiques (Travaux en cours avec Marie-France Vignéras et Rachel Ollivier)
rec.speaker: Guy Henniart
rec.abstract:
Soit p un nombre premier et F une extension finie de Q_p.
Soit G un groupe réductif connexe sur F, et C un corps algébriquement
clos. Dans une C-représentation admissible irréductible π du groupe
G(F), les points fixes par un sous-groupe ouvert K forment un C-espace
vectoriel de dimension finie d(K, π). Si π est de dimension infinie,
il est intéressant de savoir comment d(K, π) croît quand K devient de
plus en plus petit. Par exemple, on peut partir d’un sous-groupe de
Moy-Prasad G_x,r (pour x dans l’immeuble de G sur F et r un nombre
réel positif), et faire croître r. Grâce à des résultats de
Harish-Chandra (1978) et T.-C.Tsai (2025), nous prouvons que si la
caractéristique de C n'est pas p, alors pour tout entier n assez grand,
d(G_x,r+2n, π) a la forme P(p^n), où P est un polynôme à
coefficients rationnels, dépendant de x, r, et π. Nous soupçonnons
que cela reste vrai si C est de caractéristique p, mais seul le cas où
G est GL₂ et F=Q_p est connu. Pour G général, même le cas
particulier où π est la représentation de Steinberg de G(F) est
difficile. Cependant, nous obtenons un résultat asymptotique plus
faible, valable pour tout π. Au passage, nous examinons la condition
que G_x,r soit un pro-p groupe uniforme.

rec.title: Doubling modulo odd integers
rec.speaker: Jean-Paul Allouche
rec.abstract:
Once upon a time, there was a mathematical journal which was "almost'' a journal in the
sense that one could find there either papers in final form, or reports of talks given at a local
(but well-known and welcoming international researchers) Seminar, or papers that were not
necessarily in final form and could even stay forever in an almost unfinished state. This journal
was the Séminaire de Théorie des Nombres de Bordeaux, that became later a more
classical journal, the Journal de Théorie des Nombres de Bordeaux.
Among the many papers that were not in a final form in the Séminaire (and that were
not necessarily followed by a "real paper'' appeared later elsewhere), one can find a quite
modest paper entitled "Suites infinies à répétitions bornées'' (in the 1983--1984 issue).
In that paper there was a short study of the number of cycles of a family of permutations
related to the Toeplitz transform of sequences.
Up to notation the number of cycles of the same family of permutations appeared in 2021 in
a paper by Y. Guo, G. Han, and W. Wu about "apwenian sequences''.
The formulas given in these two papers were distinct, though---of course---equivalent.
Thus it was tempting to prove directly their equality.
This possibly frivolous question lead to unexpected discoveries: the family of permutations
above or a variation of it are linked to numerous subjects, not only in mathematics (combinatorics
of words, dynamical systems, number theory, correcting algorithms), but also in card-shuffling,
juggling, change-ringing, poetry, and music composition.
The details can be found in a paper by J.-P. A., M. Stipulanti, and J.-Y. Yao, appeared in
The Mathematical Intelligencer in 2026.

rec.title: A planar model for odd Khovanov homology
rec.speaker: Naageswaran Manikandan
rec.abstract:
In this talk, we will discuss an extension of odd Khovanov homology to tangles. This construction is closely related in spirit to the approach introduced by Bar-Natan for even Khovanov homology. We will first review Bar-Natan's construction for even Khovanov homology and then describe a modification of this framework that produces the odd Khovanov invariant. If time permits, we will also briefly discuss the functorial properties of this construction.
This is a joint work in progress with Shun Ming Samuel Lee and Léo Schelstraete.
rec.location_text: Sophie Germain, Salle Pierre Grisvard, IHP
rec.organizer: Najib Idrissi et Emmanuel Wagner

rec.title: What does it mean to formalize a proof? Can we really trust a formalized proof, even if written by an LLM?
rec.speaker: Riccardo BRASCA
rec.abstract: Formalization of mathematics began in the 1970s with various goals. Verifying the correctness of proofs was only one of them and, for most researchers, not the most important. With the rise of AI-assisted and AI-generated proofs, however, the need for reliable verification tools has become increasingly important. In this talk, we will use examples from differential geometry and other areas to explain what it means for a proof to be formalized, whether by a human or by a large language model. We will explain which problems formalization can, and cannot, solve. Finally, we will discuss its role in recent announcements, including the claimed solution to the Navier–Stokes problem.
rec.location_text: Sophie Germain, 1013
rec.organizer: G. Franz, L. Hauswirth, P. Laurain, R. Petrides, R. Souam

rec.title: A mathematical perspective on Transformers
rec.speaker: Borjan GESHKOVSKI
rec.abstract: Physics has long supplied mathematics with some of its central equations. I will argue that Transformers, the engine of large language models, are becoming a source of the same kind. Starting from raw code, under various scaling assumptions, one can interpret Transformers as an interacting particle system in continuous time; tools from PDE and kinetic theory then explain empirically observed phenomena such as representation collapse and “lost in the middle”. Unlike in physics, however, the laws here are designed rather than given, so mathematical understanding can be written back into the architecture. I will close with some thoughts on what this two-way exchange means for applied mathematics.
rec.location_text: Sophie Germain, 1013
rec.organizer: G. Franz, L. Hauswirth, P. Laurain, R. Petrides, R. Souam

rec.title: The Spectral Gap for the Steklov Problem
rec.speaker: Asma HASSANNEZHAD
rec.abstract: We study the spectral gap for the Steklov problem on a Riemannian manifold. When a manifold has only one boundary component, it is known that the geometry of a boundary collar alone can provide a lower bound on the spectral gap. We therefore focus on manifolds with at least two boundary components. We show how the interior geometry can influence the spectral gap and establish a new connection between Steklov spectral gaps and the Neumann eigenvalues of interior subdomains. We then discuss applications of this connection to negatively curved manifolds. It is based on joint work with Tirumala Chakradhar and Bruno Colbois.
rec.location_text: Sophie Germain, 1013
rec.organizer: G. Franz, L. Hauswirth, P. Laurain, R. Petrides, R. Souam

rec.title: A Cartan Geometry from a Correspondence Space in Riemannian Geometry
rec.speaker: Rodrigo MORÓN SANZ
rec.abstract: Cartan geometries are curved analogues of homogeneous spaces, and the correspondence space construction produces, from a Cartan geometry of one type, another of a different type over a larger base manifold. The unit tangent bundle of a Riemannian manifold is, in this language, a Cartan geometry of type (Euc(n), O(n-1)) obtained in this way; we study Cartan geometries of this type in general, whether or not they arise as correspondence spaces. We show that every such geometry induces on its base manifold an almost contact metric structure, together with an orthogonal splitting of the tangent bundle and a compatible linear connection; conversely, these data determine the geometry, so that the correspondence is a bijection. Moreover, we single out a distinguished Cartan connection, which we call normal, by a condition on its torsion formulated in terms of the Spencer differential. This normalization is dictated by the correspondence space construction: the Cartan connection induced on the unit tangent bundle of a Riemannian manifold is normal.

rec.organizer: G. Franz, L. Hauswirth, P. Laurain, R. Petrides, R. Souam

rec.title: Model theory of limits
rec.speaker: Leo Gitin
rec.abstract:
We propose a model theory for directed limits and colimits of first-order structures, motivated by applications to commutative algebra and the model theory of valued fields. The treatment emphasises the natural assumption that transition maps are definable in a suitable sense.
Time permitting, I will explain connections to other approaches to this topic, including infinitary logic, Feferman’s local functors, ultraproducts, and pro- and ind-definable sets.
rec.location_text: Sophie Germain, 1013
rec.organizer: S. Anscombe, V. Bagayoko, H. Fournier

rec.title: Can you compute the operator norm in group C*-algebras?
rec.speaker: Isaac Goldbring
rec.abstract:
A paper by Fritz, Netzer, and Thom from 2012, titled "Can you compute the operator norm?", in essence initiated the computable structure theory for C*-algebras. The primary question involved is: given some "standard" presentation of a C*-algebra, is there an algorithm for computing the norm on the algebra? In this talk, I will focus on the case of C*-algebras arising from groups. In fact, most of the talk will focus on the case of the following four group C*-algebras: C^*(F_2), C^*(F_2\times F_2), C^*_r(F_2), C^*_r(F_2\times F_2). Here, for a group G, C^*(G) and C^*_r(G) denote the universal and reduced group C*-algebras associated to G, and F_2 denotes the free group on two generators. The answers to the question about computability of the norm for these four group C*-algebras turn out to be: yes, no, yes, and yes. The first is a result of FNT, the second a result due to myself and Thomas Sinclair from a year ago (answering a question of FN,T using recent results from quantum complexity theory), and the third and fourth recent results of mine (answering a question of Sinclair). Time permitting, I will discuss a potential generation of the latter results to wider classes of groups.
No prior knowledge of C*-algebra theory will be assumed.

rec.title: A homotopy-theoretic approach to representation stability
rec.speaker: Nicolas Guès
rec.abstract:
In a series of papers from the 2010s, Church, Ellenberg and Farb developed the notion of representation stability, aimed at understanding the asymptotic behavior of natural sequences of representations of the symmetric groups S_n, particularly those arising from homological invariants. Such phenomena typically occur for FI-modules, i.e., functors from FI (the category of finite sets and injections) to abelian groups.
In this talk, I will propose a homotopical refinement of representation stability: a derived version adapted to (co)FI-spaces. This viewpoint sheds light on how the phenomenon of representation stability can arise from the high (co)cartesianity of certain cubical diagrams. With this point of view, I will show how one can deduce polynomial growth results for the homotopy groups of ordered configuration spaces on closed manifolds, recover the best known bounds on their cohomology, and generalize stability results of Palmer concerning moduli spaces of submanifolds.

rec.title: Braided module categories from small braidings
rec.speaker: Tyler Franke
rec.abstract: Braided module categories are module categories over braided monoidal categories equipped with extra structure providing an action of the braid group of the annulus on endomorphism spaces. In this talk, I will define a small braiding on an inclusion of monoidal categories, which provides a braiding between objects in these categories. Small braidings give certain tensor ideals the canonical structure of a braided module category. Quantum groups are a natural source of small braidings, and from this we construct concrete examples of braided module categories and quantum moment maps. I will outline how we plan to use these examples in skein-theoretic realisations of double affine Hecke algebras and certain modules thereof. Based on joint work-in-progress with Ingo Runkel and Volker Schomerus.

rec.abstract: The Milnor conjecture, a theorem of Kato and Voevodsky, asserts a close relation between bilinear forms, Milnor K-theory, Galois cohomology and differential forms defined over fields. I want to explain an extension of these results in mixed characteristics, building on work of Jacobson and obtained in joint work with Arnab Kundu which relies on recent development in syntomic and motivic cohomology.

rec.title: Condensed homotopy types in algebraic geometry, arithmetic geometry, and logic
rec.speaker: Peter Haine
rec.abstract:
Let X be a locally topologically noetherian scheme. In their paper on the proétale topology, Bhatt and Scholze defined the proétale fundamental group π1proét(X). The profinite completion of π1proét(X) recovers the usual étale fundamental group. Moreover, π1proét(X) agrees with π1ét(X) when X is normal, but π1proét(X) has the better property that it classifies Qp-local systems. In this talk, we’ll explain how to use condensed mathematics to define a “condensed homotopy type” whose fundamental group refines the proétale fundamental group. We’ll also talk about two related “condensed homotopy types”: one for adic spaces and one in the setting of logic. All three are special cases of a more general invariant of ∞-topoi. For adic spaces, the fundamental group refines the de Jong fundamental group, and in logic, the fundamental group recovers the Lascar group of a complete first-order theory.
These results come from several projects, carried out jointly with Holzschuh–Lara–Mair–Martini–Wolf, Achinger–Holzschuh–Lara–Mair–Wolf, and Damaj–Zhang.

rec.title: Topological freeness for minimal actions of groups with the rapid decay property
rec.speaker: Joseph Gondek
rec.abstract: We apply an operator-algebraic property of finitely generated groups, called rapid decay (RD), to topological dynamics. The class of groups with RD includes the hyperbolic groups and cocompact lattices in SL3(R), among many other examples. We show that the compact, minimal G-spaces of an RD group G with amenable neighbourhood stabilizers have some rigidity properties; under general conditions, all such actions are topologically free. This is joint work with Nazmul Alam, Mehrdad Kalantar, and Randy Pham.

rec.title: How to draw a module category: a glimpse into Auslander-Reiten theory
rec.speaker: Marius Goguet
rec.abstract:
Categories are often seen as very abstract mathematical objects that are hard to grasp. However, in the case of module categories of finite dimensional algebras, we can understand and represent them in a very concrete way by drawing their Auslander-Reiten quiver.
The general strategy is to break down the category into appropriate building blocks: indecomposable objects, irreducible morphisms and almost split sequences. We will define all these notions and illustrate them on examples of algebras given by quivers with relations.

It relies on two main results of independent interest: a Nash structure theorem for the stable completion of an algebraic curve and a tame descent theorem for abstract open polydiscs.

rec.title: Sard’s theorem in infinite dimension: from real algebraic geometry to sub-Riemannian geometry
rec.speaker: Antonio Lerario
rec.abstract:
Sard’s theorem can fail in infinite dimension, even for polynomial maps with finite-dimensional targets. I will explain how quantitative estimates in real algebraic geometry, combined with finite-dimensional approximation, yield Sard criteria in this setting. I will then show how Kupka’s classical counterexample can be realized inside a sub-Riemannian endpoint map. This produces a smooth bracket-generating distribution whose endpoint map has no regular values, disproving the sub-Riemannian Sard conjecture in the smooth category.
Based on joint works with Luca Rizzi and Daniele Tiberio.

rec.title: On the undecidability of the QWEP for C*-algebras
rec.speaker: Isaac Goldring
rec.abstract: In his landmark 1993 paper, Kirchberg introduced a property of C*-algebras called the QWEP, which stands for “quotient of the weak expectation property”. As the name suggests, the property is defined by the fact that the algebra is a quotient of a C*-algebra with the weak expectation property, which was a property introduced by Lance years earlier in connection with the theory of tensor products of C*-algebras. While at first glance this seems to be a strange property, Kirchberg showed that whether or not every C*-algebra has the QWEP is equivalent to the famous Connes Embedding Problem (CEP) from von Neumann algebra theory. The CEP remained open for nearly 50 years until its recent refutation in 2020 via a result in quantum complexity theory (as well as the equivalence with Kirchberg’s QWEP conjecture). Several years ago, I showed that the QWEP is an axiomatizable property of C*-algebras. In this talk, I will present joint work with Aruseelan and Hart where we show that the QWEP does not have an effective axiomatization and, in fact, there can be no effectively axiomatizable satisfiable theory of C*-algebras all of whose models have the QWEP (modulo some nontrivially conditions). The proofs uses the connection with the quantum complexity results mentioned above as well as other techniques from C*-algebra theory. No prior knowledge of continuous logic, operator algebras, or quantum complexity will be assumed.

rec.title: Algebraic Hodge-Generic Points and the Period Conjecture
rec.speaker: Gregorio Baldi
rec.abstract: Let f:X\to S be a quasi-projective family of varieties defined over Qbar. We prove that the points of S(Qbar) that are Hodge generic for the variation of Hodge structures associated to f are analytically dense in S. More generally, motivated by the Grothendieck period conjecture and under a large-monodromy assumption, we establish the density of algebraic points at which the periods of the fibre satisfy no unexpected relations of degree at most delta. The main technical input is a new result on relations among solutions of G-operators, based on height estimates of Bombieri and André. This is a joint work with Gal Binyamini and David Urbanik.

rec.title: Eliminating imaginaries in perfect, bounded, multi valued PAC fields
rec.speaker: Bryan Gonzalez Leandro
rec.abstract: Elimination of imaginaries is a fundamental structural property in model theory, which roughly means that definable equivalence classes can be coded by tuples of elements from the structure, allowing us to treat them as ordinary elements of the structure. In the context of valued fields, significant progress was initiated by Haskell, Hrushovski, and Macpherson, who described a language in which the theory ACVF eliminates imaginaries. Building on this foundation, Rideau-Kikuchi and Montenegro proved elimination of imaginaries for bounded pseudo p-adically closed fields equipped with finitely many independent valuations. In this talk, I will explain how their techniques can be adapted to prove weak elimination of imaginaries for perfect bounded PAC fields equipped with finitely many independent valuations. The strategy combines an extension theorem for types to invariant types with an amalgamation result.

rec.title: Constructing actions with Fraïssé limits
rec.speaker: Paolo Boldrini
rec.abstract: Given an action of a countable group on the Cantor space, clopen subsets can be compared by cutting and moving through the action or by evaluating them on invariant measures. Dynamical comparison asserts that the measure-theoretic notion controls the dynamical one. Since its first appearance, dynamical comparison has been verified for a wide variety of actions. In this talk, I will survey some recent positive results in this direction and present the construction of the first examples of topologically free minimal actions that fail dynamical comparison, obtained in a joint work with Akshara Prasad. The construction is based on an algebraic invariant known as the type semigroup and involves Fraïssé limits of Boolean algebras equipped with monoid-valued measures.

rec.title: F-CohFTs, their Givental group and tautological relations
rec.speaker: Paolo Rossi
rec.abstract: F-CohFTs are the natural generalization of cohomological field theories (CohFTs) when moving from the Deligne- Mumford compactification of the moduli space of stable curves given by nodal stable curves to the partial compactification given by curves with only separating nodes. They are natural under various viewpoints and were inspired by integrable systems considerations. As it happens for CohFTs, F-CohFTs can be used to probe the cohomology of this partial compactification, based on an analogue of the Givental-Teleman classification of semisimple CohFTs and similar nonsemisimple limiting techniques.

rec.title: Curve counting through intrinsic mirror symmetry
rec.speaker: Michel van Garrel
rec.abstract: According to Mirror Symmetry, the generating function of curve counting Gromov-Witten invariants of a Calabi-Yau threefold is conjectured to equal the integral over the positive real locus of a mirror-dual family of Calabi-Yau threefolds. In this joint work with Siebert, we prove that this conjecture holds as stated in the case of the canonical bundle of the projective plane with its mirror family constructed via the intrinsic mirror construction of Gross-Siebert. A key feature of the proof is that at no point do we calculate any invariants. Instead, we work with the punctured Gromov-Witten invariants that govern the intrinsic mirror construction.

rec.title: Torus actions on compactified braid varieties and polytopality of subword complexes
rec.speaker: Mikhail Gorsky
rec.abstract:
Every cluster variety admits a faithful regular group action scaling all cluster variables. Given a partial compactification of a cluster variety, a natural question is whether this action extends to a regular action on the compactification. I will explain that, in the case of braid varieties for simple Lie groups, the answer is affirmative for brick compactifications. If the braid variety is an open Richardson variety in the flag variety, the same result holds for the corresponding closed Richardson variety. In the latter case, the faithfully acting group is a torus of rank the Kazhdan-Lusztig d-invariant. The same result holds for projected Richardson varieties. I will also explain that, in general, a braid variety is a torus if and only if each of its brick compactifications is a toric variety with respect to this extended action, if and only if the polar dual of the moment polytope for this action realizes the corresponding subword complex. The braid words satisfying this property turn out to be precisely the double root free words of V. Pilaud and C. Stump. This provides a novel approach to the longstanding open question of the polytopality of spherical subword complexes asked by A. Knutson and E. Miller in 2004, and in particular gives infinite families of subword complexes admitting polytopal realizations in dimension higher than the rank of the corresponding Coxeter group. The talk is based on joint work with Lara Bossinger and José Simental, arXiv:2609.12414.
This talk will take place in hybrid mode at the Institut Henri Poincaré.

rec.title: "Quantum'' rational numbers, q-deformed Coxeter friezes, and the cross-ratio
rec.speaker: Valentin OVSIENKO
rec.abstract:
The classical cross-ratio ``crosses'' both classical and modern mathematics, linking geometry with combinatorics, dynamics, and mathematical physics. It provides natural coordinates on many moduli spaces. In this talk, I will introduce a new q-deformed, or ``quantum'' cross-ratio: a PSL(2,Z)-invariant of ordered quadruples of distinct points on the rational projective line. The construction is based on the theory of q-deformed rational numbers developed jointly with Sophie Morier-Genoud. I will discuss several properties of this new invariant, with its close connection to q-deformed Coxeter frieze patterns taking centre stage.
This talk will take place in hybrid mode at the Institut Henri Poincaré.

rec.title: Braid group invariance of quantum tori and applications
rec.speaker: Francesca Paganelli
rec.abstract:
A well-known fact in classical Lie theory is that the Weyl group W associated with a simple, complex, finite-dimensional Lie algebra g acts by isometries on the dual of the Cartan subalgebra. In particular, the symmetric bilinear form defined on the weight lattice is invariant under the W-action.
In this talk, I will present an analogue of this invariance phenomenon for skew-symmetric bicharacters in the context of quantum affine algebras. Specifically, we will consider the groups of fundamental and pre-fundamental l-weights (which can be viewed as affine analogues of the fundamental weights of g). By results of Chari and Frenkel–Hernandez, the braid group B associated with g acts on these groups of l-weights. We then introduce the skew-symmetric bicharacters on the groups of l-weights defined by Nakajima and Hernandez, and extended by Bittmann and myself. I will show that these bicharacters are invariant under the B-action on l-weight groups, and present an application concerning quantum QQ-systems in the theory of shifted quantum groups.
This talk will take place in hybrid mode at the Institut Henri Poincaré.

rec.title: Left Structures and Purity
rec.speaker: Kevin Schlegel
rec.abstract:
Under mild assumptions on a small additive category, we establish a one-to-one correspondence
between its exact structures and certain closed subsets of the Ziegler spectrum of the ind-completion
of the category. This is based on a newly developed connection between exact structures and the theory
of purity. In fact, our results also apply to left structures, which vastly generalize exact structures.

rec.title: The Simplicial Cylinder DG Ring
rec.speaker: Amnon YEKUTIELI
rec.speaker_affiliation: Ben Gurion University, Israel et Université Paris 7
rec.abstract:
The Keller cylinder DG ring encodes homotopies between DG ring homomorphisms f_0, f_1 : A --> B.
Recently we discovered the higher cylinder DG rings Cyl_q(B), which assemble into the simplicial cylinder DG ring Cyl(B). For q=1 this recovers Keller's original construction.
The sets SHom_q(A,B) of DG ring homomorphisms A \to Cyl_q(B) form the simplicial Hom set SHom(A,B). Our main result is that when A is a semi-free DG ring, the simplicial set SHom(A,B) is a Kan complex.
We prove several results about the fundamental groupoid SHom_{\leq 1}(A,B), including invariance under quasi-isomorphism B' \to B, and that the automorphism groups are abelian. We also indicate some applications of this work, including to DG categories.
This talk will take place on Zoom only.

rec.title: Cohomologie étale des algèbres de Stein.
rec.speaker: Olivier Benoist
rec.abstract: Les variétés de Stein sont les analogues, en géométrie analytique complexe, des variétés algébriques affines. Je présenterai une version du théorème de comparaison d'Artin dans ce cadre : la cohomologie singulière à coefficients finis d'une variété de Stein est isomorphe à la cohomologie étale de son algèbre de fonctions holomorphes globales. Comme application, je montrerai que toute classe de cohomologie entière de degré au moins 2 sur une variété de Stein est supportée sur un sous-ensemble analytique strict. rec.abstract:
The theory of weight functions by Mustaţă-Nicaise on Berkovich spaces hints at an intrinsic approach to studying skeleta without the limitations of the usual tools from algebraic geometry, i.e., semistable reduction or resolution of singularities. In this talk we discuss how Mustaţă-Nicaise's construction can be generalised to define weight functions intrinsically on any quasi-smooth Berkovich space as a sort of normalised log-discrepancy of a canonical form.
Next, we turn our attention to computing weight functions on the Berkovich affine line over any non-Archimedean field K. This question reduces to the entirely value-theoretic problem of describing the integral log differentials $\Omega^{\log}_{L^\circ / K^\circ}$ for a simple extension of real valued fields $L / K$ , which we describe using the data in MacLane-Vaquié chains.
We find that on the affine line, weight functions are completely determined by the integral piecewise linear (Z-PL) structure the affine line and vice versa, yielding new insight into the Z-PL structure.
Finally, we discuss how this can be used to define and compute the essential skeleton of certain Berkovich spaces.

rec.title: Origami Tori
rec.speaker: Richard Schwartz
rec.abstract: An origami torus is a piecewise affine isometric embedding of a flat torus into R^3. It is surprising that these things exist, but they have been known to exist since 1960. How many vertices do you need to make an origami torus? In my talk, I will explain my proof that you can do it with 8 but not with 7. I will also explain why almost every flat torus is isometric to an origami torus -- this is joint work with Peter Doyle. If time permits I will also explain why, in fact, every flat torus is isometric to an 8-vertex origami torus. This is upcoming work with Doyle, Fabian Lander, and Steve Trettel.

rec.title: Séparer les composantes des variétés algébriques réelles par des invariants cohomologiques.
rec.speaker: Samuel Lerbet
rec.abstract: Si X est une variété algébrique complexe, il suit du théorème de comparaison de M. Artin que X et son lieu complexe X(C) ont le même nombre de composantes connexes, la première pour la topologie de Zariski, le second pour la topologie analytique ou forte. Au contraire, si X est une variété algébrique réelle connexe, son lieu réel X(R) est disconnexe pour la topologie forte en général. On peut néanmoins se demander si l'on peut séparer les composantes connexes de X(R) par des invariants algébriques de X. On peut pour cela utiliser des invariants de nature cohomologique : ainsi, E. Witt a montré que le signe des classes dans le groupe de Brauer d'une courbe algébrique réelle lisse séparent les composantes connexes de son lieu réel. La possibilité d'une telle séparation par un invariant cohomologique de degré donné dépend cependant de la relation entre ce dernier et la dimension : cela motive l'étude de l'optimalité de ce degré pour une dimension donnée. Le but de l'exposé est d'expliquer des résultats autour de cette question pour la séparation par la cohomologie et par son raffinement non ramifié et, si le temps le permet, des applications à la signature globale des formes quadratiques. Il s'agit d'un travail en commun avec Olivier Benoist.

rec.title: Sur l´homologie asymptotique des graphes Lagrangians. (Avec Alfonso Sorrentino)
rec.speaker: Rafael Ruggiero
rec.abstract: Nous demontrons que les directions homologiques asymptotiques des orbites dans un graphe Lagrangien invariant par un flot Hamiltonien de Tonelli dans le tore au dessus du niveau critique de Mañé sont contenues dans un cône positif dans la norme stable autour d´un vecteur dans le premier group d'homologie à coefficients réels. En dimension 3, nous trouvons un rapport entre l´homologie asymptotique d´un graphe Lagrangien invariant et l´ensemble de rotation de Misiurewicz-Ziemann. Comme application, nous demontrons qu´il n'existent pas de graphes de Hedlund dans le 3-tore, ceux-ci sont des graphes avec exactement 3 orbites périodiques dont l´homologie engendre le premier group d´homologie.
