rec.title: Les polygraphes réguliers et leur théorème de recollement homotopique
rec.speaker: Clémence Chanavat
rec.abstract:
Je commencerai par présenter deux (ou trois) manières de régulariser les polygraphes, que j'appellerai méthode-Hadzihasanovic, méthode-Steiner et, si le temps le permet, méthode-Henry.
J'expliquerai pourquoi la méthode-Hadzihasanovic ne produit pas toujours des polygraphes, à moins que l'on impose aux ∞-catégories strictes des lois d'échange supplémentaires, dictées par des égalités de topologie combinatoire.
Je terminerai par un théorème de recollement, issu de mes derniers travaux, qui assure que certains de ces polygraphes sont librement générés en un sens homotopique, ce qui signifie que ce sont aussi des polygraphes dans la théorie des (∞, n)-catégories.

rec.title: Combinatoire des mots, combinatoire énumérative et combinatoire algébrique autour de la forme normale alternante des tresses
rec.speaker: June Roupin
rec.abstract:
Les tresses sont des objets topologiques qui possèdent de très bonnes propriétés combinatoires, et peuvent en particulier être représentées et étudiées comme des classes d’équivalence de mots sur l'alphabet des transpositions. Un concept naturel dans ce contexte est la notion de forme normale : le choix d’un représentant unique pour chaque tresse. La forme normale alternante, dont l’étude a initialement été motivée par ses liens avec l’ordre standard des tresses, associe à chaque tresse sur n fils une séquence unique de tresses sur n-1 fils, appelés des blocs, permettant de définir récursivement un unique représentant.
Dans cet exposé, je vais présenter quelques propriétés combinatoires et algébriques importante de la forme normale alternante, notamment la régularité et l'automaticité du langage associé. Je vais ensuite aborder plusieurs applications de ces résultats couvrant divers domaines de combinatoires : énumération des tresses ; bon ordre totale sur le monoïde de tresse ; généralisations aux monoïdes d'Artin-Tits.

rec.title: Well-typed program generation, with prenex polymorphism
rec.speaker: Gabriel Scherer
rec.abstract:
Fuzzing” is a popular testing approach where we throw random inputs at a program and check that it respects some expected properties on all inputs. Fuzzing a metaprogram such as a compiler requires producing random input programs. To exercise interesting behaviors of the compiler, we want our input programs to be well-formed in a strong sense, in particular to be well-typed. Generating random well-typed program is difficult when the type-system is powerful, there is a whole scientific literature on the topic, see for example [Testing an Optimising Compiler by Generating Random Lambda Terms, Pałka, 2012].
Most existing generators integrate a large part of the implementation of a type-checker, “inverted” to assist in top-down random term generation by efficiently discarding choices that result in ill-typed programs. Scaling this approach to a full language would result in implementing two sophisticated type-checkers, once in the compiler and once in the program generator. This is one type-checker too many!
We present preliminary work on reusing the constraint-based type inference approach [The Essence of ML-based type inference, Pottier and Rémy, 2004] to write a single type-checker that can be used for both purposes: to check types of user-provided programs, and to efficiently guide a random program generator. This only requires a fairly simple modification to constraint generators: parametrizing them over a search monad. We have succesfully implemented a generator of simply-typed terms in this style, and are in the process (almost done) of scaling it to Hindley-Milner type inference.
(Relevant previous work is [Making Random Judgments: Automatically Generating Well-Typed Terms from the Definition of a Type-System, Fetscher, Claessen, Pałka, Hughes, Findler]. They start from Redex, a Racket DSL to implement simple type systems, and derive a random program generator. The limitation of this approach is that Redex only works with fairly simple type systems, in particular we do not expect it to scale to ML-style type inference with polymorphism, which is the part that hand-crafted generators also struggle on.)
Note: I gave a Formath talk on a preliminary version of this work in March 2024. At the time my prototype only supported the simply-typed lambda-calculus. The extension to Hindley-Milner is follow-up joint work with my 2025 intern Hugo Barreiro. I will also discuss optimizations to the search monad that are necessary to effectively generate terms of larger size.

rec.title: Remarques autour de la formule U^X = ∑_A:U X^A
rec.speaker: Mathieu Anel
rec.abstract: Cette formule classique de théorie des types est remarquable en ce qu’elle égalise des constructions contravariante et covariante en X. Pour l'étudier, je vais me placer dans la catégorie des algèbres sous la monade polynomiale associée à la famille universelle de types U’—>U. Cette catégorie est additive et monoïdale et on peut y relire la formule en terme de dualité et de formes quadratiques. Cela permet une caractérisation précise des paires (U,X) pour lesquelles la formule est vraie.

rec.title: ProofTree: Structured Representations for Human-Centred Mathematical Exploration
rec.speaker: Carl Jontza
rec.abstract:
If formal proofs become abundant, how can we help people find mathematics they care about and explore it in ways that are understandable and engaging? I will present ongoing work on ProofTree, investigating a persistent, versioned graph of goals, assumptions, and alternative arguments as an intermediate representation connecting human-readable reasoning with formal proofs. The aim is to support discovery, understanding, and human guidance at levels of abstraction suited to a person’s background, interests, and objectives.
A case study from Lean-based proof hierarchies, involving confusion between an induction hypothesis and a proof obligation, will motivate technical questions about preserving logical scope, revising arguments, and maintaining links to checked proofs. I will discuss what records of exploration should preserve for subsequent reuse, and outline an evaluation agenda that considers mathematical relevance, understanding, and user experience alongside proof completion and human and computational cost.

rec.title: Verso Blueprint: Reimagining Blueprints for the AI Era
rec.speaker: Emilio Gallego Arias
rec.abstract:
Large-scale formalization projects have long needed tools to
coordinate contributions, track dependencies, and connect mathematical
exposition with formal proofs. A key example is Lean
Blueprint. Introduced in 2020 for the sphere eversion project, Lean
Blueprint extends plasTeX to provide a shared map of statements,
dependencies, Lean declarations, and progress. Lean Blueprint's model
has been quite influential and has helped shape how mathematicians and
formalizers work together on large-scale formalization projects.
This talk presents recent work on Verso Blueprint, a Lean-native
implementation of the Lean Blueprint concept built on Verso, Lean's
official markup language. Designed for close integration with Lean,
Verso Blueprint maintains a three-layer database linking source
material, informal statements, and their formalized counterparts. The
database is populated from Verso documents, analysis of Lean
declarations, and other user-provided data. Interactive HTML views
provide navigation and previews, connecting mathematical exposition
with the formal development. We have now largely reached our original
goal, with functionality comparable to Lean Blueprint or Lean
Architect.
But matching that functionality is no longer enough: this is an
extraordinary moment for formalisation. The practice is radically
chaining even as we build its tools.
When we began this project, our central use case was for humans to
write detailed statements and dependencies to guide
formalization. Today, coding agents are increasingly writing and
interacting with the blueprints themselves in an autonomous
fashion. Blueprints are taking on the reverse role: not just guiding
the construction of formal proofs, but making AI-generated proofs
intelligible to humans. At the same time, dependency tracking and
organizational information remain essential for coordinating
large-scale autoformalization. For example, Prove2Me, a theorem
database with dependency tracking, played a key coordination role in
the recent Fermat's Last Theorem auto-formalization milestone.
What comes next for blueprints in this extraordinary moment? We are
redesigning Verso Blueprint around the idea of "programmatic
blueprints": human-readable, machine-actionable objects synchronized
with formal developments. Our ambition is for blueprints to become a
*foundational harness for AI-assisted formalization*, maintaining the
shared state of a project and coordinating what happens next across
mathematicians, formalizers, code repository workflows, and agents.

rec.title: Compilation of pattern-matching by small inversion
rec.speaker: W. Ait Moussa
rec.abstract:
Dependent inductive data types are an essential part of type theory based proof-assistant, where they close the gap between theorem proving and functional programming. Their meaning and computational behavior are given by dependent recursors, but those are tedious and unintuitive to work with in a dependent setting. Today, the established practice in dependent settings is to have an expressive high-level dependent pattern matching construct with the same logical power as recursors but which is more natural to work with.
This talk will be split into three parts. First, I will go over the history and established theory of dependent-pattern matching and its correspondence to recursors. Then I will present an alternative translation of the non-recursive part of pattern matching to recursors using small-inversion. Finally, I will present an implementation for Rocq of the latter, written by Thierry Martinez a few years back ; in addition to its value as a basis for a specification for this translation, of particular interest is its extensive use of Ocaml's GADTs in order to formalize a notion of intrinsically well-formed Rocq terms.

rec.title: Dynamics of singularity surfaces for the compressible viscous fluids.
rec.speaker: Marcel Zodji
rec.speaker_affiliation: Laboratoire de Mathématiques et Modélisation d'Évry
rec.abstract:
The motion of a compressible viscous fluid is described by the Navier-Stokes system.
It is a system of hyperbolic-parabolic mixed-type PDEs. In this talk, we will study
the so-called density patch problem: \emph{If we are given a density that is initially "regular"
on both sides of a hypersurface across which it is discontinuous, will this structure
be preserved over time?}
An important quantity in the mathematical analysis of this system is the so-called effective flux,
which was discovered by Hoff and Smoller (1985). More precisely, the mathematical properties
of this quantity play a crucial role in the study of the propagation of oscillations in
compressible fluids [Serre, 1991], in the construction of weak solutions [P-L Lions, 1996] or the
propagation of discontinuity surfaces [Hoff, 2002], to cite just a few examples.
In the case of density-dependent viscosities, the behavior of the effective flux degenerates,
which renders the analysis more subtle.

rec.title: Multi-scale modeling and analysis of signal processing in neurons
rec.speaker: Claire Guerrier
rec.abstract: In this talk, I will present models for signal propagation in neurons, ranging from the macro- to the micro-scale, with various applications to neuronal signalling. The first application concerns myelin plasticity, and the influence of neuronal myelin geometry on signal transmission. We investigate the evolution of the maximum of a signal in a damped heat equation on x>0, with a Dirichlet boundary condition representing the signal, which models signal transmission in a myelinated internode. We derive an expression of the solution, and derive the Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator at x=0. We then investigate the max. At a more refined scale, to investigate signal summation in the neuronal dendritic tree, we consider the Poisson-Nernst Planck system of equations representing ionic electrodiffusion in an electrolyte. This system expresses a sharp boundary layer of the size of the Debye length at the boundary, where the extra-charges accumulates. In particular, we derive an asymptotic approximation of the solution at steady state, in the regime of small Debye length.

rec.title: Mosquito borne disease outbreak : Climate change impact to Physics Informed Neural Network use
rec.speaker: Aniket Banerjee
rec.abstract:
Dengue, Zika and chikungunya are expanding across new
territories as their vector, the tiger mosquito _Aedes albopictus_,
tracks a warming climate. Forecasting where and when outbreaks will
occur requires models that are both mechanistically faithful to mosquito
ecology and disciplined by real observational data — yet the
biological parameters that govern transmission, such as the biting rate,
the extrinsic incubation period and mosquito survival, are precisely the
ones we cannot measure directly in the field.
In this talk, I present a national -scale furcating framework that
couples a mechanistic _Aedes albopictus_ population model, in the spirit
of the Arbocarto approach, to a vector-to-human transmission layer, and
the use of Neural Network use to predict diffusion pattern in
epidemiological systems. I will explain the modelling choices behind the
population and transmission layers, the structure of the inverse
problem, and how PINNs let a mechanistic model "speak" to messy,
heterogeneous data.

rec.title: Lissage par peignes et trivialité locale pour les espaces homogènes au-dessus d’une courbe relative
rec.speaker: Margot Bruneaux
rec.abstract:
Soit $R$ un anneau local hensélien, de corps résiduel $\kappa$, soit $C$ une courbe projective lisse sur $R$, à fibres géométriquement connexes, soit $G$ un $C$-groupe réductif dont le tore radical $\operatorname{rad}(G)$ est isotrivial, et soit $E\to C$ un $G$-torseur.
Nous montrons que, si le noyau de l'isogénie centrale
\[
G_{\mathrm{sc}}\times_C \operatorname{rad}(G)\longrightarrow G
\]
est étale sur $C$, ou bien si $\kappa$ est un corps suffisamment grand, alors la trivialité de $E_\kappa\to C_\kappa$ pour la topologie de Zariski implique la trivialité de $E\to C$ pour cette même topologie.
Nous démontrons également une version « moyennée » de ce résultat, en supposant seulement que $\operatorname{rad}(G)$ est isotrivial, ainsi qu'une variante concernant les espaces homogènes projectifs, sans aucune hypothèse restrictive sur $G$.
Ces résultats ont notamment pour conséquences un principe local-global pour les torseurs sur les corps de fonctions de courbes au-dessus d'anneaux de valuation discrète henséliens, renforçant des travaux de Gille--Parimala--Suresh, ainsi qu'une version hensélienne d'un théorème de Drinfeld--Simpson.
Nos démonstrations sont de nature géométrique. Elles reposent sur des compactifications de torseurs et sur une technique de lissage par peignes, dans une version relative et arithmétique que nous développons en détail, en nous appuyant sur les travaux de Kollár et de Graber--Harris--Starr.
En collaboration avec Federico Scavia.

rec.title: Mod p de Rham cohomology of Shimura varieties
rec.speaker: Martin Ortiz
rec.abstract: The weight part of Serre's conjecture studies the modularity of certain spaces of mod p automorphic forms. In the case of Shimura varieties, this is usually done by considering their etale cohomology, with Serre weights as coefficients. One can also propose a similar conjecture for mod p de Rham cohomology of Shimura varieties, and I conjecture that the two approaches are equivalent. I can prove this generically for G=GL3, and some cases in GSp4. Moreover, for GSp4 this approach produces a generic entailment of Serre weights, which is completely invisible from the etale cohomology perspective.

rec.title: Le principe d'incertitude fort sur les groupes abéliens finis
rec.speaker: Emma Weschler
rec.abstract:
En mécanique quantique, le principe d'incertitude d'Heisenberg stipule qu'on ne peut connaître simultanément avec précision la position et la vitesse d'une particule. Cette célèbre inégalité relie en réalité une fonction et sa transformée de Fourier.
En 1989, motivés par des applications en traitement du signal, Donoho et Stark donnent un nouveau principe d'incertitude, non plus pour des fonctions définies sur les réels mais sur un groupe abélien fini. Ce dernier a ensuite été significativement amélioré : en 2006, Tao prouve ce qu'on peut appeler un principe d'incertitude fort pour des fonctions définies sur Z/pZ, où p est premier.
Plus récemment, en 2021, Garcia, Karaali et Katz généralisent ce principe aux corps finis, pour des fonctions vérifiant une certaine condition de symétrie qu'on détaillera.
Dans cet exposé, on présentera une généralisation du principe d'incertitude fort pour des groupes abéliens finis quelconques et nous verrons ce que donne l'étude de ce dernier sur les groupes cycliques.

rec.title: Biased random walk on dynamical percolation
rec.speaker: Nina Gantert
rec.abstract:
As an example for a random walk in random environment, we
study biased random walk for dynamical percolation on the
d-dimensional lattice. We establish a law
of large numbers and an invariance principle for this random walk
using regeneration times.
Moreover, we verify that the Einstein relation holds, and we
investigate the speed of the walk
as a function of the bias. While for d = 1 the speed is
increasing, we show that in general this
fails in dimension d ? 2. As our main result, we establish two
regimes of parameters, separated
by a critical curve, such that the speed is either eventually
strictly increasing or eventually
strictly decreasing. This is in sharp contrast to the biased
random walk on a static supercritical
percolation cluster, where the speed is known to be eventually
zero.
Based on joint work with Sebastian Andres, Dominik Schmid and
Perla Sousi.

rec.title: Percolation de premier passage brochette
rec.speaker: Maxime Marivain
rec.abstract:
Nous étudions un nouveau modèle de percolation de premier passage, appelé percolation de premier passage brochette, dans lequel les temps de passage associés aux arêtes situées sur une même droite sont égaux. Nous établissons tout d'abord un théorème de convergence point à point, où la constante de temps est identifiée. En particulier, nous étudions le cas où cette constante de temps est nulle et mettons en évidence l'existence d'une grande variété de comportements possibles.
Nous démontrons ensuite un théorème de forme, montrant que la forme limite est le diamant L^1. Nous étendons ensuite l'analyse en établissant un théorème de convergence point à point dans le cadre où les temps de passage peuvent prendre la valeur infinie. Enfin, nous nous intéressons à la déviation transversale maximale des géodésiques par rapport à la ligne droite. Nous démontrons l'existence de géodésiques sous des hypothèses faibles et déterminons l'ordre de grandeur de leur déviation par rapport à la ligne droite en fonction du comportement de la distribution des temps de passage au voisinage de son infimum.

rec.title: À propos de la tessellation de Poisson-Delaunay : quelques techniques classiques et de nouveaux résultats de loi
rec.speaker: Cecilia d'Errico
rec.abstract:
Dans cet exposé, nous présentons la tessellation de Delaunay issue d’un processus ponctuel de Poisson homogène sur Rd. Dans une première partie, nous parlerons de la cellule typique et montrerons comment obtenir sa loi à l’aide d’une technique 'combo'
classique : la formule de Mecke + changement de variable de Blaschke-Petkantschin. Dans la deuxième partie, nous étudions le volume de cette cellule : nous voyons comment obtenir ses moments, puis nous résolvons le problème des moments pour déterminer la loi
du volume de la cellule typique. Enfin, nous présenterons d’autres résultats de loi de fonctionnelles de la cellule typique que nous avons obtenus en étendant ces techniques.

rec.title: Delocalisation of the disordered long-range discrete Gaussian chain
rec.speaker: Corentin Faipeur
rec.abstract:
The long-range discrete Gaussian chain (DGC) is a 1D height function model with $1/r^\alpha$ interactions between pairs of sites at distance $r$. The DGC is known to delocalise at every temperature when $\alpha>2$ (i.e. the typical height at the origin diverges when the size of the system goes to infinity), to localise when $1<\alpha<2$, and to present a localisation/delocalisation phase transition at $\alpha=2$.
In this talk, we will consider a disordered version of the long-range DGC, obtained by adding an external random field. We will show that this disordered model becomes delocalised at all temperatures for all $\alpha>3/2$, and provide quantitative estimates of this delocalisation phenomenon. If time permits, I will also present a central limit theorem for the height at the origin. Joint work with Christopher Chalhoub, Paul Dario and Arnaud Le Ny.

rec.title: [mini-cours] Combinatorics and Geometry: Crossing paths—in the age of AI. (Part 1)
rec.speaker: János Pach
rec.speaker_affiliation: Rényi Institute, Budapest, et EPFL, Lausanne
rec.abstract:
Crossing numbers: Dead or alive. The crossing
number of a graph G, denoted by cr(G), is the smallest number of
edge crossings in any drawing of G in the plane. Clearly, cr(G)=0
if and only if G is planar. Garey and Johnson proved that
determining cr(G) is an NP-complete problem. Over the past forty
years, crossing numbers have proven to play a vital role in
various fields, including discrete and computational geometry,
number theory, and circuit layout (such as providing lower bounds
on the chip area required for a graph's physical layout). Yet,
many of the foundational questions that inspired research in this
area remain open, and new mysteries continue to emerge. Quo
vadis?
rec.location_text: Salle B107
rec.series_name: Séminaire de l'équipe Probabilités et Statistique

rec.title: [mini-cours] Combinatorics and Geometry: Crossing paths—in the age of AI. (Part 2)
rec.speaker: János Pach
rec.speaker_affiliation: Rényi Institute, Budapest, et EPFL, Lausanne
rec.abstract:
What makes the chromatic number of a graph large?
There have been many attempts to answer this question. The
most natural approach is to look for unavoidable substructures in
graphs of large chromatic number. In 1943, Hadwiger made the
conjecture that every graph of chromatic number r can be
transformed into a complete graph of r vertices by a series of
edge contractions and vertex and edge deletions. This is one of
the most important unsolved problems in graph theory. After giving
a somewhat biased survey of the problem, I plan to report on some
related recent results, joint with Fox and Suk.

rec.title: Height one phenomena in p-adic Hodge theory
rec.speaker: Tasos MOULINOS
rec.abstract:
The syntomification of the integers (Z_p^syn) acts as a parameter space for p-adic cohomology theories. By the work of Drinfeld and others, it is known to carry a canonical formal group, and hence a map to the moduli stack of formal groups. Pulling back along this map gives rise to a certain line bundle equipped with a distinguished section "v_1". On the p-completed moduli stack of formal groups, the nonvanishing of v_1 defines the substack parametrizing "height-1" formal groups. Yet the preimage of this locus on Z_p^syn, when computed in p-adic formal stacks, is empty. There is a mismatch here because inverting v_1 on syntomic cohomology gives p-adic étale cohomology, but inverting it on the stack itself before passing to global sections gives nothing.
I will explain how passing to analytic stacks brings this missing locus into view. By realizing the p-completed moduli stack of formal groups as an analytic stack, we construct an algebro-geometric shadow of K(1)-localization. Applied to syntomification, this produces an analytic stack whose dualizable quasi-coherent sheaves recover p-adic Galois representations, and more generally lisse étale sheaves on the generic fiber of a p-adic formal scheme. I will explain how a perfected version of this construction depends only on the generic fiber, providing a geometric counterpart to purity results for K(1)-localized K-theory.
This is joint work in progress with Greg Andreychev.

rec.title: Dynamique de Aut(F_n) sur G^n, pour G compact et n grand
rec.speaker: Serge Cantat
rec.abstract:
Donnons nous un groupe de Lie compact G et un entier n.
Un n-uplet (g_1, …, g_n) étant donné, on peut changer l’un des g_i en son inverse, ou multiplier l’un des
g_i par g_j (avec j différent de i) : ces opérations élémentaires ne changent pas le sous-groupe de G
engendré par les g_i. Ces opérations engendrent un groupe de difféomorphismes de G^n, et le problème
que nous aborderons est d’étudier la dynamique de ce groupe. Pour n suffisamment grand, nous verrons
qu’il est possible de classer les fermés et les mesures invariants.

rec.title: Characterizing totally geodesic manifolds in negative curvature
rec.speaker: David Fisher
rec.abstract: The talk centers around the question of what invariant sets for Anosov flows and diffeomorphisms can look like. It is known that closed invariant sets can be arbitrarily bad and for example be fractals of arbitrary Hausdorff dimension. An old and interesting question, first raised by Hirsch in 1968 is what closed invariant submanifolds can look like. There are many surprising rigidity results in this direction, some quite old, and recently Rose Eliott Smith and I proved a new one, giving a dynamical characterization of totally geodesic submanifolds in negative curvature. I will explain the theorem and both the classical motivation and some more contemporary motivation. If time permits I will give some hints about the proof and particularly how it uses very old results from Smale and Mane.

L'ambiance y est informelle ; poser des questions naïves est encouragé, et les questions moins naïves sont bienvenues dans la mesure où elles n'entravent pas le bon déroulement de l'exposé.
Chaque jeudi à 18h, en alternance entre Jussieu et Sophie Germain.
The PhD seminar is an opportnuity for PhD students to present results and topics worthy of interest in front of a non-specialist audience. The mood is informal ; asking naive questions is highly encouraged and less naive questions are also welcomed, as long as they don't intefere with the smoothness of the talk.
Every Thursday at 6pm, alternating between Jussieu and Sophie Germain.

imj-96.name: Groupe de travail Preuve de la conjecture de Bogomolov-Fu-Tschinkel par J. Poineau
imj-96.description:
Voici le calendrier du groupe de travail sur la preuve de la conjecture de Bogomolov-Fu-Tschinkel par J. Poineau :
0) 24/01 Introduction générale : Conjecture de Bogomolov-Fu-Tschinkel et morphismes de Lattès, stratégie de la preuve
1) 31/01 Analytification de Berkovich sur un corps valué complet et sur un anneau de Banach
2) 07/02 Théorie du (pluri)potentiel global sur les espaces de Berkovich : métriques FS, CPSH (continue psh), métrique d'équilibre d'un système dynamique polarisé (thèse de Pille-Schneider); sur un corps: mesures de MA de métriques CPSH, estimée de Chern-Levine-Nirenberg (Boucksom-Eriksson?)
3) 07/03 Continuité des mesures canoniques (Haar ou Dirac au point de Gauss) sur P^1 [I, Thm 6.8] et des mesures d'équilibre (via Chern-Levine-Nirenberg)
4) 21/03 Hauteurs, énergie mutuelle des mesures et continuité [II et Favre--Riviera-Letelier]
5) 04/04 Cas des Lattès : minoration centrale (énergie mutuelle d'intervalles en valuation triviale) et globale [II, section 6]
6) 18/04 Minoration globale de l'énergie mutuelle et fin de la preuve [II, sections 7-8]
Les séances auront lieu de 10h à 12h en salle 15.25.502 à Jussieu sauf pour le 24/1 qui aura lieu en salle 15.16.413.

arxiv:2609.30409.title: Volume stability of plank covers
arxiv:2609.30409.summary: We prove a longstanding conjecture of Andr\'as Bezdek on the stability of plank covers of the planar disk $D$. If a sufficiently small disk $\varepsilon D$ is removed, then every finite family of planks covering the resulting annulus can be rearranged to cover the whole disk. For the proof, we establish a stronger dimension-independent stability theorem.

arxiv:2610.04834.title: Quantum codes in the Lee metric
arxiv:2610.04834.summary: We introduce a quantum coding framework for discrete small-shift noise, in which errors on qudits are modeled as low-weight $X$- and $Z$-type Pauli shifts, analogous to small phase-space displacements in continuous-variable systems. This structure is approximately respected by nuclear-spin noise and captured by the Lee metric, motivating a quantum extension of classical Lee-metric coding theory. We develop such a formalism for stabilizer codes over $\mathbb{Z}_q$ for arbitrary $q$, using joint and separate Lee metrics for the $X$- and $Z$-components of errors.
arxiv:2610.04834.authors: Jinkang Guo, Yiqiu Han, Aranya Chakraborty, Shubham P. Jain, Tianhao Liu, Victor V. Albert, Andrew Lucas

arxiv:2610.10545.title: A Proof of the Dittert Conjecture via Boundary Rigidity
arxiv:2610.10545.summary: Let $\mathcal{K}_n$ be the simplex of nonnegative $n \times n$ matrices whose entries sum to $n$. For $A$ in $\mathcal{K}_n$, with row sums $r_1,\ldots,r_n$ and column sums $c_1,\ldots,c_n$, define $\Phi(A)=\prod_{i=1}^n r_i+\prod_{j=1}^n c_j-\mathrm{per}(A)$. Dittert conjectured that $\Phi$ is uniquely maximized by the uniform matrix $U_n=J_n/n$, with maximum $2-n!/n^n$.
arxiv:2610.10545.authors: Xinan Dai, Wenhao Deng, Yingdong Shi, Tailin Wu, Yuchen Yang

arxiv:2610.10553.title: The Conway-Wales lattice and the Rudvalis and Tits groups
arxiv:2610.10553.summary: We construct the Conway-Wales lattice from a self-dual even code $C$ over $\mathbb{Z}_4$ whose binary layers interweave the Hamming codes $\mathcal{H}_7$ and $\mathcal{H}_8$. Explicit signed symmetries lift every automorphism of the binary residue, and the full signed code group is the coordinate-frame stabilizer of the Gaussian lattice. An integral reflection in an embedded scaled self-dual sublattice supplies an additional symmetry, from which the classical frame exchange is recovered.

arxiv:2610.10558.title: Foliations forcing closed orbits
arxiv:2610.10558.summary: We study foliations which force every transverse flow to have a closed orbit. We fully characterize this property among $C^2$ finite depth foliations on atoroidal 3-manifolds. We also show that for many foliations, this property can be broken by a $C^0$-small modification of the foliation.

arxiv:2610.10559.title: Edge-Connectivity versus Lin--Lu--Yau Curvature
arxiv:2610.10559.summary: We systematically explore the relationship between edge-connectivity and Lin--Lu--Yau curvature for graphs. The intuition is that a connected graph with large Lin--Lu--Yau curvature should also have large edge-connectivity, and vice versa under suitable conditions. We prove that the edge-connectivity of a connected graph is bounded lower by the product of its minimum degree, its Lin--Lu--Yau curvature and the constant $\frac{3}{2}$.

arxiv:2610.10577.title: A Faithful Action of the Mapping Class Group $\mathrm{Mod}(S_g)$ on the $(2g-1)$-Sphere
arxiv:2610.10577.summary: We prove that $\mathrm{Mod}(S_g)$ acts faithfully by orientation-preserving homeomorphisms on a $(2g-1)$-sphere when $g \geq 3$ using equivariant blow-up and bi-orderability of the Torelli group.

arxiv:2610.10602.title: Gain of Entrainment in Ribosome Flow Models with Nonlinear Steric Hindrance: Global Rigidity and Dimension-Induced Gai
arxiv:2610.10602.summary: The ribosome flow model (RFM) is a nonlinear compartmental model for unidirectional transport along an mRNA chain. We study a generalized RFM in which the classical linear free-space factor is replaced by a monotone nonlinear steric-hindrance response. After recalling the global equilibrium and periodic entrainment properties needed for the analysis, we derive an exact weighted edge-dissipation identity for the gain of entrainment (GOE).

arxiv:2610.10618.title: The Hellinger Conjecture for Antipodal Boolean Functions
arxiv:2610.10618.summary: The balanced Hellinger conjecture compares the overlap of two output laws induced by a Boolean decision under binary symmetric noise. We prove that a single input coordinate minimizes this overlap among antipodal decisions, whose values reverse when all input signs are reversed, throughout the noise interval. The proof uses a normalized nuclear norm of the cross-class block of the Gram matrix of square-root channel densities.

arxiv:2610.10649.title: Two proofs and a tight Szemer\'edi--Trotter theorem
arxiv:2610.10649.summary: The Szemer\'edi--Trotter theorem, a fundamental theorem in incidence geometry, states that $n$ points and $m$ lines in $\mathbb{R}^2$ form at most $O(m+n+m^{2/3}n^{2/3})$ incidences. Recently, Lewko and independently Miao--Xie extended the Szemer\'edi--Trotter theorem to arbitrary fields with a correction term $O(\frac{mn}{\mathfrak{p}})$ if the field has positive characteristic $\mathfrak{p}$. In this paper, we provide some geometric intuition for the two proofs and compare them.

arxiv:2610.10652.title: Fourier quasicrystals with positive integer masses are sections of Lee-Yang cycles
arxiv:2610.10652.summary: We characterize Fourier quasicrystal measures with positive integer masses as real sections of effective Lee-Yang cycles, with weighted local intersection degrees. The section matrix has positive maximal minors, and the mass at each root is its weighted local intersection degree. For Delone support the reduced support of the cycle can be chosen strict.

arxiv:2610.10665.title: The Erd\H{o}s-Falconer distance problem in the integer lattice
arxiv:2610.10665.summary: In this paper we propose and study what we call the Erd\H{o}s-Falconer distance problem in the integer lattice. One motivation is Magyar's discrete analog of the result of Furstenberg, Katznelson, and Weiss, who showed that all arbitrarily large distances had to appear for a set of positive upper Banach density in $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\geq 2$. Another motivation is the Falconer distance problem, which can be viewed as a refinement of a result of Steinhaus, dropping assumptions from positive Lebesgue measure to merely asking about the dimension of sets.

arxiv:2610.10708.title: Embeddings of Derived Categories of Moduli Spaces into Symmetric Powers
arxiv:2610.10708.summary: We give a criterion for the box product of a Fourier--Mukai kernel to induce a fully faithful functor to the derived category of a symmetric quotient stack. This leads to many new examples of embeddings of derived categories of moduli spaces. We study in more detail the case of the moduli space of stable bundles on a curve.

arxiv:2610.10730.title: Finite group actions on nonpositively curved 3-manifolds
arxiv:2610.10730.summary: We show that every orientation-preserving action of a finite group on a closed nonpositively curved 3-manifold preserves a nonpositively curved metric.

arxiv:2610.10737.title: Obstructions to $k$-colouring $H$-free graphs
arxiv:2610.10737.summary: A graph is $H$-free if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$. In 2020, Chudnovsky, Goedgebeur, Schaudt, and Zhong characterized all graphs $H$ such that there are only finitely many minimal obstructions to $3$-colouring $H$-free graphs. In general, the minimal obstructions to $k$-colouring $H$-free graphs are the $(k+1)$-vertex-critical $H$-free graphs, those are, the $H$-free graphs $G$ with $\chi(G)=k+1$ but $\chi(G-v)=k$ for every vertex in $G$.
arxiv:2610.10737.authors: Iain Beaton, Ben Cameron, Adam van Omme

arxiv:2610.10747.title: Bounds on Legendrian Double Twist Knots
arxiv:2610.10747.summary: We study Legendrian realizations of double twist knots in the standard tight contact 3-sphere. For the family K(4,m), we give upper bounds on the number of oriented and unoriented Legendrian isotopy classes of maximal Thurston--Bennequin representatives. The proof uses bypass techniques in convex surface theory and the classification of tight contact structures.

arxiv:2610.10757.title: Lifting braids over $\mathbb{RP}^2$ and non-orientable Lefschetz fibrations
arxiv:2610.10757.summary: We show that, given a closed connected non-orientable surface $F$ and a simple branched cover $p \colon F \rightarrow \mathbb{RP}^2$ of degree $d \geq 5$, every self-diffeomorphism of $F$ is isotopic to the lift of a self-diffeomorphism of $\mathbb{RP}^2$ with respect to $p$. As an application, we show that every Lefschetz fibration over a connected surface $B$ with $\partial B\neq \emptyset$ and closed non-orientable regular fiber can be expressed as the composition of a simple cover of $B\times \mathbb{RP}^2$ branched over a surface braided over $B$ and projection onto the $B$-factor.
arxiv:2610.10757.authors: Valentina Bais, Porter Morgan, Daniele Zuddas

arxiv:2610.10775.title: The rational homology of quotients of the curve complex
arxiv:2610.10775.summary: Let $\mathop{Mod}_{g,n}$ be the mapping class group of a genus-$g$ surface with $n$ punctures and let $\mathcal{C}_{g,n}$ be its curve complex. For a finite-index subgroup $G < \mathop{Mod}_{g,n}$, Boggi proved that $\widetilde{H}_k(\mathcal{C}_{g,n}/G;\mathbb{Q}) = 0$ for $g+n \gg k$. This plays an important role in the work of Putman-Wieland on the virtual first Betti number of $\mathop{Mod}_{g,n}$.

arxiv:2610.10777.title: K-Moduli Wall Crossing and Automorphic Forms for the Moduli Space of Rational Elliptic Surfaces
arxiv:2610.10777.summary: Using K-moduli spaces for log quasimaps $q_t\colon\left(\mathbb P^1,\frac{1-t}{12}D\right)\to[\mathbb A^2/\mathbb G_m]$ of degree twelve with twelve points and weight $t/12$, we construct a modular interpolation $\{\mathcal M_t\}_{0\le t\le1}$ between the Baily--Borel compactification of the Heckman--Looijenga ball quotient $X_o$ and Miranda's GIT compactification of the moduli space of rational elliptic surfaces. We completely determine the wall-crossing and, for every rational $t\in[0,1]$, identify \[ \mathcal M_t\cong\operatorname{Proj}R\!\left(X_o,\mathcal L+\frac t2\Delta(6)+\frac t3\Delta(9)\right), \] where $\mathcal L$ is the automorphic $\mathbb Q$-line bundle and…

arxiv:2610.10784.title: K-moduli wall crossing for quasimaps to a projective variety
arxiv:2610.10784.summary: We develop a modular wall crossing theory for quasimaps to a projective variety, allowing independent variation of the boundary coefficients and the quasimap weight. Building on the K-stability of quasimaps introduced by Hashizume and the first author, we construct projective moduli spaces in the stable, Calabi--Yau, and log Fano regimes, together with wall crossing morphisms. A central construction is the moduli theory of boundary polarized Calabi--Yau quasimaps, which retains an ample polarization at the numerically trivial locus and allows comparison with suitable perturbations toward the stable and log Fano regions.

arxiv:2610.10800.title: Decomposition Profiles and Weisfeiler-Leman Dimension for Graphs of Bounded Rank Width
arxiv:2610.10800.summary: The Weisfeiler-Leman (WL) algorithm tests graph isomorphism by assigning colours to $d$-tuples of vertices and iteratively refining the colouring according to neighbourhood configurations until it stabilizes. Increasing $d$ allows the test to detect finer structural differences between graphs, but the computational cost grows exponentially with $d$. The central question is which dimension allows us to distinguish nonisomorphic graphs.

arxiv:2610.10804.title: Motion groups, Legendrian links, and non-trivial loops of embeddings
arxiv:2610.10804.summary: We introduce, for an embedded Legendrian link~$L$ in a contact 3-manifold~$(M,\xi)$, the group of its \emph{Legendrian motions}. Analogously with the smooth case, we prove that this Legendrian motion group is isomorphic to the fundamental group of the space of unparametrised Legendrian embeddings. For all Legendrian knots in the standard contact 3-sphere, we characterise Legendrian motions in terms of contact mapping classes of the knot exterior.

arxiv:2610.10821.title: The three- and four-loop equal-mass sunset integrals and local Calabi--Yau fourfolds and fivefolds
arxiv:2610.10821.summary: We determine the equal-mass two-dimensional three- and four-loop sunset Feynman integrals $I^{(3)}_\circleddash$ and $I^{(4)}_\circleddash$ at large Euclidean momentum in terms of the genus-zero Gromov--Witten theory of the local Calabi--Yau fourfold and fivefold $X_L=\operatorname{Tot}(K_{F_L})$, where $F_L\subset(\mathbb P^1)^{L+1}$, $L=3,4$, is a smooth hypersurface of multidegree $(1,\ldots,1)$. At two loops the sunset integral is governed by the prepotential of a local Calabi--Yau threefold. For $L\geq3$ the moduli spaces of unmarked stable maps have positive virtual dimension and there is no prepotential, therefore the Feynman integral is governed instead by the one-point potential…

arxiv:2610.10828.title: Equal-mass sunset integrals and genus-zero local Gromov--Witten theory of Calabi--Yau $n$-folds
arxiv:2610.10828.summary: We prove an exact identity, as convergent logarithmic germs at large Euclidean momentum, between the equal-mass two-dimensional $(n-1)$-loop sunset Feynman integral, with $n\geq4$, and the genus-zero one-point descendant invariants of the local Calabi--Yau $n$-fold $X_n=\operatorname{Tot}(K_{F_n})$, where $F_n\subset(\mathbb P^1)^{n}$ is a smooth $(1,\ldots,1)$ hypersurface. arxiv:2610.10831.title: Tweaking the constant in the Linear Hadwiger Theorem
arxiv:2610.10831.summary: Norin and Steiner recently proved the Linear Hadwiger Conjecture. That is, there is an absolute constant $C$ such that every graph $G$ satisfies $\chi(G)\leqslant C\,\text{had}(G)$, where $\chi(G)$ is the chromatic number and $\text{had}(G)$ is the Hadwiger number of $G$. Their proof gives a non-optimised constant $C$ of order $10^{100}$.

arxiv:2610.10880.title: Effective syzygies of secant varieties
arxiv:2610.10880.summary: We provide effective bounds on adjoint line bundles on $X$ for which the secant variety $\Sigma(X)$ satisfies property $N_{3,p}$. The given bounds only depend on $\operatorname{dim}(X)$ and $p$.

arxiv:2610.10894.title: Splitting fields of complex hyperbolic groups: matrix extraction, Hermitian descent, and spectral fields
arxiv:2610.10894.summary: Let $\Gamma<\mathrm{SU}(n,1)$, $n\ge2$, be Zariski-dense and contain a regular loxodromic element $A$. The splitting-field problem asks how far traces and spectra determine a field of definition for $\Gamma$. We show first that traces together with the spectrum of $A$ always give a linear realization over $K=\mathbb{Q}(\textrm{tr}\Gamma,E(A))$.
arxiv:2610.10894.authors: Angel Cano, Hector Castro, Nikolay Gusevskii

arxiv:2610.10896.title: The Milnor Fiber as a Local Conley Index
arxiv:2610.10896.summary: Let $f:(\C^n,0)\to(\C,0)$ be a holomorphic germ with an isolated critical point at the origin, and let $\varphi_f$ be the negative gradient flow of $\re f$ with respect to a Riemannian metric. We show that the origin is an isolated invariant set of $\varphi_f$ and that its Conley index is the suspension of the Milnor fiber, \[ h(\varphi_f,\{0\})\;\simeq\;\Sigma F_f\;\simeq\;\bigvee_{\mu(f)}S^n , \] so that $\mu(f)=\rank \CH_n(\varphi_f,\{0\};\Z)$: the Milnor number is the rank of the homological Conley index of the flow in degree $n$. The proof uses continuation to a holomorphic morsification of $f$.

arxiv:2610.10930.title: Inter-Categorical Subobject Analysis
arxiv:2610.10930.summary: We introduce a systematic way to use the subobject functor on any category to set up an framework for generalized topological and measure-theoretic notions and inferences. Concretely, we develop two connected calculi: 1. a fourfold calculus derived from notions of smallness and density that generalizes, among other things, topological density and measure-theoretic negligibility, 2. a twofold calculus that generalizes topological and measure-theoretic inference procedures. The resulting theory is distinguished in that it is inter-categorical in character: its definitions can be applied not just to describe smallness and density of subobjects in any category and classify morphisms by how they…

arxiv:2610.10940.title: Quantum geometry at arbitrary genus - I: Anharmonic potentials
arxiv:2610.10940.summary: In quantum mechanics of genus-1 potentials, perturbation theory around the topologically trivial saddle and non-perturbative instanton saddle are constructively related via the P/NP relation. Whether such a relation persists for higher-genus potentials has remained an open problem. In this work, we resolve it using tools from complex algebraic geometry combined with exact WKB.

arxiv:2610.10950.title: Smallest String Attractors and Minimal Coverage Certificates of Thue--Morse Words
arxiv:2610.10950.summary: String attractors provide a compact way of representing the complete factor structure of a word: a set of positions is an attractor if every distinct factor has at least one occurrence crossing one of the selected positions. Although the minimum attractor size is known for several classical families of words, describing \emph{all} optimal attractors is typically much more difficult, since it requires understanding the geometry of all factor occurrences rather than constructing a single optimal solution. We give a complete description for the finite Thue--Morse words.
arxiv:2610.10950.authors: Simone Faro, Francesco Pio Marino, Arianna Pavone

arxiv:2610.10973.title: A $G$-Invariant Erd\H{o}s--Hanani Theorem with Applications to Optical Orthogonal and Constant-Weight Codes
arxiv:2610.10973.summary: Let $k>t\ge 2$ be fixed integers, and let $G$ be a permutation group on a set of $v$ points. A $G$-invariant packing is free if every block has $|G|$ distinct images under $G$. We give two conditions on $G$ under which, as $v\to\infty$, there is a free $G$-invariant $t$-$(v,k,1)$ packing with $(1-o(1))\binom{v}{t}/\binom{k}{t}$ blocks.

arxiv:2610.10993.title: Morse-Smale dynamics in discrete Huygens networks
arxiv:2610.10993.summary: We study discrete networks of $N+1$ identical phase oscillators with positive reciprocal weights and smooth odd periodic interactions, motivated by discrete models of Huygens synchronisation. The interaction laws define an intrinsic potential, and removing the common phase gives a gradient map on the $N$-torus. A weighted graph Laplacian yields explicit step sizes for strict Lyapunov decrease and global invertibility.
arxiv:2610.10993.authors: Jorge Buescu, Emma D'Aniello, Henrique M. Oliveira

arxiv:2610.11013.title: An explicit tame factorization of the four-variable Anick automorphism
arxiv:2610.11013.summary: Let $\delta=xz-yt$. We give an explicit tame factorization of the Anick automorphism $(x+\delta t,y+\delta z,z,t)$ of $F[x,y,z,t]$. After a linear change of coordinates, the factorization consists of sixteen elementary automorphisms, all fixing $z$.

arxiv:2610.11017.title: The Computational Complexity of the Ungar Games on Distributive Lattices
arxiv:2610.11017.summary: The Ungar game, introduced by Defant et al., is a combinatorial game played on a finite lattice, which originates from a geometric transformation introduced by Ungar to resolve Scott's slope problem. When played on a distributive lattice $L$, the Ungar game reduces to repeatedly choosing and removing a non-empty set of maximal elements from a finite poset $P$, where $L$ is represented as the lattice $J(P)$ of the order ideals of $P$ by Birkhoff's representation theorem. Defant et al. raised the open question of whether determining the outcome of the Ungar game on $J(P)$ is PSPACE-complete with respect to $|P|$.

arxiv:2610.11032.title: Frobenius splitting of valuation rings revisited
arxiv:2610.11032.summary: Let $K$ be a function field over an $F$-finite field $k$ of characteristic $p > 0$ and let $\nu$ be a valuation of $K/k$. We show $\nu$ is an Abhyankar valuation of $K/k$ if and only if the corresponding valuation ring is Frobenius split. The proof proceeds by analyzing when ideals of a valuation ring are uniformly $F$-compatible and establishing a general ramification-theoretic characterization of Frobenius split valuation rings of $F$-finite fields.

arxiv:2610.11047.title: Almost all graphs are determined by their generalized spectrum
arxiv:2610.11047.summary: Haemers' conjecture for the generalized spectrum asserts that almost all graphs are determined by their generalized spectrum, that is, for almost all graphs $G$, every graph with the same spectrum as $G$ whose complement has the same spectrum as the complement of $G$ is isomorphic to $G$. We prove this conjecture by showing that the random graph $G(n,1/2)$ is determined by its generalized spectrum with probability tending to one. The proof combines a local theory of the denominators of the rational orthogonal matrices that relate generalized cospectral graphs, Fourier analysis of random symmetric matrices over finite rings, Seidel switching, inverse Littlewood--Offord theory over finite…

arxiv:2610.11101.title: Quantum super Schur--Weyl duality and character formulas for mirabolic Hecke algebras
arxiv:2610.11101.summary: We establish a quantum super Schur--Weyl duality for the mirabolic Hecke algebra \(H_n^{\mathrm{mir}}(q)\) with \(q\) indeterminate and determine the corresponding bimodule decomposition. The centralizer of the mirabolic action is shown as a direct sum of homogeneous quantum Schur superalgebras. We describe the tensor-space annihilator and the resulting faithful quotient.

arxiv:2610.11109.title: A Proof of Mongardi's Conjecture on Finite Symplectic Group Actions on Hyperk\"ahler Manifolds of $K3^{[n]}$ Type
arxiv:2610.11109.summary: Let a finite group act faithfully by symplectic automorphisms on a manifold of $K3^{[n]}$ type for $n\geq2$. We prove Mongardi's conjecture that the strict inequality $\mathrm{rk}(S)+\ell(A_S)<24$ holds for its associated Leech coinvariant lattice $S$. The converse was already proved independently by Huybrechts and Mongardi: any Leech coinvariant lattice $S$ satisfying the strict inequality and of rank at most $20$ is realized by such an action for some $n\geq2$.
arxiv:2610.11109.authors: Jie Fu, Shihao Wang, Zhiwei Zheng

arxiv:2610.11110.title: Braidings of Self-Equivalences and Bordism
arxiv:2610.11110.summary: Let $M$ be a closed, smooth or topological $n$-manifold, with $n \geq 4$. We construct a homotopy highly cartesian square relating the space ${\mathcal E}(M (\ell))$ of homotopy self-equivalences of $M$ (in a suitable range) over the Postnikov $\ell$-sections of its stable normal microbundle, and an $(\infty + n)$-fold loop space representing an associated (normal) bordism theory. This implies the existence of braids of interlocking exact sequences involving the homotopy groups of ${\mathcal E}(M(\ell))$ and certain Lashof bordism groups, leading to a conceptual explanation and broad generalization of earlier work of Hambleton--Kreck for closed, oriented $4$-manifolds.

arxiv:2610.11124.title: Conjugacy problems in higher-dimensional Thompson groups
arxiv:2610.11124.summary: We prove that topological conjugacy of elements of the Brin--Thompson group $nV$ is undecidable for every $n\geq2$. From a Turing machine $T$, the reduction produces two elements of $nV$, which are conjugate by an involution in $nV$ if $T$ halts on the empty tape. If $T$ does not halt on the empty tape, the topological dynamics of the two group elements are distinguished by their visits to minimal subsystems of the set of (germ-)aperiodic points.

arxiv:2610.11151.title: Star-critical Ramsey numbers involving large generalized books
arxiv:2610.11151.summary: For graphs $F$, $G$, and $H$, we write $F \to (G, H)$ if every red/blue edge-coloring of $F$ contains either a red copy of $G$ or a blue copy of $H$. The Ramsey number $R(G, H)$ is the smallest integer $N$ such that $K_N \to (G, H)$. Let $H := K_k + nK_h$ be the generalized book graph, and let $G := K_{p+1}(a_1, a_2, \dots, a_{p+1})$ be a complete $(p+1)$-partite graph satisfying $a_1 = 1$, $a_2 \mid (nh-1)$, and $a_i \le a_{i+1}$.
arxiv:2610.11151.authors: Peiyu Huang, Qizhong Lin, Lin Niu

arxiv:2610.11243.title: Bi-contact plugs and dynamical hyperbolicity
arxiv:2610.11243.summary: We develop a theory of bi-contact plugs in dimension three to construct Anosov flows or, more generally, structurally stable nonsingular flows. For a transversely orientable hyperbolic plug with orientable filling Morse-Smale boundary laminations, we prove that every strongly transverse gluing map can be isotoped through strongly transverse maps to identify a strongly adapted contact form up to sign. The resulting flow is hyperbolic and is Anosov when the quotient is closed.

arxiv:2610.11265.title: The domination number of the $2$-token graph of path graphs
arxiv:2610.11265.summary: We prove that the domination number of the $2$-token graph of the path $P_n$ is $\gamma(F_2(P_n))=d(n)$ for every $n\ge 13$, where $d(n)=\frac1{10}(n^2+5n+c)$ and $c$ is an explicit constant that depends on $n \bmod 5$. This settles a conjecture by Lea\~nos and the authors, who previously proved the upper bound. The lower bound is computer-assisted and follows the method used by Gon\c{c}alves, Pinlou, Rao and Thomass\'e for grid graphs.
arxiv:2610.11265.authors: Emmanuel Acosta Troncoso, Luis Manuel Rivera

arxiv:2610.11271.title: Distinct flattened partitions avoiding a pattern of length four
arxiv:2610.11271.summary: Let $\mathcal{P}_n$ denote the set of distinct permutations of length $n$ that arise from the flattening process applied to the partitions of $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$. In this paper, we consider the problem of avoidance of a single classical pattern of length four by members of $\mathcal{P}_n$. Let $p_n(\tau)$ denote the number of members of $\mathcal{P}_n$ that avoid the pattern $\tau$.
arxiv:2610.11271.authors: Toufik Mansour, Olivia Nabawanda, Mark Shattuck

arxiv:2610.11326.title: Toric flatness I
arxiv:2610.11326.summary: We establish some basic properties of t-flat fine log schemes, i.e., fine log schemes whose underlying schemes are flat over their log structure (in a suitable sense). Notably, we show that the depth of a t-flat fs log scheme is simply determined by its logarithmic stratification. We also show that there is a good theory of log cotangent complexes for t-flat fine log schemes, and use the log cotangent complex to give a homological criterion for t-flatness.

arxiv:2610.11327.title: Bounded cohomology of transformation groups in all degrees
arxiv:2610.11327.summary: Let $M$ be a compact connected oriented smooth manifold, of dimension $n\ge2$. Let $\mathcal T_MG$ be one of the following transformation groups: $Homeo_0(M,\mu)$, $Diff_0(M,\mu)$, $Symp_0(M, \omega)$ (in case $M$ is symplectic) and $Ham(M, \omega )$ (in case $M$ is symplectic). Denote by $\overline{H}_b^d(\mathcal T_M)$ reduced bounded cohomology of $\mathcal T_M$ in degree $d$, and by $\overline{EH}^d(\mathcal T_M)$ reduced exact bounded cohomology of $\mathcal T_M$ in degree $d$.

arxiv:2610.11340.title: Helly Numbers for Connected Reductive Groups and Splitting of Toric Principal Bundles
arxiv:2610.11340.summary: For an almost simple complex algebraic group $G$ of semisimple rank $m$, we prove that a finite family of parabolic subgroups contains a common maximal torus whenever every subfamily of at most $m+2$ members does. We determine the resulting Helly number $(h(G))$ for almost simple groups of types $A$, $B$, $C$, $G_2$, $F_4$, $E_7$, and $E_8$, and obtain bounds differing by one in types $D$ and $E_6$. For general reductive groups of positive semisimple rank, the Helly number is the maximum of those of the almost simple factors.

arxiv:2610.11390.title: Weak and genuine A_n-formality for number fields
arxiv:2610.11390.summary: We introduce weak $A_n$-formality for Galois cochain algebras and, for profinite groups whose mod-$p$ cohomology is concentrated in degrees at most two, characterise weak and genuine $A_n$-formality through finite embedding problems and the projective system they form. We then study $A_n$-formality for number fields. Let $K$ be a number field and let $p$ be an odd prime with $\mu_p\not\subset K$.

arxiv:2610.11395.title: Spreads of degrees in maximal planar graphs -- an exposition
arxiv:2610.11395.summary: For a graph $G$ and a set $B\subseteq V(G)$, the spread $\mathrm{sp}(B)$ of $B$ is the difference between the largest and the smallest degree in $G$ of a vertex of $B$, and for an integer $k\geq 0$ the parameter $\mathrm{sp}(G,k)$ is the largest cardinality of a set $B$ with $\mathrm{sp}(B)\leq k$. Caro, Lauri and Zarb asked for the minimum of $\mathrm{sp}(G,k)$ over the maximal planar graphs of order $n$; we write $\mathrm{MP}(n,\delta ,k)$ for this minimum over the maximal planar graphs of order $n$ and minimum degree $\delta \in \{3,4,5\}$. This manuscript is intended as an exposition of the subject of spread in the degree sequence of a graph $G$, with emphasis on maximal planar graphs.

arxiv:2610.11409.title: A linear upper bound for Berge saturation numbers
arxiv:2610.11409.summary: For a graph $F$ with at least one edge, a $k$-uniform hypergraph is Berge-$F$-saturated if it contains no Berge-$F$, but adding any missing hyperedge creates a Berge-$F$. The saturation number $\text{sat}_k(n,\text{Berge-}F)$ is the minimum number of edges in such a hypergraph on $n$ vertices. English, Gordon, Graber, Methuku and Sullivan conjectured a linear upper bound for every fixed finite family of forbidden graphs.

arxiv:2610.11426.title: The chromatic number of the associahedron: simple and logarithmic
arxiv:2610.11426.summary: Addario-Berry, Reed, Scott, and Wood (JoCG 2026) proved that the $n$-dimensional associahedron has chromatic number at most $22500\cdot\log_3 n+O(1)$. We present a much simpler proof that the chromatic number of the $n-1$-dimensional associahedron is at most $6 \log_2 n + 18$. Since this paper's appearance as a preliminary abstract in the Japan Conference on Discrete and Computational Geometry, Graphs, and Games held from September 7-10, 2026, the bound has been improved to $O(\log \log n)$ by Oum and Wood (arXiv September 30, 2026).
arxiv:2610.11426.authors: Benjamin Aram Berendsohn, Jean Cardinal, John Iacono, L\'aszl\'o Kozma

arxiv:2610.11427.title: Categorified Cluster Structures on Coulomb Branches of Certain Star-Shaped Quivers
arxiv:2610.11427.summary: We construct quantum cluster structures on a family of quantized $K$-theoretic Coulomb branches and prove that the associated loop-graded Koszul-perverse hearts give monoidal categorifications of these algebras. For each $r\geq1$, the gauge group is the image of $GL_2\times(\mathbb{C}^*)^r$ in $GL((\mathbb{C}^2)^r)$, where $(g,z_1,\ldots,z_r)$ acts on the $a$th summand by $gz_a$. Each initial seed has $r+2$ mutable and $r$ invertible frozen variables.

arxiv:2610.11441.title: Spanning Even Linear Forests with Isolated Edges Share the Anti-Ramsey Numbers of Perfect Matchings
arxiv:2610.11441.summary: The anti-Ramsey number $AR(n,F)$ is the maximum number of colors in an edge-coloring of the complete graph $K_n$ containing no rainbow copy of $F$. I prove that every spanning linear forest on an even number $n\ge6$ of vertices whose components have even orders and which has an isolated edge has the same anti-Ramsey number as a perfect matching on $n$ vertices. The orders of the longer path components may be different.

arxiv:2610.11446.title: On the local average order of dominating sets
arxiv:2610.11446.summary: The (global) average order of dominating sets of a graph is the average number of vertices of its dominating sets. Analogously, the local average order of dominating sets is the average number of vertices of its dominating sets containing a fixed vertex. In this paper, we show that the local average order of dominating sets of a graph with $n$ vertices is at least $\frac{n+1}{2}$, with equality if and only if the degree of the fixed vertex is $n-1$.
arxiv:2610.11446.authors: Tingyun Chen, Weihua He, Hong-Jian Lai, Jianping Li

arxiv:2610.11452.title: A proof of the Berkovich-Dhar conjecture modulo five
arxiv:2610.11452.summary: We prove the sign-pattern and limiting-transition assertions of the Berkovich--Dhar conjecture modulo five, covering both the square and the cube of the finite Borwein product. In each power, the coefficients in residue class zero are strictly positive, while the sequences in residue classes three and four have exactly one positive-to-negative sign change after zero terms are omitted. We determine all four transition constants, correct the preliminary numerical estimates in the conjecture, and give their linear corrections with explicit bounded errors.

arxiv:2610.11497.title: Universal Semisimple Reconstruction and Obstruction Theory
arxiv:2610.11497.summary: We develop a semisimple obstruction theory for finite-length abelian categories. To each object \(X\) we associate a canonical obstruction subobject \(\mathcal O(X)\), consisting of the part invisible to all morphisms into semisimple objects. The quotient \(X/\mathcal O(X)\) is semisimple and universal among such morphisms, yielding a canonical semisimplification reflector and characterizing semisimplicity by the vanishing of obstruction.

arxiv:2610.11515.title: Stochastic Gradient Descent for Traffic and Pedestrian Models via Neural Networks and Parameter Identification
arxiv:2610.11515.summary: We study the calibration of interaction-driven ordinary differential equation (ODE) models for traffic and pedestrian dynamics by means of optimal control and stochastic gradient descent. The interaction forces are either prescribed by classical physics-inspired laws, whose parameters are identified from trajectory data, or represented by feed-forward neural networks whose weights act as control variables. For the neural-network-driven particle system we prove well-posedness of the state equation, Lipschitz-continuous dependence of the trajectories on the initial data and on the network parameters, existence of an optimal parameter set, and a first-order optimality system with an explicit…

arxiv:2610.11517.title: An asymptotic bound for the Bermond--Thomassen Conjecture
arxiv:2610.11517.summary: The Bermond--Thomassen Conjecture asserts that every digraph with minimum out-degree at least $2k-1$ contains $k$ disjoint directed cycles; it remains open in general. We asymptotically resolve it: there exist an absolute constant $K$ and a function $g(k)=o(k)$, independent of $n$, such that every $n$-vertex finite simple loopless digraph with minimum out-degree at least $2k+g(k)$ contains $k$ disjoint directed cycles for all integers $k\ge K$ and $n\ge1$. In fact we obtain the explicit error term $g(k)=O(k^{3/4}\sqrt{\log k})$.
arxiv:2610.11517.authors: J{\o}rgen Bang-Jensen, Guanghui Wang, Yun Wang

arxiv:2610.11545.title: Continuity of the Julia sets in non-archimedean and hybrid settings
arxiv:2610.11545.summary: Let $k$ be a complete, non-archimedean. We study the dynamics of families of one-variable rational functions parametrized by Berkovich spaces over $k$ and over $\mathbb{C}$ equipped with the hybrid norm. In both settings, we show an analogue of Man\'e--Sad--Sullivan's theorem about the continuity of the Julia set (in the Hausdorff topology).

arxiv:2610.11554.title: Product approximations for uniform spanning trees and determinantal processes
arxiv:2610.11554.summary: We prove that for every finite connected simple graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with minimum degree $k\geq 2$, there is a coupling of its uniform spanning tree and its random $1$-out subgraph under which the expected number of differing edges is $O(n\log (k)/\sqrt{k})$. More generally, we establish analogous couplings between a wide class of determinantal processes and their corresponding $1$-out processes, including Kalai's determinantal hypertrees, with expected symmetric difference negligible compared to the size of the determinantal set. While the graphical case admits a surprisingly short and elegant proof, the more general result requires establishing an asymptotic equipartition property…

arxiv:2610.11565.title: Injectivity of specialization maps in critical cohomology
arxiv:2610.11565.summary: Specialization maps are natural maps from equivariant vanishing cycle cohomology to the equivariant cohomology of the ambient space. We study their injectivity problem for moduli stacks of representations of quivers with potentials, including those associated with generalized conifolds and finite subgroups of $SO(3,\mathbb{C})$.

arxiv:2610.11574.title: Cycle structures and parities of linearized permutation polynomials
arxiv:2610.11574.summary: Linearized permutation polynomials over finite fields have important applications in coding theory, cryptography, and combinatorics. In this paper, we give an explicit description of the cycle structure of a general linearized permutation polynomial in terms of the Jordan blocks of its Dickson matrix, thereby providing a Dickson-matrix formulation of a question raised by Mullen and Vaughan in 1988. Building on the cycle structure, we establish a matrix-theoretic framework to characterize their parity.
arxiv:2610.11574.authors: Huajun Bian, Shaoshi Chen, Dabin Zheng

arxiv:2610.11576.title: A Note on n-Representations of Simplicial Groups
arxiv:2610.11576.summary: For $n\ge1$, we study representations of a simplicial group $G$ in the full $\infty$-subcategory of simplicial vector spaces whose normalized homology is concentrated in degrees $0,\ldots,n-1$, retaining its full mapping spaces. The resulting functor category depends only on the $n$-truncated homotopy type of $\mathbf{B}G$ and admits projectively bifibrant strict diagram and simplicial group-algebra module models. If restriction along a specified map $f:G\to H$ is an equivalence, then $\pi_0(f)$ is a group isomorphism; the proof uses ordinary extension and restriction of scalars.

arxiv:2610.11594.title: Kuranishi spaces in a category of fibrant objects and their homotopy fiber products
arxiv:2610.11594.summary: We study several fundamental properties of the category $\mathbf{Kur}$ introduced in \cite{Kim1}. By defining fibrations and weak equivalences, we show that morphisms with manifold targets admit homotopy fiber products; this is then applied to obtain a notion of generalized intersections of two submanifolds. A definition of the Weinstein category in the context of Kuranishi spaces is also presented.

arxiv:2610.11614.title: From an entropic inequality for sums in abelian groups to the theorems of Ruzsa and Pl\"unnecke
arxiv:2610.11614.summary: We give a direct information-theoretic proof of the Pl\"unnecke--Ruzsa inequalities for finite subsets of abelian groups. The argument rests on an elementary coupling inequality proved by maximizing joint entropy, without tensor powers or asymptotic constructions. It also yields Ruzsa's sumset triangle inequality and an extension to non-abelian groups.
arxiv:2610.11614.authors: Chandra Nair, Aref Namayandeh, Zhaobang Zhu

arxiv:2610.11639.title: Variational Principles for $r$-Neutralized Pfister-Sullivan Entropy
arxiv:2610.11639.summary: In this paper, we study $r$-neutralized Pfister--Sullivan entropy, defined by measuring the complexity of orbit segments whose empirical measures lie near a prescribed invariant measure. We mainly obtain the following three results: (i) We disprove a variational conjecture posed by C.~Dong and Q.~Qiao [On $r$-neutralized entropy: entropy formula and existence of measures attaining the supremum, Comm. Math.
arxiv:2610.11639.authors: Ercai Chen, Yunxiang Xie, Xiaoyao Zhou

arxiv:2610.11642.title: A counterexample to the Erd\H{o}s--S\'os bipartite-link conjecture
arxiv:2610.11642.summary: Erd\H{o}s and S\'os conjectured that every $n$-vertex $3$-uniform hypergraph whose link graphs are all bipartite has at most $(1/4+o(1))\binom n3$ edges. We disprove this conjecture by constructing counterexamples with edge density at least $0.250000356>1/4$ for all sufficiently large $n$.

arxiv:2610.11652.title: Triangular prism equations for near-group categories: algebraic solutions and a unitary conjecture
arxiv:2610.11652.summary: We derive the triangular prism equations (TPE) for near-group fusion rules of type $G+|G|$, where $G$ is a finite abelian group. We prove that spherical categorification with trivial Frobenius--Schur indicator over any field in which $|G|$ is invertible is equivalent to the solvability of the TPE system. For every cyclic group, we construct an explicit solution to the TPE system using hyperbolic gamma functions, yielding both a spherical category with negative simple-object dimensions and, after Galois conjugation, a pseudo-unitary category with positive dimensions.
arxiv:2610.11652.authors: Huixuan He, Zhengwei Liu, Fan Lu, Sebastien Palcoux, Yunxiang Ren

arxiv:2610.11671.title: A complete classification of the rational realization of gap-two products of Eilenberg--MacLane spaces as classifying spaces
arxiv:2610.11671.summary: In this paper, we study the rational realization of the gap-two product $K(\Q,n)\times K(\Q,n+2)$ as the classifying space $\B(X)$ for a simply-connected $\pi$-finite space $X$ with rational homology of finite type. We prove that $K(\Q,n)\times K(\Q,n+2)$ can be realized as $\B(X)$ up to rational homotopy equivalence if and only if $n=3,4$ or $4m+2$ for $m\geq 1$. Moreover, we determine all their minimal Sullivan models up to isomorphism.
arxiv:2610.11671.authors: Yang Bai, Xiugui Liu, Jiaxi Zha

arxiv:2610.11679.title: Persistence of bounded trajectories in positively transverse reaction networks
arxiv:2610.11679.summary: We introduce positively transverse reaction networks and show that, with mass-action kinetics, no bounded trajectory with positive initial condition has a boundary omega-limit point. These networks are characterized by a geometric property of a collection of polytopes defined by a subset of complexes of the network.

arxiv:2610.11708.title: Equivariant noncommutative crepant resolutions and $G$-maximal modifying modules
arxiv:2610.11708.summary: Let $S$ be a Cohen-Macaulay normal domain containing a field $k$ with an action of a finite group $G$ with $|G|$ invertible in $k$. We prove that $G$-equivariant noncommutative crepant resolutions of $S$ induce noncommutative crepant resolutions of $S^G$ if the $G$-action is small. We also discuss similar results for equivariant maximal modification algebras.

arxiv:2610.11718.title: A Fast and High-Accuracy Finite-Time Sliding-Mode Algorithm for Computing Local Stackelberg Equilibria in Nonlinear Bilevel Games
arxiv:2610.11718.summary: Computing local Stackelberg equilibria in nonlinear sequential games is challenging because gradient-based best-response methods may diverge, cycle, or converge to stationary points that do not satisfy the required equilibrium conditions. These failures can result from curvature asymmetry, unstable response mappings, and lack of invariance with respect to the follower's best-response manifold. This paper introduces the Stackelberg Sliding-Mode Algorithm (SSMA), a control-theoretic framework that recasts Stackelberg equilibrium computation as a manifold-stabilization problem.
arxiv:2610.11718.authors: Abdelhafid Zenati, Dave D Muir, Kamal Youcef-Toumi

arxiv:2610.11728.title: Noncrossing combinatorics of quasi-Coxeter elements
arxiv:2610.11728.summary: We study the combinatorics of the intervals below quasi-Coxeter elements in the absolute order of finite Coxeter groups. In particular, we prove that these intervals are EL-shellable, except possibly for quasi-Coxeter elements of types $E_7$ and $E_8$, and we compute their zeta polynomials. We also show that a total order of the reflections yields an EL-labeling if it does so on all rank-two subintervals, which proves a conjecture of Williams for Coxeter elements.
arxiv:2610.11728.authors: Eugenio Cainelli, Giovanni Paolini, Riccardo Zaccaria

arxiv:2610.11757.title: Tur\'an densities of hypergraph augmentations
arxiv:2610.11757.summary: For a $t$-graph $F$ and an integer $r\ge t$, the \emph{$r$-augmentation} $F(r)$ is the $r$-graph obtained by adding the same set of $r-t$ new vertices to every edge of $F$. We investigate the behaviour of the \emph{Tur\'an density $\pi(F(r))$}, which is the asymptotically maximum edge density of a large $F(r)$-free $r$-graph, as a function of $r$. Let $H_k^r$ be the $r$-augmentation of the complete $(k-1)$-graph on $k$ vertices; equivalently, $H_k^r$ is the (unique up to isomorphism) $r$-graph with $r+1$ vertices and $k$ edges.
arxiv:2610.11757.authors: Oleg Pikhurko, Jiabao Yang, Xiutao Zhu

arxiv:2610.11785.title: Facets of nondegeneracy: central type factor groups, Heisenberg representations and Hadamard matrices
arxiv:2610.11785.summary: Given a pair of complementary subgroups $P$ and $N$ of a finite group $G$, we first discuss how the same type of functions $\mathbb E\colon P\times N\to \mathbb T$, which we call bi-$1$-cocycles, appear naturally in the study of projective representations of $G$ of Heisenberg type and second cohomology of $G$ and of its dual quantum group $\widehat G$. We show then that such representations are irreducible and the corresponding ordinary and dual $2$-cocycles are nondegenerate if and only if the matrix $(\mathbb E(p,n))_{p,n}$ is invertible, if and only if it is Hadamard. We illustrate the result with examples arising from symplectic nilpotent Lie algebras over finite fields with two…
arxiv:2610.11785.authors: Pierre Bieliavsky, Victor Gayral, Sergey Neshveyev, lars Tuset

arxiv:2610.11793.title: Local Connectivity of the Filled Julia Set Bundle over the Mandelbrot Set
arxiv:2610.11793.summary: For the quadratic family $f_c(z)=z^2+c$, we study the non-escaping locus $\KM=\{(c,z):c\in\M,\ z\in K_c\}$, the model space for cubic capture straightening in the framework of Inou and Kiwi. Here $\M$ is the Mandelbrot set, $K_c$ is the filled Julia set of $f_c$, and $J_c=\partial K_c$. We prove that $\partial\KM$ has full Hausdorff dimension $4$.

arxiv:2610.11802.title: Loyalty of the affine line in motivic homotopy theory
arxiv:2610.11802.summary: We show that integers act invertibly on a derived scheme $S$ if and only if they act invertibly on the reduced motivic suspension spectrum of the affine line in $\mathrm{MS}_S$. As a consequence, over regular locally noetherian schemes and derived schemes on which some nonzero integer acts as zero, the motivic sphere spectrum is $\mathbf{A}^1$-invariant after inverting primes that are not invertible in the base scheme. In particular, over regular locally noetherian $\mathbf{Q}$-schemes, the motivic sphere spectrum is $\mathbf{A}^1$-invariant.

arxiv:2610.11817.title: Postcritically finite endomorphisms I: Kobayashi hyperbolicity and tautness
arxiv:2610.11817.summary: Let $f:\mathbb{P}^N\to\mathbb{P}^N$ be a postcritically finite endomorphism of degree at least two. Combining Yamanoi's hyperbolicity results with the dynamical property of $f$, we prove that the complement of its postcritical divisor is taut unless $f$ is a monomial power map or admits a nontrivial equivariant rational fibration with a polarized divisorially postcritically finite base map. We establish analogous alternatives for polarized PCF endomorphisms of rationally connected projective manifolds and, for Kobayashi hyperbolicity, on normal rationally connected projective varieties.

arxiv:2610.11829.title: A rank bound for bases and circuits in binary matroids
arxiv:2610.11829.summary: Let \(b(M)\), \(d(M)\), and \(r(M)\) denote the number of bases, the number of circuits, and the rank of a matroid \(M\), respectively. We prove that every nonempty simple binary matroid with no coloops satisfies \[ 2b(M)\ge(r(M)+1)d(M), \] with equality if and only if \(M\) is isomorphic to the Fano matroid. This confirms a conjecture recorded by Oxley in 1983.

arxiv:2610.11840.title: Partition regular linear equations over Sidon sets
arxiv:2610.11840.summary: In this article, we show that the Sidon subsets of $[N]^d$ are Fourier uniform, and we prove a dense model lemma for Sidon sets. Using these results and a higher-dimensional version of Rado's theorem, we prove that given any partition regular linear equation in $s \geq 5$ variables with nonzero coefficients, and any finite partition of a sufficiently dense Sidon subset $S$ of $[N]^d$, the number of monochromatic solutions to this equation is $\gg |S|^s N^{-d}$ for all large $N$. As a corollary of the Fourier uniformity result, we show that dense Sidon subsets of $[N]^d$ are equidistributed in certain arithmetic and Bohr structures.

arxiv:2610.11847.title: Arithmetic Progressions in Midpoint Colourings
arxiv:2610.11847.summary: We introduce an asymmetric variant of a classic problem by Roth about colourings of integers and midpoints. The new problem cannot be solved with the standard approach by Erd\"os-S\'ark\"ozy-S\'os which uses symmetry. We describe a Fourier Analytic approach which gives asymptotically tight bounds.

arxiv:2610.11849.title: A note on realizing triples of slice, concordance and Seifert genera
arxiv:2610.11849.summary: We show that every triple of integers $(a,b,c)$ satisfying $1\leq a\leq b\leq c$ is realized as the smooth slice genus, smooth concordance genus, and Seifert genus of a knot, respectively. This proves a conjecture of Kearney.

arxiv:2610.11864.title: Largeness of the wild locus
arxiv:2610.11864.summary: We show that the wild locus of an \'etale morphism of smooth adic spaces over an affinoid field is either empty or contains a divisorial point. As a consequence, we establish the equivalence of curve tameness and valuation tameness without using resolution of singularities. Moreover, given a finite \'etale map of regular schemes $f \colon Y \to X$ that is curve tame over a base $S$, we construct a compactification $\bar{f} \colon \overline{Y} \to \overline{X}$ over $S$ that is numerically tame.

arxiv:2610.11866.title: Understanding Latent-Dimension Scaling in Dynamical-System Learning through Spectral Reliability
arxiv:2610.11866.summary: In deep learning, approximation theory motivates increasing representation size. We ask whether this benefit extends to dynamics learning through autoregressive prediction. We analyze the learned time evolution through the eigenstructure of Koopman operators, using relative residuals to detect spurious eigenpairs arising even as one-step error falls.
arxiv:2610.11866.authors: Itsushi Sakata, Yuta Miyauchi, Yoshinobu Kawahara

arxiv:2610.11887.title: Breaking linearity in the sum-rank metric: MSRD codes from switched $\sigma$-rational normal curves
arxiv:2610.11887.summary: We construct a family of scalar-closed, non-additive maximum sum-rank distance codes (MSRD) by switching norm components of a $\sigma$-rational normal curve and lifting the resulting point set through a linearized Reed--Solomon syndrome map. We characterize the admissible switches by a multiplicative stability condition on the norm classes. In particular, for $1 \leq n_i \leq m$, $N=n_1+\ldots+n_{\ell}$ and $2\leq\delta\leq N-1$, every partition of $\mathbb{F}_q^*$ satisfying a specific condition, referred to as Condition $(\diamond)$, yields a code in $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}^{N}$ of size $q^{m(N-\delta+1)}$ and minimum sum-rank distance $\delta$; the code is non-additive whenever a curve…
