On the odd cycle $C_{2r+1}$, we determine the largest repair distance from arbitrary color assignments with a prescribed color-count vector (profile) $\mathbf m$ to proper colorings with any realizable target profile $\mathbf p$: it equals $2r+1-\sum_X\min\{p_X,\lceil m_X/2\rceil\}$.
arxiv:2610.13580.authors: Jiang Jiang, Yuhan Jiang, Yiyang Li, Lujia Wang, Aitao Zhang

arxiv:2610.13581.title: On the Cohomology Classes of Certain Eisenstein-Kronecker Forms
arxiv:2610.13581.summary: We study the de Rham cohomology and Deligne splitting for a class of Eisenstein-Kronecker forms by introducing a modular weight grading. As an application, we compute a particular cohomology class that gives rise to generating series of Gromov-Witten invariants of elliptic curves.

arxiv:2610.13645.title: Finding the Birman-Series set
arxiv:2610.13645.summary: By a celebrated result of Birman and Series, the set of simple complete geodesics form a nowhere dense subset of a hyperbolic surface. We show that a segment of finite length is in a (small) neighborhood of this set if it can be "extended simply" in both directions for long enough. We deduce that, for large enough genus $g$, there exist surfaces with a Birman-Series set that is roughly $\frac{1}{g^{\sfrac{2}{3}}}$-dense.

arxiv:2610.13658.title: Regularization of a Divergent Arithmetic Product via the Asymptotic Monoid: The Case of $(-1)^{\omega(n)}$
arxiv:2610.13658.summary: We apply the generalized monoid of words and logarithmic-prefix functionals of \cite{C1} to the regularization of the divergent product \[ P_{\omega}=\prod_{n=1}^{\infty} n^{(-1)^{\omega(n)}}, \] where \(\omega(n)\) is the number of distinct prime divisors of \(n\). The associated Dirichlet series \(D_{\omega}(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}(-1)^{\omega(n)}n^{-s}\) has a natural boundary at \(\Re(s)=0\), as established by Meretov (1987) and recovered here as a special case of the Estermann--Dahlquist theory of Euler products, which makes zeta regularization impossible: the derivative \(D_{\omega}'(0)\) does not exist. This product therefore lies completely beyond the reach of classical regularization…
arxiv:2610.13658.authors: A. Alvarez Cruz, E. A. Alvarez Gutierrez

arxiv:2610.13667.title: A discrete analogue of $\mathscr{N}=2$ super Weil-Petersson volumes
arxiv:2610.13667.summary: We introduce a discrete spectral curve from $\mathscr{N}=2$ double-scaled SYK whose topological recursion defines quasi-polynomial volumes in integer boundary lengths. The curve has two edge theories: a local $\mathscr{N}=2$ theory at the lower edge and a bosonic theory at the upper edge. Focusing on the local $\mathscr{N}=2$ theory, we compute its finite-$q$ volumes and independently check the first few using the string equation.

arxiv:2610.13677.title: Spread-out Furstenberg sets I: the sticky case
arxiv:2610.13677.summary: We introduce spread-out measures, a notion of local non-concentration near pencils for measures on Grassmannians. We establish an optimal $\delta$-discretized dual Furstenberg estimate for ``sticky spread-out'' shadings. A simple-to-state corollary is the following.

arxiv:2610.13682.title: Spread-out Furstenberg sets II: general configurations and fractal restricted projections
arxiv:2610.13682.summary: We prove optimal dual Furstenberg estimates for Frostman and Katz--Tao configurations for which the shadings are not locally concentrated near pencils. The starting point is the sticky estimate of Orponen and Shmerkin in a companion paper. We deduce restricted projection theorems in the plane and in higher dimensions.
arxiv:2610.13682.authors: Alex Cohen, Pablo Shmerkin, Hong Wang, Dmitrii Zakharov

arxiv:2610.13709.title: Dynamical Lie Algebras for Fixed-Gate Quantum Ans\"atze
arxiv:2610.13709.summary: Parameterized Quantum Circuits have emerged as a central framework for variational quantum algorithms in the NISQ regime, with major applications in quantum simulation, combinatorial optimization, and, more recently, quantum machine learning (QML). By developing a new approach for computing dynamical Lie algebras associated with quantum circuits combining parametrized gates and non-parametrized entangling gates, we aim to extend the applicability of recent algebraic results to architectures that are actually used in quantum machine learning.
arxiv:2610.13709.authors: Orlane Zang, Daniel Juteau, Tony Quertier, Gr\'egoire Barru\'e

arxiv:2610.13723.title: List chromatic number of $G(n,r,s)$ graphs
arxiv:2610.13723.summary: We study the list chromatic number of generalized Johnson graphs. Recall that the vertices of such graphs are all possible $r$-element subsets of $[n] = \{1, \dotsc, n\}$ and an edge is drawn between two vertices if and only if corresponding sets have exactly $s$ common elements. We prove that for any fixed $s \geq 1$ and $r \geq 2s + 2$ we have $\chi_L(G(n,r,s)) = \Theta(n^{s+1}\ln n)$.

arxiv:2610.13736.title: Adjoint-Based Stochastic Analysis for Fatigue of Aeroelastic and Frictional Systems
arxiv:2610.13736.summary: As engineering systems are optimized to reduce weight and improve performance, vibration behavior, including nonlinear effects, is becoming increasingly important to analyze. While methods such as harmonic balance are popular for analyzing periodic nonlinear vibration behavior, these analyses often only consider deterministic loading. However, real applications experience additional noise in the excitation, and alternative approaches are frequently limited to smaller models.

arxiv:2610.13747.title: Travel time tomography for elliptically anisotropic elastic planar media
arxiv:2610.13747.summary: We study the gauge of the travel time tomography problem for elliptically anisotropic planar media. Under this assumption the respective slowness surfaces consist of an inner ellipse and an outer circle. Hence, the singularities of seismic waves propagate on geodesics given by two Riemannian metrics of which the one related to shear waves is conformally Euclidean.
arxiv:2610.13747.authors: Joonas Ilmavirta, Teemu Saksala, Hj{\o}rdis Schl\"uter

arxiv:2610.13798.title: On the failure of additivity of inversion numbers for dijoins
arxiv:2610.13798.summary: Let $D$ be an oriented graph. For $X \subseteq V(D)$, the inversion of $X$ in $D$ is the oriented graph that is obtained via changing the direction of all edges which have both endpoints in $X$. The inversion number of $D$, $\operatorname{inv}(D)$, is the minimum number of inversions necessary in order to remove all cycles from $D$.

arxiv:2610.13801.title: Linearity of Graph Manifold Groups
arxiv:2610.13801.summary: We complete the proof that every compact 3-manifold group is linear. Specifically, we construct a faithful representation in GL5(Q[u]) for a finite-index subgroup of every closed non-geometric graph-manifold group.

arxiv:2610.13803.title: The (right) homotopy between two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms
arxiv:2610.13803.summary: Let $f$, $g\colon A\to B$ be two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms between two A$_{\infty}$-algebras (linear over a commutative ring $\mathbb{K}$). In this paper, we compare different notions of (right) homotopy between $f$ and $g$. We note that the A$_{\infty}$-algebra $B\otimes R$, where $R:=\mathbb{K}[t,dt]$, is a model for the interval $[0,1]\times B$ in the sense of Fukaya-Oh-Ohta-Ono, and we give a short alternative proof, in the unfiltered case, of the existence of comparison morphisms between such models.

arxiv:2610.13817.title: Two-orbit right-angled Polytopes and Hypertopes
arxiv:2610.13817.summary: Abstract polytopes and hypertopes are thin and residually-connected incidence geometries or, equivalently, chamber systems. Their degree of regularity is understood by looking at the action of their automorphism group on the set of their chambers. When this action has only one orbit, they are called regular.

arxiv:2610.13820.title: Counting cographs in locally dense graphs
arxiv:2610.13820.summary: An $n$-vertex graph $G$ is $(\rho, d)$-dense if for all $U \subseteq V(G)$ of size at least $\rho n$, the induced subgraph $G[U]$ contains at least $\frac{d}{2}|U|^2$ edges. In 2010, partly motivated by the theory of quasirandomness, Kohayakawa, Nagle, R\"{o}dl, and Schacht conjectured that, for any fixed graph $F$, the number of homomorphic copies of $F$ in a given $n$-vertex $(o(1),d)$-dense graph is at least $(1-o(1))d^{e(F)}n^{v(F)}$. Despite considerable effort, only a few graphs are known to satisfy the conjecture.

arxiv:2610.13827.title: Monodromy of Tate-Linear varieties
arxiv:2610.13827.summary: We answer a question of Chai about the rigidity of Tate-linear subvarieties of $\mathcal{A}_g$ over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$: we show that that a smooth subvariety of a central leaf of $\mathcal{A}_g$ which is Tate-linear at one point is Tate-linear at every point. This is achieved by a careful analysis of the $p$-adic monodromy groups of Tate-linear varieties, building on recent work of D'Addezio and van Hoften.

arxiv:2610.13831.title: Biholomorphic rigidity and symmetry breaking for domains with Bergman metric of constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature
arxiv:2610.13831.summary: Based on earlier work by Wiegerinck and Huang-Li, Hayashida-Kamimoto constructed unbounded non-smooth Reinhardt domains in \({\mathbb C}^n\), \(n\geq 3\), whose Bergman spaces are finite-dimensional and whose Bergman metrics have constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature \(2\). In this note, we prove a Sandwich Principle for the Hayashida-Kamimoto domains that allows us to construct, inside every prescribed sandwich, uncountably many pairwise biholomorphically inequivalent smooth non-Reinhardt domains whose Bergman metrics also have constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature \(2\). We also classify biholomorphisms between domains sandwiched by the domains of…
arxiv:2610.13831.authors: Gordon Heier, Ravi Mudaliar, Haotian Zuo

arxiv:2610.13850.title: Weighted, GIT and N\'eron--Tate heights on genus-two moduli and Jacobians
arxiv:2610.13850.summary: We compare three heights attached to a curve of genus two: the weighted height of its Igusa--Clebsch invariants, the GIT height of a binary sextic defining it, and the N\'eron--Tate height on its Jacobian. For a morphism from an abelian variety to a weighted projective space we define a weighted N\'eron--Tate height and show that the weighted height differs from it by a linear form and a bounded function; the linear form vanishes when inversion is induced by an automorphism of the weighted projective space. For binary sextics we prove the explicit inequality $h_{\inv}\le h_{\text{GIT}} + \frac{1}{2} \log 302$, with nonnegative local differences at the finite places that vanish at places of…

arxiv:2610.13852.title: Clique and chromatic numbers of graph powers: spectral bounds and anticodes
arxiv:2610.13852.summary: Using spectral and polynomial methods, we show several sharp spectral bounds for the clique and chromatic numbers of graph powers that only use spectral information from the original graph. In particular, we strengthen earlier spectral-radius estimates to obtain an asymptotically sharp colouring bound for general graph powers, and prove a sharp bound for powers of line graphs with a complete characterisation of equality. We also develop polynomial methods yielding upper and lower bounds for clique numbers of graph powers.
arxiv:2610.13852.authors: Aida Abiad, Gabriel Coutinho, Hitesh Kumar, Emanuel Juliano, Michael Tait

arxiv:2610.13863.title: Degree similar and net-degree similar signed graphs
arxiv:2610.13863.summary: Two graphs are degree similar if their adjacency matrices and their degree matrices are simultaneously similar, a notion recently introduced by Godsil and Sun. We extend it to signed graphs in two ways, degree similarity and net-degree similarity, according to whether the degree or the net-degree matrix is used. We prove that signed trees are determined by their degree similarity class, but not by their net-degree similarity class.

arxiv:2610.13908.title: Counting with Hiccup Sequences
arxiv:2610.13908.summary: The $(0,x,1,2)$-hiccup sequence starts at $x$ and increases by 1 when the current index has already appeared as a value, and by 2 otherwise. We prove directly that for $x\geq3$ the gaps between its missing values are $1,2,3,\ldots$, each repeated $x-2$ times, and we derive closed formulas, an explicit error bound, and a generating function in terms of Ramanujan's theta functions. The counting functions of the complements satisfy nested recurrences.

arxiv:2610.13927.title: On some rigidity results for high-dimensional confoliations
arxiv:2610.13927.summary: The main result is an obstruction to the presence of contact regions for c-symplectic confoliations in any odd ambient dimension. As a first application, we prove a 5-dimensional analogue (under stronger assumptions) of a Reeb stability theorem for confoliations in dimension 3 due to Eliashberg and Thurston. Refining work of the first author with Cardona, we further give two new notions of contact approximations of c-symplectic confoliations in any odd ambient dimension generalizing the 3-dimensional notion of Eliashberg-Thurston.

arxiv:2610.13931.title: Constructive Bounds for the Topological Expressivity of Neural Networks
arxiv:2610.13931.summary: The expressivity of a neural network $\Phi$ describes the class of functions that a network can express. The term topological expressivity refers to a family of measures particularly suited to understand binary classification and is often formulated in terms of the Betti numbers of a decision boundary $\beta (\Phi^{-1}(0))$. Despite its popularity, this measure is not as useful for regression and other problems that do not involve a decision boundary.

arxiv:2610.13933.title: The Haagerup VOA at $c=8$
arxiv:2610.13933.summary: We announce an explicit construction of a unitary, strongly rational vertex operator algebra $U$ of central charge $8$ inside $V_{E_6\oplus A_2}$, with a ribbon equivalence $\mathrm{Rep}(U)\simeq Z(\mathcal H_3)$ realizing the Haagerup double. The vertex algebra is generated by six affine currents and three specified weight-two fields; its weight-one Lie algebra is $\mathfrak{sl}_2\oplus\mathfrak{sl}_2$, at levels $1$ and $39$. We outline the argument, which combines exact lattice calculations, an all-weight strong-generation induction and $C_2$-cofiniteness, semisimple descent for a full corner of Zhu's algebra, modular Galois symmetry, and holomorphic $E_8$ extensions.

arxiv:2610.13939.title: The Tate Conjecture for Ordinary Calabi-Yau Threefolds
arxiv:2610.13939.summary: We use the theory of canonical lifts to prove the integral geometric Tate conjecture for ordinary Calabi-Yau threefolds over finite fields, and also for divisor classes on certain ordinary Calabi-Yau varieties.

arxiv:2610.13965.title: Jensen's inequality on parity classes of jump M-convex functions
arxiv:2610.13965.summary: We prove Jensen's inequality on each coordinatewise parity class of a jump $M$-convex function on $\mathbb{Z}^n$, without assuming strong base orderability or a finite effective domain. If a finite convex combination of domain points has its barycenter in the same parity class, then the barycenter belongs to the domain and satisfies Jensen's inequality. We also prove that every domain point admits an affine support on its entire parity class.

arxiv:2610.13969.title: Global Regularization of the Spatial Elliptic Restricted Three-body Problem: Quaternionic, Hamiltonian Formulation
arxiv:2610.13969.summary: Any objects in space may encounter singularity due to the inverse-square law of the gravitational force, hindering the analysis and propagation of particle motion in space. Regularization in celestial mechanics removes such gravitational singularities in equations of motion by transforming the time and coordinates. This paper addresses a class of regularization methods known as global regularization for restricted three-body problems (R3BPs), which simultaneously removes the two singularities (e.g., Earth and Moon in cislunar space).

arxiv:2610.13972.title: Insertion and expansion of cylinders around the unit ball
arxiv:2610.13972.summary: Surround a unit ball with a ring of $n$ equal infinite circular cylinders, each touching the ball and its two neighbors. Can one more such cylinder be added, for a total of $n+1$, if we are allowed to rearrange the configuration? We prove that the answer is ``no'' for $3\le n\le 7$, and ``yes'' if $n\geq 9$.
arxiv:2610.13972.authors: Ivan Mati\'c, Rado\v{s} Radoi\v{c}i\'c, Andreas Spomer

arxiv:2610.13975.title: The rhombic dodecahedral conjecture
arxiv:2610.13975.summary: We prove that every three-dimensional parallelohedron $P$ satisfies \[ \mathcal H^2(\partial P)\ge 12\sqrt2\,r(P)^2, \] where $r(P)$ is the inradius of $P$, with equality if and only if $P$ is similar to the regular rhombic dodecahedron.

arxiv:2610.13977.title: Local Fan-type obstructions and Ore-type conditions for rainbow Hamiltonicity in graph systems
arxiv:2610.13977.summary: Let $G=(G_1,...,G_n)$ be a graph system on a common $n$-vertex set $V$. For $v\in V$, set \[ \delta(v)=\min_{i\in[n]}d_{G_i}(v), \qquad E_{\cap}=\bigcap_{i=1}^n E(G_i), \] and let $d^c(u,v)$ denote the length of a shortest rainbow $u$--$v$ path. We study Hamiltonicity conditions imposed only on pairs at small rainbow distance.

arxiv:2610.13979.title: A Counterexample to Three Conjectures of Luo
arxiv:2610.13979.summary: We give a single counterexample to Conjectures 1--3 as stated in Luo's paper: a minimal two-tetrahedron triangulation of the lens space L(3,1) with a null-homotopic loop edge. The proof uses quadrilateral matching equations, an explicit calculation of shape parameters, and known results on volume maximization.

arxiv:2610.13983.title: Equilateral sets in $\ell_p^n$ beyond $n+1$: Linear excess and dimension cost
arxiv:2610.13983.summary: How many equilateral points can $\ell_p^n$ contain beyond $n+1$? For every fixed real $p>4$, we construct equilateral sets for which the number of points beyond $n+1$ grows at least linearly with $n$. For every fixed dimension, we prove that the maximum is $n+1$ at all sufficiently large finite $p$, with an explicit threshold.
arxiv:2610.13983.authors: Logan R. Chalmers, Aran S. Ziegler

arxiv:2610.13987.title: Forbidding $r$-extension of $C_4$ -- a counterexample of the Anstee-Sali conjecture
arxiv:2610.13987.summary: In this note we prove $\mathrm{forb}(n,\mathbf{1}_{r-2}\times C_4)=\Theta(n^{r-1/2})$, thus providing a series of counterexamples of a 2005 conjecture of the first two authors. Here $\mathbf{1}_{r-2}\times C_4$ is the $r$-extension of the 4-cycle, that is the $r$-uniform hypergraph of four edges obtained by joining a set of $r-2$ vertices to each edge of $C_4$. $\mathrm{forb}(n,F)$ is the largest number of edges of a simple hypergraph $G$ on $n$ vertices without \emph{trace} (induced subhypergraph) $F$.
arxiv:2610.13987.authors: Richard P. Anstee, Attila Sali, Pei Wu

arxiv:2610.14002.title: Upper Bounds on the Comon Rank Gap of Real Symmetric Third-Order Tensors
arxiv:2610.14002.summary: Let $T$ be a nonzero real symmetric third-order tensor. Denote by $r(T)$ its CP rank, by $s(T)$ its symmetric rank, by $d(T)$ its essential dimension, and put $e(T)=r(T)-d(T)$. We establish two complementary upper bounds for the Comon rank gap $$\Delta(T):= s(T)-r(T)\leq\min\{C_{ec}(e(T)),\ C_{dc}(d(T))\}.$$ The excess-controlled function $C_{ec}(e)$ is zero for $0\leq e\leq3$ and equals $9e-3$ for $e\geq4$.

arxiv:2610.14032.title: Polygons and coplanar points on submanifolds of codimension 2
arxiv:2610.14032.summary: Problem 73 on Green's list of open problems asks whether a smooth submanifold of codimension two in $\mathbb{R}^n$ must meet some affine two-plane in five points when $n$ is large. In this paper, we answer this question for every $n \geq 6$. Every nonempty relatively open subset of such a submanifold contains the vertices of an affinely regular pentagon, and the bound $n \geq 6$ is sharp for affinely regular pentagons.

arxiv:2610.14037.title: Sharp Antipode-Neighbor Bounds in Every Dimension
arxiv:2610.14037.summary: Let $P\subset\mathbb R^d$ be finite with $\operatorname{diam}(P)\le1$. For $0<\varepsilon<1$, let $\mathcal N_\varepsilon(P)$ denote the number of ordered pairs at distance at most $\varepsilon$, including the diagonal, and let $\mathcal A_\varepsilon(P)$ denote the number of ordered pairs at distance at least $1-\varepsilon$. We prove the sharp bound \[ \mathcal N_\varepsilon(P)\gtrsim_d \varepsilon^{(d-1)/2}\mathcal A_\varepsilon(P) \] conjectured by Steinerberger (2025).

arxiv:2610.14055.title: Upper bounds for Jung constants of $\ell_1^d$
arxiv:2610.14055.summary: For every integer $k\ge1$, we prove that each nonempty bounded set in real $\ell_1^{4k+1}$ has an ambient enclosing ball of radius at most $(4k-1)/(4k)$ times its diameter. The bound is sharp in dimension five: $J(\ell_1^5)=3/4$. If a Hadamard matrix of order $4k$ exists, then $J(\ell_1^{4k-1})=J(\ell_1^{4k})=J(\ell_1^{4k+1})=(4k-1)/(4k)$.

arxiv:2610.14083.title: Analytic Criteria for Detecting Bernstein-Sato Roots
arxiv:2610.14083.summary: We study roots of Bernstein-Sato polynomials of ideals. Our first main result gives a general partial differential equation criterion for detecting roots of the Bernstein-Sato polynomial of an ideal. For homogeneous case, we recast this criterion as an analytic condition, connecting the algebraic problem of locating roots with analytic properties of the defining data.

arxiv:2610.14084.title: A proof of the Auluck-Chowla-Gupta Conjecture
arxiv:2610.14084.summary: Let p(n,k) denote the number of partitions of n into exactly k parts. In 1942 Auluck, Chowla and Gupta conjectured that for every n the sequence p(n,1), p(n,2), ..., p(n,n) is unimodal. Szekeres proved this for all sufficiently large n, but with a threshold that was never made explicit.

arxiv:2610.14085.title: Satisfiability and freezing in random integer programs
arxiv:2610.14085.summary: We study a model of a random centrally symmetric polytope and ask about the existence of points in the polytope with non-zero, integer coordinates. Our main results are the location of a sharp threshold for the existence of these integer points, a characterization of the typical empirical distribution of their coordinates, and showing that near the feasibility threshold these integer points are almost always totally isolated --- at linear Hamming distance to the nearest other integer point in the polytope. The behavior of these random integer programs is related to that of the symmetric binary perceptron (the case when coordinates of points are $\pm 1$-valued).
arxiv:2610.14085.authors: Dylan J. Altschuler, Ruben Ascoli, Will Perkins

arxiv:2610.14099.title: Maximally symmetric $(23_4)$ configurations and the end of the existence problem for geometric $(n_4)$ configurations
arxiv:2610.14099.summary: A geometric $(n_4)$ configuration is a set of $n$ points and $n$ lines in the real projective plane such that every point lies on exactly four of the lines and every line contains exactly four of the points. The question of which $n$ admit such a configuration was posed by Gr\"unbaum in 2000, following his 1990 paper with Rigby that gave the first geometric $4$-configuration, a $(21_4)$. Successive work of Bokowski-Schewe, of Bokowski, Gr\"unbaum and Schewe, of Bokowski-Pilaud, and of Cuntz settled every case but one.

arxiv:2610.14100.title: Digraph Laplacian spectra: Counterexamples to the 2005 polygon conjecture
arxiv:2610.14100.summary: Let $\Lambda_n$ be the set of all eigenvalues of standardized Laplacian matrices of order $n$. In 2005, a polygon $S_n\subseteq\Lambda_n$ was constructed, and it was conjectured that $\Lambda_n=S_n$. We observe that $S_n$ is a zonotope, which gives a short proof of $S_n\subseteq\Lambda_n$, and we describe $\Lambda_n$ as a union, over all vectors $v$, of intersections of zonotopes $Z_i(v)$ built from the ratios $v_j/v_i$.

arxiv:2610.14107.title: The weight enumerators of irreducible cyclic codes of length $2^\ell$
arxiv:2610.14107.summary: Using the spectral relation between irreducible cyclic codes (ICC) and generalized Paley (GP) graphs recently found by the authors, we study the weight distribution of irreducible cyclic codes of length $2^\ell$, $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$. These codes were previously studied by Sharma, Bakshi and Raka, who divided them into two families (each having two cases). First we characterize the GP-graphs spectrally related to these families of ICCs: they are complete, semiprimitive, Hamming, or Cartesian products of semiprimitive GP-graphs.
arxiv:2610.14107.authors: Ricardo A. Podest\'a, Denis E. Videla

arxiv:2610.14110.title: New mixed cages, bounds and computational results
arxiv:2610.14110.summary: An $(r,z,g)$-mixed cage is a mixed graph that is $r$-regular in edges, $z$-regular in arcs, of girth $g$ and of minimum order $n=n(r,z,g)$. We give a general lower bound for $n(r,z,g)$. In the case $g=3$, we determine the exact value $n(r,z,3)=r+2z+1$.
arxiv:2610.14110.authors: Claudia Marlene De la Cruz, Miguel \'Angel Piza\~na

arxiv:2610.14111.title: Free products, principal sums, bipartition complete matroids and the linking operation $(\mathcal{M}_{SP} \vee \mathcal{M}_{PQ}) \times (S \uplus Q)$
arxiv:2610.14111.summary: In this paper we examine the special class of bipartition complete matroids, which includes free products and principal sums of matroids (Crapo and Schmitt, 2005; Bonin and Kung, 2015). A matroid $\mathcal{M}_{SQ}$ on $S \uplus Q$ is said to be $\{S,Q\}$--complete iff whenever $b^1_S \uplus b^1_Q, \, b^1_S \uplus b^2_Q,$ and $b^2_S \uplus b^1_Q$ are bases of $\mathcal{M}_{SQ},$ we also have $b^2_S \uplus b^2_Q$ as a base of $\mathcal{M}_{SQ}.$ We use the linking operation $\mathcal{M}_{SP} \leftrightarrow_{\mathcal{M}} \mathcal{M}_{PQ} :\equiv (\mathcal{M}_{SP} \vee \mathcal{M}_{PQ}) \times (S \uplus Q)$ (Theja and Narayanan, 2014) for this study. We construct the $\{S, Q\}$--augmentation…

arxiv:2610.14135.title: Reconstruction and Symmetry of Two-Token Graphs
arxiv:2610.14135.summary: We present a proof of the two-token graph reconstruction conjecture. Every finite simple graph $G,H$ of order at least three, $F_2(G) \cong F_2(H)$ if and only if $G \cong H$. We also classify the automorphism groups of two-token graphs whose connected roots have order at least five.

arxiv:2610.14165.title: Categorifying Quantum Spin Systems
arxiv:2610.14165.summary: We develop a homotopical framework for understanding the space of quantum spin systems based on topological $n$-nets, which assign associative unital algebras to local regions in an $n$-dimensional space in a manner that captures the locality structure of the underlying lattice theories. The net-theoretic perspective admits a natural categorification, in which the category of topological $n$-nets carries the structure of a higher Morita category. Moreover, the nets of greatest physical interest form a Karoubi-complete subcategory that shares many of the characteristic structural features of the category of finite TQFTs.

arxiv:2610.14189.title: Gauss-Manin Connection in Disguise: Holomorphic Anomaly Equations and Higher Genus Real Gromov-Witten Invariants
arxiv:2610.14189.summary: We construct an algebraic framework for the extended holomorphic anomaly equations following ideas of Alim, Movasati, Scheidegger and Yau. We choose the quintic threefold as our main model and use this framework to solve the equations and fix the ambiguity up to genus 5. We obtain predictions for real Gromov-Witten invariants, or, equivalently, real Gopakumar-Vafa invariants that are integers and agree with their complex counterparts modulo 2.

arxiv:2610.14198.title: A Functorial Classification of Toric Stacks
arxiv:2610.14198.summary: Toric stacks enrich the study of toric varieties by accounting for quotients of actions of diagonalizable groups. In practice, toric stacks are constructed and understood via "stacky fans" generalizing the fans appearing in toric geometry. Previous attempts to make this construction into an equivalence of categories have either run into crucial errors or have been restricted to special cases (e.g. only considering separated Deligne-Mumford stacks).

arxiv:2610.14217.title: The Path Partition Conjecture and 3-(quasi-)Transitive Digraphs
arxiv:2610.14217.summary: A digraph $D = (V,E)$ is 3-transitive (respectively, 3-quasi-transitive) if whenever $(u,v,w,z)$ is a directed path of length 3, $(u,z) \in E$ (respectively, $(u,z) \in E$ or $(z,u) \in E$). These digraphs extend the concepts of transitive and quasi-transitive digraphs, respectively. For 3-transitive and 3-quasi-transitive digraphs, only the strong case has been characterized.

arxiv:2610.14218.title: Tight surgeries on torus knots
arxiv:2610.14218.summary: We give a complete classification of tight contact structures on manifolds obtained from any surgery along any torus knot, which provides the first such classification on an infinite family of knots. The main tools are the classification of non-loose torus knots, bordered contact invariants via their immersed curve interpretations, and non-thickenable tori in knot complements. As a byproduct of this classification, we also give the first classification of contact structures on some surface bundles over the circle with fibers of genus larger than $1$.
arxiv:2610.14218.authors: John B. Etnyre, Hyunki Min, B\"ulent Tosun, Konstantinos Varvarezos

arxiv:2610.14241.title: Restricting Odd Antiholes in Critical Graphs via List Coloring
arxiv:2610.14241.summary: By the Strong Perfect Graph Theorem, every graph whose chromatic number exceeds its clique number contains an odd hole or an odd antihole. We investigate the structure of odd antiholes in critical graphs with fixed maximum degree. We prove that if $G$ is a $k$-critical graph with maximum degree $\Delta$ then every odd antihole in $G$ has length at most $2(\Delta-k)+7$, and conjecture that, in the odd-hole-free setting, equality forces the graph itself to be the corresponding odd antihole.

arxiv:2610.14243.title: Dynamical degrees of automorphisms of non-projective hyperk\"ahler manifolds
arxiv:2610.14243.summary: We determine the dynamical degrees of bimeromorphic automorphisms of hyperk\"ahler manifolds of all known deformation types with irreducible characteristic polynomial.
arxiv:2610.14243.authors: Eva Bayer-Fluckiger, Stevell Muller, Matthias Sch\"utt

arxiv:2610.14256.title: Explicit Solutions in a Probabilistic Cellular Automaton Model for Self-Assembled Monolayer Degradation
arxiv:2610.14256.summary: Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs), formed by the adsorption of a monomolecular layer of adsorbate onto a surface, have emerged as leading candidates for plat- forms for electrochemical biosensors. In order to characterize the working age of a SAM-based biosensor, it is necessary to understand the long-term degradation of the monolayer, with particular emphasis on the intermolecular forces present in the self-assembly process. In this work, discrete- and continuous-time proba- bilistic cellular automaton (PCA) models for the degradation of SAMs involving adsorbate-adsorbate interactions are proposed in which adsorbate molecules desorb at a rate dependent only on the number of adsorbed…
arxiv:2610.14256.authors: Wes Caldwell, Ryan Evans, Jacob Majikes, Anthony Kearsley

arxiv:2610.14263.title: Bipartite Carrier Compression and Machine-Certified Bounds in Sch\"onhage Trilinear Multiplication Tensors
arxiv:2610.14263.summary: Under the conditional framework breaking the longstanding O(n log n) integer multiplication barrier (originating from OpenAI Preprint #109), the asymptotic time complexity exponent T(n) = O(n (log n)^{1-\kappa}) is governed by bounding the second moment E[X^2] < 1 of recursive branching processes over trilinear tensor carrier graphs. In this work, we present a constructive combinatorial optimization over the alternating carrier bipartite matching graphs of the Sch\"onhage trilinear tensor decomposition at dimensions h=23 and h=25. Through an alternating augmenting path search, we uncover a non-trivial cluster-unlocking cascade that eliminates 185 carrier roles (95 roles in h=23 and 90 roles…
arxiv:2610.14263.authors: Volkan Da\u{g}l{\i}, Zerrin Da\u{g}l{\i}, Da\u{g}han Da\u{g}l{\i}

arxiv:2610.14275.title: Polytopal invariance for Lusztig's $q$-weight multiplicities
arxiv:2610.14275.summary: Let $\Phi$ be an irreducible root system normalized so that long roots have length $\sqrt{2}$, and let $\mu\leq\lambda$ be dominant weights. We associate to $(\Phi,\mu,\lambda)$ the convex polytope $$P^{\Phi}_{\mu,\lambda} = (\mu+C)\cap(\lambda-C)\cap(\overline{D}-\rho),$$ where $C=\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\Phi^+$ and $\overline{D}$ is the closed dominant Weyl chamber. We prove that if $P^{\Phi}_{\mu,\lambda}$ and $P^{\Phi'}_{\mu',\lambda'}$ are isometric, then $$K^{\Phi}_{\lambda\mu}(q)=K^{\Phi'}_{\lambda'\mu'}(q),$$ where $K^{\Phi}_{\lambda\mu}(q)$ is Lusztig's $q$-analogue of the $\mu$-weight multiplicity in the irreducible highest-weight representation $V(\lambda)$, often called the…

arxiv:2610.14276.title: Stability of vector bundles and reduction mod $p$
arxiv:2610.14276.summary: Let $E$ be a vector bundle on a normal complex projective variety. We prove that slope stability of $\mathop{Sym}^2E$ and Zariski density of the reductions of $E$ modulo $p$ that are not strongly geometrically stable imply that the bundle $E$ is projectively unitary flat. This generalizes Shepherd--Barron's result from rank $2$ to arbitrary rank.

arxiv:2610.14278.title: Representation homology of involutive algebras and hyperoctaherdral homology
arxiv:2610.14278.summary: In this paper, we introduce and study the (involutive) representation homology of involutive algebras, following the development of representation homology of associative algebra in our earlier papers. Our main motivation is to understand the hyperoctahedral homology of involutive algebras. We show that over a field of characteristic $0$, the hyperoctahedral homology of an involutive algebra is isomorphic (as a graded commutative algebra) to its one dimensional involutive representation homology.
arxiv:2610.14278.authors: Yuri Berest, Ajay C. Ramadoss, John Wood

arxiv:2610.14282.title: Example of exponential many collisions of identical hard disks in the plane
arxiv:2610.14282.summary: Let $ \operatorname{MaxCol}(n,d) $ denote the maximal number of nonsimultaneous elastic collisions among $n$ identical hard balls moving freely in $\mathbb{R}^d$. We give a planar construction with exponential lower bound with respect to $n$: $ \operatorname{MaxCol}(n,2)\geq 2^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}, \quad n\geq3 $.

arxiv:2610.14292.title: The Exact Degree Threshold for Complement Connectivity
arxiv:2610.14292.summary: For a graph $G$, we investigate sufficient degree conditions under which either $G$ or its complement $\overline{G}$ is $k$-connected. Motivated by a theorem of Hellwig and Volkmann, we introduce the notion of complement connectivity admissible pairs and define the parameter $\mathcal{C}(k)$ as the minimum degree threshold guaranteeing that either $G$ or $\overline{G}$ is $k$-connected whenever $\delta(G)\ge\mathcal{C}(k)$ and $\Delta(G)\le |V(G)|-1-\mathcal{C}(k)$. We prove that $\mathcal{C}(k)=2k-2$ for every $k\ge2$, thereby determining the exact degree threshold.

arxiv:2610.14331.title: Cardinalities of Kiselman monoids and their parity asymptotics
arxiv:2610.14331.summary: The cardinalities of Kiselman's semigroups $K_n$ are known to grow double exponentially in $n$: the sequence $2^{-n/2}\log_2|K_n|$ converges along the even and odd $n$ subsequences to positive limits $c_{\mathrm{even}}$ and $c_{\mathrm{odd}}$ that appear to coincide. In this paper we prove that they are indeed distinct. Since Kiselman's semigroups are $\mathcal{L}$-trivial, the suffix relation defines a partial order on $K_n$.

arxiv:2610.14340.title: H\"older regularity for metric Anosov flows
arxiv:2610.14340.summary: We define a class of flows on compact metric spaces that we call \emph{$C^\alpha$ metric Anosov flows}, $0 < \alpha < 1$ or $\alpha = \mathrm{Lip}$. We give verifiable criteria for a metric Anosov flow to be $C^\alpha$. We show that $C^\alpha$ metric Anosov flows have H\"older continuous local product structure, and in particular H\"older continuous holonomies.

arxiv:2610.14370.title: A Sharp Basis-Mass Inequality for Binary Matroids without a Fano Minor
arxiv:2610.14370.summary: Let $M$ be a binary matroid of rank $r$ with no $F_7$-minor, and let $B_M^\star$ denote the maximum of its basis-generating polynomial over nonnegative weights of total mass $r$. We prove the sharp inequality $B_M^\star\leq 2^r/(r+1)$, with equality holding if and only if the nonloop simplification of $M$ is $M(K_{r+1})$. Binary matroids with no $F_7$-minor also form the largest minor-closed class of matroids on which this inequality holds.

arxiv:2610.14373.title: Transposition Cayley Spectra and Subgraph Counts
arxiv:2610.14373.summary: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on the vertex set $[n]$, and let $\Gamma(G)$ be the Cayley graph of the symmetric group $S_n$ generated by the transpositions corresponding to the edges of $G$. We study the inverse spectral problem for the assignment $G\mapsto \Gamma(G)$ through the group-algebra operator $A_G=\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E(G)}(ij)$ and its regular spectral moments $M_k(G)=\operatorname{tr}(A_G^k)$. The moments admit two all-order forms: a universal support expansion in non-induced subgraph counts of $G$, and a representation-theoretic expansion over the irreducible representations of $S_n$.

arxiv:2610.14374.title: Greedy Coloring and Simple Exponential Strengthenings of Brooks-Type Theorems
arxiv:2610.14374.summary: Brooks' Theorem is a foundational result in graph coloring: if a graph is connected, not a clique, and has maximum degree $\Delta \geq 3$, then it admits a proper $\Delta$-coloring. In this paper, we give a new proof of a much stronger result: every such graph admits exponentially many proper $\Delta$-colorings. Exponential lower bounds have been obtained previously by applying the Combinatorial Nullstellensatz.
arxiv:2610.14374.authors: Alex Crane, Carl Feghali, Felicia Lucke, Blair D. Sullivan, Madelyn J. Warr

arxiv:2610.14377.title: The fifteenth cohomology group of moduli spaces of stable curves
arxiv:2610.14377.summary: The new framework of semi-tautological extensions has allowed for explicit understanding of low-degree odd cohomology groups of moduli spaces of stable curves. Let $S^*_\omega(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}) \subset H^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ denote the semi-tautological extension generated by $H^{11}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,11})$, that is, the smallest system of subrings of $H^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ containing $H^{11}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,11})$ and the tautological subrings, which is also closed under pullbacks along forgetful maps and pushforwards along gluing maps. Recently, it has been shown that $H^{11}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}) = S^{11}_\omega(\overline{\mathcal…
arxiv:2610.14377.authors: Amy Bradford, Aitor Iribar L\'opez, Andreas Kretschmer, Hannah Larson

arxiv:2610.14420.title: Flat and Ghost dimensions in tensor triangulated categories with a compact tilting generator
arxiv:2610.14420.summary: Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a tensor triangulated category with a compact tilting generator $M$ and abelian heart $\mathcal{H}_M = M^{\bot_{\neq0}}$. We define a triangulated flat dimension $\mathrm{flatdim}_{\mathcal{T}}X$ for $X\in\mathcal{T}$, and give criteria in terms of tensor vanishing and resolutions by the class of pure quotients of $\mathrm{Add}(M)$. We further introduce $M$-ghost length and $M$-ghost dimension, and show that the global dimension of $\mathcal{H}_M$ controls the $M$-ghost length of all objects in $\mathcal{T}$, and that the $M$-ghost dimension of $\mathcal{T}$ coincides with the weak global dimension of $\mathcal{H}_M$ and the supremum of…

arxiv:2610.14421.title: A framework for spanning forest identities
arxiv:2610.14421.summary: Identities of spanning forest polynomials can come from determinantal identities such as the classical Dodgson identity. They can also be useful in quantum field theory calculations, particularly the quadratic ones. To better understand the structure of spanning forest polynomial identities, we look at when identities on a given graph are generic for all graphs, we ask about dimensions of spaces of spanning forest identities indexed by certain parameters, and we set up a framework that we hope will be helpful for further progress in these directions.

arxiv:2610.14441.title: Haagerup conformal field theory at central charge eight
arxiv:2610.14441.summary: We construct a chiral algebra $U$ of central charge eight inside the lattice vertex operator algebra $V_{E_6\oplus A_2}$. It is generated by two commuting affine $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ current algebras at levels $1$ and $39$, the stress tensor of the lattice theory, and a single weight-two field built from three lattice exponentials. We announce that $U$ is strongly rational and completely unitary, and that $Rep(U)$ is equivalent, as a unitary ribbon category, to the Drinfeld center $Z(\mathcal{H}_3)$ of the Haagerup fusion category $\mathcal{H}_3$.

arxiv:2610.14467.title: Harmonic Reduction of Spin-Coupled Grover Walks on Hypercubes via Quantum Bernoulli Noises
arxiv:2610.14467.summary: We consider spin-coupled Grover walks on hypercubes within the framework of quantum Bernoulli noises (QBN). We identify parity-dependent harmonic subspaces generated by the central Hamming layers: in even dimension they give a fixed-point subspace, whereas in odd dimension the walk reduces on the harmonic subspace to an explicit eight-dimensional reduced dynamics. Using symmetric-group representation theory, we characterize the corresponding isotypic structure and determine the reduced spectrum.

arxiv:2610.14468.title: Localization of Floer homology for $\mathbb{Z}_p$-actions
arxiv:2610.14468.summary: For an odd prime $p$, we prove a Smith inequality over $\mathbb{F}_p$ for exact Lagrangian Floer homology under a symplectic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-action, assuming an equivariant stable normal trivialization compatible with the Lagrangians and the required relative Pin data. As an application, we obtain a rank inequality between the symplectic Khovanov homology of a $p$-periodic link and that of its quotient. These results extend the involutive localization of Seidel and Smith.
arxiv:2610.14468.authors: Erkao Bao, Tyler Lawson, Cheuk Yu Mak

arxiv:2610.14486.title: Local Antimagic Chromatic Number of Middle Graph and Direct Product of Graphs
arxiv:2610.14486.summary: An edge labeling of a connected graph $G=(V, E)$ is called a local antimagic labeling if it is a bijection $f: E\rightarrow \{1, 2, \cdots, \left | E \right | \}$ such that for any pair of adjacent vertices $u$ and $v$, $f^{+}(u)\neq f^{+}(v)$ where $f^{+}(x)=\sum f(e)$, with $e$ ranging over all the edges incident to $x$. The local antimagic chromatic number of $G$, denoted $\chi_{la}(G)$, is the minimum number of distinct induced vertex labels across all possible local antimagic labelings of $G$. This paper investigates two families of graphs $G(m^{[n]})$ (a graph class constructed by augmenting a bipartite structure $B(m^{[n]})$ with cyclic edges) and $K_{1,s}\times C_n$ (the direct…
arxiv:2610.14486.authors: Huimin Xu, Gee-Choon Lau, Ruixue Zhang

arxiv:2610.14491.title: The canonical class and Chern character operators on Hilbert schemes of points
arxiv:2610.14491.summary: Let $X$ be a smooth projective complex surface. We obtain explicit formulas for the Chern character operators on the Hilbert schemes of points $X^{[n]}$ in terms of Nakajima operators, determining in particular the coefficients of the terms involving the canonical class $K_X$ and its square. Consequently, the cohomology ring structure of the Hilbert scheme is determined.

arxiv:2610.14496.title: When Do Restricted Sumsets Cover a Finite Abelian Group?
arxiv:2610.14496.summary: For a subset $A$ of a finite abelian group $G$, let $\Sigma_k(A)$ denote the set of sums of $k$ distinct elements of $A$, and let $\Sigma(A)=\bigcup_{k\ge1}\Sigma_k(A)$. The problem of determining when $\Sigma(A)=G$ goes back to Erd\H{o}s and Heilbronn. Nguyen and Vu later formulated the corresponding fixed-length question: for a prescribed $k$, when does $\Sigma_k(A)=G$?

arxiv:2610.14502.title: Monophobic Neighborhoods of Cubes
arxiv:2610.14502.summary: We define a $d$-cube in a graph $G$ to be monophobic in $G$ if, whenever it supports a $d$-face of a discrete singular $d+1$-cube, it must also support another face. In many cases, the presence of such cubes implies the nontriviality of discrete cubical homology and homotopy groups associated with $G$. We describe several large classes of examples and characterize the property completely when $d=2$.

arxiv:2610.14503.title: A sharp bound for the least signless Laplacian eigenvalue of triangle-free graphs
arxiv:2610.14503.summary: We prove that every finite simple triangle-free graph $G$ on $n\geq1$ vertices satisfies $q_{\min}(G)\leq7n/50$, where $q_{\min}(G)$ is the least eigenvalue of its signless Laplacian matrix $Q_G=D_G+A_G$, with $D_G$ the diagonal matrix of vertex degrees and $A_G$ the adjacency matrix. The constant is sharp, since the Higman--Sims graph and its balanced blow-ups attain equality, as shown by de Lima, Nikiforov and Oliveira (2016). This proves the bound conjectured by Balogh, Clemen, Lidick\'y, Norin and Volec (2023).
arxiv:2610.14503.authors: Dongxiu Cai, Zhengbo Chen, Xiao-Dong Zhang

arxiv:2610.14506.title: Characterization of $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor numbers of small rank
arxiv:2610.14506.summary: The $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor number of a polynomial map is a quadratic enrichment of the classical Milnor number, defined as the local $\mathbb{A}^1$-Brouwer degree of the gradient. We study which elements of the Grothendieck-Witt ring of nondegenerate symmetric bilinear forms arise as $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor numbers. Over fields of characteristic not $2$, $3$, or $5$, we show that every element of the Grothendieck-Witt ring of rank at most $7$ that is a local $\mathbb{A}^1$-Brouwer degree is also an $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor number.
arxiv:2610.14506.authors: C-Y. Jean Chan, Thomas Hagedorn, Joel Louwsma, Michael Wijaya

arxiv:2610.14534.title: Survivor Set of Gauss Map with a Hole at $1$
arxiv:2610.14534.summary: Let $T$ be the Gauss map. For each $\alpha\in [0,1]$, let $E(\alpha)$ be the survivor set consisting of all $x\in [0,1]$ whose orbit $\{T^k(x):k\ge 0\}$ never enters the interval $(\alpha,1]$. We prove that the set-valued function $\alpha\mapsto E(\alpha)$ is increasing and locally constant almost everywhere.

arxiv:2610.14535.title: A degree-linear upper bound for the P\'olya exponent of forms with fixed arity
arxiv:2610.14535.summary: Let $P = \sum_{\omega} a_\omega x^\omega$ be a degree $d$ homogeneous polynomial in $x_0, \dots, x_n$ with real coefficients. P\'olya showed that, if $P$ is strictly positive on the standard $n$-simplex, then $(x_0 + \cdots + x_n)^M P$ has strictly positive coefficients for all $M \gg 0$. The least such $M$ is known as the \emph{P\'olya exponent} of $P$. de Klerk-Laurent-Parrilo showed that the P\'olya exponent is $O(d^2) P^{(0)}_{\max}/\lambda(P)$, where $P^{(0)}_{\max} := \max_\omega a_\omega/\binom{d}{\omega}$ and $\lambda(P)$ is the infimum of $P$ on the standard simplex.

arxiv:2610.14563.title: Sharp projection inequalities for antichains in cone orders
arxiv:2610.14563.summary: We establish sharp projection inequalities for $k$-antichains under orders defined by open convex cones. For integers $n\geq2$ and $k\ge 1$, let $C\subsetneq\mathbb R^n$ be a nonempty open convex cone. A set $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is a $k$-antichain with respect to the order $x\prec_C y\iff y-x\in C$ if it contains no chain $x^1\prec_C\cdots\prec_C x^{k+1}$.

arxiv:2610.14575.title: Shake concordance in the topological concordance class of the Hopf link
arxiv:2610.14575.summary: Within the topological concordance class of the Hopf link, we construct infinitely many classes under the equivalence relation generated by smooth $0$-shake concordance. Each contains infinitely many smooth concordance classes represented by links that are pairwise strongly $0$-shake concordant and whose second components have unbounded smooth slice genus.

arxiv:2610.14608.title: Cetraro lectures on integrable systems and moduli spaces of curves
arxiv:2610.14608.summary: In these lecture notes we review some constructions and results on the relation between topology of the moduli space of stable curves and integrable systems of evolutionary PDEs.

arxiv:2610.14637.title: Generalized reflection complexity
arxiv:2610.14637.summary: The reflection complexity of a sequence, introduced recently by Allouche, Campbell, Li, Shallit, and Stipulanti, counts the factors of a given length up to reversal. We generalize this notion considering a group $G$ generated by antimorphisms over a given alphabet $\mathcal A$. The $G$-complexity of a sequence over $\mathcal A$ counts the factors of a given length up to the action of $G$.
arxiv:2610.14637.authors: Adam Bla\v{z}ek, Lubom\'ira Dvo\v{r}\'akov\'a, Edita Pelantov\'a

arxiv:2610.14681.title: Pairwise Compatibility Graphs of Unweighted Caterpillars
arxiv:2610.14681.summary: In this paper we study pairwise compatibility graphs whose witness tree is required to be an unweighted caterpillar. This is a natural restriction of PCGs, in the same line of research as the study of star witnesses, which led to the class of double-threshold graphs. In the caterpillar case, we show that this restriction is equivalent to a one-dimensional difference-labelling problem: a graph admits such a representation if and only if its vertices can be assigned integer labels so that adjacency is determined exactly by whether the absolute difference of two labels belongs to a given interval.
arxiv:2610.14681.authors: Cyriac Antony, Manuel Lafond, Angelo Monti, Blerina Sinaimeri

arxiv:2610.14712.title: Induced-Count Discrepancy in Uniform Hypergraphs
arxiv:2610.14712.summary: Let $u_k^{(r)}(H,p)$ be the maximum, over all $k$-vertex $r$-uniform hypergraphs $F$, of the absolute difference between the number of induced copies of $F$ in $H$ and its expectation in the binomial random $r$-graph with the same number of vertices as $H$ and edge probability $p$. Let $u_k^{(r)}(n,p)$ be the minimum of $u_k^{(r)}(H,p)$ over all $n$-vertex $r$-uniform hypergraphs, and let $D_r(n,p)$ be the distance from $p\binom nr$ to the nearest integer. For fixed $r\ge3$, $k\ge2r$ and $\varepsilon>0$, the quantity $u_k^{(r)}(n,p)$ has order $\max\!\left\{D_r(n,p),p(1-p)\right\}n^{k-r}$ whenever $p(1-p)n^{\lfloor r/2\rfloor/(\binom{2r-2}{r}-1)}\ge\varepsilon$.

arxiv:2610.14794.title: On the Julia sets of the non-autonomous iteration of exponential maps
arxiv:2610.14794.summary: This paper studies non-autonomous iterations of $\lambda e^z$, where at each step the parameter $\lambda$ is chosen from a bounded interval. Urba\'nski and Zdunik introduced and developed a thermodynamic formalism for random dynamics of exponential maps, extending the autonomous result established independently by Rees and Lyubich to typical parameter sequences in $[A, B]^{\mathbb{N}}$ with $1/e<A<B<\infty$. In this paper, we show that the same conclusion indeed holds for all parameters in $[A, B]^{\mathbb{N}}$, Our proof is based on carefully crafted uniform versions of pullback arguments, inspired by the original methods of Rees and Lyubich.

arxiv:2610.14803.title: Combinatorics of degeneracy in vertical systems
arxiv:2610.14803.summary: We characterize the generic consistency of vertical systems in terms of the iterated circuits of the column matroid of the coefficient matrix. More precisely, we prove that such a system is generically consistent if and only if there exists an iterated circuit such that the dimension of the Minkowski sum of the associated Newton polytopes is equal to the rank of the coefficient matrix. We also give an equivalent characterization in terms of $G$-spanning flags of the dual matroid.

arxiv:2610.14829.title: New bounds for off-diagonal hypergraph Ramsey numbers
arxiv:2610.14829.summary: We study a conjecture of Conlon, Fox, Gunby, He, Mubayi, Suk, Verstra\"ete, and Yu, which characterizes the $3$-graphs $H$ for which the off-diagonal Ramsey number $r(H,n)$ is polynomial. We prove the conjecture for $3$-graphs with at most five tight components. Additionally, we show that the full conjecture is equivalent to its specialization to linear $3$-graphs.
arxiv:2610.14829.authors: David Conlon, Xiaoyu He, Jiaxi Nie, Logan Post

arxiv:2610.14847.title: Lifts of symmetries to minimal nondegenerate extensions are unique up to fermion attachment
arxiv:2610.14847.summary: Gauging fermion parity in a $(2+1)$-dimensional fermionic topological order requires lifting its symmetries to the resulting bosonic theory. We give a direct tensor-categorical proof that, for a slightly degenerate braided fusion category $\mathcal{C}$ and a fixed minimal nondegenerate extension ${\cal E}$, the restriction homomorphism $r\colon\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{LR}}(\mathcal{E})\to \operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{LR}}(\mathcal{C})$ on classes of complex-linear locality-respecting (LR) braided autoequivalences is surjective with central kernel $\mathbb{Z}/2$, generated by fermion attachment. Thus each symmetry class has exactly two LR lift classes, related by attaching the fermion to…

arxiv:2610.14874.title: A smooth non-compactly generated category
arxiv:2610.14874.summary: Let $A=\mathbb{Q}[t^{\frac{1}{2^n}}:n\geq 0]$ and consider $A[u,u^{-1};\sigma]$, a skew Laurent polynomial ring, where $\sigma(t^q)=t^{2q}$. We study the kernel of derived extension of scalars along $ A[u,u^{-1};\sigma]\longrightarrow\mathbb{Q}[u,u^{-1}], $ the quotient by $\mathfrak{m}A[u,u^{-1};\sigma]$, with $\mathfrak{m}=(t^{\frac{1}{2^n}}:n\geq 0)$. A finite free resolution of $\mathfrak{m}A[u,u^{-1};\sigma]$ over $ A[u,u^{-1};\sigma]\otimes_{\mathbb{Q}} \bigl(A[u,u^{-1};\sigma]\bigr)^{\mathrm{op}} $ proves smoothness.

arxiv:2610.14876.title: Conley Index of Limit Cycles in Filippov Vector Fields
arxiv:2610.14876.summary: Within the framework of multivalued dynamical systems, we compute the Conley index for a class of limit cycles in planar Filippov systems. We classify these cycles according to their interaction with the switching manifold, including crossing, sliding, and mixed regimes. Using the Conley index for multivalued admissible maps developed by Mrozek, we construct the appropriate index pairs and determine the corresponding indices for each class.
arxiv:2610.14876.authors: Let\'icia C\^andido, Dahisy Lima, Ketty de Rezende

arxiv:2610.14892.title: Coefficientwise Extremality and Rigidity for Independent Sets in Bipartite Graph Covers
arxiv:2610.14892.summary: Let $G$ be a finite bipartite graph and let $\widetilde G$ be an $M$-fold cover. We compare independent sets of $\widetilde G$ with those of the trivial cover, consisting of $M$ disjoint copies of $G$, after prescribing how many vertices are selected above each vertex of $G$. A conjecture from 2011, motivated by the Bethe approximation, asserts that the trivial cover maximizes every such count.

arxiv:2610.14897.title: Boundary of Anosov coaffine representations
arxiv:2610.14897.summary: Let $\Gamma \le \mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb R)$ be a torsion-free hyperbolic group dividing a properly and strictly convex domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb R\mathrm P^d$, and let $\rho: \Gamma \to \mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb R)$ be the inclusion. We study representations of $\Gamma$ into the coaffine group that are deformations of $\rho\oplus 1 \in \mathrm{Hom}(\Gamma, \mathrm{GL}(d+2,\mathbb R))$ and that lie on the boundary of the locus of projective Anosov representations. In this setting, we identify a canonical limit set $\Lambda$ for the action and study its fine geometric features which are, in a suitable sense, stable.

arxiv:2610.14931.title: Local coherence and recollement of abelian categories
arxiv:2610.14931.summary: We study how local coherenAAce of abelian categories behaves under gluing. For AB5 locally finitely presentable abelian categories, we give conditions on the gluing functors under which local coherence is transferred along a gluing $(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{B}, \mathcal{C})$: from $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{C}$ to $\mathcal{B}$, and conversely from $\mathcal{B}$ to $\mathcal{A}$ or $\mathcal{C}$. The coherence theorem for augmented homotopes of Bondal and Zhdanovskiy is recovered as a special case, the coherence theorem for trivial extensions of Fossum, Griffith, and Reiten is a companion result in the same direction.

arxiv:2610.14972.title: Stable Manifolds and Uniqueness of Parabolic Rays in the Newtonian $N$-Body Problem
arxiv:2610.14972.summary: We study uniqueness for parabolic motions in the Newtonian $N$-body problem with a prescribed minimal normalized central configuration at infinity. A McGehee compactification identifies their tails with the strong stable manifold of the corresponding outgoing zero-energy equilibrium. The configuration projection of this manifold is locally a smooth graph, yielding a smooth initial-velocity field and uniqueness among all parabolic motions confined to a sufficiently narrow truncated cone, without any minimizing assumption.

arxiv:2610.14979.title: Sharp bounds and extremal structure of minimally strongly $k$-connected digraphs
arxiv:2610.14979.summary: Let $D$ be a finite simple minimally strongly $k$-connected digraph, where $k\ge 2$, and let $n=|V(D)|$. Mader proved in 1985 that $|A(D)|\le 2k(n-k)$ for all sufficiently large $n$, with equality if and only if $D\cong \overleftrightarrow{K}_{k,n-k}$ (JCTB 1985). We prove that this bound holds whenever $n\ge 3k-1$ and that the order threshold $3k-1$ is best possible.
arxiv:2610.14979.authors: Junran Yu, Gregory Gutin, Hong-Jian Lai, Xiaoyan Zhang

arxiv:2610.14985.title: Hilbert functions over the exterior algebra and f-vectors in higher rank II: Generalizing Linusson's count to sumsets of f-vectors
arxiv:2610.14985.summary: Let $E$ be the exterior algebra of an $n$-dimensional vector space over a field, let $F$ be a graded free $E$-module with $r$ generators of degrees $d_1 \le \dots \le d_r$, and let $M$ range over the monomial submodules of Amata and Crupi. The Hilbert function of $F/M$ is a shifted sum of $f$-vectors of simplicial complexes; the companion paper determines the convex hull of such sums, and here we count them. For $r = 1$ the count is Linusson's (1999); we show that no new recursion is needed for general $r$.

arxiv:2610.14991.title: Affine realization of tilted Richardson varieties
arxiv:2610.14991.summary: Richardson varieties provide geometric representatives for products of Schubert classes, with stratifications indexed by the subintervals of Bruhat intervals. We construct analogous geometric models for tilted Bruhat intervals for all split connected reductive groups. Our construction uses Richardson varieties in affine flag varieties and yields abstract tilted Richardson varieties whose isomorphism classes, together with their labeled stratifications, are independent of the choices involved.

arxiv:2610.15006.title: DisCo Algebra: Why Disintegration and Combination Are Not Inverses
arxiv:2610.15006.summary: We present DisCo algebra---a compositional framework for joint probability built from a symmetric cooperad (disintegration) and a symmetric operad (combination) on the bare family $\mathcal{P}_n=\mathrm{Prob}([0,1]^n)$. No probability integral transform, no external summary functions, no enrichment of objects with conditional kernels. The disintegration side uses block-wise joint CDFs as intrinsic, measure-determined 1D summaries, yielding a lossy compression.

arxiv:2610.15023.title: Dynamical Properties of Perturbed Weighted Shifts
arxiv:2610.15023.summary: In this paper, sufficient conditions are established for diagonal perturbations of weighted shifts to be supercyclic, hypercyclic, and frequently hypercyclic, extending several classical results for weighted shifts to this more general setting. In addition, a complete analytic characterization of the shadowing property for these operators is obtained. Consequently, examples of frequently hypercyclic perturbed weighted shifts with the shadowing property are constructed.
arxiv:2610.15023.authors: Ali Messaoudi, Jos\'e Luiz Tofanin Neto, Ioannis Tsokanos

arxiv:2610.15024.title: Sharp lower bounds for bisections of graphs with bounded maximum degree
arxiv:2610.15024.summary: A bisection of a graph is a partition of its vertex set into two parts whose sizes differ by at most one. We prove that every graph with $m$ edges and maximum degree at most $k$ has a bisection of size at least $\frac{k+1}{2k}m$ when $k$ is odd, and at least $\frac{k+2}{2(k+1)}m$ when $k$ is even. Both bounds are sharp, with equality for complete graphs.

arxiv:2610.15057.title: Almost every Boolean function has central threshold degree
arxiv:2610.15057.summary: The polynomial threshold degree (or threshold degree) of a Boolean function is the least degree of a real polynomial whose sign represents it. We prove that almost every Boolean function has polynomial threshold degree among the central one or two integers. More precisely, a uniformly chosen Boolean function on $n$ variables has threshold degree $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ or $\lceil n/2\rceil$ except with probability at most $\exp(-c2^{n/2}/n)$, for an absolute constant $c>0$ and all sufficiently large $n$.

arxiv:2610.15069.title: How iterated sumsets grow under the assumption of small doubling
arxiv:2610.15069.summary: Let $K>1$ be a real number and let $A\subsetneq \mathbb Z$ be a finite and nonempty subset. Suppose $|A+A|<K|A|$. A fundamental open problem is to characterize the size of higher iterated sumsets $nA = A+\cdots+A$ ($n$-fold sumset).

arxiv:2610.15080.title: Internal Languages for Thin Epsilon-Hyperdoctrines: Soundness, Completeness, and Rocq Formalization
arxiv:2610.15080.summary: We present a typed proof-term calculus for intuitionistic intensional first-order logic with Hilbert's epsilon-operator and prove its soundness and completeness with respect to hyperdoctrinal models with thin bicartesian closed setoid categories (BiCCCs) as fibres and formula-indexed witness selections. The calculus provides an explicit internal language for these epsilon-hyperdoctrines: for each fixed typed signature, its syntactic term model is initial for syntax-indexed, interpretation-preserving model morphisms, with uniqueness up to setoid equality. The nested epsilon syntax is organized by a well-founded dependency relation on formula labels.

arxiv:2610.15099.title: Topological realizations of finite posets
arxiv:2610.15099.summary: I introduce a new class of cell complexes, called CL-complexes, that provide alternative topological realizations of finite posets. Each realization of a given poset has the same homotopy type as the order complex of that, so in some sense these spaces do not provide anything really new. Their value is that they enable short transparent proofs of standard results in poset homotopy.

arxiv:2610.15102.title: Davenport Constants of Finite Abelian Groups
arxiv:2610.15102.summary: A central problem in zero-sum theory is to determine the Davenport constant of a finite abelian group. For a finite abelian group $G\cong C_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus C_{n_r}$, with $1<n_1\mid\cdots\mid n_r$, let $\mathsf D(G)$ be the least integer $t$ such that every sequence of $t$ elements of $G$ contains a nonempty zero-sum subsequence, and denote $\mathsf D^*(G):= 1+\sum_{i=1}^r(n_i-1)$. The standard construction shows that $\mathsf D(G)\ge\mathsf D^*(G)$.

arxiv:2610.15123.title: Computation of Attractor Lattices for a Class of Hybrid Systems
arxiv:2610.15123.summary: We study the attractor lattice of a class of hybrid dynamical systems on compact metric spaces. Under the trapping guard condition, we prove that hybrid attractors form a bounded distributive lattice isomorphic to the attractor lattice of an associated semiflow. The regularized preimages define a lattice epimorphism from a sublattice of the regular closed, attracting neighborhoods of the semiflow onto those of the hybrid system, and from the whole lattice when the guard set and its reset image have empty interior.
arxiv:2610.15123.authors: William Kalies, Bernardo Rivas, Tony Wehbe

arxiv:2610.15131.title: Polynomial Identities for Generalized Fibonacci Sequences
arxiv:2610.15131.summary: The Fibonacci, Lucas, and Pell sequences satisfy certain families of ``polynomial'' identities. While a few members of these families are well-known, we are not able to find a general statement of these identities in the mathematical literature. We show that such polynomial identities exist for many generalized Fibonacci sequences, and we classify sequences that have these identities obtained by two distinct approaches.
arxiv:2610.15131.authors: Joey Glampe, Aryaman Joshi, Swagat Malla, Matthew Richey, Matthew Wright

arxiv:2610.15132.title: Cones of Theta Graphs are Enumeratively Chromatic-Choosable
arxiv:2610.15132.summary: Chromatic choosability is a fundamental notion in list coloring. A graph $G$ is chromatic-choosable if its chromatic number $\chi(G)$ equals its list chromatic number $\chi_{\ell}(G)$. In 1990, Kostochka and Sidorenko introduced the list color function of a graph $G$, denoted by $P_{\ell}(G,m)$, which is the list-coloring analogue of its chromatic polynomial $P(G,m)$.
arxiv:2610.15132.authors: Kingston Barnes, Vincent Fesenmeier, Braxton Gaither, Michael Guthrie, Leonardo Marciaga, Lucas Miller, Fennec Morrissette, Jeffrey A. Mudrock, Gavin Nguyen, Rose Zellner

arxiv:2610.15145.title: Nim heaps in the Game of Cycles: the parity conjecture fails on trees
arxiv:2610.15145.summary: The Game of Cycles, invented by Francis Su, is a two-player game in which the players take turns drawing arrows on the edges of a plane graph, never creating a sink or a source. On a tree only the sink-source rule matters, and the player who makes the last move wins. Several authors conjectured that on a tree the second player wins exactly when the number of markable edges is even.

arxiv:2610.15147.title: A quotient of the Bruhat-Tits building classifying maximal matrix orders over curves
arxiv:2610.15147.summary: In a previous work, we defined a quotient graph of the Bruhat-Tits tree associated to the degree two special linear group over a local field whose vertex set is in correspondence with the maximal orders in a certain number of spinor genera. This graph has been applied to the study of the structure of some arithmetic groups, their presentations and their (co)homology groups. The genera of Eichler orders, which, for instance, are related to the problem of finding a basis that simultaneously splits two vector bundles with the same generic fiber, can often be described in terms of simpler genera via quotients.
arxiv:2610.15147.authors: Luis Arenas-Carmona, Claudio Bravo, Ignacio Saavedra

arxiv:2610.15151.title: Extremal graphs with cycle lengths in a fixed residue class
arxiv:2610.15151.summary: For integers $k\ge3$ and $0\le \ell<k$, we call a graph $(\ell\bmod k)$-cycle-restricted if every cycle has length congruent to $\ell$ modulo $k$. Akbari, Jamaali, Mahmoody, and Seyed Fakhari [On the size of graphs whose cycles have length divisible by a fixed integer, Australas. J.

arxiv:2610.15161.title: On Chow and Picard groups of Richardson varieties
arxiv:2610.15161.summary: We show that if $\Pi \subseteq G/P$ is a projected Richardson variety, then the degree map $\mathrm{Pic}(\Pi) \to A_1(\Pi)^\vee$ is injective. Moreover, it is an isomorphism in characteristic zero and in all but finitely many positive characteristics. We conjecture that it is an isomorphism in every characteristic.

arxiv:2610.15169.title: Sparsity and uniformity in dynamical Manin--Mumford problems
arxiv:2610.15169.summary: For endomorphisms of the complex projective plane of a given degree, we prove that the existence of a special curve of bounded degree, in the sense of the dynamical Manin--Mumford conjecture, is confined to a proper algebraic subvariety of the parameter space. This confirms a conjecture of DeMarco and Mavraki in dimension two. For general regular polynomial endomorphisms of $\mathbb A^k$, we obtain a uniform dynamical Manin--Mumford bound outside an exceptional hypersurface.

arxiv:2610.15234.title: Quantum Pick's Theorem in two dimensions
arxiv:2610.15234.summary: Consider an $n$-dimensional sum of the form $S_k=\sum{q^{f({\bf z})}}$ over lattice points ${\bf z}$ which lie in $K{\mathcal P}$, the $K$ scaling of an $n$-dimensional rational polytope $\mathcal P$. We formulate a conjecture on the structure of $S_K$ considered for $K$ prime, as a power series in $h=q-1$ modulo the $K^{th}$ cyclotomic polynomial, and in particular the existence of a decomposition in powers of the Gauss sum $\mathbb G$, up to the $n^{th}$, whose coefficients are almost independent of $K$, where the leading coefficient is related to the volume of $\mathcal P$ and the coefficient of ${\mathbb G}^r$ has contributions from the codimension $r$ skeleton of $\mathcal P$. The…

arxiv:2610.15253.title: Stabilizers and maximal subgroups of topological full groups
arxiv:2610.15253.summary: We study closed-set stabilizers in topological full groups of minimal effective ample groupoids with Cantor unit space. For almost finite or purely infinite groupoids, we extend the maximal stabilizer theorem of Grigorchuk and Vorobets to every subgroup containing the commutator subgroup. For a nonempty closed nowhere dense set, maximality of its stabilizer is equivalent to minimality of its stabilizer action, minimality of the regular reduction, and primeness of a canonical wide open subgroupoid.

arxiv:2610.15261.title: Some Remarks on Regular Sequences and Complete Intersections
arxiv:2610.15261.summary: We give an ideal in a polynomial ring in three variables, generated by three elements and having height equal to three, but for which no permutation of its generators is a regular sequence. We prove that in a polynomial ring over an infinite field, an ideal of height n generated by n polynomials, always admits a set of n generators, for which any permutation is a regular sequence.

arxiv:2610.15265.title: Asymptotics of Random-Lattice Enumeration: Beyond HKZ via Dense Sublattices
arxiv:2610.15265.summary: To bridge the gap between worst-case and heuristic analyses of lattice enumeration, we study the sizes of (unpruned) enumeration trees on $n$-dimensional Haar-random lattices. Writing $n^{cn+o(n)}$ for the tree size at the shortest vector radius, we investigate the asymptotic scaling of $c$, and which bases minimize it. For quasi-HKZ bases, we rigorously analyze the random-lattice HKZ geometry and establish $c=1/(2e)\approx 0.1839$.

arxiv:2610.15266.title: The a-number of the Serre-type maximal curves of Abd\'on-Bezerra-Quoos
arxiv:2610.15266.summary: For every prime power $q$, we determine the $a$-number of the Serre-type maximal curves $X(q,n)$: $y^{q^2}-y=x^{(q^n+1)/(q+1)}$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q^{2n}}$, $n\ge 3$ odd, introduced by Abd\'on, Bezerra and Quoos as a generalization of Serre's curve $y^4+y=x^3$ over $\mathbb{F}_{64}$. The Weierstrass semigroup at the unique point at infinity gives an explicit basis of holomorphic differentials, on which the Cartier operator acts by monomials; this reduces the $a$-number to a lattice-point count, which we evaluate in closed form.

arxiv:2610.15269.title: Tuza's Conjecture for Graphs of Maximum Degree at Most 10
arxiv:2610.15269.summary: For a finite simple graph $G$, let $\nu(G)$ be the maximum number of pairwise edge disjoint triangles and $\tau(G)$ the minimum number of edges meeting every triangle. Tuza conjectured in 1981 that every such $G$ satisfies $\tau(G) \le 2 \nu(G).$ We prove the conjecture for the class of graphs with $\Delta\le10.$

arxiv:2610.15276.title: A note on stability conditions on product-quotient surfaces
arxiv:2610.15276.summary: Let $X$ be a product-quotient surface, which is by definition a minimal resolution of $(C_1\times C_2)/G$, where $C_i$ are smooth curves of genus $\geq 2$ and $G$ is a finite group. When $G$ acts freely, we show that every product Bridgeland stability condition on $C_1\times C_2$ induces a tilt stability condition on $X$, and that, if $p_g(X)=q(X)=0$, every tilt stability condition on $X$ arises this way. When $(C_1\times C_2)/G$ has only $A_1$-singularities, we use induction \cite{MMS} and derived McKay correspondence \cite{BKR} to produce non-geometric stability conditions $\sigma_X$ on $X$, which satisfy the full support property and lie in the closure of the geometric chamber.

arxiv:2610.15278.title: Unipotent quotients in compactified Coxeter varieties
arxiv:2610.15278.summary: In this paper, we extend Lusztig's description of quotients of Coxeter varieties by unipotent radicals of parabolic subgroups, to quotients of certain open neighbourhoods in the smooth compactification of Coxeter varieties. These quotients are products of an affine space with a Coxeter variety for an associated Levi quotient, and this result holds uniformly for any connected reductive group over a finite field. As an application, we prove a conjecture of Wang computing the invariants, under the action of unipotent subgroups, of the cohomology of the Deligne-Lusztig coverings of Coxeter varieties.

arxiv:2610.15288.title: The Norm Spectrum of Barnes-Wall Lattices Below Twice the Minimum
arxiv:2610.15288.summary: Let $\Lambda_m$ be the Barnes-Wall lattice of dimension $2^m$, normalized to have minimum squared norm $d_m:=2^{m-1}$. We determine its complete norm spectrum strictly between $d_m$ and $2d_m$, proving that, for every integer $m\ge1$, $\{\|x\|^2:x\in\Lambda_m,\ d_m<\|x\|^2<2d_m\}=\{2d_m-2^j:j\in\mathbb Z,\ \lceil m/2\rceil\le j\le m-2\}$. In particular, the norm spectrum in this interval is nonempty for $m\ge4$.
arxiv:2610.15288.authors: Yuhang Cao, Sihuang Hu, Hexiang Huang, Mengrui Yang

arxiv:2610.15293.title: A note on the logarithmic exponent of Ramsey number $r(4,t)$
arxiv:2610.15293.summary: In this short note, we point out that the recent lower bounds for off-diagonal Ramsey numbers $r(s,t)$ with fixed $s\ge 5$, together with the recent proof of the Ajtai--Erd\H{o}s--Koml\'os--Szemer\'edi independence conjecture, imply \[ r(4,t)=\frac{t^3}{(\log t)^{2+o(1)}}. \] This note is solely for informal circulation and will not be submitted for publication.

arxiv:2610.15320.title: Quadratic polynomials preserving free infinite divisibility
arxiv:2610.15320.summary: We characterize non-commutative polynomials of degree 2 which preserve free infinite divisibility as self-adjoint Lie polynomials of degree 2. This extends previous results which characterized homogeneous quadratic forms only. The proof is based on an involution of colored noncrossing partitions cancelling many terms; positive definiteness of the remaining terms is established by an explicit operator model on Fock space.
arxiv:2610.15320.authors: Wiktor Ejsmont, Franz Lehner, Mihai Popa, Kamil Szpojankowski

arxiv:2610.15344.title: Type $B$- and $C$- trigonometric weight functions
arxiv:2610.15344.summary: We introduce and study trigonometric weight functions of type $B$ and type $C$ arising from integrable lattice models. These functions give $q$-deformations of the factorial $K$-theoretic Schur $P$- and $Q$-functions of Ikeda and Naruse, with the $P$-functions specialized to the type $B$ case. We realize them as specializations of partition functions of a six-vertex model with triangular boundary conditions and derive their algebraic properties using the Yang-Baxter equation and properties of the $R$- and $K$-matrices.

arxiv:2610.15347.title: A categorical approach to the set-theoretic Yang-Baxter equation
arxiv:2610.15347.summary: We investigate set-theoretic solutions of the Yang--Baxter equation from a categorical perspective. The paper has two main objectives. On the one hand, several existing constructions and classification results in the literature are recast in categorical terms, thereby showing that certain hypotheses previously imposed on such solutions are in fact superfluous.
arxiv:2610.15347.authors: A. L. Agore, A. Chirvasitu, G. Militaru

arxiv:2610.15348.title: Supersaturation thresholds for expanded color-critical graphs
arxiv:2610.15348.summary: For a $k$-uniform hypergraph $L$, let $h_L(n,q)$ be the minimum number of copies of $L$ in an $n$-vertex $k$-graph with $\mathrm{ex}(n,L)+q$ edges. Let $t_L(n,q)$ be the minimum number of copies obtained by adding $q$ edges to an extremal $L$-free $k$-graph. A graph is color-critical if deleting a suitable edge decreases its chromatic number.
arxiv:2610.15348.authors: Liping Zhang, Qinghai Liu, Yanmei Hong, Jinze Hu

arxiv:2610.15370.title: A Four-by-Four Obstruction to Polynomial Removal for Ordered Binary Matrices
arxiv:2610.15370.summary: We exhibit a fixed $4\times 4$ binary matrix with no polynomial induced ordered removal bound. At depth $h\geq 1$, let $m=2^h$. Our explicit host has order $(14h+2)m$, exactly $2m^6+\frac{1}{2}(m-2)m^5$ induced copies, and exact editing distance $m^2$ cells.

arxiv:2610.15383.title: Maximum index of unbalanced signed graphs without a positive odd cycle
arxiv:2610.15383.summary: Let $\mathcal{C}_{r}^+$ be the set of all balanced signed graphs with underlying graphs $C_r$. A signed graph is called $\mathcal{C}_{r}^+$-free if it contains no subgraph isomorphic to any member of $\mathcal{C}_{r}^+$. In this paper, we characterize the extremal graphs that achieve the maximum index among all $\mathcal{C}_{2k+1}^+$-free unbalanced signed graphs of order $n$ when $k\ge 2$ and $n\ge 187k$.
arxiv:2610.15383.authors: Li Ma, Linfeng Xie, Xiaogang Liu

arxiv:2610.15406.title: One boundary, infinitely geometries
arxiv:2610.15406.summary: Let $N$ be a 3-dimensional integral homology sphere. We prove the existence of a sequence of 4-dimensional topologically negatively curved manifolds $M_k$, $k=1,2,\dots$, satisfying the following: (1) all aspherical manifolds $M_k$ have the same universal cover $U_N$ depending only on $N$; (2) all fundamental groups $\pi_1(M_k)$ are hyperbolic and share the same Gromov boundary $X_N$ depending only on $N$; (3) the groups $\pi_1(M_k)$ represent infinitely many distinct quasi-isometry classes. The last conclusion, which represents the new feature, shows that negatively curved geometries in dimension 4 exhibit substantially richer structure than those in dimension 3.

arxiv:2610.15416.title: On strongly minimal asymptotic bases of order $h$ generated by powers of $2$
arxiv:2610.15416.summary: Let $h\geq2$ be an integer and let $\mathbb{N}_0=W_1\cup\cdots\cup W_h$ be a partition into infinite sets. For $W\subseteq\mathbb{N}_0$, let $A(W)$ denote the set of all finite nonempty sums of distinct powers $2^w$ with $w\in W$. We give a necessary and sufficient condition for $A=A(W_1)\cup\cdots\cup A(W_h)$ to be a strongly minimal asymptotic basis of order $h$.

arxiv:2610.15421.title: General Constructions of Permutation-Fair Dice
arxiv:2610.15421.summary: Suppose that each of $n$ players rolls a different die and the players are ordered by their rolls.
