Can the dice use disjoint labels such that ties are impossible, while all $n!$ orders remain equally likely? We give two general constructions of such dice and solve some related problems.
arxiv:2610.15421.authors: Tom\'a\v{s} Gaven\v{c}iak, Bernhard Haeupler, V\'aclav Rozho\v{n}

arxiv:2610.15424.title: Every n points in the plane contain (m1 + o(1)) n points with no unit distance
arxiv:2610.15424.summary: Let $f(n)$ be the largest integer such that every set of $n$ points in the plane contains $f(n)$ points no two at distance $1$, and let $m_1$ be the supremum of the upper densities of Lebesgue measurable planar sets with no two points at distance $1$. Larman and Rogers observed that $f(n) \ge m_1 n$. We prove that $f(n)/n \to m_1$; that is, $f(n) = (m_1 + o(1))n$.

arxiv:2610.15434.title: Spectral G\aa rding Elliptic Equations
arxiv:2610.15434.summary: We study spectral G\aa rding elliptic equations on compact K\"ahler manifolds. Smooth solvability is equivalent to the existence of a smooth representative in the admissible domain. The concavity theorem for ideal G\aa rding polynomials gives a fixed concave formulation to which Sz\'ekelyhidi's second-order argument applies in every degree $2\le d\le n$, extending Lin's top-degree solvability theorem.

arxiv:2610.15447.title: Tur\'an Numbers of Linear Stars and Expanded Trees
arxiv:2610.15447.summary: For an $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal H$, let $\ex_r(n,\mathcal H)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $r$-uniform hypergraph containing no copy of $\mathcal H$. The $r$-uniform expansion $T^{(r)}$ of a tree $T$ is obtained by adding $r-2$ new vertices to each edge, with the added sets pairwise disjoint and disjoint from $V(T)$. In particular, the expansion of $K_{1,k}$ is the linear star $\mathcal L_k^r$, whose $k$ edges intersect pairwise in a single common vertex.

arxiv:2610.15448.title: The First Modular Zhu Algebra of $L(\frac12,0)_F$ in Characteristic Seven
arxiv:2610.15448.summary: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $7$, and let $V=L(\frac12,0)_F$. For the degree-four singular vector $q=(L(-2)^2-2L(-4))\mathbf1$ in the universal vacuum vertex operator algebra $\bar V$, set $V_q=\bar V/I(q)$. We prove that the natural quotient map induces an isomorphism $A_1(V_q)\cong A_1(V)\cong F[T]/(T(T-4)(T-5))\cong F^3$.

arxiv:2610.15466.title: Temporal invariance of evolutionary entropy and comparative demographic analysis
arxiv:2610.15466.summary: Does evolutionary entropy depend on the width of the age classes used to describe a population? We show that the apparent dependence on temporal resolution is a consequence of the loss of information about reproductive timing within discrete classes. When this information is retained, corresponding continuous and discrete representations yield the same cycle entropy, generation time, evolutionary entropy, and reproductive potential in a common unit of time.

arxiv:2610.15468.title: FirstFit coloring process of random bipartite graphs and an online coloring lower bound in the random order model
arxiv:2610.15468.summary: FirstFit colors each arriving vertex with the smallest positive integer absent from its previously colored neighborhood. We prove that this rule can require $n^{\Omega(1)}$ many colors on certain bipartite graph of $n$ vertices even when the vertices arrive in a uniformly random order. This refutes the conjecture of Bosek, Gutowski, Laso\'{n}, and Przyby\l{}o [BGLP24] that FirstFit uses a polylogarithmic expected number of colors on every bipartite graph in the random order model.

arxiv:2610.15469.title: Bimodule duality and Artin's problem for skew field extensions
arxiv:2610.15469.summary: Emil Artin asked whether the left and right dimensions of an extension of skew fields must agree. Cohn and Schofield gave counterexamples through elaborate constructions. It has been a long-standing open question whether there is any division ring, infinite-dimensional over its center, for which the left and right indices agree whenever at least one is finite.

arxiv:2610.15473.title: A noetherian Hopf algebra has bijective antipode
arxiv:2610.15473.summary: We prove that a Hopf algebra over an arbitrary field has a bijective antipode if either its left or right regular module has finite uniform dimension. In particular, this solves Skryabin's conjecture, posed in 2006, that every noetherian Hopf algebra has a bijective antipode. Starting from Skryabin's injectivity theorem for weakly finite Hopf algebras, we associate to each finite-dimensional subcoalgebra an essential left ideal of common denominators that is also a right coideal in the antipode image.

arxiv:2610.15485.title: Dimension of affine iterated function systems on $\mathbb{R}^d$
arxiv:2610.15485.summary: Let $\{f_i(x)=M_ix+a_i\}_{i\in I}$ be an affine iterated function system on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with attractor $\Lambda$, and let $\mu$ be an associated self-affine measure. Assume that the $M_i$ generate a Zariski dense subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb{R})$. Under the strong open set condition, we show that $\dim_{\mathrm{H}}\Lambda$ equals the affinity dimension and that $\dim_{\mathrm{H}}\mu$ equals the Lyapunov dimension.
arxiv:2610.15485.authors: Jialun Li, Wenyu Pan, Zhiyuan Zhang

arxiv:2610.15487.title: Rationality of Kontsevich moduli of stable maps, and their Galois descents
arxiv:2610.15487.summary: Let k be a field and X be a geometrically rational variety over k. We investigate the Kontsevich moduli spaces of genus zero, stable maps with curve classes of low degree on X over k, and define their twisted Galois descents. We study the k-rationality of these spaces in detail when X is a projective space/Severi Brauer variety and when X is moduli of genus zero n-marked points.

arxiv:2610.15521.title: Crystals and the parabolicity conjecture
arxiv:2610.15521.summary: These notes introduce crystals and crystalline Dieudonn\'e theory through the example of abelian varieties. After discussing $p$-divisible groups, $F$-isocrystals, slope filtrations, and overconvergence, we explain the parabolicity theorem for $F$-isocrystals and some of its applications to monodromy and Hecke orbits. Two appendices formulate research projects on isocrystals over formal schemes and on monodromy beyond the constant-slope setting.

arxiv:2610.15534.title: A chain theorem for planar PM-compact bricks
arxiv:2610.15534.summary: A connected graph $G$ is matching covered if it contains at least one edge and every edge belongs to some perfect matching of $G$. A matching covered graph is a brick if it is 3-connected and after removing any two vertices, the resulting graph has a perfect matching. Bricks are the building blocks of matching covered graphs.
arxiv:2610.15534.authors: Yaxian zhang, Qiuli Li, Fuliang Lu

arxiv:2610.15535.title: Hull Variation in Symplectic Linear Codes
arxiv:2610.15535.summary: We study the variation of hull dimensions of symplectic linear codes under equivalence transformations preserving the symplectic distance. For a symplectic linear code $C$, we introduce an even-valued invariant $\Delta(C)$, which depends only on the equivalence class of $C$. This invariant can be expressed as the generic rank of an associated space of alternating matrices and, equivalently, as twice a corresponding matroid matching number.
arxiv:2610.15535.authors: Kanat Abdukhalikov, Somi Gupta, Duy Ho

arxiv:2610.15539.title: Tuza's Conjecture under an Edge-Count Condition
arxiv:2610.15539.summary:
For a graph $G$, let $
u(G)$ denote the maximum number of pairwise edge-disjoint triangles and let $	au(G)$ denote the minimum number of edges meeting every triangle. Tuza's conjecture asserts that $	au(G)\le 2
u(G)$ for every graph $G$. We first note that Tuza's conjecture is equivalent to the following statement: for every fixed $c\ge 0$, if $G$ is a sufficiently large $n$-vertex graph with $e(G)\ge n^2/4-cn$, then $	au(G)\le 2
u(G)$.

arxiv:2610.15550.title: Topological Classification of Univariate Sparse Polynomials via Tropical Geometry
arxiv:2610.15550.summary: We give the topological classification of some simplest univariate complex fewnomials, and find tropical fans of the fewnomial strata with each topological type. Specifically, for the support $ A=\{d,d+1,d+2,d+3,d+4\},\quad d\geq3, $ we classify the topological equivalence classes of polynomials having two critical values of ramification type $(2,2)$. There is one class for odd $d$ and two classes for even $d$.

arxiv:2610.15551.title: K_1 of matroids
arxiv:2610.15551.summary: Using the geometric realization spectral sequence and the Serre spectral sequence, we compute $K_1(\operatorname{Mat}_*)$, the first K-theory group of the proto-exact category of pointed matroids, answering a question of Jun, Sistko and Wright.

arxiv:2610.15592.title: The Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture after OpenAI
arxiv:2610.15592.summary: We provide a simplified and more human-friendly version of the proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture recently given by OpenAI. No originality is claimed.

arxiv:2610.15599.title: Beyond Amoeba Boundaries
arxiv:2610.15599.summary: We construct smooth plane curves whose logarithmic contours are smooth and embedded but strictly larger than their amoeba boundaries. The examples include connected irreducible curves, disconnected unions of nonlinear components with two-dimensional amoebas, nested families with arbitrarily many components, and a uniform construction realizing every positive genus. Exact critical-locus calculations distinguish the boundary-producing folds from compact or noncompact contour branches lying in the amoeba interior.

arxiv:2610.15607.title: Beyond Harnack Amoeba Boundaries
arxiv:2610.15607.summary: We construct smooth irreducible plane curves whose complete amoeba contour is a smooth embedded curve equal to the amoeba boundary, although the curves are not torically equivalent to simple Harnack curves. Finite monomial coverings yield explicit infinite families with higher logarithmic multiplicity and nonmaximal normalized amoeba area. We classify the Newton polygons admitting such covering constructions through their exponent lattices, give an exact connectedness criterion in terms of monodromy, and treat primitive polygons by a separate phase-sensitive construction.

arxiv:2610.15635.title: Covering powers of cycles with equivalence subgraphs
arxiv:2610.15635.summary: Let $C_n^k$ denote the $k$th power of the cycle $C_n$. The equivalence covering number $\operatorname{eq}(G)$, studied by Alon, is the minimum number of equivalence subgraphs needed to cover all edges of $G$. King conjectured that $\operatorname{eq}(C_n^k)=\Omega(k)$ for sufficiently large $n$ relative to $k$.

arxiv:2610.15643.title: A trace lower bound for totally positive units in $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p)^+$ and its application to fusion category
arxiv:2610.15643.summary: Let $p = 4q + 1$ be a prime integer, where $q$ is an odd prime. Let $L = \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p)^+$ denote the maximal totally real subfield of the $p$-th cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p)$. In this paper, we prove that if $U_L^+=U_L^2$ (i.e., every totally positive unit is a square in $L$), then for any non-trivial subfield $K \subseteq L$ and any non-trivial totally positive unit $\varepsilon \in U_K^+$, the absolute trace satisfies the sharp lower bound $\Tr_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(\varepsilon) \ge p - 4$.

arxiv:2610.15648.title: Post-critically finite polynomials in characteristic $p$
arxiv:2610.15648.summary: It follows from the compactness of the connectedness locus that the locus of PCF polynomials in the moduli space of polynomials of degree d (at least 2) over the complex number is a countable union of zero-dimensional subvarieties. Over fields of characteristic p the analogous claim is certainly false, so it is natural to ask how large the components of the PCF locus can be. We show that the components of the PCF locus in the moduli space of polynomials of degree d over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0 have dimension at most d/p and that this bound is sharp, in the strong sense that for every p and d there are infinitely many distinct PCF components whose dimension is the…

arxiv:2610.15653.title: Continuum-many discontinuous actions of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{Q})$ on manifolds
arxiv:2610.15653.summary: For any $n\geq 1$, we construct a continuum of non-conjugate actions by homeomorphisms of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{Q})$ on the $n$-sphere $S^{n}$ that do not extend to a continuous action of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{R})$. We do this by adapting a blow-up construction of Bowden and Mann. We motivate studying these actions and note down some related observations.

arxiv:2610.15668.title: Geodesic Models for Loop Spaces on Riemannian Manifolds
arxiv:2610.15668.summary: A topological group, defined in terms of ``composable minimal geodesics'' is constructed and shown to be homotopy equivalent to the pointed loop space of a path-connected, simply connected Riemannian manifold $M$ of positive convexity radius. This construction is analogous to John Milnor's free group model for the pointed loop space of a connected simplicial complex. Related models built from composable minimal geodesics are also obtained for the free loop space of $M$ and for the space of maps from any finite two-dimensional CW-complex into $M$.
arxiv:2610.15668.authors: Abbas Bahri, Fred Cohen, Moncef Ghazel, Sadok Kallel

arxiv:2610.15670.title: The entry-exit function and nilpotent corrections in multidimensional slow-fast systems
arxiv:2610.15670.summary: We study multidimensional entry-exit phenomena in slow-fast systems whose fast linearization contains a nilpotent component. We show that the classical spectral balance still determines the exit point as $\varepsilon \to 0$, however the nilpotent component induces an algebraic amplification invisible to the spectrum, producing a $\varepsilon|\log\varepsilon|$-shift of the exit point for $0 <\varepsilon \ll 1$. We further extend the analysis to systems with several spectral branches and show that mode dominance follows a hierarchical, lexicographic selection principle: accumulated spectral growth determines the leading order, while the nilpotent component resolves degeneracies between…

arxiv:2610.15679.title: Bipartite edge frustration of nut graphs: proofs and constructions
arxiv:2610.15679.summary: The bipartite edge frustration of a graph $G$, $\varphi(G)$, is the minimum number of edges that must be removed from $G$ to obtain a graph that is bipartite. Core graphs are singular graphs on $2$ or more vertices, for which the kernel of the adjacency matrix contains a full eigenvector. A nut graph is a core graph of nullity one.

arxiv:2610.15686.title: **Winding number forces universal synchronisation**
arxiv:2610.15686.summary: We prove that two completely different oscillators synchronise through arbitrarily weak reciprocal impulses. Any two planar oscillators with hyperbolic attracting limit cycles and equal natural periods lock stably one-to-one under translation impulses with generic directions and a suitable range of positive strength ratios, whatever their vector fields, limit cycles and transverse contraction rates. The mechanism is topological: the winding of the asymptotic phase gradient forces phase advances and delays, and the relative winding number of an effective impulse field gives lower bounds on attracting and unstable locked states.

arxiv:2610.15688.title: Total Cohomology of Hilbert schemes of Orbisurfaces I: Reduction to Stacky Loci
arxiv:2610.15688.summary: We generalize Nakajima's theory of Hilbert schemes of points on surfaces to Hilbert schemes of points on \textit{orbisurfaces}, and obtain initial factorization based on stratification by stabilizers. While the usual formula is retained for the trivial stabilizer stratum and for those strata of codimension $1$, genuine difficulties arise with stacky points strata. In the local picture of an isolated stacky point, the theory reduce to the study of $\Quot^\bfv[\CC^2/G]$ for a \textit{small} finite subgroup of $GL_2(\CC)$.

arxiv:2610.15698.title: Symplectic four-manifolds and hyperbolic $\pi$-orbifolds
arxiv:2610.15698.summary: We construct closed symplectic 4-manifolds admitting the structure of hyperbolic $\pi$-orbifold, addressing LeBrun's conjecture. Our simplest example has Euler characteristic $304$, is tessellated by $64$ copies of the right-angled hyperbolic $120$-cell and admits a four-fold branched covering over a product of two surfaces of genus $4$.

arxiv:2610.15717.title: A Smooth Autonomous Flow with Exponential Mixing on the Three-Torus
arxiv:2610.15717.summary: We construct a smooth autonomous divergence-free vector field on $\mathbb{T}^3$ whose flow is exponentially mixing with respect to Lebesgue measure. This answers an open question about smooth autonomous exponential mixing in three dimensions. Starting from an exponentially mixing Anosov suspension flow, we perform surgery near four periodic orbits and show that the resulting manifold is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{T}^3$.

arxiv:2610.15720.title: Multivariate stable mixing local limit theorem for intermittent diffeomorphisms and flows
arxiv:2610.15720.summary: We prove mixing local limit theorems for dynamical systems in the superdiffusive regime where there is convergence to a multivariate stable law (including the nonstandard domain of the central limit theorem). We apply our results to d-dimensional observables for intermittent maps and solenoids, as well as intermittent semiflows and flows.
arxiv:2610.15720.authors: Ian Melbourne, Fran\c{c}oise P\`{e}ne, Dalia Terhesiu

arxiv:2610.15736.title: Remarks on the disjoint minimal graphs conjecture
arxiv:2610.15736.summary: It is known that there can be at most 3 disjoint nontrivial minimal graphs in R^3 with 0 boundary values, and conjectured that there can be at most 2. We explore properties that the graphs would have if there were 3.

arxiv:2610.15777.title: Minimal Product Sets in Finite Metacyclic Groups
arxiv:2610.15777.summary: Minimum product-set problems ask how small a product of two subsets of prescribed cardinalities can be in a finite group. Although the problem is completely understood for finite abelian groups, exact results in the nonabelian setting are available only for particular classes. We determine the minimum product-set function $\mu_G$ for every finite metacyclic group, without assuming that the relevant cyclic extension splits.

arxiv:2610.15785.title: Translational tilings by axis-parallel polygonal sets
arxiv:2610.15785.summary: The periodic tiling conjecture asserts that if a bounded set $\Omega\subset \mathbb R^d$ of finite measure tiles $\mathbb R^d$ by translations, then it admits at least one fully periodic tiling. This conjecture was proved to hold in $\mathbb R$ by Lagarias and Wang, and was recently disproved by Greenfeld and Tao in sufficiently high dimensions. Its discrete analogue in $\mathbb Z^2$ was proved by Bhattacharya, whereas the conjecture in $\mathbb R^2$ remains open.
arxiv:2610.15785.authors: Jaume de Dios Pont, Jan Greb\'ik, Rachel Greenfeld, Jos\'e Madrid

arxiv:2610.15792.title: A Multiplicative Horn Obstruction to the Unitary Categorification of a Rank-Twelve Modular Datum
arxiv:2610.15792.summary: We study the rank-twelve potential modular datum denoted $12^{39,406}_{4,1276.}$ in the low-rank classification tables. Its global dimension is $(1287+351\sqrt{13})/2$, and its fusion ring agrees with that of the known rank-twelve Haagerup modular category. The datum satisfies the modular relations, has nonnegative integral Verlinde coefficients, and passes several familiar genus-one necessary tests.

arxiv:2610.15803.title: A Sharp Bound for the Second Betti Number of Hyperk\"ahler Sixfolds
arxiv:2610.15803.summary: Let $X$ be a smooth compact irreducible hyperk\"ahler manifold of dimension six. We prove that the second Betti number satisfies $b_2(X) \le 23$. Furthermore, we show that the third cohomology vanishes whenever $b_2(X) \ge 19$, and that all odd cohomology vanishes when $b_2(X) = 23$.
arxiv:2610.15803.authors: Jie Fu, Bin Wang, Shihao Wang, Zhiwei Zheng

arxiv:2610.15817.title: Koszul Duality in an Equivariant Context
arxiv:2610.15817.summary: This article takes steps to show that an equivariant version of the well known phenomena of Koszul Duality can be formulated in a manner not considered prior: via dg (co)algebra valued functors on the orbit category. As such techniques used in this article mix traditional and modern categorical methods in homotopy theory.

arxiv:2610.15822.title: Equivariant formality for rational $\C_{p^k}$-spaces
arxiv:2610.15822.summary: In this paper, we discuss equivariant formality for spaces equipped with a primary cyclic group action. We study the behavior of equivariant formality with some topological constructions. The algebraic complexity needs to deal with injectivity.
arxiv:2610.15822.authors: Rekha Santhanam, Bittu Singh, Soumyadip Thandar

arxiv:2610.15826.title: The theory of $(\lambda,\mu)$-fold factorizations of groups
arxiv:2610.15826.summary: Motivated by the recent study of $\lambda$-fold near-factorizations of finite groups by Kreher, Li, and Stinson (Designs, Codes and Cryptography, 2026), we introduce and systematically investigate $(\lambda,\mu)$-fold factorizations of finite groups, with particular emphasis on the abelian case. These structures form a natural relaxation of $\lambda$-fold near-factorizations and encompass several related families that have previously been studied in different contexts. We establish the foundational theory of $(\lambda,\mu)$-fold factorizations, provide two general constructions, and prove several nonexistence results for finite abelian groups.
arxiv:2610.15826.authors: Donald L. Kreher, Shuxing Li, Douglas R. Stinson

arxiv:2610.15831.title: Open substacks preserving moduli spaces: classification and bounds
arxiv:2610.15831.summary: For a smooth locally reductive stack admitting an adequate moduli space, we show that there are finitely many open substacks preserving the adequate moduli space, and give a complete classification of such opens. For $\mathbb{G}_m$-actions, this becomes an explicit description in terms of the codimension-one Bialynicki-Birula strata. Moreover, for a stable adequate moduli space, we show that the number of preserving opens are bounded by 3 raised to the relative Picard rank.

arxiv:2610.15849.title: Universal Shift Congruences for Weighted Permutation Sequences
arxiv:2610.15849.summary: The involution numbers $1,1,2,4,10,26,\ldots$ repeat modulo $3$, $5$ and $7$. We explain this, and many similar patterns, by one rule. Many sequences count permutations in which every cycle of length $m$ carries a weight $w_m$ (involutions, derangements, "sets of lists", and many others in the OEIS).

arxiv:2610.15860.title: A note on the Slater$\unicode{x2013}$V\'elez permutation
arxiv:2610.15860.summary: We study the greedy sequence of positive integers introduced by Slater and V\'elez. They proved that it is a permutation of the positive integers but left open whether its sequence of consecutive absolute differences is also a permutation. We prove that it is.

arxiv:2610.15868.title: Higher-order nonhomomorphicity under affine restrictions
arxiv:2610.15868.summary: We study the behavior of the $k$-th-order nonhomomorphicity of Boolean functions under restriction to affine subspaces. For odd $k\ge3$ and $0\le t<n$, we introduce the $t$-restriction $k$-th-order nonhomomorphicity $P_{k,t}(f)$, defined as the minimum of $P_k(f_{\mid A})$ over affine spaces of codimension at most $t$. For a direct sum of $m$ monomials of degrees at least two, we determine $P_{k,t}$ exactly.
arxiv:2610.15868.authors: Serge Feukoua, Ana S\u{a}l\u{a}gean, Pantelimon St\u{a}nic\u{a}

arxiv:2610.15887.title: Hilbert's Nullstellensatz and the real Nullstellensatz for modules and sheaves
arxiv:2610.15887.summary: We prove the geometric halves of Hilbert's Nullstellensatz and of the real Nullstellensatz for submodules of finitely generated modules and for coherent sheaves, complementing our earlier result that semiprime (resp. real) submodules are intersections of prime (resp. real prime) submodules. First, we pass from prime to maximal submodules: over a Jacobson ring, a prime submodule $P$ of $M$ is an intersection of maximal submodules whenever $M/P$ is a torsionless $R/(P:M)$-module, in particular whenever $M/P$ is finitely generated (the latter case is due to Maani Shirazi and Sharif). Consequently, if $R$ is a finitely generated algebra over an algebraically closed field and $M$ is finitely…

arxiv:2610.15909.title: Two Linear Programs are Better than One
arxiv:2610.15909.summary: The extension complexity $\operatorname{xc}(P)$ of a polytope $P$ is the minimum number of facets of a polytope that projects onto it. Motivated by the complexity of neural networks, Hertrich and Loho introduced the virtual extension complexity $\operatorname{vxc}(P)$ of a polytope $P$, which is the minimum of $\operatorname{xc}(Q) + \operatorname{xc}(R)$ among all polytopes $Q$ and $R$ such that $P+Q=R$. We show the following results pertaining to virtual extension complexity.
arxiv:2610.15909.authors: Alexander E. Black, Christoph Hertrich, Stefan Kober, Georg Loho

arxiv:2610.15926.title: The inf spectrum of moduli space
arxiv:2610.15926.summary: Given a surface of genus $g \geq 2$, its inf spectrum is the ordered multiset of inf lengths of curves on the surface, the infimum being over all hyperbolic metrics. We show that the inf spectrum has exponential growth with coefficients that only depend on g, improving the earlier double exponential upper bound. The proof involves developing a number of tools including the process of "thickening" a surface and the notion of model surfaces.
arxiv:2610.15926.authors: Ara Basmajian, Sayantika Mondal, Hugo Parlier

arxiv:2610.15942.title: Nonlinear Feedback Control in High Dimensions using the Polynomial-Polynomial Regulator
arxiv:2610.15942.summary: We consider the problem of computing Taylor approximations to the optimal feedback law and value function for infinite-horizon finite-dimensional nonlinear optimal control problem---also known as Al'brekht's method. The scalability of existing Al'brekht-based approaches to computing approximate solutions to the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation associated with the optimal control problem has been severely limited by computational resources. The computational time issue has been partially mitigated by recent works leveraging tensor-structure to develop efficient numerical methods.

arxiv:2610.15971.title: The $\lambda$-chain condition of a finite partially ordered set
arxiv:2610.15971.summary: It is shown that a certain finite partially ordered set arising from an algebra with straightening laws on a finite distributive lattice satisfies the $\lambda$-chain condition. In addition, its application to commutative algebra is briefly discussed.

arxiv:2610.15981.title: A Sharp Lower Bound for Integral Menger Curvature
arxiv:2610.15981.summary: We prove that round circles $C_L$ are the unique minimisers of integral Menger curvature among embedded closed $C^1$ curves $\gamma$ of prescribed length $L$ for every $p\geq 2$, i.e. $M_p(C_L) \leq M_p(\gamma)$, with equality if and only if $\gamma$ parametrises a round circle. The proof combines a three-point symmetrisation, an analysis of diagonal truncations, and the periodic Wirtinger inequality.

arxiv:2610.15984.title: Stability of Diophantine Minimal Foliations in Arbitrary Codimension
arxiv:2610.15984.summary: We generalize Moser's stability theorem for minimal hypersurface foliations to arbitrary codimension. Let $\mathbb{T}^N=\mathbb{R}^N/\mathbb{Z}^N$ be the standard torus, and let $P\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be an $m$-plane satisfying a Diophantine condition relative to $\mathbb{Z}^N$. We prove that, under every sufficiently small smooth $\mathbb{Z}^N$-periodic perturbation of the Euclidean metric, the affine foliation of $\mathbb{T}^N$ induced by $P$ persists as a smoothly conjugate foliation by minimal $m$-dimensional submanifolds.

arxiv:2610.16001.title: Dot actions and Hessenberg spaces for dihedral groups
arxiv:2610.16001.summary: Splines on Weyl groups model the equivariant cohomology of regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties, and the natural group action on them encodes the monodromy action. The resulting representations are of great interest in algebraic combinatorics for their connections to Hecke algebra characters, LLT polynomials, and chromatic symmetric functions. We study the analogous construction for dihedral groups, which in general have no underlying geometry.
arxiv:2610.16001.authors: Jonathan Boretsky, Reuven Hodges, Nathan Lesnevich, Tyrrell McAllister, Joseph Pappe

arxiv:2610.16017.title: On infinite knot families with the same HOMFLYPT polynomial
arxiv:2610.16017.summary: In this paper, we focus on the examples constructed by Kanenobu and provide new family knots with the same HOMFLYPT polynomial invariants, which are distinguished by the Kauffman polynomial.

arxiv:2610.16024.title: Uniform Asymptotics for Andrews-Beck Partition Statistics
arxiv:2610.16024.summary: Let $\NT(m,n)$ be the total number of parts in the partitions of $n$ with rank $m$, and let $\MW(m,n)$ be the total number of ones in the partitions of $n$ with crank $m$. Using the uniform generalized-rank estimate of Liu and Zhou, we establish asymptotic formulas for $NT(m,n)$ and $\MW(m,n)$. Put $\beta_n=\pi/\sqrt{6n}$ and $L_n=\log(1/\beta_n)$.

arxiv:2610.16025.title: QPTAS for Max Weight Independent Set in Graphs with Strongly Edge-Sublinear Separators
arxiv:2610.16025.summary: A hereditary graph class has strongly edge-sublinear separators if, for some constant $0 \leqslant b < 1$, every graph in the class with $m$ edges admits a balanced separator of size $\mathcal O(m^b)$. We show that Max Weight Independent Set (MWIS) admits a deterministic quasipolynomial-time approximation scheme (QPTAS) on every such class. In particular, this applies to graphs excluding any fixed graph as an induced minor, by a separator theorem of Korhonen and Lokshtanov [SODA 2024].

arxiv:2610.16056.title: Loop Fundamental Quandles: A Geometric Generalization of the Knot Quandle
arxiv:2610.16056.summary: The knot quandle, introduced independently by Joyce and Matveev, admits a geometric description in terms of nooses. Motivated by this description, we introduce the \textit{loop fundamental quandle} $LQ(X,A,\ast)$ of a pair $(X,A)$ with a fixed base point $\ast\in X$. Its elements are represented by pairs consisting of a loop in $A$ and a path joining the base point of the loop to the fixed base point $\ast$.

arxiv:2610.16080.title: The moduli space of cubic surfaces and its orbifold fundamental group
arxiv:2610.16080.summary: We find a new presentation of the orbifold fundamental group of the moduli space of cubic surfaces, based on the Artin group of the Petersen graph. This group has two well-known quotients, which appear in the simplest possible way: killing the squares resp. sixth powers of our generators yields the Coxeter group $W(E_6)$ resp. a certain arithmetic group in $\operatorname{PU}(1,4)$. Along the way we present a certain central extension by $\mathbb{Z}$, of the genus zero mapping class group with any number of punctures.
arxiv:2610.16080.authors: Daniel Allcock, Tathagata Basak, Eduard Looijenga

arxiv:2610.16094.title: (Super-)fast convergence rates for Chernoff approximations via centered differences and Richardson extrapolation
arxiv:2610.16094.summary: We use centered differences to construct Chernoff families and derive even asymptotic expansions for their iterated products. Richardson extrapolation is then used to cancel polynomial part and thereby raise the convergence order. As illustrations, we apply the construction to uniformly parabolic, Schr\"odinger-type second-order operators and to a third-order dispersive operator, obtaining, at extrapolation depth $m$, the rates $ O(n^{-2m}) $ on the Sobolev scales $H^{2m+\delta}$, $H^{4m}$, and $H^{5m}$, respectively, with arbitrary $\delta>0$.

arxiv:2610.16107.title: Finiteness of planar central configurations of five bodies for all positive masses: On Smale's sixth problem
arxiv:2610.16107.summary: We prove that for every choice of five positive masses the planar five-body problem has only finitely many central configurations up to rotation, translation and scaling. This answers Smale's sixth problem for five bodies. Albouy and Kaloshin proved the statement for all masses outside a closed algebraic subset of codimension two of the mass space.

arxiv:2610.16112.title: Cohen-Lenstra heuristics and vanishing of zeta functions for superelliptic curves over finite fields
arxiv:2610.16112.summary: We prove a Cohen-Lenstra type result commenting on the distribution of class group structures amongst function fields of superelliptic curves over finite fields. We also prove a result commenting on the sparsity of such superelliptic curves whose zeta functions vanish at a fixed complex number. These results are proven via point-counting techniques on certain Hurwitz schemes generalizing techniques of Ellenberg-Venkatesh-Westerland and Ellenberg-Li-Shusterman.

arxiv:2610.16114.title: On Mattila's intersection problem in the plane: sharp dimension and positive measure of rotated difference sets
arxiv:2610.16114.summary: Let \(A,B\subset\R^2\) be nonempty Borel sets. We prove that \[ \dimH(gA-B)\ge\min\{\dimH A+\dimH B,2\} \] for almost all \(g\in\mathrm O(2)\). This bound is sharp in general, and the proof gives a corresponding statement for the lower Hausdorff dimension of convolutions of Frostman measures.
arxiv:2610.16114.authors: Thang Pham, Chun-Yen Shen, Dung The Tran

arxiv:2610.16203.title: A Proof of the Erd\H{o}s Matching Conjecture for Large Matchings via Sharp Tail Probability for Sums of i.i.d. Nonnegative Random Variables
arxiv:2610.16203.summary: We resolve a conjecture of \L{}uczak, Mieczkowska and \v{S}ileikis on the maximal tail probability of sums of independent and identically distributed nonnegative random variables. Specifically, for every integer $k\ge1$ and every $0\le x\le1/k$, we prove \[ \sup_{\mathbb E X_1\le x}\mathbb{P}(X_1+\cdots+X_k\ge1) =\max\{1-(1-x)^k,(kx)^k\}, \] where the supremum is over nonnegative i.i.d.\ random variables $X_1,\ldots,X_k$. We also characterize all maximizing distributions.
arxiv:2610.16203.authors: Cheng Chi, Shuang Sun, Yan Wang

arxiv:2610.16205.title: Stein degree over fields of characteristic zero
arxiv:2610.16205.summary: We show that the Stein degree of horizontal divisors on generalised log Calabi-Yau fibrations or certain vertical divisors of Fano type fibrations over arbitrary fields of characteristic zero is bounded by constants that are independent on the ground field.

arxiv:2610.16230.title: Mixed Hodge structure in the cohomology of moment-angle complexes
arxiv:2610.16230.summary: This work studies the relationship between the multigrading in the cohomology of moment-angle complexes, introduced by V. Buchstaber and T. Panov in their computation of these cohomology groups, and the multigrading in the cohomology of the corresponding complements of coordinate subspace arrangements, arising from the mixed Hodge structure.

arxiv:2610.16235.title: Subgroup Perfect Codes in Bi-Cayley Graphs
arxiv:2610.16235.summary: In this paper, we study perfect codes in bi-Cayley graphs, focusing on when two subgroups $H$ and $K$ of a group G can form a perfect code of the form $H_0 \cup K_1$. We first consider the problem for a general group G and then examine what happens for special classes of groups, particularly abelian groups. Along the way, we obtain several results, including a necessary and sufficient condition for normal subgroups to form a perfect code, as well as an equivalent condition for abelian groups in terms of their Sylow 2-subgroups.
arxiv:2610.16235.authors: Masoumeh Koohestani, Nasrin Soltankhah, Mohsen Ghasemi

arxiv:2610.16241.title: A non-nilpotent localization of a finite p-group
arxiv:2610.16241.summary: We give negative answers to two questions of Farjoun about localizations of groups. For every odd prime $p$, we construct a finite $p$-group $G$, an infinite non-nilpotent group $H$, and a local embedding $f\colon G\hookrightarrow H$. The associated localization satisfies $L_f(G)\cong H$, showing that localizations need not preserve nilpotence and that the localization map $G\to L(G)$ need not be surjective when $G$ is a finite $p$-group.

arxiv:2610.16245.title: Tournaments with many Hamilton cycles
arxiv:2610.16245.summary: The object of interest is the maximum number, $h(n)$, of Hamilton cycles in an $n$-tournament. By considering the expected number of Hamilton cycles in various classes of random tournaments, we obtain new asymptotic lower bounds on $h(n)$. The best result so far is approximately $ 2.85584...$ times the expected number $g(n)$ of Hamilton cycles in a random $n$-tournament, and it is conjectured that $h(n)\sim cg(n)$ where $c\approx 2.855958$.

arxiv:2610.16258.title: Elementary graphs are chromatic-choosable
arxiv:2610.16258.summary: A graph is \emph{elementary} if its edges can be coloured with two colours so that the two edges of every induced path on three vertices receive different colours. Elementary graphs are one of the two basic classes in the Chv\'atal--Sbihi decomposition of claw-free perfect graphs; they include all line graphs of bipartite multigraphs and all complements of bipartite graphs. We prove that every elementary graph $G$ satisfies $\ch(G)=\chi(G)=\omega(G)$, confirming for this class the conjecture of Gravier and Maffray that claw-free graphs are chromatic-choosable.
arxiv:2610.16258.authors: Narayanan N, Nandana K. Vasudevan, K. Somasundaram

arxiv:2610.16266.title: Towards a Sum-of-Squares Proof for the Nonexistence of Conway's 99-graph
arxiv:2610.16266.summary: Conway's $99$-graph is a strongly regular graph with parameters $(v,k,\lambda,\mu) = (99,14,1,2)$ and whose existence has long been an open problem. We use both a sum-of-squares program and the fact that a strongly regular graph with $\lambda = 1, \mu = 2$ has no diamond or $K_{2,3}$ subgraph to derive a loose upper bound for the number of triangles that such a graph could contain. This bound is less than the number of triangles that the graph's spectrum asserts, implying that it does not exist.

arxiv:2610.16300.title: Derivation based noncommutative geometry of quiver path algebras
arxiv:2610.16300.summary: In this paper, we study derivation based noncommutative geometry of path algebras arising from quivers by identifying a Lie algebra of derivations from which a differential calculus is constructed. We show that properties of the differential calculus are intimately connected with the structure of the quiver. In particular, by introducing the notion of a separating quiver, we find a condition on the quiver which is equivalent to the module of differential forms being a projective bimodule.

arxiv:2610.16307.title: Logarithmic Kunz and Radu--Andr\'e Theorems
arxiv:2610.16307.summary: Frobenius morphisms play a crucial role in algebraic geometry and commutative algebra in positive characteristic. In particular, \textit{the Kunz theorem}, characterizing non-singularity via Frobenius morphisms, is a monumental work and has a relative version, called \textit{the Radu--Andr\'e theorem}. In this paper, we extend the Kunz theorem and the Radu--Andr\'e theorem to logarithmic algebraic geometry in positive characteristic.

arxiv:2610.16332.title: Regularity of Totally Nonnegative Wonderful Compactification
arxiv:2610.16332.summary: Let $G$ be a split real semisimple group of adjoint type. We prove that the cellular decomposition of the totally nonnegative part of its wonderful compactification is a regular CW complex, confirming a conjecture of Galashin, Karp, and Lam. In particular, the closure of every cell is homeomorphic to a closed ball.

arxiv:2610.16339.title: Distinguishing sets and measures from their planar Brownian images
arxiv:2610.16339.summary: Motivated by a question of Hochman, we investigate whether two deterministic time measures or time sets can be distinguished almost surely from a single planar Brownian image. Using rescaled correlation integrals, we give a criterion for mutual singularity of the laws of the image measures, even when the time measures have the same dimension. For self-similar time sets satisfying the open set condition, we also recover the natural occupation measure from the compact image.

arxiv:2610.16350.title: Generalizing Green's Syzygy Theorems to Symmetric Products of Curves
arxiv:2610.16350.summary: Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve of genus $g$, and let $T_{n,L}$ denote the tautological line bundle on its $n$-th symmetric product $C_n$. We prove effective vanishing criteria for Koszul cohomology $K_{p,q}(C_n,T_{n,B};T_{n,L})$, extending two classical theorems of Mark Green. The main ingredient is a weight-one vanishing theorem proved by induction on $n$, using a filtration of the kernel bundle of $T_{n,L}$ to reduce the required cohomological vanishings to lower symmetric products.

arxiv:2610.16353.title: The $(km,kn)$-square paths theorem
arxiv:2610.16353.summary: For positive integers $k,m,n$ with $\gcd(m,n)=1$, we prove a $(km,kn)$-square paths theorem: the symmetric function $(-1)^{k-1}\frac{[km]_q}{[k]_q}p_k[-MX^{m,n}]\cdot1$ is a weighted sum over $(km,kn)$-preference functions. This proves a corrected form of the conjecture of Iraci, Pagaria, Paolini, and Vanden Wyngaerd and generalizes the square paths theorem of Sergel. We encode preference functions by row strict tableaux and closed walks on a set of states, compare them with parking functions for each value of the touch statistic, and apply Mellit's compositional $(km,kn)$-shuffle theorem.

arxiv:2610.16358.title: NP-hardness of additive approximation for generalized Tur\'{a}n problems
arxiv:2610.16358.summary: For a fixed graph $T$ and a fixed nonempty family $\mathcal{F}$ of graphs, let $\operatorname{ex}(G, T, \mathcal{F})$ denote the maximum number of copies of $T$ in an $\mathcal{F}$-free subgraph of a graph $G$. Alon and Shikhelman~[Algorithmica, 2022] conjectured that if $e(T)> 0$ and no member of $\mathcal{F}$ is a subgraph of a blow-up of $T$, then for every $\varepsilon>0$, approximating $\operatorname{ex}(G, T, \mathcal{F})$ within an additive error $n^{v(T)-\varepsilon}$ is NP-hard for an input graph $G$ on $n$ vertices. The previously established general cases for this conjecture include $\operatorname{ex}(G, K_2, \mathcal{F})$ by Alon, Shapira and Sudakov~[Ann. of Math., 2009], and…
arxiv:2610.16358.authors: Yihan Chen, Jialin He, Xihe Li, Jie Ma, Tianying Xie

arxiv:2610.16362.title: Double Bruhat cells in symmetric spaces
arxiv:2610.16362.summary: This paper studies the closures of the double Bruhat cells of symmetric spacess in its equivariant embeddings. We call them large double Bruhat varieties. Our aim is to establish the double Bruhat stratification as a natural setting for extending the geometry of Richardson varieties to symmetric spaces.

arxiv:2610.16376.title: Track objects in cubical presheaf automata
arxiv:2610.16376.summary: Using the formalism of presheaf automata, we introduce new classes of automata for modelling concurrency that extend higher-dimensional automata and symmetric higher-dimensional automata. We study their languages and characterise these languages in terms of posetal cospans.

arxiv:2610.16386.title: Persistence diagrams of finite topological spaces
arxiv:2610.16386.summary: In this paper, we apply persistent homology to study finite topological spaces by associating persistence diagrams with their elements through the furtherness function. This approach enables us to classify elements according to their topological evolution within the space. We further establish a bottleneck stability theorem showing that the bottleneck distance between the persistence diagrams associated with two elements is bounded above by their mutual furtherness.

arxiv:2610.16388.title: $\mathcal{D}$-Pullback Measure Attractors of McKean-Vlasov Stochastic Lattice Wave Equations
arxiv:2610.16388.summary: This paper deals with the pullback measure attractor for a non-autonomous distribution-dependent stochastic lattice wave equation with nonlinear noise on $\mathbb{Z}$. We establish well-posedness in the energy space $\ell^{2}\times\ell^{2}$ and show that the solution generates a continuous non-autonomous dynamical system on $\mathcal{P}_{4}(\ell^{2}\times\ell^{2})$, which possesses a unique pullback measure attractor $\mathcal{A}$. Furthermore, we prove the convergence of the attractor $\mathcal{A}^{\varepsilon}$ as $\varepsilon\to 0^{+}$ to the attractor of the corresponding distribution-independent limit system.
arxiv:2610.16388.authors: Huixia Wen, Ji Shu, Gang He

arxiv:2610.16394.title: Dynamical generalizations of the two-point Chowla conjecture
arxiv:2610.16394.summary: In 1965, Chowla conjectured that the values of the Liouville function become asymptotically uncorrelated at consecutive natural numbers. Recently, the two-point case is resolved by OpenAI. In 2026, Charamaras and Richter conjectured a generalization of the Chowla conjecture to the asymptotic independence of the consecutive prime Omega functions.

arxiv:2610.16404.title: Effective shadowing of transition maps for a Hamiltonian saddle-center-center equilibrium
arxiv:2610.16404.summary: We introduce a general methodology to construct globally unstable trajectories near the normally hyperbolic invariant manifold (NHIM) of a saddle-center-center Hamiltonian equilibrium. The proposed approach builds upon the classical geometric mechanism of searching for trajectories near heteroclinic connections between invariant tori of the NHIM. The main ingredient is the Birkhoff normal form near the NHIM, which allows us to control the dynamics of the hyperbolic and center components.
arxiv:2610.16404.authors: Rodney L. Anderson, Amadeu Delshams, Marian Gidea, Pablo Roldan

arxiv:2610.16407.title: Stable reduction and large Nielsen orbits on generalized Markoff surfaces
arxiv:2610.16407.summary: We establish lower bounds on the orbit cardinalities of $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ on the $\mathbb{F}_p$-points of the generalized Markoff surfaces given by $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 - xyz = \tau+2$. We show that outside of the reductions of a certain exceptional finite set of $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$-points found by Dubrovin and Mazzocco, every orbit has cardinality $\ge p$. Together with a recent result of Nathaniel Kingsbury-Neuschotz, this establishes, for all but finitely many primes $p$, the classification conjectures of McCullough-Wanderley (2013), and gives a complete classification of the connected components of the Hurwitz stack of $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{F}_p)$-covers of elliptic curves, only…

arxiv:2610.16408.title: Classification of Projective Models of $K3$-surfaces
arxiv:2610.16408.summary: Extending the methods previously established for plane sextics and quartic surfaces, we develop a unified and systematic framework for the equisingular deformation classification of projective models of $K3$-surfaces of arbitrary polarization. We treat all polarizations of degree $2n$ with $n\le 4$, including the higher-degree cases of sextic surfaces in $\mathbb{P}^{4}$ and octic surfaces in $\mathbb{P}^{5}$. The computational machinery developed here is degree-independent and provides a complete tool for enumerating and distinguishing the deformation classes arising from singular projective models of $K3$-surfaces.

arxiv:2610.16431.title: Lens spaces that cannot be obtained by two integral surgeries
arxiv:2610.16431.summary: In this article, we demonstrate that there exists an infinite family of lens spaces L(p,q) that cannot be obtained from the 3-sphere by two integral surgeries. The first such lens space in our family is L(177,29).

arxiv:2610.16445.title: Depth-zero local Langlands via shtukas in mixed characteristic
arxiv:2610.16445.summary: Assuming a smoothness property for mixed-characteristic shtuka spaces and hyperbolic localization for twisted sheaves, we determine the inertial restriction of the Fargues-Scholze $L$-parameter for irreducible depth-zero representations. Let $E$ be a non-archimedean local field of residue characteristic $p$, let $G$ be an unramified connected reductive group over $E$, and let $\pi$ be an irreducible smooth depth-zero representation of $G(E)$ over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_{\ell}$ where $\ell$ is a prime number which does not divide $p|\pi_0Z(G)|$. Let $\varphi_{\pi}^{\operatorname{FS}}$ be the Fargues-Scholze $L$-parameter associated to $\pi$.

arxiv:2610.16446.title: The rich-neighbor chromatic index is linear in the maximum degree
arxiv:2610.16446.summary: An edge of a multigraph is rich with respect to a proper edge-coloring if all the edges adjacent to it receive mutually distinct colors, and a proper edge-coloring is a rich-neighbor coloring if every non-isolated edge has a rich edge adjacent to it. The least number of colors in such a coloring is the rich-neighbor chromatic index chi'_rn(G). So far it was studied for subcubic graphs only, and multigraphs of larger maximum degree are considered here for the first time.
arxiv:2610.16446.authors: Masaki Kashima, Mirko Petru\v{s}evski, Jelena Sedlar, Riste \v{S}krekovski

arxiv:2610.16454.title: Axioms and internal rigidity of spectral duality structures
arxiv:2610.16454.summary: Spectral duality structures (SDS) explain why a distinguished family of initial distributions makes the absorption probabilities of resetting processes insensitive to the resetting mechanism. Here we study their axioms. We prove that the six defining conditions are mutually independent and determine what each one contributes.

arxiv:2610.16459.title: Edge and spectral conditions for rainbow bipancyclicity in bipartite graph collections
arxiv:2610.16459.summary: Let $\mathbf{G}=\{G_1,\dots,G_{2n}\}$ be a collection of not necessarily distinct balanced bipartite graphs of order $2n$ with a common bipartition $V=(X,Y)$. A cycle $C$ with $V(C)\subseteq V$ and $|E(C)|\leq 2n$ is called \emph{rainbow} in $\mathbf{G}$, if there exists an injection $\phi\colon E(C)\to [2n]$ such that $e\in E(G_{\phi(e)})$ for each $e\in E(C)$. The graph collection $\mathbf{G}$ is said to be \emph{rainbow bipancyclic} if it contains a rainbow cycle of every even length from 4 to $2n$.
arxiv:2610.16459.authors: Lihua You, Xiaoxue Zhang, Xinghui Zhao

arxiv:2610.16475.title: Remarks on ultrafilters exponentiation
arxiv:2610.16475.summary: Recently, two exponentiations of ultrafilters have been introduced in [7]. We rephrase them in nonstandard terms, and use the nonstandard formulations to characterize some of their properties. We also study their relations with divisibility by introducing factor-picking functions and highly exponential ultrafilters.

arxiv:2610.16487.title: The triangular metric on projective surfaces
arxiv:2610.16487.summary: In \cite{ThurstonStretch} Thurston introduced stretch paths and stretch maps between hyperbolic surfaces. In this paper we extend similar constructions to the space of convex real projective structures on surfaces. Using Fock-Goncharov-like parameters, we introduce stretch paths and construct explicit stretch maps between the projective surface.
arxiv:2610.16487.authors: Le\'on Carvajales, Xian Dai, Beatrice Pozzetti, Anna Wienhard

arxiv:2610.16514.title: An Algebraic Matching Algorithm for the Genus of Grid Diagrams
arxiv:2610.16514.summary: Grid diagrams encode knots and links combinatorially through an (n,n) winding matrix W(G). A fundamental invariant of the grid diagram is its genus g(G), which records essential topological information about the underlying knot. We give an algebraic algorithm that computes g(G) directly from W(G).

arxiv:2610.16539.title: Knot Floer homology of fibered positive links
arxiv:2610.16539.summary: We determine the Maslov-graded next-to-top term of knot Floer homology for fibered positive links. Its rank in Maslov grading (-1) is the number of nontrivial prime connected-sum factors plus the number of components minus one, and the remaining summand is supported in Maslov grading zero. For a knot, the dimension of this remaining summand is determined by its Alexander polynomial.

arxiv:2610.16541.title: Spectra and Support Theory for Wide Subcategories in $n$-Abelian Categories
arxiv:2610.16541.summary: We develop a support theory for wide subcategories of essentially small Krull--Schmidt \(n\)-abelian categories. We construct spectra associated with families of wide subcategories and establish the corresponding support and radical theories. In particular, we characterize prime wide subcategories as the completely meet-irreducible elements of the lattice of wide subcategories and prove that every wide subcategory is recovered from the prime wide subcategories containing it.

arxiv:2610.16555.title: AI Discovery in Combinatorics: From Problems to Solutions and Back to Bigger Problems
arxiv:2610.16555.summary: We introduce $qt$Bench, a benchmark of 29 open problems in algebraic combinatorics. These problems ask for a simple combinatorial algorithm that explains given polynomial coefficients or identities. To help AI agents search for such algorithms, we provide a scaffold for playing with combinatorial objects, countering cheating attempts, and testing candidate solutions.
arxiv:2610.16555.authors: Eugenio Cainelli, Lorenzo Luccioli, Alessandro Iraci, Giovanni Paolini

arxiv:2610.16561.title: Period Piece: NEXPTIME-complete problems on digraphs via Boolean network dynamics
arxiv:2610.16561.summary: The central object in this work is the Boolean network, a function $f:\{0,1\}^V \to \{0,1\}^V$. Often identified with $f$ is its dynamics $D_f$, the digraph with exactly $\{x \to y : f(x)=y\}$ as its arcs. The interaction graph of $f$ is the digraph $G$ on $V$ which can be thought of as representing the dependencies of the components of $f$ on one another.
arxiv:2610.16561.authors: Florian Bridoux, Maximilien Gadouleau, David C. Kutner, Adrien Richard

arxiv:2610.16562.title: The Davenport constant of low-dimensional boxes
arxiv:2610.16562.summary: In this paper, we study the maximal length of a minimal zero-sum sequence over $\left[\!\left[ -m,m \right]\!\right]^d$ having a support of size $d+1$. When $d=2$, we find the exact value of this maximal length for all $m \ge 2$, as well as the exact structure of all extremal sequences for this problem. When $d=3$, we obtain lower and upper bounds that asymptotically match each other as $m$ tends to infinity.

arxiv:2610.16572.title: New tools for sparse graph embeddings: Hybrid expanders and application to nested cycles
arxiv:2610.16572.summary: We introduce \emph{hybrid expanders}, sparse graphs which combine sublinear expansion across all scales with strong constant-factor expansion on smaller, polylogarithmic sets. We show that every $n$-vertex graph of average degree at least $2^{\omega(\log^*n)}$ contains such a subgraph, and use this local expansion to bring into the sparse setting tree-embedding and rollback tools more commonly associated with random or pseudorandom graphs. As an application, for fixed $k\in\mathbb N$, we prove that every graph satisfying this average-degree condition contains $k$ pairwise edge-disjoint cycles with nested vertex sets and compatible cyclic orders, resolving up to a quasi-constant factor a…

arxiv:2610.16580.title: Pointwise Ergodic Theorems Along Reiter Sequences on Locally Compact Groups
arxiv:2610.16580.summary: Let $G$ be a locally compact, second countable group admitting a Reiter sequence, and suppose that $G$ acts on a von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{M}$ equipped with a semifinite trace $\tau$ via trace-preserving automorphisms. In this paper, we prove a maximal inequality for ergodic averages along such Reiter sequences. Our approach relies on approximating the Reiter sequence by a linear combination of characteristic functions of F{\o}lner sequences using the layer-cake representation.
arxiv:2610.16580.authors: Panchugopal Bikram, Sudipta Kundu, Hariharan G, Diptesh Saha

arxiv:2610.16583.title: Fatou Components of Attracting Skew Products: From Polynomial Classification to Transcendental Complexity
arxiv:2610.16583.summary: We study the Fatou components of holomorphic skew products $F \colon \mathbb{C}^2 \to \mathbb{C}^2, F(z,w) = (f(z) + r(z,w), g(w))$ near an attracting invariant fiber, introducing a refined classification of components on the fiber: bulging, partial bulging, and nowhere bulging. For polynomial skew products, we give a complete characterization of when the basin at infinity is non-bulging, and show that in this case non-bulging implies nowhere bulging, ruling out partial bulging entirely. In the transcendental setting, the behavior is richer: we construct partially bulging wandering domains and Baker domains, show that any orbitally unbounded Fatou component can be made nowhere bulging by…

arxiv:2610.16600.title: The symmetry group of Turk's head knots
arxiv:2610.16600.summary: For p, q >= 3 with gcd(p,q) = 1 we show that the symmetry group of the Turk's head knot Th(p,q), the closure of the braid (sigma_1 sigma_2^{-1} sigma_3 sigma_4^{-1} ... sigma_{p-1}^{+-1})^q, is the dihedral group of order 4q. This proves Conjecture R of Di Prisa and \c{S}avk for q >= 3; the case p = 3 is due to Sakuma and Weeks. The argument is diagrammatic: by the flyping theorem of Menasco and Thistlethwaite, the symmetries of a knot with a prime, reduced alternating diagram without non-trivial flypes are the symmetries of the diagram (we write out a proof for the diagrams at hand), and we show that the standard diagram of Th(p,q) has no non-trivial flypes and exactly 4q symmetries.

arxiv:2610.16605.title: $2$-large sets are sets of nil-Bohr recurrence
arxiv:2610.16605.summary: A set $S$ of positive integers is $2$-large if every two-coloring contains arbitrarily long monochromatic arithmetic progressions with common difference in $S$. We prove that every such set meets every nil-Bohr neighborhood of $0$. This proves a conjecture of the first author and gives a sharp answer to a question of Host, Kra, and Maass.

arxiv:2610.16606.title: Homotopy Self-Equivalences of $\mathbb{R}P^2\times S^2$ and a Braid for non-orientable $4$-Manifolds
arxiv:2610.16606.summary: We compute the group of based homotopy classes of self-homotopy equivalences of the non-orientable $4$-manifold $\RP^2\times S^2$. It is an elementary abelian $2$-group of rank $5$. The subgroup of classes whose based lift to the universal cover $S^2\times S^2$ has degree $+1$ has rank $4$ and is isomorphic to the group of free homotopy classes.

arxiv:2610.16608.title: How Mobile Oscillators Reshape Dynamical Robustness in Complex Networks
arxiv:2610.16608.summary: While the robustness of collective dynamics in static networks is well established, how agent mobility and network topology jointly shape dynamical robustness remains largely unexplored. In this letter, we investigate the robustness of mobile Stuart-Landau oscillators performing random walks on networks and interacting diffusively when co-located. In the rapid-mobility regime, we reduce the dynamics to a mean-field framework linking network degree statistics to an effective global coupling strength.

arxiv:2610.16612.title: On the singular set of the geodesic flow on nonpositively curved surfaces
arxiv:2610.16612.summary: We prove that the singular locus of the geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle of a nonpositively curved surface enjoys an additional regularity property: its characteristic function belongs to the geometric anisotropic Sobolev space $H^{5/8-}_xH^{-13/16}_\theta$. In particular, this implies that if the geodesic flow is not ergodic with respect to the Liouville measure, then the zero set of the curvature must be thick in the sense that it supports a nonzero, nonnegative function in $H^{5/8-}$. The proof relies on semiclassical analysis and a new radial estimate for parabolic flows.

arxiv:2610.16640.title: Analytic Liouville Integrable Geodesic Flow Has Zero Entropy
arxiv:2610.16640.summary: This paper studies the topological entropy of real-analytic Liouville integrable Hamiltonian systems. We prove that the Hamiltonian flow on a compact connected regular energy hypersurface has zero topological entropy whenever a complete family of commuting real-analytic first integrals is generically independent in a connected neighborhood of that hypersurface. The proof uses finite normal expansions along minimal analytic carriers and an ergodic version of Ziglin's leading-term argument to obtain independent invariant normal polynomials, whose Poisson geometry makes all tangent Lyapunov exponents of the carriers vanish.
arxiv:2610.16640.authors: Fei Liu, Xiaokai Liu, Xiang Zhang

arxiv:2610.16648.title: Perfect matchings in planar 3-connected graphs: girth five and minimum degree five
arxiv:2610.16648.summary: Let $\Phi(G)$ denote the number of perfect matchings of a graph $G$. Goedgebeur et al. posted two questions about the perfect matchings of planar 3-connected graphs: does there exist an infinite family of matchable planar 3-connected graphs of girth 5 with a constant number of perfect matchings? Whether there exist infinitely many planar 3-connected graphs with minimum degree 5 which have a constant number of perfect matchings.

arxiv:2610.16657.title: On disjointness of 3-IETs from mixing and lightly mixing systems
arxiv:2610.16657.summary: In this note we show that all interval exchange transformations of three intervals (3-IETs) are spectrally disjoint from all mixing and disjoint from lightly mixing systems. Until now, it was known that almost every 3-IET is rigid, which implies this property. However, not all 3-IETs are rigid, hence our result is a strict improvement of current knowledge.

arxiv:2610.16658.title: On the non-existence of certain maximizing curves of degree 7
arxiv:2610.16658.summary: In this paper we show there does not exist any arrangement of degree $7$ consisting of $k\geq 1$ conics and $d\geq 1$ lines admitting certain naturally chosen ${\rm ADE}$-singularities.

arxiv:2610.16665.title: On the Drinfeld doubles of Laistrygonian algebras in positive characteristic
arxiv:2610.16665.summary: In this work, we study restricted Laistrygonian algebras over a field of positive characteristic $p$. We compute their Drinfeld double $\mathtt{D_p(q,a)}$ and give explicit presentations by generators and relations. We prove that $\mathtt{D_p(q,a)}$ is a pointed Hopf algebra.
arxiv:2610.16665.authors: Nicol\'as Andruskiewitsch, Dirceu Bagio, Saradia Della Flora, Daiana Flores, Oscar M\'arquez, H\'ector Mart\'in Pe\~na Pollastri

arxiv:2610.16703.title: Piercing boxes and products of trees
arxiv:2610.16703.summary: We give a new upper bound on the piercing number $\tau(\mathcal{F})$ of a finite family $\mathcal{F}$ of axis-parallel rectangles in the plane when every $p$ members contain an intersecting pair. Namely, we prove $\tau(\mathcal{F}) = O(p(\log\log p)(\log\log\log p))$, improving the factor $(\log\log p)^2$ in the best previously known bound to $(\log\log p)(\log\log\log p)$. For each $d>2$, when $\mathcal{F}$ is a finite family of axis-parallel boxes in $\mathbb{R}^d$, this yields $\tau(\mathcal{F}) = O(p(\log p)^{d-2}(\log\log p)(\log\log\log p))$.
arxiv:2610.16703.authors: Wei Rao, Taehyun Eom, Minki Kim

arxiv:2610.16706.title: Finiteness of open substacks with proper moduli spaces
arxiv:2610.16706.summary: For an algebraic stack of finite type, we construct a finite stratification of an atlas such that every universally closed open substack pulls back to a union of strata. As a result, there are only finitely many open substacks admitting a proper adequate moduli space.

arxiv:2610.16712.title: Spectral extremal problems on $[a,b]$-factors in binding graphs, and beyond
arxiv:2610.16712.summary: The binding number $b(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the minimum value of $|N_{G}(X)|/|X|$ taken over all nonempty sets $X\subseteq V(G)$ such that $N_{G}(X)\neq V(G)$. A graph $G$ is 1-binding if $b(G)\geq 1$. Fan and Lin [Electron.

arxiv:2610.16715.title: The Online Steinitz Problem
arxiv:2610.16715.summary: Inspired by Steinitz's celebrated result (1913) and recent online vector-balancing results of Kulkarni et al. (2024) and Aden-Ali (2026), we introduce the online Steinitz problem: $T$ vectors in $\mathbb R^d$, each of $\ell_2$-norm at most $1$ and with total sum zero, arrive one at a time and must be assigned immediately and irrevocably to unused positions of an array. The goal is to keep every prefix sum of the resulting order small.

arxiv:2610.16724.title: Universal Varieties for Signatures of Membranes
arxiv:2610.16724.summary: Membranes are sufficiently smooth vector-valued functions defined on the unit square, widely used in applications such as interpolation of image data. The signature of a membrane is a collection of nonlinear features that capture its essential geometry. We index these features in the graded Hopf algebra of two-parameter shuffle products and study the algebraic varieties for each graded component.
arxiv:2610.16724.authors: Carlos Am\'endola, Gabriel Riffo, Leonard Schmitz

arxiv:2610.16727.title: MMP for smooth co-rank one foliations
arxiv:2610.16727.summary: We prove the existence of minimal models for smooth co-rank one foliations of general type.

arxiv:2610.16731.title: On Intersection of Character Varieties Associated to Dehn Fillings of the Whitehead Link and Its Generalization
arxiv:2610.16731.summary: The canonical component of the character variety of a hyperbolic 2-bridge link complement M is an algebraic surface, from the work of Thurston. If we fix a boundary component T of M and perform a Dehn-filling on T, we get a 1-cusped manifold whose character variety is commonly a generalized curve that is naturally embedded in the character variety of M. If we perform distinct Dehn-fillings on M, we get various generalized curves on the canonical surface.

arxiv:2610.16743.title: Essential factors for surface homeomorphisms
arxiv:2610.16743.summary: Let $f$ be a homeomorphism of a closed orientable surface of genus at least one that is isotopic to a pseudo-Anosov homeomorphism, possibly relative to a finite invariant set. We construct an intrinsic monotone factor by collapsing the maximal continua whose iterates have uniformly bounded diameter in the universal cover. The quotient is homeomorphic to the original surface and the factor is isotopic to $f$ and has several strongly chaotic dynamical features.

arxiv:2610.16756.title: The nabla operator, Hall--Littlewood polynomials and LLT polynomials
arxiv:2610.16756.summary:
Bergeron, Garsia, Haiman, and Tesler conjectured that $(-1)^{n-\ell(\mu)}
abla\widetilde H_\mu[X;0,t]$ and $
abla\omega \widetilde H_\mu[X;0,t^{-1}]$ are Schur positive, and that $
abla\omega \widetilde H_\mu[X;0,t^{-1}]-
abla\omega \widetilde H_
u[X;0,t^{-1}]$ is Schur positive when $\mu$ dominates $
u$. The first statement follows from the compositional shuffle conjecture of Haglund, Morse, and Zabrocki, proved by Carlsson and Mellit. We prove the other two statements.
arxiv:2610.16756.authors: Feng Gu, Mingyang Kang, Dun Qiu, Minhao Zhang

arxiv:2610.16760.title: Galois coinvariants and fundamental groups of arithmetic schemes
arxiv:2610.16760.summary: We study Galois coinvariants of the geometric \'etale fundamental group and \'etale cohomology of varieties over a finitely generated field $k$. We establish finiteness properties of these coinvariants for (possibly infinite) Galois extensions $L/k$ such that $\operatorname{Gal}(L/k)^{\mathrm{ab}}$ has finite exponent. As an application, we obtain a finiteness result for \'etale fundamental groups of arithmetic schemes over number fields.

arxiv:2610.16783.title: Two indecomposable Enriques categories
arxiv:2610.16783.summary: This note proves that the Kuznetsov component of a quartic double solid or a special Gushel-Mukai threefold does not have non-trivial admissible subcategories.

arxiv:2610.16803.title: The weak cylinder conjecture for polynomial graphs of bounded degree
arxiv:2610.16803.summary: Ball's weak cylinder conjecture asserts that a set of $p^2$ points in $\mathrm{AG}(3,p)$ with at least $p$ non-determined directions is a union of $p$ parallel lines. We prove the conjecture for sets admitting a polynomial graph representation of total degree at most $D$, provided that $p>D^{9/2}$. More precisely, a non-cylindrical graph of degree $D\ge3$ satisfies $|\mathcal{N}_S|\le p+1-\lceil p/(D-1)\rceil$ under the same hypothesis.

arxiv:2610.16818.title: Very high genus double Hurwitz numbers via mixing times
arxiv:2610.16818.summary: We obtain very high genus asymptotics for double Hurwitz numbers when both the size $n$ and the genus $g$ go to infinity, under the constraint that $g$ grows much faster than $n$, more precisely that $\frac{2g}{n}-\ln n\to\infty$. Our proof relies on adapting arguments about the mixing time of the transposition random walk introduced by Diaconis and Shahshahani.

arxiv:2610.16853.title: Non-algebraicity of the Lawson surfaces $\xi_{k,l}$
arxiv:2610.16853.summary: We prove that every Lawson surface $\xi_{k,l}\subset\mathbb S^3$ of genus $kl>1$ is non-algebraic: any real polynomial vanishing on $\xi_{k,l}$ vanishes identically on $\mathbb S^3$. This answers a question posed by Hsiang in 1967 and proves Lawson's 1970 conjecture for $\xi_{2,2}$. The proof uses a reflection principle for the monodromy of the associated family of flat connections.

arxiv:2610.16873.title: Finite noncommutative coinvariant algebras
arxiv:2610.16873.summary: We study quotients of free associative algebras by the two-sided ideals generated by positive-degree symmetric, quasisymmetric, or free quasisymmetric polynomials. Free quasisymmetric functions give a word realization of the Malvenuto-Reutenauer Hopf algebra of permutations. For quotients on $n$ variables, finiteness in the symmetric and quasisymmetric cases follows from a theorem of Bergman--Isaacs when $n!$ is invertible in the field.
arxiv:2610.16873.authors: Farid Aliniaeifard, Nantel Bergeron, Huilan Li, Shu Xiao Li

arxiv:2610.16880.title: On a Combinatorial Characterization of Abelian Group Actions
arxiv:2610.16880.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $n$ and $X$ a finite $G$-set. We give a necessary and sufficient condition on $G$ for any $X$ to be determined up to isomorphism by certain combinatorial data. Specifically, if $M_H^X$ is the number of $H$-orbits in $X$, and $a_d^X$ is the number of $G$-orbits in $X$ of cardinality $d$, we characterize when equalities $M_H^{X_1} = M_H^{X_2}$ and $a_d^{X_1}=a_d^{X_2}$ for all $H \leq G$ and $d|n$, respectively, force an isomorphism $X_1 \simeq X_2$.
arxiv:2610.16880.authors: Carson Gull, Arthur Illidge, Benjamin Mudrak, Joshua Park, Shaver Phagan

arxiv:2610.16885.title: Morita Invariance of Saturated and Split Subgroupoids for Orbifold Embeddings
arxiv:2610.16885.summary: Borzellino and Brunsden introduced a general notion of suborbifold and proved that a suborbifold is the image of a complete orbifold embedding if and only if it is both saturated and split. Their definitions and proofs are formulated in the classical language of orbifold charts. In this paper we translate these notions into the language of proper \'etale Lie groupoids.We introduce the groupoid analogues of saturation and splitting, which we call \emph{orbit saturation} and \emph{stabilizer splitting}, and prove that they coincide with the chart-based conditions.

arxiv:2610.16898.title: Exponential Local Search in Bounded-Occurrence MAX-CSP
arxiv:2610.16898.summary: We study the number of improving steps that local search may require for $(2,2,r)$-MCA (Maximum Constraint Assignment), a bounded-occurrence version of MAX-CSP with valued constraints in which every constraint involves at most two variables, every variable occurs in at most two constraints, and every variable takes one of $r$ values. We consider the flip neighborhood, where two assignments are neighbors if they differ in the value of exactly one variable; moving to such a neighbor is called a flip. Local search repeatedly performs improving flips, that is, flips that strictly increase the objective value, until a local optimum is reached.
arxiv:2610.16898.authors: Sophia Heimann, Hung P. Hoang, Stefan Hougardy

arxiv:2610.16926.title: Graph Distortion Distances, Gromov-Hausdorff and the Hardness of Gromov-Wasserstein
arxiv:2610.16926.summary: We study the computational complexity of graph distortion distances, a family of graph metrics measuring how vertex distances differ between two graphs. Formally, these distances are defined in terms of standard matrix norms on the difference of distance matrices under an optimal vertex alignment. The resulting metrics have natural interpretations, corresponding to three ways of measuring the distortion of shortest-path distances: the maximum distortion among all vertex pairs (entrywise maximum norm), global aggregation (entrywise $p$-norms), and local aggregation (operator $p$-norms) of distortions.
arxiv:2610.16926.authors: Jens Breitung, Timo Gervens, Julius P\"orzgen

arxiv:2610.16932.title: The quarter-point theorem for Gromov hyperbolic graphs
arxiv:2610.16932.summary: Gromov hyperbolicity measures the geometric complexity of metric spaces and metric graphs through geodesic triangles and four-point conditions. While calculating the exact continuous hyperbolicity constant $\delta^*(G)$ of a graph $G$ typically requires evaluating quadruples of points over an infinite metric continuum, discretizing this domain is a fundamental challenge in metric graph theory. In this paper, we study the continuous Gromov hyperbolicity constant via the Gromov product.
arxiv:2610.16932.authors: Walter Carballosa, Jesus Mendez, Rosalio Reyes, Jos\'e M. Sigarreta

arxiv:2610.16941.title: On Intersection Hypergraph of Finite Non-Cyclic Abelian Groups
arxiv:2610.16941.summary: In this paper, we study various structural properties like girth, chromatic num ber, etc. of the intersection hypergraph on the subgroups of nite non-cyclic abelian group and we characterize for the star and hypertree structures. Fur thermore, we characterize hypergraphs which are embeddable on plane, torus and projective plane.

arxiv:2610.16951.title: Solomon--Terao Algebras: Top Degree, Dimension, and Homology
arxiv:2610.16951.summary: We study the Solomon--Terao algebra and the Solomon--Terao complex of a central hyperplane arrangement $\mathcal A$ in $\mathbb C^\ell$. Let $\eta$ be a homogeneous polynomial of degree $d\geq2$ whose restriction to every flat of $\mathcal A$ has no critical point away from the origin. We prove that the Solomon--Terao algebra $\mathrm{ST}(\mathcal A,\eta)$ has top degree $|\mathcal A|+\ell(d-2)$ and a one-dimensional top graded component with an explicit generator, solving a conjecture of Abe, Maeno, Murai, and Numata.
arxiv:2610.16951.authors: Hanyu Cai, Haiyang Chen, Shixuan Zeng, Shanwei Zhang

arxiv:2610.16955.title: On the Stability of the Independence Number of the Distance Graph G(n,r,<s) for Growing r and s
arxiv:2610.16955.summary: We consider a random subgraph G_p(n,r,<s) of the complete distance graph G(n,r,<s) whose vertices are the r-element subsets of the set {1,...,n} and whose edges join pairs of subsets that intersect in fewer than s elements; each edge survives independently of the others with probability p. The stability of the Erdos-Ko-Rado theorem is the event that the independence number of the random subgraph equals that of the original graph, N = C_{n-s}^{r-s}. For fixed r and s, two-sided bounds for the critical probability, whose ratio depends on r and s, were obtained by P.

arxiv:2610.16962.title: Crepant resolutions of four-dimensional finite quotients
arxiv:2610.16962.summary: We give counterexamples to the conjecture of Dais-Henk-Ziegler on projective crepant resolutions of complete-intersection quotient singularities. For finite $G\subset\operatorname{SL}_4(\mathbb{Z})$, we determine whether $\mathbb{C}^4/G$ admits a projective crepant resolution, with the representations considered up to conjugacy in $\operatorname{SL}_4(\mathbb{C})$. Ten explicit criteria decide all cases.

arxiv:2610.16963.title: Determinantal linear spanning forests
arxiv:2610.16963.summary: We introduce a determinantal linear process on the space of $1$-forms over a weighted graph endowed with a unitary local system, which we call the determinantal linear spanning forest (DLSF). This process is the analog of the uniform spanning tree in the presence of an arbitrary rank $n$ quenched gauge field in ${\rm U}(n)$ (or ${\rm O}(n)$, ${\rm SO}(n)$, ${\rm SU}(n)$, ${\rm Sp}(n)$), and generalizes the determinantal random cycle-rooted spanning forest which corresponds to the case of ${\rm U}(1)$ and ${\rm SU}(2)$. We describe the support of this process by means of a polymatroid which is described in terms of the circular and bicircular matroids.

arxiv:2610.16999.title: Spectral Measure and Tail Process for Multivariate Dynamical Extremes
arxiv:2610.16999.summary: We study the asymptotic behavior of extreme events in multivariate stationary sequences, with particular emphasis on stochastic processes generated by dynamical systems. We develop a general framework for describing the dependence structure of extremes through two complementary objects: the tail process and the spectral measure. We first extend the enriched point-process convergence of the univariate theory to the multivariate setting, proving that the decorated point process of exceedances converges to a marked Poisson cluster process whose marks retain the componentwise and temporal structure of extreme clusters.

arxiv:2610.17000.title: Stably ergodic endomorphisms with positive Lyapunov exponents
arxiv:2610.17000.summary: We introduce a new criterion which guarantees that a conservative local diffeomorphism is both non-uniformly expanding (in particular has all its Lyapunov exponents positive) and stably ergodic. The criterion involves averaging expansion rates over preimages and allows us to construct explicit examples in a variety of homotopy classes, including those represented by linear endomorphisms with contracting directions.

arxiv:2610.17005.title: On Sums of "Small" Cantor Sets
arxiv:2610.17005.summary: We provide several results showing that sums of ``small'' Cantor sets can turn into an interval or a finite union of intervals. Specifically, we show that 1) There exists a Cantor set $C\subset [0,1]$ of zero logarithmic capacity such that $C+C=[0,2]$. 2) For any $n\ge 2$ there exists a Cantor set $C\subset [0,1]$ of zero logarithmic capacity such that a Minkowski sum of $n$ copies of $C$ is an interval $[0,n]$, while a sum of any smaller number of copies of $C$ is still a Cantor set. 3) For any $n\ge 2$ there exists a collection of Cantor sets $C_1, C_2, \ldots, C_n\subset [0,1]$ of zero lower box-counting dimension such that a Minkowski sum of any $n-1$ sets from this collection is a…
arxiv:2610.17005.authors: Anton Gorodetski, Alexandro Luna, William Wood

arxiv:2610.17006.title: Sensitivity of Rotation Symmetric Boolean Functions via Binary Necklaces
arxiv:2610.17006.summary: Rotation symmetric Boolean functions are Boolean functions invariant under cyclic permutation of their variables and can be represented by binary necklaces.
