We express local sensitivity as a weighted bichromatic degree in the necklace quotient and derive an exact formula for the multiplicities between neighboring necklaces. For an odd prime number of variables, we obtain explicit sensitivity formulas and show that multiplicity corrections occur only on an asymptotically negligible family of necklaces.

arxiv:2610.17028.title: Universality of $\mathsf{CohFT}$ of $\mathsf{Hilb}_n(S)$
arxiv:2610.17028.summary: By virtue of their relation to Fulton--MacPherson compactifications, the cohomological field theory of Hilbert schemes of points on a surface, in extremal curve classes, is universally and effectively determined by the characteristic numbers of the surface and by the corresponding theory of Hilbert schemes of the affine plane. As a consequence, we compute the extremal genus 1 Gromov--Witten invariants of Hilbert schemes of all surfaces.

arxiv:2610.17044.title: Oka realizations, fundamental groups, and holomorphic cofibrations
arxiv:2610.17044.summary: The homotopy types of Oka manifolds are exactly those of countable finite-dimensional CW complexes. We construct realizations as open subsets of complex Euclidean spaces with explicit dimension bounds. Other realizations have good open covers by sets biholomorphic to $\C^N$, with prescribed finite nerves, or are unions of Fatou--Bieberbach domains whose nonempty finite intersections are again Fatou--Bieberbach domains.
arxiv:2610.17044.authors: Bin Guo, Yuta Kusakabe, Peng-Chao Wang

arxiv:2610.17045.title: Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations for Finsler metrics on symmetric spaces
arxiv:2610.17045.summary: Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations are random tessellations that arise as limits of Voronoi diagrams for Poisson point processes as their intensity tends to zero. For the Riemannian metric on a symmetric space of higher rank, Fr\k{a}czyk, Mellick, and Wilkens (arXiv:2307.01194) proved that the corresponding ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellation is almost surely completely connected, with an unbounded side between any two cells. This contrasts sharply with the geometry of ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations in hyperbolic spaces studied by D'Achille, Curien, Enriquez, Lyons, and \"Unel (arXiv:2303.16831).
arxiv:2610.17045.authors: Colin Davalo, J. Maxwell Riestenberg, Anna Wienhard

arxiv:2610.17055.title: Construction of Regular Fat Linear Sets and Non-Representable q-Matroids
arxiv:2610.17055.summary: Let $q$ be a prime power. An $(r, i)$-regular fat $\mathbb F_q$-linear set has exactly $r$ points of weight $i\ge2$, called fat points. All of its remaining points have weight one, and at least one such point occurs.
arxiv:2610.17055.authors: Yufei Qiu, Valentino Smaldore, Zhenpeng Wang, Corrado Zanella, Ferdinando Zullo

arxiv:2610.17060.title: A higher categorical approach to graded bivariant $K$-theories for Real $C^*$-algebras
arxiv:2610.17060.summary: We present an $\infty$-categorical refinement of classical $KK$-theory and $E$-theory for graded, $G$-equivariant for a locally compact second countable group $G$, Real $C^*$-algebras. As a consequence, we obtain a couple of fiber sequences connecting the different $K$-theory spectra, and explicitly analyse the induced endomorphisms on $K_0$-groups. We also answer precisely some folklore questions in the area.

arxiv:2610.17078.title: Sustainable trees
arxiv:2610.17078.summary: Let $X$ be a connected graph and let $\lambda_1(X)$ denote the spectral radius of its adjacency matrix. An edge $e$ of $X$ is sustainable if it can be deleted and replaced by a non-edge so that the resulting graph is connected and its spectral radius does not decrease; $X$ is sustainable if every edge is. We study this edgewise notion of spectral robustness for trees, where each replacement is an elementary exchange between trees on the same vertex set.
arxiv:2610.17078.authors: Ferenc Bencs, Maarten van Dijk, Krystal Guo

arxiv:2610.17100.title: Block Sensitivity and Certificate Complexity of Rotation Symmetric Boolean Functions
arxiv:2610.17100.summary: We study block sensitivity and certificate complexity of rotation symmetric Boolean functions, with particular emphasis on monomial rotation symmetric Boolean functions. We first show that every odd-degree monomial rotation symmetric Boolean function on $n$ variables satisfies $s=bs=C=n$. We then determine sensitivity, block sensitivity, and certificate complexity for every quadratic monomial rotation symmetric Boolean function.

arxiv:2610.17107.title: The majority of a cactus is prickly
arxiv:2610.17107.summary: We characterise all (undirected) cacti graphs, and forests of cacti, with an edge-preserving near-unanimity operation, by means of forbidden induced subgraphs. Indeed all such graphs also have an edge-preserving majority operation. We show that said majority can be chosen to be symmetric and explicitly construct it for all forests of cacti without the forbidden induced subgraphs.
arxiv:2610.17107.authors: Catarina Carvalho, Mathison Knight, Barnaby Martin

arxiv:2610.17135.title: Chow polynomials and chain polynomials of matroids are not log-concave
arxiv:2610.17135.summary: The Hilbert--Poincar\'{e} series of the Chow rings of the toric varieties of matroids, often called the \emph{Chow polynomials}, and the $f$-polynomial of their boundary complexes, called the \emph{chain polynomials}, have been conjectured to only have real zeros. We construct several explicit infinite families of matroids from finite geometries, whose multichain counts fail to be log-concave. They share a common geometric construction called \emph{hyperplane coalescence}, together with several classical operations in projective geometry and combinatorial designs.
arxiv:2610.17135.authors: Gergely B\'erczi, Basile Coron, Christopher Eur, Shiyue Li

arxiv:2610.17139.title: (Sharp arithmetic) localization beyond transversality
arxiv:2610.17139.summary: We prove sharp arithmetic localization for one-dimensional quasiperiodic potentials with jump discontinuities, beyond uniform transversality. Our results include every non-constant $C^1$ monotone sampling function, even with arbitrarily large flat regions, and also certain non-monotone potentials. A key new mechanism is a symbolic unique-continuation principle: first-return words to the region where $f'>0$ have no common Dirichlet resonance, forcing eigenfunction mass to transfer away from flat or negatively sloped regions and recovering quantitative monotonicity of finite-volume eigenvalue branches.
arxiv:2610.17139.authors: Svetlana Jitomirskaya, Netanel Levi, Tom Stoiber

arxiv:2610.17147.title: Collisions of Nilpotent Higgs Fields
arxiv:2610.17147.summary: We prove the non-characteristicness of the completed self-sum of the universal nilpotent cone in $T^*\mathrm{Bun}_G$ relative to the moduli of curves, for reductive groups $G$ of semi-simple rank $1$. In particular, this implies the non-characteristicness of the $\mathcal{H}om$-sheaf between Betti automorphic sheaves for groups of semi-simple rank $1$. We also construct an example of a collision of universal nilpotent Higgs fields, proving that the completed self-sum is not non-characteristic for $\mathrm{GL}_n$, $n\ge 3$, relative to the moduli of curves of genus $g\ge 4$.

arxiv:2610.17153.title: H\"older regularity of the top Lyapunov exponent for random matrix products with low-dimensional equator
arxiv:2610.17153.summary: We investigate the regularity of Lyapunov exponents for products of random invertible matrices of arbitrary dimension $d\ge 2$. We prove that the top Lyapunov exponent is pointwise H\"older continuous with respect to the Wasserstein-Hausdorff distance in the space of probability measures with compact support, in the case where this exponent is simple and the equator has dimension equal to or less than one.
arxiv:2610.17153.authors: Ana Cristina Barreto, Adriana S\'anchez, El Hadji Yaya Tall, Marcelo Viana

arxiv:2610.17157.title: Pushed colorful polytopal KKMS Theorem and orthogonal star transversals
arxiv:2610.17157.summary: A classical theorem of Kaiser and Rabinovich implies that if every subfamily of size at most $\lfloor\log_2(d+1)\rfloor+1$ of a finite family of compact connected sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$ has a common axis-parallel hyperplane transversal, then the entire family has an orthogonal star transversal, i.e., a union of $d$ hyperplanes, one perpendicular to each coordinate axis. We study colorful variants of this result. First, we use standard KKM machinery to establish a colorful analogue with $d+1$ color classes and a $\lfloor\log_2(d+1)\rfloor+1$ transversal hypothesis for rainbow subfamiles.

arxiv:2610.17162.title: Finite-order exponential mixing does not imply the central limit theorem
arxiv:2610.17162.summary: We show that finite-order exponential mixing does not imply the central limit theorem for smooth diffeomorphisms. For every integer $R\geq2$, we construct a $\mathcal{C}^{\infty}$ diffeomorphism $T:M\to M$ of a compact smooth manifold $M$ and a $T$-invariant probability measure $\mu$ such that $(T,\mu)$ is exponentially mixing of order $R$ for $\mathcal{C}^1(M)$ observables, but not of order $2R+2$. For some centred observable $f_0\in\mathcal{C}^{\infty}(M)$, no subsequence of the normalised sums $\frac{1}{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}f_0\circ T^i$ converges in distribution to a Gaussian law.
arxiv:2610.17162.authors: Bernat Bassols Cornudella, Matheus M Castro

arxiv:2610.17169.title: p-adic Hodge theory of unipotent completions revisited
arxiv:2610.17169.summary: Let $K/\mathbb{Q}_p$ be a finite extension, and let $X/K$ be an algebraic variety. We present a new proof that the unipotent completion of the \'etale fundamental group of $X_{\bar{K}}$ is a pro-de Rham representation, and show that it is pro-semi-stable whenever $X$ has semi-stable \'etale cohomology. We also reprove, using syntomic methods, that it is pro-crystalline at integral base points whenever $X$ admits a smooth proper formal model.

arxiv:2610.17173.title: Privileged $\mathrm{SL}_3$-local systems are motivic
arxiv:2610.17173.summary: Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety over the complex numbers, and let $\mathbb{V}$ be an irreducible privileged $\mathrm{SL}_3$-local system on $X$ in the sense of Esnault and Groechenig. We show that $\mathbb{V}$ is of geometric origin. We also give an example of a privileged but non-rigid $\mathrm{SL}_3$-local system.

arxiv:2610.17188.title: A Generalisation of Maximal $(k,b)$-Linear-Free Sets of Integers
arxiv:2610.17188.summary: Fix integers $k,b,q$ with $k\ge 2,b\ge 0,q\ge 2$. Define the function $p$ to be: $p(x)=kx+b$. We call a set $S$ of integers $(k,b,q)$-linear-free if $x\in S$ implies $p^i (x)\notin S$ for all $i=1,2,\dots,q-1$, where $p^i (x)=p\left(p^{i-1}(x)\right)$ and $p^0 (x)=x$.

arxiv:2610.17196.title: Classifying quasi-representations of groups via their characters
arxiv:2610.17196.summary: For every countable discrete group, we construct a character for finite-dimensional unitary quasi-representations, with values in the inverse limit of the equivariant $K$-theory of its Rips complexes. The character is a complete invariant for quasi-representations up to stable equivalence for amenable groups and, more generally, for groups satisfying the Haagerup property and QR-quasidiagonality. For Haagerup groups satisfying quantitative QR-quasidiagonality, we also obtain a quantiative version of the theorems.
arxiv:2610.17196.authors: Shmuel Weinberger, Jianchao Wu, Guoliang Yu

arxiv:2610.17235.title: Turaev cobracket, synthetic geometry and applications
arxiv:2610.17235.summary: A teardrop geodesic on a hyperbolic surface is a closed curve that is geodesic except at exactly one point, called its vertex. One imagines a closed curve with one point held down as it deforms to a geodesic. For each teardrop geodesic, we give an explicit geometric construction of the closed geodesic in its free homotopy class.

arxiv:2610.17236.title: Whither quantum advantage? New classical lower bounds for Max-Cut on large-girth 3-regular graphs
arxiv:2610.17236.summary: Every 3-regular graph of girth at least $g$ has a cut containing at least a fraction $M_g$ of its edges, and the best rigorous bounds at large girth are $0.912\le \lim_{g\to\infty}M_g \le 0.92386$. Lower bounds on $M_g$ follow from the performance of local algorithms: on a graph of girth $g \ge 2p+2$ a depth-$p$ local algorithm sees the same tree around every edge, so its expected cut fraction on that tree bounds $M_g$ from below. We apply this strategy to the Variational Iterative Rotation Algorithm (VIRAL), a classical local algorithm, and evaluate it on the depth-$p$ tree for every even depth up to $p=32$.
arxiv:2610.17236.authors: Flaviano Morone, Shivang Rawat, Dries Sels

arxiv:2610.17270.title: Integer decomposition property of three-dimensional smooth polytopes: a shorter proof
arxiv:2610.17270.summary: Oda's smoothness conjecture asserts that every smooth lattice polytope has the integer decomposition property. The three-dimensional case of this conjecture was recently proven by AI. Here we give a much shorter proof of this result.

arxiv:2610.17277.title: Point Processes and Gap Statistics for Translation Surfaces
arxiv:2610.17277.summary: We study the behavior of saddle connection directions on translation surfaces from the point process viewpoint. We define a direction point process for saddle connections of length at most $R>0$ on every translation surface. Given a general ergodic $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb R)$-invariant measure $\mu$ on a stratum of translation surfaces, we also define a slope point process associated with $\mu$.

arxiv:2610.17311.title: Models for dagger $(\infty,1)$-categories III: Univalent flagged dagger $(\infty,1)$-categories and unitarily complete dagger Segal anima
arxiv:2610.17311.summary: We identify the $(\infty,1)$-category presented by the dagger Bergner, dagger Joyal, and dagger Rezk models of Parts I and II with that of univalent flagged dagger $(\infty,1)$-categories. We first construct a realization--nerve adjunction between reversal simplicial anima and Hermitian flags. We prove that its nerve restricts to an equivalence between flagged dagger $(\infty,1)$-categories and dagger Segal anima, under which univalence corresponds to unitary completeness.

arxiv:2610.17317.title: Square integrable representations and Hecke eigenvalues over a local non-archimedian field
arxiv:2610.17317.summary: Let $G$ be a split connected semi-simple group over a local non-archimedean field $F$. In this paper we study the action of Hecke operators on the Schwartz space of half-densities on the moduli stack $\bpo$ of $G$-bundles on ${\mathbb P}^1$ endowed with a trivialization at $0$ and $\infty$. This space is a representation of $G(F)\times G(F)$ which contains the regular representation of $G(F)$.

arxiv:2610.17325.title: Arithmetic jet spaces and the unramified Zilber--Pink conjecture for subvarieties of abelian varieties
arxiv:2610.17325.summary: We show how the methods of delta geometry can be used to bound the degree of points in the Zilber--Pink locus of a subvariety of an abelian variety, if the varieties are defined over a number field and we restrict to points with bounded ramification at a fixed prime.

arxiv:2610.17335.title: On the rank-one limit sets for maps in the constant-Jacobian shear group of $\mathbb{C}^2$
arxiv:2610.17335.summary: Let $\mathcal{S}_c$ be the subgroup of $Aut(\mathbb{C}^2)$ generated by affine maps and shear automorphisms with constant Jacobian. We determine the possible conformal types of the rank-one limit set of an invariant recurrent Fatou component when the induced dynamics has infinite order. In particular we show that, under this infinite-order hypothesis, the limit set of a finite composition of H\'enon maps (polynomial or transcendental), can only be conformally equivalent to a disk or an annulus.

arxiv:2610.17388.title: Hanslick's Musical Formalism as a Mathematical Structure - Examining meaning in Music through the Lens of Category Theory
arxiv:2610.17388.summary: We investigate Eduard Hanslicks formalist aesthetics through the prism of Category Theory

arxiv:2610.17389.title: A characterization of central extensions relative to n-nilpotent objects
arxiv:2610.17389.summary: We characterize the central extensions, in the sense of the categorical theory of central extensions of Janelidze and Kelly, relative to the Birkhoff subcategory of $n$-nilpotent objects of a semi-abelian and algebraically coherent category. An extension $f \colon A \to B$ with kernel $K$ turns out to be central precisely when the iterated Huq commutator $[A,[A,\dots,[A,K]\dots]]$, with $n$ occurrences of $A$, vanishes. For $n=2$ this condition reads $[A,[K,A]] = 0$, that is, $[K,A]$ is a central subobject of $A$.
arxiv:2610.17389.authors: Marino Gran, James R. A. Gray

arxiv:2610.17394.title: The rational homology of independence complexes of Kneser graphs on triples
arxiv:2610.17394.summary: The independence complex of the Kneser graph $\KG(n,k)$ is the simplicial complex of pairwise intersecting families of $n$-subsets of $[2n+k]$; equivalently, it is a Vietoris--Rips complex of the $n$-subsets of $[2n+k]$ under the symmetric-difference metric. Feng and Wang asked whether, for $n=3$, its reduced homology is nontrivial only in dimensions $6$ and $9$, and conjectured the rank in dimension $9$. We answer the question affirmatively over the rationals and determine all the associated Betti numbers.

arxiv:2610.17405.title: Purely non-free actions on Riemann surfaces
arxiv:2610.17405.summary: A group of conformal automorphisms of a Riemann surface is said to act purely non-free, or to produce a gpnf-action, if each of its finite-order elements has fixed points. It is known that every finite group admits a gpnf-action on a suitable closed Riemann surface of genus at least two. If $G$ is an infinite countable group, and $X$ is an infinite-type orientable surface, without planar ends and whose space of ends is self-similar, then we observe that there is a Riemann surface structure on $X$ admitting a gpnf-action by $G$.
arxiv:2610.17405.authors: Rub\'en A. Hidalgo, Jhony S. Leyca

arxiv:2610.17432.title: Plane Cremona maps preserving a Euclidean volume form
arxiv:2610.17432.summary: We give a presentation by generators and relations of the group of birational transformations of the plane preserving a differential form with poles along a triple line. This group strictly contains the automorphism group of the affine plane.
arxiv:2610.17432.authors: Marc Abboud, J\'er\'emy Blanc, St\'ephane Lamy

arxiv:2610.17441.title: Linear Laurent phenomenon algebras are of finite type
arxiv:2610.17441.summary: Laurent phenomenon algebras generalise cluster algebras by allowing irreducible exchange polynomials in place of binomials. Lam and Pylyavskyy proved finite type for those arising from graphs and conjectured that the same holds for every Laurent phenomenon algebra admitting a linear seed. We prove this conjecture over an arbitrary unique factorisation domain.

arxiv:2610.17476.title: $a$-Numbers, higher Cartier ranks and maximality of van der Geer-van der Vlugt curves
arxiv:2610.17476.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $C_R$ be the van der Geer-van der Vlugt curve $y^p-y=xR(x)$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$, where $R(x)=\sum_{i=0}^{h}a_ix^{p^i}$ is an additive polynomial of degree $p^h$. We determine the image and the rank of every power of the Cartier operator $\Cart$ on $H^0(C_R,\Omg)$. For $1\le r\le h-1$ the image of $\Cart^r$ is spanned by an explicit set of monomial differentials that does not depend on $R$, and $\rank(\Cart^r)=p^{h-r-1}\binom{p+r}{r+2}$.
arxiv:2610.17476.authors: Gilberto B. Almeida Filho, Saeed Tafazolian, St\'efani C. Vieira

arxiv:2610.17482.title: Cyclic reflections and the flip equation for the graded Grothendieck-Teichm\"uller group
arxiv:2610.17482.summary: Furusho, Hirose and Komiyama reformulated the pentagon equation using an involution called the flip, which led to a new characterisation of the graded Grothendieck-Teichm\"uller group $\mathsf{GRT}_1$. We show that the flip is a reflection in the cyclic structure of the operad of framed Drinfeld-Kohno Lie algebras, with the framings removed. Applying the reflection twice to the pentagon gives the two-cycle relation for every Drinfeld associator.

arxiv:2610.17489.title: What remains when integrability fails? Mathematical structure in the K(m,m) compacton equations
arxiv:2610.17489.summary: Peter Lax's 1968 discovery that certain nonlinear wave equations possess operator pairs (Lax pairs) opened the theory of completely integrable systems, yielding exact solutions, infinite conservation hierarchies, and perfectly elastic soliton collisions. When a nonlinear dispersive equation is provably non-integrable (admitting no Lax pair and only finitely many conservation laws), what mathematical structure governs its dynamics? The K(m,m) compacton equations, u_t + (u^m)_x + (u^m)_{xxx} = 0 for m >= 2, provide a testing ground: they support traveling waves with compact support, yet fail every known integrability test.

arxiv:2610.17508.title: Another Brick in the Wall: A Computationally Assisted Proof of an Improved Upper Bound for Thrackles
arxiv:2610.17508.summary: Let $G$ be a thrackle, where a thrackle is a graph drawing in which each edge meets every other edge exactly once, either at a vertex or at a crossing. It is conjectured that, for all thrackles, the number of edges is less than or equal to the number of vertices. Fulek and Pach created a program to determine whether or not a graph can be a thrackle.

arxiv:2610.17516.title: Alpern Lemma Independent of a Partition for Aperiodic Systems
arxiv:2610.17516.summary: We prove that for every $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$, an aperiodic, probability preserving system and $\mathcal{P}$ a finite measurable partition of $X$, there exists an Alpern Multitower whose base is independent of $\mathcal{P}$. This removes the ergodicity assumption in the original proof of the independent Alpern Lemma of \cite{MR3373823}. As a consequence, we remove ergodicity assumption from recent results on limit theorems in deterministic systems \cite{Kosloff_Volny_2022,kosloffVolnyStableCLT,MR4955410}.
arxiv:2610.17516.authors: Nishant Chandgotia, Zemer Kosloff, Shrey Sanadhya

arxiv:2610.17525.title: Monoidal structure on Rota-Baxter algebras via augmentation, and free cocycle bialgebras
arxiv:2610.17525.summary: A tensor product is known for commutative Rota--Baxter algebras through a universal construction, but its underlying algebra need not be the ordinary tensor product $A\otimes B$ and can be substantially larger. We show that, after passing to augmented Rota--Baxter algebras, the ordinary tensor product itself carries a natural Rota--Baxter operator which makes the category monoidal with the usual associator and unit constraints. The resulting structure is intrinsically nonsymmetric: over a field of characteristic zero, this operator and its flip-conjugated counterpart are the only possibilities among linear combinations of five natural terms, while over any field the full category admits no…
arxiv:2610.17525.authors: Li Guo, Yunzhou Xie, Yi Zhang

arxiv:2610.17536.title: Hyperelliptic curves on $K3$ surfaces
arxiv:2610.17536.summary: We study hyperelliptic curves on $K3$ surfaces. We show that any number of general points on a $K3$ surface of Picard rank one can be connected by a hyperelliptic curve. As a by-product we recover the Beauville--Voisin decomposition of the small diagonal, together with some new bounds on its torsion order in the integral Chow group.

arxiv:2610.17548.title: On the generalized cospectral mates of chain graphs of rank 4
arxiv:2610.17548.summary: A graph is called a chain graph if it is bipartite and the neighborhoods of the vertices in each color class are linearly ordered by inclusion. We study the generalized spectral determination of chain graphs of adjacency rank $4$. We first show that generalized cospectral chain graphs have the same number of isolated vertices, reducing the problem to the connected case.

arxiv:2610.17558.title: The $\ell$-degree Tur\'an densities of hypergraphs: infinite families and their finite subfamilies
arxiv:2610.17558.summary: Let $k>\ell\ge 1$ be integers. For a family $\mathcal{F}$ of $k$-uniform hypergraphs ($k$-graphs), its $\ell$-degree Tur\'an density $\gamma^{(k)}_\ell(\mathcal{F})$ is the asymptotic maximum of the normalized minimum $\ell$-degree over all $\mathcal{F}$-free $k$-graphs. In this paper, we prove that for all integers $k>\ell>2$ and every $\alpha\in[0,1)$, there exists an infinite family $\mathcal{F}$ of $k$-graphs such that $\gamma^{(k)}_\ell(\mathcal{F})=\alpha$, while every finite subfamily $\mathcal{F}'\subset \mathcal{F}$ satisfies $\gamma^{(k)}_\ell(\mathcal{F}')>\alpha$.

arxiv:2610.17598.title: On extending induced subgraphs
arxiv:2610.17598.summary: When characterizing graphs defined by forbidden induced subgraphs, it is often desirable to understand how a graph $G$ can be generated incrementally from a given induced subgraph $H$. In this paper, we study a number of problems within this framework. First, for several notions of connectivity, we determine all minimal induced subgraphs of $G$ that contain $H$ and attain the connectivity of $G$.
arxiv:2610.17598.authors: Guoli Ding, Jake Weber, Weihao Xia

arxiv:2610.17602.title: Clean handshake sequences
arxiv:2610.17602.summary: After a basketball game, each of the $n$ players on Team A must shake hands with each of the $n$ players on Team B. What is the minimum number of (reversible, ambidextrous) gloves required so that zero germ transmission occurs? We show that the answer is $3n/2+o(n)$ and develop a general theory for prescribed handshake sets.
arxiv:2610.17602.authors: John Byrne, Colby Sherwood, Ioannis Tsokanos, Brian Wilmarth

arxiv:2610.17608.title: $3$-manifold groups are linear
arxiv:2610.17608.summary: We prove that the fundamental group of every compact graph $3$-manifold is linear over the complex numbers. As a corollary, all fundamental groups of compact $3$-manifolds are linear over the complex numbers.

arxiv:2610.17631.title: Complete mappings stabilizing Sylow $2$-subgroups in central quotients of special linear groups
arxiv:2610.17631.summary: A complete mapping of a finite group $G$ is a permutation $\theta$ of $G$ such that $x\mapsto x\theta(x)$ is also a permutation of $G$. Complete mappings have applications in cryptography, particularly in the design of round functions for cryptographic systems. The study of their parity has led to the question of which finite groups admit complete mappings of both parities.
arxiv:2610.17631.authors: Shixin Wang, Shikang Yu, Tao Feng

arxiv:2610.17646.title: A subcategory with remarkable homological properties via actions of tensor categories
arxiv:2610.17646.summary: By equipping the category $\mathcal{M}$ of modules over a finite dimensional algebra with the action of a finite tensor category $\mathcal{C}$, we introduce a subcategory $\mathcal{PM}$ satisfying numerous remarkable properties: it is generating and cogenerating, functorially finite, closed under Auslander--Reiten translations (i.e. precluster tilting), and it computes the finitistic dimension. Through a functor category perspective, $\mathcal{PM}$ is identified with the $\mathcal{C}$-module functors that are projective, and we also prove a $\mathcal{C}$-equivariant version of the Auslander(--Solberg) correspondence. As examples, we show that $\mathcal{PM}$ contains only finitely many…

arxiv:2610.17650.title: Simultaneously preperiodic points and colliding orbits for families of polynomials in characteristic $p$
arxiv:2610.17650.summary: Let $k=\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$ and let $f\in k[X]$ be a polynomial of degree at least $2$ such that $f-f(0)$ is non-additive. For $\alpha,\beta$ in an algebraically closed extension $L$ of $k$, we prove that there are infinitely many $\lambda\in L$ for which both points are preperiodic under $f(X)+\lambda$ if and only if $\alpha,\beta\in k$ or $f(\beta)-f(\alpha)\in E_f$. Here $E_f=\{c\in G_f:(f-f(0))^n(c)\in G_f\text{ for every }n\ge0\}$, where $G_f=\{c\in k : f(X+c)-f(X)\in k\}$.

arxiv:2610.17676.title: On quasi-lisse affine vertex algebras $L_{-1-h/6}(\mathfrak{g})$ from rank-one Argyres-Douglas theories
arxiv:2610.17676.summary: We study certain simple affine vertex algebras $L_{-1-h/6}(\mathfrak{g})$ from rank-one Argyres-Douglas theories, where $\mathfrak{g}$ is a non-simply-laced simple Lie algebra and $h$ is its Coxeter number. For $L_{-3}(F_4)$, we determine the maximal ideal of $V^{-3}(F_4)$, Zhu's algebra, and the associated variety. We also classify the irreducible highest-weight $L_{-3}(F_4)$-modules and determine the characters of its irreducible ordinary modules.
arxiv:2610.17676.authors: Drazen Adamovic, Xuanzhong Dai, Kaiwen Sun

arxiv:2610.17677.title: A Minimum Exact Disjunctive Basis for Two-Robot Solvability Profiles
arxiv:2610.17677.summary: We completely characterize the solvability profiles of tasks for two autonomous mobile robots in the plane under variable disorientation, chirality, and rigid movements. The four standard capability models and the schedulers considered here have a known quotient order Q of thirteen computational classes. A task's solvability profile is the set of classes in which it is solvable, and is necessarily an upset of Q.
arxiv:2610.17677.authors: Tsukasa Ninomiya, Shota Naito, Naoki Kitamura, Yuichi Sudo, Koichi Wada

arxiv:2610.17737.title: Dimensions and maximal-dimensional components of higher commuting varieties of symmetric pairs
arxiv:2610.17737.summary: Let $\mathfrak p$ be the $(-1)$-eigenspace of a complex semisimple symmetric pair. For every $r\ge2$, we prove $\dim C_r(\mathcal N(\mathfrak p))\le \lfloor r\dim\mathfrak p/2\rfloor$ and show that every irreducible component is isotropic for a natural family of alternating forms. For a nonzero Hermitian pair with $\mathfrak g$ simple and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak p^-\oplus\mathfrak p^+$, put $d=\dim\mathfrak p^+$ and $\ell=\operatorname{rk}(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak k)$.

arxiv:2610.17769.title: Quandles with isomorphic representation categories
arxiv:2610.17769.summary: We give two types of examples where two non isomorphic finite quandles have isomorphic enveloping groups. This implies that two non-isomorphic finite quandles can share isomorphic representation categories (as additive and tensor categories simultaneously).

arxiv:2610.17798.title: Lattice Bruhat intervals are polytopal
arxiv:2610.17798.summary: For a Bruhat interval $[x,y]$ in an arbitrary Coxeter group which is a lattice, we give a type-uniform construction of a convex polytope whose complete face lattice realizes $[x,y]$. This gives a polytopal realization of the coincidence between classical Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials for lattice Bruhat intervals and Stanley's toric $g$-polynomials. Consequently, the Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial of a lattice Bruhat interval cannot have internal zeros, satisfies a multiplicative strengthening of monotonicity, and obeys the generalized upper bound theorem for polytopes.

arxiv:2610.17817.title: Aspects of deformation invariance of plurigenera of K\"ahler varieties
arxiv:2610.17817.summary: We study several aspects of deformation invariance of plurigenera in K\"ahler families over a smooth curve. First, for a relatively flat coherent sheaf, we characterize local constancy of fiberwise cohomology dimension by equivalent conditions in terms of extension, base change, torsion freeness of higher direct images, and the vanishing of jumping classes. Then, combining this criterion with the K\"ahler minimal model program, we prove invariance of plurigenera for K\"ahler families of threefolds whose central fiber has canonical singularities, and for smooth K\"ahler families of maximal Albanese dimension.
arxiv:2610.17817.authors: Jiawei Feng, Yi Li, Sheng Rao

arxiv:2610.17839.title: Counting triangles in graphs without suspensions of paths
arxiv:2610.17839.summary: For a graph $H$, the suspension $\widehat H$ of $H$ is a graph obtained from $H$ by joining a new vertex to every vertex of $H$. The generalized Tur\'an number $\textrm{ex}(n,K_3,\widehat H)$ is the maximum number of triangles in an $n$-vertex $\widehat H$-free graph. For fixed $k \ge 4$, Mubayi and Mukherjee conjectured that \[ \textrm{ex}(n,K_3,\widehat P_k) =\left\lfloor\frac{k-2}{2}\right\rfloor\frac{n^2}{8}+o(n^2), \] as $n \to \infty$, where $P_k$ is the path on $k$ vertices.

arxiv:2610.17842.title: Theoretical and Computational Advances in Birkhoff Pseudospectral Transcription for Aerospace Optimal Control
arxiv:2610.17842.summary: This paper develops theoretical and numerical extensions of Birkhoff pseudospectral transcription for aerospace optimal control problems. Building on the recently proposed body of knowledge, a Birkhoff integration operator is derived for flipped Legendre Gauss Radau (fLGR) grids, drawing connections to regular LGR grids and to the favorable conditioning properties that make Birkhoff interpolants particularly appealing. We also propose the enforcement of differential constraints via pseudospectral operators, and the primal and dual equivalence of this approach to state augmentation is established for control-rate limits.

arxiv:2610.17852.title: $\ell$-Independence, slopes, and weights of $\ell$-adic cohomology groups of rigid spaces
arxiv:2610.17852.summary: Let $\ell$ and $p$ be distinct prime numbers, $K$ a local field with residue characteristic $p$, $C$ a complete algebraically closed extension of $K$, and $X$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated rigid space over $K$. When $\mathop{\mathrm{char}} K = 0$, we prove that the alternating sum of traces of elements in the positive part of the Weil group acting on $R\Gamma(X_C,\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})$ is independent of $\ell$ and is an integer, extending a result of Mieda to the singular case. We also give optimal bounds for the $p$-adic valuations of the eigenvalues of geometric Frobenius liftings acting on $H^i(X_C,\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})$, proving a conjecture of Lu--Zheng.

arxiv:2610.17875.title: Geometric and homological interpretations of tensor flattenings
arxiv:2610.17875.summary: We relate several nonlinear flattenings of structure tensors of finite algebras and modules to their algebraic and homological invariants. Since smoothability of algebras is equivalent to their structure tensors having minimal border rank, this shows equivalence of several tensor-theoretic nonsmoothability certificates to known classical ones. Particularly, we prove two conjectures of Dole\v{z}\'alek and Micha{\l}ek relating the tangency flattening and the $3\times3$ minor flattening to dimensions of tangent spaces to the Hilbert scheme of points.
arxiv:2610.17875.authors: Mat\v{e}j Dole\v{z}\'alek, Jakub Jagie{\l}{\l}a, Piotr Oszer, Tim Seynnaeve, Colin Stastny

arxiv:2610.17878.title: Moduli descriptions of v-sheaf local models
arxiv:2610.17878.summary: We propose a uniform moduli-theoretic description of the v-sheaf local model $\mathbb{M}_{\mathcal G,\mu}$ for an arbitrary parahoric group scheme $\mathcal G$ and an arbitrary dominant cocharacter $\mu$. Our approach is Tannakian and builds on a new theory of parahoric induced modules. When $\mu$ is minuscule, this framework explains the linear-algebraic conditions arising in the theory of local models of Shimura varieties.
arxiv:2610.17878.authors: Jo\~ao Louren\c{c}o, Timo Richarz, Eva Viehmann, Torsten Wedhorn

arxiv:2610.17884.title: The chromatic number of $G$-stable Kneser graphs
arxiv:2610.17884.summary: Extending the notions of Kneser graphs and Schrijver graphs, we define the $G$-stable Kneser graph $KG(G,k)$ (where $k\geq 2$ and $G$ is a graph on $n\geq 2k$ vertices) as the graph whose vertices are the $k$-element independent sets in $G$ and whose edges join pairs of disjoint independent sets. The well-known result of Lov\'{a}sz on the chromatic number of Kneser graphs implies that $\chi(KG(G,k)) \leq n-2k+2$ for any $G$. We call $G$ $k$-tight if equality holds, and we study the following question: Which graphs are $k$-tight?
arxiv:2610.17884.authors: Carmen Arana, Penny Haxell, Tom\'{a}\v{s} Kaiser, Mat\v{e}j Stehl\'{i}k

arxiv:2610.17891.title: The logarithmic exponent of the Ramsey number $r(4,t)$
arxiv:2610.17891.summary: We prove that $r(4,t) \ge \frac{t^3}{(\log t)^{2+o(1)}}$. This improves the lower bound of Mattheus and Verstra\"ete (Ann. of Math., 2024) by a factor of $(\log t)^{2-o(1)}$.

arxiv:2610.17964.title: Two-Dimensional Torus Action on the Quadric Threefold and GW-DT-GV Correspondence
arxiv:2610.17964.summary: We compute Gromov--Witten (GW) and Donaldson-Thomas (DT) invariants (including descendant invariants) for local CY $4$-folds over a smooth quadric threefold $Q$, up to degree $4$. We use the virtual localization formula with respect to a two-dimensional torus action to compute DT invariants. Combining these results with the computation of the J-function of the variety $Q$, we confirm the correspondence between DT and Gopakumar--Vafa invariants suggested by Cao--Maulik--Toda in genus zero.

arxiv:2610.17985.title: Cohomology ring of the strata of holomorphic differentials of genus 3
arxiv:2610.17985.summary: We prove that the rational Chow ring of every connected component of the multi-scale compactifications of the genus three strata $\mathcal{H}(4), \mathcal{H}(2,2)$ and $\mathcal{H}(3,1)$ is generated by boundary-stratum classes. Our proof shows Chow-K\"unneth generation property of boundary strata of the multi-scale compactification by reducing the boundary analysis to lower-genus generalized strata of meromorphic differentials, including residueless loci, described through plane-quartic and plane-cubic models. As a consequence, the rational cycle-class map is an isomorphism and the compactifications have no odd rational cohomology.

arxiv:2610.17988.title: The equivariant Ehrhart theory of polytopes with order-two symmetries: Part II
arxiv:2610.17988.summary: We give two counterexamples to Stapledon's Effectiveness Conjecture. Each counterexample is a $6$-dimensional lattice polytope with an order-two symmetry whose equivariant $H^*$-series $\varphi[t]$ is a polynomial with one coefficient that is not effective. For polytopes with a symmetry of order two, the goal of this paper is to build up a picture of the landscape of results for when the Effectiveness Conjecture holds.

arxiv:2610.17992.title: Colored Tur\'an densities and finite directed templates
arxiv:2610.17992.summary: Classical Tur\'an theory relates the asymptotic extremal problem for an ordinary forbidden graph to its chromatic number. This principle fails when a forbidden copy must respect prescribed vertex colors, as occurs naturally in multipartite extremal problems and in embeddings with prescribed clusters. We study properly vertex-colored graphs whose hosts have a prescribed density between every pair of color classes, with containment interpreted through color-preserving homomorphisms.
arxiv:2610.17992.authors: Nannan Chen, Ander Lamaison, Heng Li, Hong Liu

arxiv:2610.18040.title: Contractor Filters
arxiv:2610.18040.summary: We introduce Contractor Filters (CFs), a set-membership architecture for nonlinear continuous-time state estimation with bounded uncertainties and sporadic outliers. CFs represent feasible states symbolically by compositions of contractors rather than rematerializing a geometric enclosure after each update. This provides an abstraction layer between the set-theoretic filtering equations and their numerical realization, so prediction, correction, ambiguity, and outlier handling can be expressed within one algebra without prescribing a state geometry.

arxiv:2610.18061.title: Non-additive symmetric rank-metric codes
arxiv:2610.18061.summary: We study non-additive rank-metric codes contained in the space of symmetric matrices over a finite field. Our main focus is on symmetric $2$-codes. For odd $q$, we introduce a quotient construction for $\mathrm{Sym}_3(q)$ in which rank-one differences are described by isotropic vectors of a nondegenerate quadratic form on $\mathbb F_q^4$.

arxiv:2610.18070.title: Groups with the fixed-point property
arxiv:2610.18070.summary: We propose the study of the class of groups that fix a point for every continuous action on any convex compact space. Oliver completed the corresponding program of classifying the finite groups that have this fixed-point property in finite dimensions. Turning to infinite groups, the Schauder--Tychonoff theorem establishes that the integers have the fixed-point property, but this has not been shown for any other infinite, finitely generated group.
arxiv:2610.18070.authors: Nicolas Monod, Omer Tamuz, Lizzy Teryoshin

arxiv:2610.18078.title: An application of the parameterization method to evolution flows associated to nonautonomous systems
arxiv:2610.18078.summary: Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional complete Riemannian manifold of bounded geometry. We consider a time-dependent vector field $X : \mathbb{R} \times M \to TM$ with $X_t:=X(t,\cdot) \in \mathfrak{X}^r(M)$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$ that satisfies some further uniform continuity assumptions. We suppose that $X$ admits a globally defined integral curve $\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to M$.

arxiv:2610.18087.title: Computational framework NetBiF predicts and classifies steady-state bifurcations in biochemical systems via reaction network structure
arxiv:2610.18087.summary: Dynamics of biochemical systems are dictated by the stoichiometry and kinetics of reaction networks. These systems may admit positive steady states that could undergo qualitative change in response to varying rate parameters. These changes are called steady-state bifurcations, and they correspond to biologically meaningful processes.
arxiv:2610.18087.authors: Al Jay Lan J. Alamin, Bryan S. Hernandez

arxiv:2610.18094.title: Degree growth of rational and meromorphic self-maps
arxiv:2610.18094.summary: Let $f$ be a dominant rational self-map of a normal projective variety over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic, or a dominant meromorphic self-map of a compact K\"ahler manifold. We prove that in every codimension, the degree sequence of $f$ differs from its dynamical-degree growth by at most a polynomial factor, with an explicit universal bound on the polynomial exponent. In particular, subexponential but superpolynomial degree growth cannot occur.

arxiv:2610.18148.title: Topological entropy of saturated sets for Lorenz attractors
arxiv:2610.18148.summary: We study the topological entropy of saturated sets for continuous flows, with emphasis on singular hyperbolic dynamics. For a $C^r$-generic ($r \geq 2$) vector field $X$ carrying a geometric Lorenz attractor $\Lambda$, we prove that for every nonempty compact connected set $\mathcal{K} \subseteq \mathcal{M}(\Phi,\Lambda)$ and every open set $U \subseteq M$ with $U \cap \Lambda \neq \emptyset$, $h_{\mathrm{top}}(\Phi,G_{\mathcal{K}}(\Phi) \cap \operatorname{Trans}(\Phi,\Lambda) \cap U)=\inf_{\mu \in \mathcal{K}} h_\mu(\phi_1)$, where $\Phi=(\phi_t)_{t \in \mathbb{R}}$ is the flow induced by $X$ and $\operatorname{Trans}(\Phi,\Lambda)$ denotes the set of points whose positive orbits are dense…
arxiv:2610.18148.authors: Zheng Huang, Xueting Tian, Xiaodong Wang, Xutong Zhao

arxiv:2610.18152.title: Alternating Hamilton Paths and Cycles in Poset Products
arxiv:2610.18152.summary: We study alternating Hamilton paths and cycles in the comparability graphs of finite posets. We prove that if a finite poset $P$ with at least two elements admits an alternating Hamilton path, then $P\times B_r$ admits an alternating Hamilton cycle for every $r\ge2$, where $B_r$ is the Boolean lattice. As a corollary, we settle a conjecture of Katona [Discrete Appl.

arxiv:2610.18170.title: Automorphisms of medium algebras and quasi-anisotropic real affine Grassmannians
arxiv:2610.18170.summary: We study automorphisms of Hausel's medium algebras by identifying them with equivariant cohomology algebras of affine Schubert varieties of a complex reductive group $G$. The automorphisms in question are then given by the action of either complex automorphisms or real structures of $G$ on affine Schubert varieties. We focus on describing the fixed points of those automorphisms on the spectra of medium algebras, and prove that the torsion-free quotients of the corresponding coinvariant algebras are isomorphic to equivariant cohomology rings of fixed loci in affine Schubert varieties.

arxiv:2610.18199.title: A counting proof for the smallest critical set in a Latin square
arxiv:2610.18199.summary: A critical set in a Latin square is a set of entries that determines the square uniquely and is minimal with this property. We prove that every partial Latin square of order $n$ with fewer than $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor$ filled cells has an even number of completions. Consequently every critical set in every Latin square of order $n$ has at least $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor$ entries.

arxiv:2610.18213.title: Combinatorial bounds for the v-number of binomial edge ideals
arxiv:2610.18213.summary: We study the local $\mathrm v$-numbers of binomial edge ideals from a combinatorial perspective. For each minimal prime $P_{\mathcal S}$ of $J_G$, indexed by a cutset $\mathcal S$ of $G$, we consider two combinatorial invariants, $\mathrm v^-_{\mathcal S}(G)$ and $\mathrm v^+_{\mathcal S}(G)$, defined in terms of transversals of suitable hypergraphs, and show that the local $\mathrm v$-number $\mathrm v_{P_{\mathcal S}}(J_G)$ satisfies $\mathrm v^-_{\mathcal S}(G)\leq \mathrm v_{P_{\mathcal S}}(J_G)\leq \mathrm v^+_{\mathcal S}(G)$. Under a suitable hypothesis on the connected components, we provide explicit graph-theoretic descriptions of these invariants and analyze when they coincide,…

arxiv:2610.18221.title: Frobenius liftability of isolated complete intersections
arxiv:2610.18221.summary: We classify Frobenius liftable normal isolated complete intersection singularities of dimension at least three over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic. In dimension three, they are precisely the regular points and the ordinary double points; in higher dimensions, they are regular. We also characterize Frobenius liftability of the complete local hypersurfaces defined by $xy-g(z,t)$ without assuming that the singularity is isolated.

arxiv:2610.18226.title: Counting matrices with given characteristic polynomial
arxiv:2610.18226.summary: Let $f$ be a monic polynomial of degree $n$ with integer coefficients. We use Fourier analysis to prove a new upper bound on the number of $n\times n$ matrices with characteristic polynomial $f$ and integer entries in $[-T,T]$, as $T\to \infty$. The implied constant in our bound only depends on $n$ and is otherwise uniform in $f$.
arxiv:2610.18226.authors: Tim Browning, Fabian Gundlach, Will Sawin

arxiv:2610.18235.title: On Chen's conjecture for the log-concavity of the longest increasing subsequence distribution
arxiv:2610.18235.summary: Let $P_{n,k}$ count permutations of $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ whose longest increasing subsequence has length $k$. Chen conjectured that $(P_{n,k})_{k=1}^n$ is log-concave for every positive integer $n$. In this paper, we prove that Chen's conjecture is true when $n\ge 10^{10^{65}}$.

arxiv:2610.18239.title: River ribbon tableaux and symmetric group characters
arxiv:2610.18239.summary: We introduce river ribbon tableaux, where a river of non-trivial ribbons is placed between two banks of single boxes. Compared to other ribbon peelings, this reduces the geometric differences across diagrams of different shapes, and the maximal number of ribbon configurations. This allows us to prove a uniform character bound for symmetric groups which, specialized to balanced diagrams, proves the conjecture of Moore and Russell.

arxiv:2610.18246.title: Integral trace duality and the Witt filtration on Lubin--Tate space
arxiv:2610.18246.summary: Let $\mathcal O$ be the Lubin--Tate deformation ring of a one-dimensional commutative formal group of finite height $n\geq1$ over a perfect field $k$ of characteristic $p$. We identify Rezk's Witt filtration $\{I_d\}$ with the divisibility filtration of integral trace pairings on subgroup algebras of fixed source lifts. This gives the geometric recursion \[ I_{d+1}=pI_d+J_{d,z}\qquad(d\geq0), \] where $J_{d,z}$ defines the targets of order-$p^d$ quotient isogenies from a $W(k)$-valued lift $z$ of the closed point.

arxiv:2610.18259.title: Square-Root Profiles and Sharp Fourier Decay of Quasiperiodic Spectral Measures
arxiv:2610.18259.summary: We study spectral measures of one-dimensional quasiperiodic Schr\"odinger operators. For subcritical Schr\"odinger operator with Diophantine frequency, we prove sharp measurable-set bounds, answering a question of Avila and Jitomirskaya \cite{AJ}; we prove optimal Fourier decay and the sharp decay order of the time-averaged quantum return probability, confirming a conjecture of Aloisio, Carvalho, and de Oliveira \cite{ACO} and a prediction of Zhong and Mosseri \cite{ZhongMosseri}. For the subcritical almost Mathieu operator, we establish summable square-root envelopes for the spectral density, with an optimal density-one formulation of the lower bound, thereby answering a question of Avila…

arxiv:2610.18261.title: The influence of decay in dynamic models of gene regulatory networks
arxiv:2610.18261.summary: We investigate the influence of decay rates on the dynamics of three-dimensional gene regulatory networks modeled by nonlinear differential equations with logistic sigmoidal regulatory functions. Particular attention is paid to the existence, location, and stability of equilibrium points in systems involving numerous interacting parameters. An explicit analytical representation of a central equilibrium is obtained under suitable relations between the regulatory weights, thresholds, and decay coefficients, allowing its location to be determined without solving the corresponding nonlinear algebraic system numerically.

arxiv:2610.18277.title: Goodman-type lower bounds for odd cycles I: The dense regime
arxiv:2610.18277.summary: Goodman proved a lower bound on triangle counts which, in graphon language, states that every graphon of edge density $p$ has triangle density at least $2p^2-p$. Bennett, Dudek, Lidick\'{y}, and Pikhurko established the corresponding bound for $C_5$, determining its minimum density at every Tur\'an density $p=1-1/k$ with an integer $k\ge3$. We extend this bound to every odd cycle in the dense regime: for every odd integer $m\ge3$ and every graphon $W$ with edge density $p\ge2/3$, $t(C_m, W) \ge p^m-p(1-p)^{m-1}.$ For $2/3\le p<1$, equality holds precisely for balanced complete $k$-partite graphons with an integer $k\ge3$, up to graphon equivalence, and we establish qualitative stability at…
arxiv:2610.18277.authors: Seonghyuk Im, Taeyoung Kim, Hongseok Yang

arxiv:2610.18283.title: Stable manifolds of heteroclinic chains in Ho\v{r}ava-Lifshitz cosmology
arxiv:2610.18283.summary: We consider vacuum spatially homogeneous models in Ho\v{r}ava-Lifshitz gravity, which are expected to describe generic singularities for these modified gravity theories. These models perturb the well-known Bianchi models in general relativity (GR) by a parameter $v\in (0,1)$, in which GR occurs at $v=1/2$. We show that all periodic heteroclinic chains of Bianchi type II orbits are robust for small perturbations of GR, i.e. they exist for any $v\approx 1/2$.

arxiv:2610.18302.title: Actions in varieties of non-associative algebras: a survey
arxiv:2610.18302.summary: This article surveys the main results on the representability of internal actions in varieties of non-associative algebras over a field. We begin by recalling the general framework of internal actions and split extensions in semi-abelian categories, before specialising to Orzech categories of interest and varieties of non-associative algebras. We discuss action representability, weak action representability, and action accessibility, with emphasis on the relationship between the latter two notions.

arxiv:2610.18319.title: Untrodden pathways in the study of partitions with parts separated by parity
arxiv:2610.18319.summary: In this paper, we study a partition function with parts separated by parity from a family of partition functions introduced by Andrews in 2019. We first show that its generating function admit representation in terms of mock modular forms of weight $3/2$. We then initiate a study of smallest-part partition function analogues of partitions with parts separated by parity, which, to the best of our knowledge, has not previously been investigated in the literature.

arxiv:2610.18324.title: Lifting Prym Divisors on a Bielliptic Loop of Loops
arxiv:2610.18324.summary: Let $C$ be a bielliptic curve over an algebraically closed nonarchimedean field of odd characteristic or characteristic zero, and let $f \colon \widetilde{C} \to C$ be an \'{e}tale double cover. We prove that, if $f$ specializes to a certain double cover of a loop of loops, then every Prym divisor on the loop of loops lifts to a Prym divisor of the same rank on $\widetilde{C}$. As consequences, we compute the dimension of the Prym-Brill-Noether variety $V^r (C,f)$, show that it is reduced and irreducible when the dimension is positive, and compute its cohomology class.
arxiv:2610.18324.authors: Phew Aung, Eric Burkholder, Joan Dalton, David Jensen, Jacob Letamendi, Brianna Nguyen, Andrew Radicker, Doel Rivera Laboy

arxiv:2610.18329.title: Nonuniform dichotomies via time rescaling
arxiv:2610.18329.summary: We establish characterizations of general nonuniform dichotomies for linear nonautonomous dynamical systems in terms of nonuniform exponential dichotomies of appropriately time-rescaled systems. In discrete time, for a class of slowly growing rates, such a characterization requires an additional condition involving a suitable notion of nonuniform ordinary dichotomy, which can be omitted for invertible systems. In continuous time, we obtain a more general characterization for a large class of growth rates, without imposing this additional condition.

arxiv:2610.18340.title: Prescribed and simultaneous failures of log-concavity in trees with perfect matchings
arxiv:2610.18340.summary: We construct trees with perfect matchings and independence sequences that fail log-concavity near the independence number $\alpha$. For every integer $k\geq1$, one family fails at $\alpha-k$ and has a witness of order $O(k^2\log(k+2))$. For every integer $t\geq2$, a single tree has simultaneous failures at $\alpha-1,\alpha-3,\ldots,\alpha-(2t-1)$, with a witness of order $O(t^3)$.

arxiv:2610.18346.title: Waring rank of certain complete intersection forms
arxiv:2610.18346.summary: The complete intersection forms are the homogeneous polynomials whose annihilator ideal or the Macaulay dual, is an Artinian complete intersection ideal. In this paper, we compute the Waring rank of certain complete intersection forms. As an application, we compute the Waring rank of binomials whose annihilator is a complete intersection ideal.
arxiv:2610.18346.authors: Meghana Bhat, Enrico Carlini, Shreedevi K. Masuti, Ronnie Sebastian

arxiv:2610.18349.title: On the existence of $F$-irregular graphs for disconnected graphs $F$
arxiv:2610.18349.summary: For a given graph $F$, a graph $G$ is $F$-irregular if all its vertices have pairwise distinct $F$-degrees, where the $F$-degree of a vertex $v$ is the number of subgraphs of $G$ containing $v$ and isomorphic to $F$. While the existence of $F$-irregular graphs has been actively studied for connected graphs $F$, the case where $F$ is disconnected remains entirely unexplored. In this paper, we provide a complete solution to this problem.

arxiv:2610.18371.title: A Combinatorial Proof of Partition Identities for the Number of Distinct Part Sizes
arxiv:2610.18371.summary: In 1984, Bressoud and Subbarao established an interesting weighted partition identity connecting the partition function and the divisor function. Recently, the first author, jointly with Bhoria, Eyyunni, and Maji, extended the work of Bressoud and Subbarao and obtained the following analogous weighted partition identity. For any $n \in \mathbb{N}$, they obtained \begin{equation*} p^{(2)}(n) = \sum_{\pi \in \mathcal{D}(n)} (-1)^{ \# (\pi) }s(\pi) \left( \ell(\pi) - s(\pi) \right).

arxiv:2610.18377.title: Proof of a nonnegativity conjecture of Prellberg--Stanton
arxiv:2610.18377.summary: In 1994, Friedman, Joichi and Stanton conjectured that coefficients of the power-series $q+(1-q)\prod_{i=n}^{2n-1}\frac{1}{1-q^{i}}$ are nonnegative for $n\geq3$ and $n$ being odd. Let $\qbinom nm$ denote the Gaussian polynomial. In 2003, Prellberg and Stanton conjectured that coefficients of the power-series $(1-q)\qbinom nm\prod_{i=0}^{m-1}\frac{1}{1-q^{i+m}}$ are nonnegative for $0<m<n$, except when $n$ is even and $m\in\{2,n-2\}$.
arxiv:2610.18377.authors: Hong-Zhang Ai, Lili Mu, Bao-Xuan Zhu

arxiv:2610.18392.title: Coding multiplicity in self-similar sets on the line
arxiv:2610.18392.summary: We study coding multiplicity for self-similar sets on the real line. When the similarity dimension exceeds one, almost every point with respect to the natural self-similar measure has infinitely many codings. We focus on the case when the similarity dimension is at most one.

arxiv:2610.18394.title: Improved Upper Bounds for the Rank of the Determinant Tensor via Glynn's Formula
arxiv:2610.18394.summary: In this paper, we improve the upper bound for the tensor rank of the $n \times n$ determinant tensor to $\mathcal{B}_n-2^{n-1}+n+1$ by finding a new tensor decomposition of the tensor, where $\mathcal{B}_n$ denotes the $n$-th Bell number. The main idea is to replace a part of the tensor decomposition suggested by Houston--Goucher--Johnston with a tensor that is essentially the same as the $n \times n$ permanent tensor, and to use Glynn's formula. This upper bound gives an improved upper bound for the Waring rank of the $n \times n$ determinant polynomial for $n \geq 17$ as well.
arxiv:2610.18394.authors: Jeong-Hoon Ju, Hayoung Choi, Taehyeong Kim

arxiv:2610.18395.title: Remarks on the monodromy conjecture for symmetric determinantal hypersurfaces
arxiv:2610.18395.summary: We compute the local and global Denef--Loeser topological zeta functions of the determinant on the space of symmetric matrices. It verifies the strong monodromy conjecture of the symmetric determinant function. The computation relates to the geometry of complete quadrics and wonderful embeddings.

arxiv:2610.18402.title: Ramsey properties of trees and $C$-relations via the partite construction
arxiv:2610.18402.summary: Finite convexly ordered binary branching $C$-relations have been viewed as a notable exception to the broad applicability of the partite construction in structural Ramsey theory. The absence of a proof of their Ramsey property by the partite construction was noted by Bodirsky in his 2015 survey and pointed out again by Hubi\v{c}ka and Kone\v{c}n\'y in their 2026 survey. We overcome this limitation by giving proofs based on the partite construction of the known Ramsey properties of the class $\mathcal{CT}$ of finite convexly ordered treeable meet semilattices and of the classes of finite convexly ordered $C$-relations with arbitrary branching and with binary branching.

arxiv:2610.18409.title: Full classification of $\mathbb{Z}_{p^s}$-linear generalized Hadamard codes
arxiv:2610.18409.summary: The $\mathbb{Z}_{p^s}$-additive codes are subgroups of $\mathbb{Z}_{p^s}^n$. A $\mathbb{Z}_{p^s}$-linear generalized Hadamard (GH) code is a GH code over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ which is the Gray map image of a $\mathbb{Z}_{p^s}$-additive code. A recursive construction gives such codes $H_p^{t_1,\dots,t_s}$, of type $(n;t_1,\dots,t_s)$ and length $p^t$, and a partial classification of them is known.

arxiv:2610.18416.title: A parity constraint on the topological numbers of self-complementary triply-periodic surfaces
arxiv:2610.18416.summary: The stability zone of Novikov's problem of planar sections of triply periodic surfaces are labeled by indivisible triples of integers, which we call the soul of the zone. Which triples may occur is not known. We show that, if a Morse function $f$ on $\mathbb T^3$ admits a translation $\tau(x)=x+v$ with $f\circ\tau=-f$, so that the sets $\{f<0\}$ and $\{f>0\}$ are congruent, then in the generic genus-$3$ situation every topological number $L$ satisfies $\langle L,2v\rangle\equiv1\pmod2$.

arxiv:2610.18463.title: The group generated by a graph's derangements
arxiv:2610.18463.summary: We introduce the leap group of a graph, the subgroup of the symmetric group on the vertex set generated by graph derangements. We summarize historical results on graph derangements, which we call hops, and prove additional existence and complexity results. The leap groups of various canonical graphs are computed, and their behavior under basic graph operations is analyzed.

arxiv:2610.18480.title: When do lazy and invertible cellular automata generate all cellular automata?
arxiv:2610.18480.summary: Let $G$ be a group and let $A$ be a set with at least two elements. A lazy cellular automaton over $A^G$ acts as the identity except at the cells where a fixed pattern occurs, where it replaces the central symbol by a fixed different symbol. Let $M(G;A)$ be the submonoid of $\mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ generated by the lazy and the invertible cellular automata.

arxiv:2610.18489.title: Irrational families of Fano weighted complete intersection fourfolds
arxiv:2610.18489.summary: We study the irrationality of smooth Fano complete intersection fourfolds in weighted projective spaces, using an atom theoretic approach based solely on Gromov--Witten invariants. We prove symplectic irrationality, and hence irrationality for every smooth member, in a wide range of families for which irrationality was previously known only for very general members.
arxiv:2610.18489.authors: Jiaji Cai, Andrew Harder, Sukjoo Lee

arxiv:2610.18493.title: Tur\'an numbers of triangular pyramids
arxiv:2610.18493.summary: Let $\TP_k$ denote the triangular pyramid with $k$ layers. For a graph family $\mathcal F$, let $\ex(n,\mathcal F)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph containing no member of $\mathcal F$ as a subgraph. For a graph $H$, let $\cJ(H)$ be the family of subgraph-minimal graphs among all such graphs $H-I$, where $I\subseteq V(H)$ is an independent set.
arxiv:2610.18493.authors: Chuanqi Xiao, Long-Tu Yuan, Xiaowen Zhang

arxiv:2610.18512.title: Haagerup-Izumi modular data from hyperbolic words: S-fold TQFTs, central charge, torsion and the Bethe vacua
arxiv:2610.18512.summary: The modular data of the doubles of the Haagerup--Izumi categories is a grafting of two finite metric groups (conjectured by Evans--Gannon, proved for untwisted categories by Gannon--Schopieray--Yadav). Gang and Kim found non-unitary modular data of this shape in the topological twist of rank-$0$ $S$-fold theories, from the Bethe vacua of an abelianised gauge theory. The aim is to understand rigorously the significance of the handle-gluing and fibering operators, and to construct the Bethe vacua.

arxiv:2610.18528.title: High-Arity Rademacher Complexity and Uniform Laws of Large Numbers
arxiv:2610.18528.summary: We characterize several properties of higher-arity function classes, specifically finite $\VC_k$-dimension, slicewise finite $\VC$-dimension, and finite slicewise Littlestone dimension, in terms of generalizations of Rademacher complexity. These characterizations sets up simple new proofs of several results on finite $\VC_k$-dimension and slicewise finite $\VC$-dimension. These include the preservation of finite $\VC_k$-dimension under taking expectations and uniform law of large numbers statements for both properties.

arxiv:2610.18530.title: Curvature, diameter and bounded Betti numbers
arxiv:2610.18530.summary: We consider the image of the comparison homomorphism from bounded cohomology to ordinary cohomology. Its dimension is called the bounded Betti number. In our earlier work we proved that the total bounded Betti number of a closed Riemannian $n$-manifold satisfying $\Ric\geq -(n-1)$ and $\Diam\leq D$ is bounded by a constant depending only on $n$ and $D$.

arxiv:2610.18562.title: Separating components of real algebraic varieties by cohomological invariants
arxiv:2610.18562.summary: Let $X$ be a smooth algebraic variety over $\mathbb{R}$. We study the separation of the connected components of $X(\mathbb{R})$ by equivariant cohomology, unramified cohomology, and signatures of unramified quadratic forms. Our results highlight how the geometry of $X$ influences these questions.

arxiv:2610.18574.title: Spectral radius and edge-disjoint spanning trees of graphs with edge connectivity
arxiv:2610.18574.summary: Let $\tau(G)$ denote the maximum number of pairwise edge-disjoint spanning trees contained in a graph $G$. Zhang and Fan [J. Graph Theory, 2026] posed the problem of determining the corresponding tight spectral-radius condition for every $s$-edge-connected graph with \[ k+1\leq s\leq2k-1, \] together with a characterization of the associated extremal graphs.
arxiv:2610.18574.authors: Jia Wei, Muhuo Liu, Zhifu You, Hong-Jian Lai

arxiv:2610.18595.title: Generalized Bogomolov--Gieseker inequalities via Frobenius
arxiv:2610.18595.summary: We establish a Bogomolov--Gieseker-type inequality for tilt-semistable objects on smooth projective varieties of dimension $\geq 3$, in the spirit of the Bayer--Macr\`i--Toda conjecture. A key ingredient is an analysis of the action of the Frobenius morphism on tilt-semistable objects. As an application, we prove the Castelnuovo Bound Conjecture, up to an explicit constant term.
arxiv:2610.18595.authors: Chunyi Li, Zhiyu Liu, Alexander Perry, Xiaolei Zhao

arxiv:2610.18600.title: Saturation and semisaturation of oriented graphs
arxiv:2610.18600.summary: We consider a natural extension of the classical saturation problem to oriented graphs, defined as the minimum number of edges in an oriented graph $H$ on $n$ vertices that avoids a fixed oriented graph $G$, but adding any missing edge to $H$ creates a copy of $G$. Our main result shows that saturation functions of oriented graphs attain at least four distinct orders of magnitude. In particular, if $G$ is acyclic, then its saturation function is bounded if and only if $G$ contains an isolated edge; otherwise, it is linear.

arxiv:2610.18618.title: A proof of the framed LMOV conjecture for links
arxiv:2610.18618.summary: We prove the Labastida--Mari\~no--Ooguri--Vafa conjecture for oriented links with arbitrary integer framings. Consequently, the framed reformulated invariants have finite integral LMOV expansions for every integer framing vector.
arxiv:2610.18618.authors: Kefeng Liu, Pan Peng, Shengmao Zhu

arxiv:2610.18620.title: On the existence of Gorenstein injective covers
arxiv:2610.18620.summary: For a locally finitely generated Grothendieck category, we characterise the Gorenstein injective covering property by several equivalent conditions, including closure under coproducts. To complete this characterisation, we construct a countable commutative Noetherian Cohen--Macaulay local ring of dimension one for which this property fails, answering negatively Iacob's question Question 1 whether character modules of Gorenstein injective modules over left Noetherian rings are Gorenstein flat. Using this characterisation, we prove that for Noetherian schemes the covering property is Zariski-local.
arxiv:2610.18620.authors: Yuhui Hua, Shun-Jie Li, Chencheng Zhang

arxiv:2610.18636.title: Two conjectures on the cospectrality of complete tripartite graphs are false
arxiv:2610.18636.summary: For a graph G of order n with adjacency eigenvalues lambda_1(G) >= ... >= lambda_n(G), the cospectrality of G within the set G of all graphs of order n is the smallest spectral distance from G to another graph of G. Abdollahi and Zakeri conjectured that for every n >= 4 the cospectrality of the complete tripartite graph K_{n,n,n}, both in the Manhattan and in the Euclidean spectral distance, is attained precisely at K_{n-1,n,n+1}. We show that both conjectures are false for every n >= 4, that is, in the whole range in which they are stated.
arxiv:2610.18636.authors: Irena M. Jovanovi\'c, Jelena Sedlar, Riste \v{S}krekovski

arxiv:2610.18647.title: Existence and Uniqueness Proof for the Transport Equation and the Orthogonal Dynamics Equation for Zwanzig's Projection on Gaussian Spaces: A Vanishing Viscosity Method
arxiv:2610.18647.summary: We prove the existence of unique solutions ${u\in H^1(0,T;L^2_\gamma(\mathbb{R}^n))\cap L^2(0,T;H^1_\gamma(\mathbb{R}^n))}$ of the transport equation $u_t=F\cdot\nabla u+f$ and the orthogonal dynamics equation ${u_t= Q_\text{Z} (F\cdot\nabla) Q_\text{Z} u+f}$, where $F$ is a time-independent vector field, $f$ is a forcing term, $P_\text{Z}=1-Q_\text{Z}$ is a Zwanzig projection (conditional expectation) on $L^2_\gamma(\mathbb{R}^n)$ defined by $P_\text{Z}h \propto \int h(\cdot ,y) \rho(\cdot,y)\rm{d}y$, and $\gamma$ is the standard Gaussian measure with density $\rho$. To this end, we develop a vanishing viscosity method based on the maximal regularity theory for the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck…

arxiv:2610.18657.title: Multidimensional Szemer\'edi Theorem for Pairwise Independent Jointly Intersective Polynomials
arxiv:2610.18657.summary: We develop a new approach to the Joint Intersectivity Conjecture of Bergelson, Leibman, and Lesigne for commuting transformations. The conjecture asserts that the necessary divisibility condition is the only obstruction to polynomial multiple recurrence and, consequently, to the multidimensional polynomial Szemer\'edi theorem. We establish the conjecture for pairwise independent polynomials, obtaining the first general result for sequences of arbitrary length beyond the classical one-transformation setting.

arxiv:2610.18666.title: Proofs of four Takigiku--Tsuchioka conjectures on level $2$ principal characters of $A_{2\ell-1}^{(2)}$
arxiv:2610.18666.summary: We prove four conjectures of Takigiku and Tsuchioka consisting of eight Rogers--Ramanujan type identities. Two conjectures involve triple sums and a third involves quadruple sums, and their product sides are certain level $2$ principal characters of $A_{13}^{(2)}$. The fourth conjecture gives multisum representations of certain level $2$ principal characters of $A_{2\ell-1}^{(2)}$.

arxiv:2610.18667.title: Analytic centralisers of quadratic germs and the Brjuno dichotomy
arxiv:2610.18667.summary: For $Q_\alpha(z)=e^{2\pi i\alpha}z+z^2$ with $\alpha$ irrational, we prove that the analytic centraliser of $Q_\alpha$ is trivial whenever $Q_\alpha$ is not analytically linearizable. Together with the quadratic Brjuno--Yoccoz theorem this gives a complete dichotomy, for the centraliser is infinite cyclic at the non-Brjuno parameters and conjugate to the group of nonzero complex dilations at the Brjuno parameters. The result extends the dense-parameter conclusion of Avila--Cheraghi--Eliad to every nonlinearizable member of the quadratic family.

arxiv:2610.18680.title: Cominuscule Richardson varieties
arxiv:2610.18680.summary: A Richardson variety in a cominuscule flag variety is defined by a skew shape of boxes. We prove that any cominuscule Richardson variety has a unique decomposition as a product of indecomposable cominuscule Richardson varieties, which are given by the connected components of the skew shape. We also prove that the first Chow group and the Picard group of a cominuscule Richardson variety are dual to each other; both are free abelian groups of rank equal to the number of indecomposable factors.

arxiv:2610.18698.title: A Randomized Approximation Algorithm for Doubly Free-Boundary Macdonald Processes
arxiv:2610.18698.summary: We construct an approximate sampler for finite doubly free-boundary Macdonald rail-yard processes with Macdonald, boundary, and edge parameters in $(0,1)$. The construction allows arbitrary finite sequences of additions and removals of horizontal or vertical strips and all four boundary types. It reverses a finite commutation--reflection history from a partition sequence whose entries are equal, with the common partition weighted by both boundaries.

arxiv:2610.18713.title: A proof of the rational exponents conjecture
arxiv:2610.18713.summary: The rational exponents conjecture of Erd\H{o}s and Simonovits asserts that for every rational $r\in [1,2]$ there exists a graph $H$ such that $\mathrm{ex}(n,H)=\Theta(n^r)$. We present a proof of this conjecture claimed by Epoch AI, explaining how it builds upon ideas and methods developed by many researchers.
arxiv:2610.18713.authors: David Conlon, Oliver Janzer, Tao Jiang, Jaehoon Kim, Joonkyung Lee, Hong Liu, Sean Longbrake, Liana Yepremyan

arxiv:2610.18718.title: The Becker-Gottlieb transfer is not functorial: An example using $C_\infty$-algebras
arxiv:2610.18718.summary: We prove that the Becker-Gottlieb transfer is not functorial, even on rational cohomology. More precisely, for any even $n \ge 4$, we construct a fibration $f \colon X \to S^{n+1}$ with fiber $S^2 \vee S^n$, and an oriented $S^1$-bundle $g \colon Y \to X$ such that the transfer of $f \circ g$ is non-trivial on rational cohomology. Since the transfer of an oriented $S^1$-bundle vanishes, this implies that the transfer of $f \circ g$ and the composite of the transfers of $f$ and $g$ induce different maps on rational cohomology and are thus not homotopic.

arxiv:2610.18720.title: The Becker--Gottlieb transfer is not functorial: An example based on units of group rings
arxiv:2610.18720.summary: We show by explicit counterexample that the Becker--Gottlieb transfer cannot be made functorial. A different counterexample using rational homotopy theory was discovered concurrently by the third author and Robin Stoll.
arxiv:2610.18720.authors: Georg Lehner, Cary Malkiewich, Florian Naef

arxiv:2610.18740.title: Selecting the 7th Smallest of 16 Elements Takes Exactly 28 Comparisons
arxiv:2610.18740.summary: Let $V_i(n)$ denote the minimum worst-case number of comparisons needed to find the $i$-th smallest of $n$ distinct elements. We construct algorithms showing $V_7(16)\le28$ and $V_8(16)\le29$, improving the previously reported upper bounds of 30 and 31. Together with known lower bounds, these results establish $V_7(16)=28$ and leave $V_8(16)\in\{28,29\}$.

arxiv:2610.18754.title: Generalized Thom Spectra, Conjugate Stacks, and truncated Brown-Peterson Spectra
arxiv:2610.18754.summary: We propose a of definition conjugate stack for a class of suitable $\mathbb{E}_3$-$\mathrm{MU}$-algebras that includes the truncated Brown-Peterson spectra $\mathrm{BP}\langle n \rangle$ for all heights $n$. Then we calculate part of $\mathrm{BP}\langle n \rangle^{\mathrm{conj}}$ as a quotient stack in terms of Witt vectors. To perform this computation we study generalized Thom spectra and their relative Topological Hochschild Homology.

arxiv:2610.18783.title: Stably exotic knotted surfaces up to equivalence
arxiv:2610.18783.summary: In this short note we show the existence of stably exotic knotted surfaces in 4-manifolds in the sense that the embedded surfaces are topologically equivalent but are not smoothly equivalent even after any number of internal and external stabilisations.

arxiv:2610.18788.title: A three-block higher-rank deformed Hermitian--Yang--Mills correspondence on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$
arxiv:2610.18788.summary: We study the invariant rank-four deformed Hermitian--Yang--Mills equation associated with the chain $\mathcal{O}(1)\to\mathcal{O}(2)^{\oplus2}\to\mathcal{O}(3)$ over $\mathbb P^1$, with vertical weights $(4,2,0)$ and a fixed product K\"ahler class and phase. For arbitrary linear arrows $\psi=Bz$ and $\phi=(Az)^T$, smooth strictly calibrated reduced solutions exist exactly when $A$ is invertible and $z^TA^TBz$ is not identically zero. The same condition characterizes stability, semistability and polystability in the specified equivariant coherent category.

arxiv:2610.18801.title: Cellular Algebra of $A_2$ webs
arxiv:2610.18801.summary: We introduce a diagram algebra $\mathcal{K}_L$ based on Kuperberg's $A_2$-webs and prove a Schur--Weyl duality $\mathcal{K}_L \cong \operatorname{End}_{U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3)}((V^+ \oplus V^-)^{\otimes L})$, where $V^\pm$ are the fundamental representations of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$. Thus, $\mathcal{K}_L$ is a natural $A_2$ analogue of the Temperley--Lieb algebra. We construct an explicit cellular structure for $\mathcal{K}_L$, with the web basis as its cellular basis and cell modules indexed by dominant $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$-weights.
arxiv:2610.18801.authors: Azat M. Gainutdinov, Jesper Lykke Jacobsen, Yueheng Li

arxiv:2610.18803.title: The Links--Gould polynomial of an alternating link is alternating
arxiv:2610.18803.summary: Building on work of Kauffman--Saleur and earlier work of the second author, we derive a determinant formula for the Links--Gould polynomial of links. As an application, we prove a 20-year-old conjecture of Ishii: for any alternating link, the Links--Gould invariant is an alternating polynomial.

arxiv:2610.18841.title: Arithmetic hyperbolic manifolds with bounded rank
arxiv:2610.18841.summary: We prove that closed arithmetic hyperbolic $n$-manifolds of bounded rank have bounded adjoint trace field degree, and consequently have lower bounded injectivity radius. From this, we obtain a number of corollaries. In particular, we obtain that closed arithmetic hyperbolic $3$-manifolds of bounded rank are contained in finitely many commensurability classes, and describe these commensurability classes.

arxiv:2610.18856.title: Exact Topological Compliance: Generating Persistence-Equivalent Graphs
arxiv:2610.18856.summary: Persistent homology summarizes the topological evolution of a graph as persistence diagrams (PDs). Generating graphs whose topology matches a target descriptor is increasingly important, yet existing topology-aware generative models rely on soft regularization, producing graphs whose PDs may only be approximately similar. We initiate a principled investigation of the generation problem: produce graphs that realize a target PD exactly.
arxiv:2610.18856.authors: Mattie Ji, Indradyumna Roy, Vikas Garg

arxiv:2610.18859.title: Szemer\'edi's theorem with random differences and arithmetic Kakeya
arxiv:2610.18859.summary: We prove that there exists an absolute constant $c > 0$ such that the following holds for every $k \ge 3$ and $p \ge n^{-c / \log \log k}$. Letting $\delta > 0$ and $D \sim [n]_p$, with high probability every ${S \subset [n]}$ with $|S| \ge \delta n$ contains a $k$-term arithmetic progression whose common difference lies in $D$. This improves the best known bounds for the threshold of Szemer\'edi's theorem with random differences for all sufficiently large $k$, previously of the form ${p \ge n^{-2/k+o(1)}}$, due to Bri\"et and Castro-Silva.

arxiv:2610.18876.title: Complete counterexamples to Mubayi's supersaturation conjecture for graphs
arxiv:2610.18876.summary: For a graph $F$, its extremal number ${\rm ex}(n,F)$ and extremal graphs denote the maximum number of edges in $F$-free graphs and the graphs attaining this maximum, respectively. Let $h_F(n,q)$ be the minimum number of copies of $F$ in an $n$-vertex graph with ${\rm ex}(n,F)+q$ edges, and let $t_F(n,q)$ denote the corresponding minimum obtained by adding $q$ edges to an extremal graph.
