Mubayi (2013) conjectured that for every non-$r$-partite stable $r$-uniform hypergraph $F$ with $r\ge 2$, $h_F(n,q)\ge q\cdot t_F(n,1)$ holds for all sufficiently large $n$ and all integers $q\ge 1$.

arxiv:2610.18887.title: Ending currents of hyperbolic group actions
arxiv:2610.18887.summary: We develop a theory of ending currents for properly discontinuous isometric actions of hyperbolic groups on Gromov hyperbolic spaces, generalizing Thurston's ending laminations. Several natural generalizations are considered, which agree in the 3-dimensional hyperbolic setting but are otherwise distinct. We illustrate these invariants and their differences by several examples, including closed surface group actions on hyperbolic group extensions arising from Teichm\"uller theory and a geometrically finite action of a closed surface group on $\mathbb{H}^4$ with a single cusp that corresponds to a non-simple curve on the surface.

arxiv:2610.18901.title: Uniform adjacency-degree probes from differential rigidity
arxiv:2610.18901.summary: We construct a fixed triangular family of noncommutative polynomials that spans the joint cyclic module of a real symmetric pair from any prescribed vector. In dimension at most $N$, when the second matrix has spectral diameter at most $N-1$, the family has $N(N+1)/2$ members, degree at most $N-1$, and a shared arithmetic circuit of size $O(N^2)$. No rank-dependent choice of coefficients is made.

arxiv:2610.18905.title: Stabilizer entropy cones as self-dual slices of linear rank cones: a five-party gap and dependence on the local dimension
arxiv:2610.18905.summary: Entanglement entropies of multipartite pure states satisfy linear inequalities; for stabilizer states, the backbone of quantum error correction, the achievable entropy vectors generate a convex cone. We show that, after a linear lift, the closure of this cone is exactly the self-dual slice of a classical object on one more element than there are parties: the closed cone generated by the rank functions of arrangements of subspaces over $\mathrm{GF}(d)$ for a prime local dimension $d$, and of subgroups of abelian groups of exponent dividing $d$ in general. This correspondence brings two features of rank inequalities into play.

arxiv:2610.18907.title: Ordinary and measurable colorings of Euclidean three-space
arxiv:2610.18907.summary: A proper coloring of Euclidean space is a coloring that assigns different colors to points at distance one. Using the planar character-law rigidity theorem of OpenAI, we prove that every finite proper coloring of $\R^3$ can be replaced by a proper Lebesgue-measurable coloring with the same number of colors. As a corollary we obtain that the ordinary and measurable chromatic numbers of $\R^3$ are equal, and both lie between $7$ and $15$.
arxiv:2610.18907.authors: Mikhail Koshelev, Andrey Kupavskii, Vsevolod Voronov

arxiv:2610.18918.title: Short Proofs for the Minimum Number of Determined Circles
arxiv:2610.18918.summary: We present short proofs for the main parts of the recently completed solution of Erd\H{o}s Problem 506, which asks for the minimum number of distinct circles determined by a finite planar point set that is neither collinear nor concyclic. An inversion argument and a seven-point line lemma show that eight points determine at least $17$ circles, and an explicit configuration attains this bound. A single argument combining Melchior's inequality with Langer's incidence bound establishes the sharp formula for every $n\ge15$.
arxiv:2610.18918.authors: Stijn Cambie, Denis Paliy, Rafa{\l} Wrona

arxiv:2610.18920.title: Physiology-Informed Sparse Identification of Dynamic Crop Models
arxiv:2610.18920.summary: Developing resilient crops requires models that accurately capture how plant growth dynamics emerge from the continuous interplay between genetic and environmental factors. While high-throughput phenotyping platforms generate data for dynamic growth models, current modelling approaches show limitations: process-based crop growth models (CGMs) capture environmental dynamics but are difficult to scale across many genotypes because they require calibration of many parameters, while quantitative genetic models allow modelling many genotypes but often summarise time-varying environments using static covariates. To address this gap, we propose a data-driven framework to identify reduced systems…
arxiv:2610.18920.authors: Corn\'{e} Verburg, Alexander Heinlein, Fred van Eeuwijk, Neil Budko

arxiv:2610.18929.title: Packing intermediate dimensions of measures and applications
arxiv:2610.18929.summary: We introduce a spectrum of dimensions of measures, the \emph{packing intermediate dimensions} $\dim_{P,\theta}\mu$, $\theta\in(0,1]$, of a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and the \emph{quasi-Hausdorff dimension} $\dim_{qH}\mu$. We show that this spectrum encodes the information on $\mu$ that governs the packing dimension of its projections and H\"{o}lder images. First, $\dim_{qH}\mu$ is the exact threshold for the packing dimension profiles of Falconer and Howroyd: for every real $0<s\leq n$, $\dim_P^s\mu=s$ if and only if $s\leq\dim_{qH}\mu$.

arxiv:2610.18940.title: Index for a mutation loop
arxiv:2610.18940.summary: Motivated by the 3d-3d correspondence, we introduce an index $\mathcal{I}_g^\phi$ for a mutation loop $\phi$ of a quiver and an integer $g \geq 0$. We prove its integrality $\mathcal{I}_g^\phi \in \mathbb{Z}$ under certain conditions, which extends the integrality conjecture of Gang--Kim--Yoon for $3$-manifolds to the broader framework of mutation loops in cluster algebras. Our index also has an interpretation as the genus-$g$ partition function of a $(1+1)$-dimensional TQFT.

arxiv:2610.18944.title: Improved Sidorenko bound for hypergraph Turan densities
arxiv:2610.18944.summary: For every fixed integer $r\ge3$, we prove that the Tur\'an density of every $r$-uniform hypergraph $F$ with $m\ge1$ edges satisfies $\pi(F)\le1-c_rm^{-(r-1)/r}$, where $c_r>0$ depends only on $r$. This improves Sidorenko's general bound, whose gap from $1$ is of order $m^{-1}$. Complete $r$-uniform hypergraphs show that the exponent $(r-1)/r$ is optimal.
arxiv:2610.18944.authors: Shuyan Chen, Xinmin Hou, Xizhi Liu

arxiv:2610.18953.title: Invertible subalgebras for chiral semion topological order
arxiv:2610.18953.summary: Chiral topological order is incompatible with strictly two-dimensional local commuting-projector Hamiltonians on finite-dimensional tensor-product Hilbert spaces. Invertible subalgebras (ISAs) provide an alternative framework. We construct an ISA supporting chiral semions, together with its anti-semion commutant, on a square lattice with one qubit per edge.
arxiv:2610.18953.authors: Yu-An Chen, Meng Sun, Nathanan Tantivasadakarn, Zongyuan Wang, Bowen Yang

arxiv:2610.19004.title: Anomalies, higher symmetries, and homotopy theory I: crossed precosheaves and a nonabelian Cech construction
arxiv:2610.19004.summary: Symmetries of a quantum field theory or a quantum lattice model are expected to be described not by a group but by a homotopy type, whose homotopy groups are the higher symmetry groups and whose Postnikov invariants encode 't Hooft anomalies. We propose a homotopy-theoretic definition of 't Hooft anomalies based on the structure of localized symmetries in the operator-algebraic approach. The input is a crossed precosheaf: a collection of groups attached to regions of space, equipped with pairings recording that the commutator of two transformations localized in two regions is localized in their intersection.

arxiv:2610.19012.title: On the work of Graeme Segal
arxiv:2610.19012.summary: This is my written Laudatio for Graeme Segal on receiving the Chern Medal at the 2026 International Congress of Mathematicians. I make some general remarks about Segal's qualities as a mathematician. Then I discuss the origins of his work on classifying spaces of categories and Gamma-spaces.

arxiv:2610.19014.title: Internal partitions of $5$-regular and $8$-regular graphs
arxiv:2610.19014.summary: An \emph{internal partition} of a graph is a partition of its vertex set into two nonempty parts such that every vertex has at least half of its neighbors in its own part. DeVos asked whether, for every fixed positive integer $r$, all but finitely many $r$-regular graphs admit an internal partition. This was previously known to hold only for $r\in\{3,4,6\}$.

arxiv:2610.19019.title: Mixing Rates for Analytic Observables: Toral Endomorphisms and Anosov Blaschke Deformations
arxiv:2610.19019.summary: We analyze exponential mixing for analytic observables and show that mixing at a double exponential rate occurs for genuinely nonlinear systems. Neither its presence nor its sharp exponent is stable under arbitrarily small area-preserving perturbations in the real-analytic topology. We construct two families of area-preserving Anosov Blaschke product diffeomorphisms that converge in the real-analytic topology to the same hyperbolic toral automorphism.

arxiv:2610.19023.title: Invariant von Neumann subalgebras of crossed products and tensor products
arxiv:2610.19023.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a countable discrete group acting on a tracial von Neumann algebra $(Q,\tau_Q)$ in a trace-preserving way. We study invariant von Neumann subalgebras of $Q\rtimes\Gamma$ and of $L(\Gamma)\bar\otimes Q$, where the latter is equipped with the diagonal action. We show that, under the pointwise weak mixing assumption, an invariant subalgebra whose image under the canonical conditional expectation onto $Q$ is scalar is necessarily contained in $L(\Gamma)$.
arxiv:2610.19023.authors: Tattwamasi Amrutam, Artem Dudko, Yongle Jiang, Adam Skalski

arxiv:2610.19037.title: Reversible Higgs Bundles
arxiv:2610.19037.summary: We study reversible Higgs bundles on a compact Riemann surface $\Sigma$ of genus $g\geq 2$, that is, $G$-Higgs bundles $(E,\Phi)$ with $(E,\Phi)\cong(E,-\Phi)$. For a complex reductive group $G$ realized as a self-adjoint subgroup of $GL(n,\mathbb{C})$, we show that if $(E,\Phi)$ corresponds to a representation $\rho$ of $\pi_1(\Sigma)$, then $(E,-\Phi)$ corresponds to $(\overline{\rho}^{\,t})^{-1}$. As a consequence, the moduli space of reversible Higgs bundles is the fixed locus of an involution of the character variety and carries the structure of a real affine algebraic set.

arxiv:2610.19093.title: Finding non-bisimplicial and triad-free minimal separators
arxiv:2610.19093.summary: A $u\hbox{-}v$ separator in $G$ is a set $S\subseteq V(G)\setminus\{u,v\}$ such that there is no $u\hbox{-}v$ path in $G\setminus S$. A minimal separator in $G$ is a set $S$ such that for some $u,v\in V(G)\setminus S$, $S$ is a $u\hbox{-}v$ separator in $G$ but no proper subset of $S$ is. A set $S$ is bisimplicial if it is the union of at most two cliques.

arxiv:2610.19117.title: An algebro-geometric approach to profinite iterated monodromy groups
arxiv:2610.19117.summary: We carefully construct the profinite iterated monodromy group of a rational map as a quotient of the \'etale fundamental group of the punctured projective line. In doing so, we prove a number of folklore results regarding profinite IMGs; in particular, their topological generation by inertia concentrated in the post-critical orbit, and their relationship with the discrete iterated monodromy group over $\mathbb{C}$.

arxiv:2610.19119.title: A combinatorial proof of the Chan--Robbins--Yuen volume formula
arxiv:2610.19119.summary: The Chan--Robbins--Yuen polytope $\mathrm{CRY}_{m+1}$ has normalized volume $\prod_{j=1}^{m-1}C_j$, a product of Catalan numbers. Zeilberger proved the formula using the Morris constant-term identity; finding a combinatorial proof remained an open problem. We give such a proof by counting nonnegative integer flows.

arxiv:2610.19161.title: Remarks on Lattice Actions Corresponding to Automorphism Groups of Smooth Cubic Fourfolds
arxiv:2610.19161.summary: The automorphism groups of smooth cubic fourfolds over the complex numbers, together with actions on defining equations, are classified in previous works. In this paper, we complete the calculation of group actions on the primitive integral cohomology lattice for all of the $156$ families in the classification. We distinguish similar families, determine the remaining action-maximal cases, and use restriction to complete the list.

arxiv:2610.19193.title: A Bounded-Defect Construction for the Mondrian Art Problem
arxiv:2610.19193.summary: We construct an infinite family of solutions to the Mondrian art problem with absolute defect bounded above by $280$, of side lengths $n_0 = 315$, $n_1 = 106785$, and $n_{j+2} = 340n_{j+1} - n_j$, where $n_j$ is congruent to $315 \pmod{630}$. This absolute bound shows that the minimum defect does not necessarily increase with $n$, providing a counterexample to a conjecture which has been open since the problem's original proposal. Our design is derived from a well-known seven-rectangle dissection over the real quadratic field $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{19})$, with non-integer side lengths; we tailor the side lengths to be integers via an infinite Pell family.

arxiv:2610.19194.title: Enumeration of one-cycle signed chord diagrams and their duals for optimal Morse flows on closed surfaces
arxiv:2610.19194.summary: Optimal Morse vector fields on closed surfaces, i.e.\ fields with the minimal possible number of critical points (a single source and a single sink), are classified up to topological trajectory equivalence by one-cycle signed chord diagrams in Kybalko, Prishlyak and Shchurko (2018). We recall this construction and the associated duality, which corresponds to reversing the direction of the flow, in a unified encoding in which both endpoints of a chord carry the same label, and we make it algorithmic. We give an explicit traversal procedure that detects one-cycle diagrams, a canonical form of an equivalence class under cyclic shifts, reversal and relabeling of chords, and a construction of…

arxiv:2610.19205.title: Invariant factors from products of cyclotomic polynomials, with applications
arxiv:2610.19205.summary: Let $f,g\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$ be products of cyclotomic polynomials such that either $g/\gcd(f,g)$ or $f/\gcd(f,g)$ (or both) is squarefree. We give explicit formulae for the invariant factors of $f(C_g)$, where $C_g$ is the companion matrix of $g$, expressing them in terms of the indices and multiplicities of the cyclotomic factors of $f$ and $g$. A more compact formula holds for the circulant case $g(t)=t^n-1$, assuming that every cyclotomic factor shared by $f$ and $g$ has multiplicity $1$ in $f$.

arxiv:2610.19214.title: Orthogonal partition by four hyperplanes
arxiv:2610.19214.summary: We study orthogonal $(4,3)$-equipartitions of finite measures absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure: every three of four mutually orthogonal affine hyperplanes must divide each measure into eight equal parts. For every number $m$ of measures, we determine the exact dimension threshold of Musin's polynomial criterion and express it in terms of the binary expansion of $m$. The threshold coincides with the geometric lower bound precisely when $m=2^j-1$.
arxiv:2610.19214.authors: Alexey Fakhrutdinov, Platon Khamatov, Oleg R. Musin

arxiv:2610.19225.title: On generalized embeddability of a non-elliptic self-map
arxiv:2610.19225.summary: We study the structure of the centralizer of a non-elliptic holomorphic self-map of the unit disc and its relation with continuous dynamical structures. We prove that if the identity is not isolated in the centralizer of a non-elliptic self-map $\varphi \in \mathrm{Hol}(\mathbb D)$, then $\varphi$ is univalent and its centralizer contains a non-trivial continuous one-parameter semigroup of holomorphic self-maps. This result provides a general criterion for the existence of continuous dynamics arising from discrete iteration.
arxiv:2610.19225.authors: Manuel D. Contreras, Santiago D\'{\i}az-Madrigal, Pavel Gumenyuk

arxiv:2610.19236.title: An oral history of FPSAC
arxiv:2610.19236.summary: As its 40th anniversary nears, we present a history of the International Conference on Formal Power Series and Algebraic Combinatorics (FPSAC), through interviews with figures from its past, present, and future.

arxiv:2610.19249.title: Graph binomial coefficients and a positivity conjecture of Guo and Krattenthaler
arxiv:2610.19249.summary: We investigate Conjecture 7.4 of Guo and Krattenthaler \cite{GK}, which predicts that for every positive integer $n$, the polynomial \[ P_n(q) = \frac{(1-q)^2}{(1-q^{10n-1})(1-q^{15n-1})}\qbin{30n}{5n} \] has non-negative coefficients, except for $q^1$ and $q^{125n^2-25n+3}$, which equal $-1$. We study this problem through three main perspectives: First, by linking the boundary coefficients to the second differences of the partition function, we settle the first and last $25n+1$ coefficients via a novel partition injection. Second, by introducing a ``defect'' generalization of Andrews' classical lemma, we reduce the conjecture to an almost-unimodality property and employ a uniform…

arxiv:2610.19263.title: Exotic $\mathbb{R}^4$'s as unions of two thickened circles
arxiv:2610.19263.summary: We give an infinite family of non-diffeomorphic exotic $\mathbb{R}^4$'s, each of which is the union of two copies of a standard open tubular neighborhood of the circle, which intersect in a standard open tubular neighborhood of the wedge of two circles. This gives the simplest known decomposition of an exotic $\mathbb{R}^4$ into two open sets, making progress on Question 4.43 (A) of Kirby's 1995 problem list. The decompositions are obtained by studying fibered slice disk complements in certain Casson-Gordon homotopy 4-balls, for which we provide similar decompositions.

arxiv:2610.19333.title: Algebraic overtwistedness of contact $(+1)$-surgeries via augmented Floer theories
arxiv:2610.19333.summary: We prove that contact $(+1)$-surgery along a Legendrian $n$-sphere $\Lambda\subset(\mathbb{S}^{2n+1},\xi_{\mathrm{std}})$ with \[ \mathrm{tb}(\Lambda)\ne (-1)^{\frac{n(n-1)}{2}+1} \] has vanishing contact homology. In dimension three, this produces new examples of tight algebraically overtwisted contact manifolds, vastly extending the authors' previous results: If a Legendrian knot in $(\mathbb{S}^3,\xi_{\mathrm{std}})$ admits an exact, oriented Lagrangian filling that is not a disk, then contact $(+1/k)$-surgery on it is algebraically overtwisted and tight for every positive integer $k$. Our proofs use versions of symplectic cohomology and wrapped Floer cohomology defined by augmentations…
arxiv:2610.19333.authors: Russell Avdek, Youlin Li, Zhengyi Zhou

arxiv:2610.19340.title: Uniqueness of Limit Cycles for Abel Equations and Planar Systems
arxiv:2610.19340.summary: We study positive limit cycles of the Abel equation $$\dot{x}=A(t)x^{3}+B(t)x^{2},$$ where $A$ and $B$ are $2\pi$-periodic functions. By developing a half-period convexity method, we establish a new criterion ensuring that the equation has at most one positive limit cycle. Moreover, if such a limit cycle exists, it is hyperbolic.
arxiv:2610.19340.authors: Jos\'e Luis Bravo Trinidad, Renhao Tian, Yulin Zhao

arxiv:2610.19355.title: Two non-semisimple quantum invariants of lens spaces
arxiv:2610.19355.summary: We calculate the chromatic spherical invariant $\mathscr{K}_{\mathrm{Rep}(H)}(L(p,q))$ of lens spaces $L(p, q)$ for arbitrary finite-dimensional unibalanced, unimodular Hopf algebras $H$. In the case of the index-2 Nichols Hopf algebra $\mathcal{K}_2$ and $q=1$, we find that the invariant of $L(p, 1)$ depends only on the parity of $p$ for $p\geq 1$. We also describe the duals $\mathcal{S_I}(M)^*$ of the admissible skein modules of handlebodies $M=H_g$ and of $M=L(p, q)$ for arbitrary tensor ideals $\mathcal{I}$ of a ribbon tensor category.
arxiv:2610.19355.authors: Rhea Palak Bakshi, Mitchell Jubeir, Quinn T. Kolt

arxiv:2610.19357.title: On the Arnold corank, the Zariski multiplicity, and the tangent Milnor fiber problems
arxiv:2610.19357.summary: In this article, we approach the Arnold corank problem posed by Arnold himself in 1975, which asks whether the corank of a holomorphic function is a topological invariant. Here, the corank of a holomorphic function is the corank of its Hessian matrix at 0, which is one of the most basic and fundamental invariants of a holomorphic function. Here, we prove the topological invariance of the corank mod 2.

arxiv:2610.19360.title: Poincar\'e compactifications of pullbacks of parallel vector fields under counterexamples to the real Jacobian conjecture
arxiv:2610.19360.summary: Let $F: \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ be a polynomial map with nowhere zero Jacobian determinant. It is known that the global invertibility of $F$ is equivalent to the pullback of a parallel vector field being parallel. In this paper, we construct the phase portraits on the Poincar\'e disc of the pullbacks of the canonical annular, radial, and strip vector fields under non-injective maps $F$ that have recently appeared in the literature.

arxiv:2610.19363.title: Bicolored Eulerian quasisymmetric functions, affine lengths, and Theta operators
arxiv:2610.19363.summary: We introduce a $q$-analogue of the bicolored Eulerian quasisymmetric functions by incorporating an additional grading arising from affine length, obtained by interpreting bicolored permutations as affine permutations. We also provide an intrinsic description of this refinement in terms of bicolored permutations by introducing notions of alignments and crossings, together with an explicit bijection identifying these statistics with the alignments and crossings in the existing literature. Finally, we prove that our refinement is symmetric by expressing it in terms of the Theta operators appearing in the Theta coinvariant Conjecture and the modified Macdonald symmetric functions.

arxiv:2610.19400.title: Reduction for flag-transitive symmetric 2-designs with gcd(k, {\lambda}) = p
arxiv:2610.19400.summary: We study symmetric 2-(v, k, {\lambda}) designs admitting a flag-transitive point-primitive subgroup G of automorphisms, where gcd(k, {\lambda}) = p and p is a prime. In this paper, we show that G is of affine or almost simple type.
arxiv:2610.19400.authors: Ziwei Lu, Yu Sun, Shenglin Zhou

arxiv:2610.19434.title: Symplectic extension graphs and Ribet's lemma
arxiv:2610.19434.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime, and let $\rho\colon G\to \GSp_{2n}(\Z_p)$ be an irreducible symplectic residually multiplicity free representation. We define the symplectic extension graph $\Gamma_\rho^\GSp$ associated with $\rho$ to be the directed graph whose vertices are the residual factors of $\rho$ and a directed edge between two vertices corresponds to a nonsplit extension between the vertices realized by $\rho$. Using the Euclidean Bruhat--Tits building associated with $\GSp_{2n}(\Q_p)$, under some assumptions, we prove the existence of certain paths in $\Gamma_\rho^\GSp$ and show that $\Gamma_\rho^\GSp$ is a disjoint union of nonempty strongly connected subgraphs.

arxiv:2610.19437.title: Birational maps of moduli spaces of stable sheaves on a K3 surface induced by Fourier-Mukai transforms
arxiv:2610.19437.summary: We shall study birational maps of moduli spaces of stable sheaves on a K3 surface with Picard number 1 induced by Fourier-Mukai transforms.

arxiv:2610.19449.title: Fourier-Mukai transforms by a family of stable sheaves and preservation of stability
arxiv:2610.19449.summary: For a Fourier-Mukai transform whose kernel is a family of Gieseker stable sheaves, we shall give a condition for the preservation of Gieseker stability of sheaves.

arxiv:2610.19450.title: Every cubic graph has four total dominating sets covering each vertex at most twice
arxiv:2610.19450.summary: In 2018, Goddard and Henning conjectured that every cubic graph has four total dominating sets covering each vertex at most twice, and asked the analogous question for transversals of $3$-uniform $3$-regular hypergraphs. We prove the conjecture, which also answers the question in the affirmative.
arxiv:2610.19450.authors: Hyemin Kwon, Boram Park, Yoshio Sano

arxiv:2610.19451.title: High-Girth QLDPC Codes from Circulant and Affine Permutation Matrices
arxiv:2610.19451.summary: We study two explicit constructions of binary Calderbank--Shor--Steane quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes with check weight six. The first uses a fixed circulant shift pattern and yields parameters $\code{6N}{2N+2}{6}$ with Tanner graph girth twelve for $N=31$ and every $N\ge37$. A graph incidence interpretation gives the ranks and girths, and a uniform weight six logical operator establishes the exact distance.
arxiv:2610.19451.authors: Vahid Nourozi, Roxana Smarandache, David G. M. Mitchell{\dag}

arxiv:2610.19459.title: Quantum LDPC Codes from Polynomial Minors
arxiv:2610.19459.summary: We construct quantum codes from codewords of a cyclic code and the minors of a polynomial matrix. The construction uses a two-row, three-column matrix whose minors yield a second matrix satisfying the CSS orthogonality condition. We derive the code dimension from the greatest common divisors of the entries and minors, with a simplified formula for odd lifting factors.
arxiv:2610.19459.authors: Vahid Nourozi, Roxana Smarandache, David G. M. Mitchell

arxiv:2610.19467.title: Relative knot concordance
arxiv:2610.19467.summary: Motivated by the relative-slice problem in $4$-manifold topology, we define for a knot $R$ the notion of a relative knot concordance group $\mathcal{C}_R$ and analyze the structure of its algebraic analogue $\mathcal{AC}_R$ modulo torsion. Using Milnor signatures, we show that $\mathcal{AC}_R$ has infinite rank for every $R$. We also show that any prescribed finite set of natural numbers can be realized as orders of elements in a single relative concordance group.

arxiv:2610.19470.title: Positivity and negativity for $h$-bases for $n$
arxiv:2610.19470.summary: A set $A$ of integers is an $h$-basis for $n$ if every integer in $[0,n] = \{0,1,2,\ldots,n\}$ belongs to the sumset $hA$, that is, can be represented as the sum of exactly $h$ not necessarily distinct elements of $A$. The classical postage stamp problem asks for the largest integer $n_h(k)$ such that $[0,n_h(k)] \subseteq hA$ for some set $A$ of nonnegative integers of size $k+1$. We consider the effect of allowing negative elements.
arxiv:2610.19470.authors: Wouter van Doorn, Pietro Monticone, Melvyn B. Nathanson

arxiv:2610.19501.title: On generators and relations for $O_n^\circ(V)$ in higher-level Zhu algebras, Part I
arxiv:2610.19501.summary: We study the circle-relation subspace $O_n^\circ(V)$ in the defining relations of the level-$n$ Zhu algebra of a vertex operator algebra $V$. We assemble the residue relations generating $O_n^\circ(V)$ into generating functions and obtain an explicit recursion that replaces every sufficiently deep mode by retained modes with indices at least $-2n-1$, modulo $O_n^\circ(V)$. This recursion is encoded in a left truncated field $Y_L$.

arxiv:2610.19503.title: Right Coideal Subalgebras, Hopf Galois Objects, and $\imath$-Hopf Algebras
arxiv:2610.19503.summary: We study right comodule algebras and their connections with Hopf bi-Galois objects and right coideal subalgebras. For a Hopf $2$-cocycle $\sigma$ on $K$ and a unital right-colinear algebra map $\Gamma:A\to K$, we show that $\Gamma:A_\sigma\to K^\sigma$ is an algebra map precisely when $\sigma$ is trivial on $\operatorname{im}\Gamma\otimes\operatorname{im}\Gamma$. We describe comodule-algebra morphisms $A_\sigma\to K^\sigma$ by characters and establish injectivity criteria using the coradical and extensions of characters to convolution-invertible functionals.

arxiv:2610.19506.title: Arithmetic Visibility in Polygons: Curved Sight in the Art Gallery
arxiv:2610.19506.summary: In the classical art gallery problem, a guard sees a target when the segment joining them lies entirely within the polygon. We explore what changes when sight may bend along regular arcs on absolutely irreducible curves, but only those defined by primitive integer polynomials of total degree at most \(d\) and coefficient height at most \(H\). We call such curves admissible sight carriers.

arxiv:2610.19546.title: Shrinking targets versus recurrence: A survey on the Hausdorff dimension theory
arxiv:2610.19546.summary: This survey reviews results on the Hausdorff dimension of shrinking target sets and recurrence sets in dynamical systems. In their basic formulations, shrinking target sets concern orbits approaching a prescribed centre, whereas recurrence sets concern orbits returning close to their initial points. A central theme is the comparison of the Hausdorff dimensions of these two classes of limsup sets.
arxiv:2610.19546.authors: Zhang-nan Hu, Jun-jie Huang, Bing Li

arxiv:2610.19548.title: Continuous Narayana Interpolations: Hankel Total Positivity and Log-Convexity Preservation
arxiv:2610.19548.summary: We study a continuous interpolation between the type $B$ and shifted type $A$ Narayana triangles and its extension through affine moments of the continuous $q$-ultraspherical (Rogers) measure. For every fixed $0<q<1$ and $-1<\beta<1$, these affine moments form a coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive sequence in the polynomial variable $t$. The proof rests on a general continuant criterion: decreasing nonnegative off-diagonal weights and coefficientwise positivity of the leading continuants imply total positivity of the full tridiagonal matrix.

arxiv:2610.19558.title: The Two-Level Poset Game is PSPACE-Complete
arxiv:2610.19558.summary: Poset games form a fundamental class of combinatorial games that includes classical games such as Nim and Chomp. Determining the outcome of a poset game is known to be PSPACE-complete even for posets of height at most three. However, the exact computational complexity of Two-Level Poset Game, played on posets of height at most two, has remained an open problem for over a decade.

arxiv:2610.19586.title: Seven Limit Cycles in a Periodically Forced Three-Zone Equation
arxiv:2610.19586.summary: We construct a seven-cycle example for a periodically forced scalar equation with a continuous three-zone piecewise-linear nonlinearity. Symbolic integration and linear elimination reduce the four-flight matching conditions to two equations in the residence times. The competing exterior visits produce an additional turn of the critical response and lead to the rational parameters $(A,B,\mu)=(9,3/2,181363/100000)$.

arxiv:2610.19606.title: The $RO(C_2)$-graded Hurewicz image of Atiyah's Real K-theory
arxiv:2610.19606.summary: We determine the $RO(C_2)$-graded $k\mathbb R$-Hurewicz image, where $k \mathbb R$ denotes the connective Atiyah's Real $K$-theory spectrum. As a consequence, we obtain four infinite families in the $RO(C_2)$-graded equivariant stable stems that are $C_2$-equivariant refinements of the classical $\mu$-families. Using a $C_2$-equivariant $v_{1,0}$-self map, we explicitly construct an equivariant Adams periodicity operator $P_{C_2}$ that captures these $v_1$-periodicity phenomena in the $C_2$-stable stems.
arxiv:2610.19606.authors: Sihao Ma, Xiaolin Danny Shi, Zhouli Xu, Albert Jinghui Yang, Shangjie Zhang

arxiv:2610.19660.title: Algebraically Integrable Smooth Convex Bodies
arxiv:2610.19660.summary: We prove that a convex body with $C^\infty$ boundary in an odd dimension $n\ge3$ is algebraically integrable if and only if it is an ellipsoid. This answers Arnold's problem for smooth convex bodies. Together with Vassiliev's even-dimensional nonexistence theorem, it gives the classification in every dimension $n\ge2$.

arxiv:2610.19669.title: Maximum Likelihood Degrees via One-Edge Chordal Completion
arxiv:2610.19669.summary: The maximum likelihood degree of a Gaussian graphical model measures the algebraic complexity of its likelihood equations. This paper studies maximum likelihood degrees of Gaussian graphical models through chordal completion. When a graph becomes chordal after one missing edge is added, its maximum likelihood degree is determined by the maximal cliques and clique-tree separators containing that edge.

arxiv:2610.19689.title: The regular inverse Galois problem over fields avoiding a curve
arxiv:2610.19689.summary: Let $k_0$ be a field of characteristic $0$, and let $C/k_0$ be a smooth geometrically integral curve of positive genus with $C(k_0)=\varnothing$. We prove that the regular inverse Galois problem is solvable over every field existentially closed in the class of $k_0$-fields avoiding $C$, including the curve-excluding fields of Johnson and the author. To this end, we show that for every finite group $G$, there is a parameter variety over $\mathbb Q$ whose function field admits a regular realization of $G$ without adding points to $C$.

arxiv:2610.19694.title: On the sum of eccentric subgraph numbers of the vertices of a connected graph
arxiv:2610.19694.summary: Let $G$ be a connected graph. The eccentric subgraph number $\epsilon(v)$ of a vertex $v$ of $G$ is defined as $\epsilon(v)=\min\{f_G(v,u): u\in V(G)\}$, where $f_G(v,u)$ is the number of connected subgraphs of $G$ containing both $v$ and $u$. The eccentric subgraph index $ES(G)$ of $G$ is defined as $ES(G)=\displaystyle\sum_{v\in V(G)}\epsilon(v).$ In this paper, we obtain the unicyclic graph that maximizes the eccentric subgraph index among all unicyclic graphs on $n$ vertices with a fixed girth.

arxiv:2610.19707.title: The Weil-Petersson diameter of moduli space for large genus
arxiv:2610.19707.summary: We determine the large-genus order of the Weil-Petersson diameter of $\mathcal{M}_{g,n}$ for each fixed number of punctures: namely, $\mathrm{diam}(\mathcal{M}_{g,n})\asymp\sqrt g\log g$. The main new ingredient is an integrated Ricci estimate for geodesics that minimize in moduli space and have thick endpoints, with no systole bound along their interiors.

arxiv:2610.19775.title: On the Lattice Tilings by Lee Balls: Q-Polynomials, Group-Ring Equations, and a Decision Algorithm
arxiv:2610.19775.summary: More than 50 years ago, Golomb and Welch conjectured that no tilings of $\mathbb{Z}^n$ by Lee balls of radius $r$ exist for $n \geq 3$ and $r \geq 2$. This conjecture remains open even under the additional assumption that the tiling is a lattice tiling. In general, there are two known effective approaches to the lattice case which are based on symmetric polynomials and on the arithmetic of group-ring equations, respectively.

arxiv:2610.19787.title: Drift and joint minimal displacement for groups acting on hyperbolic spaces
arxiv:2610.19787.summary: We obtain a uniform lower bound for the drift of random walks on hyperbolic spaces in terms of joint minimal displacement. Our main theorem applies to weakly acylindrical actions on Gromov-hyperbolic spaces and is quantitative in all relevant constants. For discrete isometry groups of Hadamard manifolds with pinched negative curvature, the required assumptions are automatically satisfied by the Margulis lemma.

arxiv:2610.19788.title: The volume of foliated surfaces with geometric genus one
arxiv:2610.19788.summary: We prove the sharp volume bound $\mathrm{vol}(\mathcal{F})\ge 1/6$ for complex foliated surfaces of general type with positive geometric genus. We also study the equality case and apply the bound to the algebraic integrability and finiteness of small volumes on irregular surfaces.
arxiv:2610.19788.authors: Zhiming Guo, Bokai Hu, Xin L\"u

arxiv:2610.19791.title: Spectral truncations of SU(2) and the spectral localizer
arxiv:2610.19791.summary: We study operator systems arising from Peter-Weyl and Dirac spectral truncations of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ in the sense of Connes-Van Suijlekom. We determine operator system invariants for these systems, including the $C^*$-envelope and uniform bounds on the propagation number. For Peter-Weyl truncations, we find $\mathrm{prop} \leq 2$ for all connected compact Lie groups, generalizing known results for the torus.

arxiv:2610.19800.title: On several judicious partitioning problems of graphs and hypergraphs
arxiv:2610.19800.summary: Judicious partition problems ask for vertex partitions of graphs or hypergraphs that optimize several quantities simultaneously. In this paper, we investigate judicious partitions of graphs and hypergraphs in which each class meets many edges and establish the following results. (1) Every hypergraph with nonnegative edge weights and all edges of size at most $2$ has a bipartition in which each vertex class meets edges of total weight at least $(w_1-\Delta_1)/2+2w_2/3$, where $w_i$ is the total weight of the edges of size $i$, and $\Delta_1$ is the maximum weight of an edge of size $1$.

arxiv:2610.19812.title: Dimension of the Green measure of skew products with dominant exponent in the fibers
arxiv:2610.19812.summary: Let $f(z,w)=(p(z),q(z,w))$ be a polynomial skew product of $\mathbb{C}^2$ of degree $d\geqslant 2$ and let $\mu$ and $\mu_p$ be the Green measures associated to $f$ and $p$ respectively. Let $\lambda_1 > \lambda_2$ and $\lambda_p$ be the Lyapunov exponents of $(f,\mu)$ and $(p,\mu_p)$ respectively. We show that if $\lambda_2 = \lambda_p$, then $\mu$ is exact dimensional and: \begin{equation*}\dim_H\mu =\frac{\log d}{\lambda_1}+\frac{\log d}{\lambda_2}.\end{equation*} The proof relies on the continuity of the conditional measures obtained by Jonsson, on the fact that $\mu$ has constant Jacobian $d^2$, and on a fibered version of a normal form theorem for the inverse branches of the iterates…

arxiv:2610.19828.title: The orientation-reversing minimal stretch factor problem in small genus
arxiv:2610.19828.summary: We determine the minimal stretch factors among all orientation-reversing pseudo-Anosov mapping classes of the closed orientable surfaces of genus two, three and four.
arxiv:2610.19828.authors: Pierre Dehornoy, Erwan Lanneau, Livio Liechti, Quentin Perroud

arxiv:2610.19953.title: Almost-global convergence to twisted states in discrete Huygens rings
arxiv:2610.19953.summary: We study the discrete Huygens phase map on the ring $C_n$, the simplest oscillator network in which the coupling can be frustrated. Reciprocal coupling favours phase opposition between neighbours, while the edge phase differences must sum to zero modulo $2\pi$ around the cycle; for odd $n$ these two requirements are incompatible. The parity of $n$ determines the absolute minima of the potential.

arxiv:2610.19954.title: Expansive operators on Fr\'echet spaces without continuous norm
arxiv:2610.19954.summary: We investigate the existence of (metrically) expansive operators on Fr\'echet spaces without continuous norm. We first solve a problem posed by Bernardes, Caraballo, Darji, F\'avaro, and Peris in 2025, by showing that there is no expansive operator on the Fr\'echet space $\omega$ of all sequences. We prove this fact by investigating the existence of orbits remaining cofinitely inside some fixed closed subspace of finite codimension.

arxiv:2610.19956.title: Two Companion $q$-Series Identities and Their Combinatorics
arxiv:2610.19956.summary: In this paper, we evaluate two companion $q$-series recently suggested for investigation by Andrews and El Bachraoui in the concluding remarks of their work. From these evaluations, we derive the corresponding partition identities and give combinatorial proofs.

arxiv:2610.19960.title: Nonlinear fixed-distance codes via real lifts of moment configurations
arxiv:2610.19960.summary: Let $A_q(n,d)$ denote the largest size of a code of length $n$ and minimum Hamming distance $d$ over an alphabet of $q$ symbols. For fixed $q\ge2$ and $d\ge4$ we construct codes with redundancy $n-\log_q A_q(n,d)\le(d-3)\log_q n+O(\sqrt{\log n})$ for all large $n$. No algebraic structure is imposed on the alphabet, and the codes are not linear.

arxiv:2610.19965.title: Proofs and disproofs of some conjectures on zero-sum problems of new types
arxiv:2610.19965.summary: For integers $r\ge1$ and $n\ge2$, let $s_r(n)$ be the least $N$ such that every sequence of $N$ vectors in $\Z^r$, each nonzero modulo $n$, contains $n$ terms whose sum is zero modulo $n$ but nonzero modulo $n^2$. Let $w_r(n)$ be the corresponding least $N$ when any nonempty subsequence is allowed. These constants were introduced as zero-sum problems of new types by Z.-W.
arxiv:2610.19965.authors: Yang Li, San Ling, Zhonghua Sun, Shixin Zhu

arxiv:2610.19974.title: Trivariate $P$- and $Q$-polynomial structures for interior shells of the Grassmann scheme
arxiv:2610.19974.summary: Association schemes induced on the shells of the Grassmann scheme $Gr_q(N,a)$ form an important family in the study of multivariate $P$- and $Q$-polynomial structures. For $a<N/2$, the scheme induced on the furthest shell $X_a$ is the known bivariate $P$- and $Q$-polynomial scheme arising from attenuated spaces. In this paper, we prove that, for every $1\leq i\leq a-1$, the association scheme induced on the interior shell $X_i$ is both trivariate $P$-polynomial and trivariate $Q$-polynomial.

arxiv:2610.19980.title: Towards Learning-Guided Discovery of Extremal Geometric Constructions: A PatternBoost Study
arxiv:2610.19980.summary: Extremal constructions play a central role in the design and analysis of algorithms. Integrality-gap instances expose the limitations of relaxations, while hard configurations reveal structural sources of computational difficulty. Such constructions, however, are still typically discovered through a slow, manual process.
arxiv:2610.19980.authors: Deepak Ajwani, Paula Carroll, Rishikesh Gajjala, Ananta Manoranjan, Ryan O'Connor, Rajiv Raman, Saurabh Ray, Aimen Taha

arxiv:2610.19990.title: An elementary proof of Br\'emont's theorem on the convergence of equilibrium measures at temperature zero
arxiv:2610.19990.summary: We give an elementary proof that if $f$ is a locally constant function on a topologically mixing subshift of finite type, then the equilibrium measures for $tf$ converge as $t\to\infty$, a result due to Br\'emont. The proof shows that the limit measure assigns an algebraic number to every cylinder.

arxiv:2610.20008.title: Avoiding a partial Latin square with an isotope of a given Latin square
arxiv:2610.20008.summary: For all sufficiently large $n$, we prove that every Latin square of order $n$ can be made to avoid any prescribed partial Latin square of order $n$ by permuting only its rows and columns. The proof combines Hall's theorem with elementary estimates for a random permutation.

arxiv:2610.20011.title: On deformations of foliated complex analytic structures III: Unfoldings
arxiv:2610.20011.summary: We study unfoldings of foliated complex analytic structures defined by locally free subsheaves of cotangent sheaves. We prove theorem of existence for unfoldings of foliated complex analytic structures defined by locally free subsheaves of cotangent sheaves for one-parameter families. We prove theorem of completeness for unfoldings of foliated complex analytic structures defined by locally free subsheaves of cotangent sheaves.

arxiv:2610.20024.title: Maximal subgroups of topological full groups of shifts of finite type
arxiv:2610.20024.summary: We study maximal subgroups of topological full groups of irreducible one-sided shifts of finite type whose associated groupoids have Cantor unit space. For each wide open subgroupoid of such a groupoid, we construct a subgroupoid graph and identify the subgroupoid with a full compact open reduction of the corresponding countable graph groupoid. Every minimal wide open subgroupoid is either AF or purely infinite.

arxiv:2610.20025.title: On the Topology of Fibers of Rational Functions
arxiv:2610.20025.summary: In 1988 Broughton proved that if a complex polynomial function on ${\mathbb C}^n$ is tame at infinity its fibers are homotopy equivalent to bouquets of some spheres. Since then several basic properties of polynomial functions were studied by many mathematicians in various situations. In this paper, we show some evidence for the possibility of extending Broughton's result to rational functions satisfying some tameness condition at infinity and the one at their points of indeterminacy.

arxiv:2610.20028.title: Sequence Factory: Families of Integer Sequences Generated by G\"odel Implication
arxiv:2610.20028.summary: A finite G\"odel chain generates not one integer sequence but a large family of them. The combinatorial mechanism is developed in a companion paper; here the sequences themselves are the primary objects. For $V_m=\{v_0<\cdots<v_{m-1}\}$, let $g_{j,n}^{(m)}$ count outputs equal to $v_j$, aggregated over all full bracketings on $n$ variables and all $m^n$ valuations.

arxiv:2610.20034.title: Maximal subsets of $n\times n$ board without cycles
arxiv:2610.20034.summary:
Define $
abla(n)$ as the least possible number of cells that must be removed from the $n	imes n$ square board in order to leave no cycles. Put $L_n=\left\lceil\left((n-1)^2+1ight)/3ightceil$. The results of Luccio, Madelaine-Stewart, and Lien-Fu-Shih imply that $
abla(n)=L_n$ in case $n\equiv 1\pmod 6$ and $n\equiv 4\pmod 6$, while for the remaining $4$ residue classes $
abla(n)=L_n$ or $
abla(n)=L_n+1$.

arxiv:2610.20044.title: Markman--Markushevich principle and Lagrangian fibrations on O'Grady six-manifolds
arxiv:2610.20044.summary: To any compact holomorphically symplectic manifold and a nef BBF-isotropic class we associate a quasi-projective variety called the Markman--Markushevich space which parametrises the Lagrangian fibrations with this isotropic class modulo Tate--Shafarevich twists. We give a systematic interpretation of known results about Tate--Shafarevich twists of Lagrangian fibrations using this space, employ it to obtain a conjectural result for the last deformation type for which such a result is not yet proposed, and make some first steps towards its proof. As a byproduct, we generalise the results of Kumar on existence Shioda--Inose partners for abelian surfaces to a slightly more general class of K3…

arxiv:2610.20046.title: Real Tree Vineyards have Vines
arxiv:2610.20046.summary: We show that every vineyard can be decomposed into vines, that is, every path in the space of persistence diagrams $\mathcal{D}$ can be decomposed into a sequence of paths in $\mathbb R^2$. Moreover, we characterize which spaces $X$ have the property that every continuous map $X\to \mathcal{D}$ has such a decomposition. Our results hold not just for $\mathcal{D}$, but also for many other spaces of unordered tuples.
arxiv:2610.20046.authors: Michael Hull, Thomas Payne, Thomas Weighill

arxiv:2610.20101.title: Connectivity keeping pendant extensions of paths in $k$-connected triangle-free graphs
arxiv:2610.20101.summary: Motivated by Mader's conjecture on connectivity keeping trees, we study the corresponding problem in triangle-free graphs. For positive integers $k,m$, we first prove that every $k$-connected triangle-free graph $G$ with $\delta(G)\geq k+\left \lceil \frac{m}{2} \right \rceil $ contains a path $P$ of order $m$ such that $G-V(P)$ remains $k$-connected. Moreover, if $\kappa(G)=k$, then for every end $F$ of $G$ and every vertex $v\in F$, the path $P$ can be chosen in $G[F]$ with $v$ as an endvertex.
arxiv:2610.20101.authors: Menghan Ma, Qinghai Liu, Liping Zhang, Yanmei Hong

arxiv:2610.20129.title: Cop number of $P_k$-free graphs without a claw or a fork
arxiv:2610.20129.summary: In 2019, Liu proved that the cop number of any $(P_k, claw)$-free graph is at most $k-3$. In 2026, Clow and Meger improved and generalized the result of Liu by showing that every connected $(P_k, E)$-free graph has cop number at most $\lceil \frac{k-1}{2} \rceil + 3$, where the graph $E$ is obtained by subdividing two edges of a claw. In this paper, we show that every $(P_k, claw)$-free graph $G$ has cop number at most $\lceil \frac{k-1}{2} \rceil$.
arxiv:2610.20129.authors: Uttam K. Gupta, Dinabandhu Pradhan, Rashmi Rekha Swain

arxiv:2610.20131.title: Mapping class groups of solenoidal manifolds
arxiv:2610.20131.summary: The goal of this work is to calculate the mapping class groups of solenoidal manifolds. We introduce the dynamical commensurator group associated to an odometer action, and develop methods to calculate the mapping class group using the dynamical commensurator. Our results generalize the previous results of Odden for the mapping class group of the universal solenoid over a Riemann surface, and of Bering and Studenmund for the pointed mapping class group of the universal solenoid over a compact aspherical manifold.

arxiv:2610.20146.title: Gaudin from Cherednik
arxiv:2610.20146.summary: Let $W$ be a complex reflection group and $X$ the De Concini-Procesi wonderful model of its reflection arrangement. Inside Etingof's sheaf of Cherednik algebras on $X$ we define a subsheaf generated by the Dunkl operators that extend the standard ones on the hyperplane complement. We conjecture that at $t=0$ the image of the logarithmic vector fields in a natural module over this subsheaf is the sheaf of Gaudin algebras on $X$ defined by Aguirre, extending a construction of Bonnaf\'e and Rouquier from the hyperplane complement to $X$.

arxiv:2610.20149.title: Elementary Proofs of Commonality of the House Graph and $K_4$ with One Edge Subdivided
arxiv:2610.20149.summary: A graph $H$ is called common if the number of monochromatic copies of $H$ in a $2$-edge-coloring of a large complete graph is asymptotically minimized by the random coloring with an equal proportion of each color. The house graph and $K_4$ with one edge subdivided once are known to be common by the flag algebra method. Grzesik, Lee, Lidick\'y, and Volec asked for ``human-friendly'' proofs of the commonality of these two graphs.

arxiv:2610.20166.title: Quantized six-vertex realizations of frustration graphs
arxiv:2610.20166.summary: A recent graph-theoretic criterion for a Hamiltonian to exhibit a free-parafermion spectrum is that its frustration graph be an indifference graph. We show that an arbitrary finite indifference graph can be realized as a frustration graph of the quantized six-vertex model at odd roots of unity, by a suitable choice of the defining wiring diagram and parameters. This provides a concrete realization of the criterion through the quantum Frobenius property of the quantized six-vertex model, recently established from its three-dimensional integrable structure.

arxiv:2610.20176.title: Reciprocal Dynamics in Congruence Jumping: Integral Orbits and Valuation Cones
arxiv:2610.20176.summary: For fixed positive degrees $n,m$, alternating monic reciprocal transformations define a rational discrete dynamical system on the finite-dimensional coefficient space of polynomial pairs. This system arises from congruence jumping in polynomial divisibility problems, where a quotient move changes the polynomial state, but its coefficient dynamics can be studied independently. We prove that every state with nonzero constant terms returns after four alternating updates to its rational gauge classes and classify when this return orbit is realized over $\mathbb Z$.
arxiv:2610.20176.authors: Max A. Alekseyev, Dmitry I. Khomovsky

arxiv:2610.20197.title: Topological obstruction for Anosov representations into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$
arxiv:2610.20197.summary: We establish new restrictions on the virtual cohomological dimension of word hyperbolic groups admitting Anosov representations into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ ($p > q \geq 2$) or the exceptional Lie group $\operatorname{G}_2'$. Our main result states that, if $P_k$ is the parabolic subgroup of $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ stabilizing an isotropic $k$-plane in $\mathbb{R}^{p, q}$, a group admitting a $\{P_1,P_q\}$-Anosov representation into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ has virtual cohomological dimension strictly less than $p$. As a result, a $\mathbf{H}^{p, q-1}$-convex cocompact subgroup of $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ cannot act properly discontinuously and cocompactly on $\mathbf{H}^{p, q-1}$.

arxiv:2610.20208.title: Uniform non-homogeneous vector bundles: A counterexample to the conjecture of Dr\'ezet and Ballico-Ellia
arxiv:2610.20208.summary: We construct a rank-9 uniform non-homogeneous vector bundle on ${\mathbb P}^5$. This yields the first counterexample to the longstanding open conjecture that every uniform vector bundle of rank $r<2n$ on ${\mathbb P}^n$ is homogeneous.
arxiv:2610.20208.authors: Graham Denham, Rosa Mir\'o-Roig, Hal Schenck

arxiv:2610.20212.title: $\chi$-Independence for BPS Invariants of Warped Local Curves
arxiv:2610.20212.summary: A well-known conjecture of Toda's asserts that the BPS invariants associated to a Calabi--Yau threefold are independent of the chosen Euler characteristic. We answer the question in the affirmative for a certain class of local surfaces, which we call warped local curves. Along the way we show that the moduli stack of sheaves on a warped local curve can be written as the global critical locus of a function.

arxiv:2610.20213.title: Stable atomic vector bundles are 1-obstructed
arxiv:2610.20213.summary: We prove that every stable atomic (twisted) vector bundle on a projective hyper-K\"ahler manifold is 1-obstructed. In the appendix, we construct a simple atomic object that is not 1-obstructed, providing a counterexample to Beckmann's conjecture.

arxiv:2610.20234.title: The parity module of a matroid
arxiv:2610.20234.summary: We introduce the parity module of a matroid with coefficients in a field $\mathbb{k}$. When $\mathbb{k}$ has characteristic zero, we show that the parity module of a matroid is isomorphic to its intersection cohomology module, yielding a new intrinsic characterization of the latter. The structure and dimension of the parity module can vary depending on the characteristic, giving rise to characteristic-dependent generalizations of the Kazhdan-Lusztig and Z-polynomials of matroids.
arxiv:2610.20234.authors: Tom Braden, June Huh, Jacob P. Matherne, Nicholas Proudfoot, Botong Wang

arxiv:2610.20239.title: Chow groups of symmetric products of projective space
arxiv:2610.20239.summary: We prove that the integral cycle class map for $\SP^d(\PP^n)$ is split injective, with finite cokernel annihilated by $d!$,and we determine the ranks of Chow groups for $\mathrm{SP}^d(\mathbb{P}^n)$. Compatible integral transfer retractions show that $\CH_q(\SP^d(\PP^n))$ stabilizes for $d\geq q$. An explicit nonalgebraic order two class persists under addition of points, producing a split cokernel summand even in the range $q\leq d$ and in the infinite symmetric product.

arxiv:2610.20259.title: Nonexistence of Strongly Regular Graphs via Gegenbauer Positivity and SRG Counting
arxiv:2610.20259.summary: This paper develops a natural extension of the multipoint spherical semidefinite method of Liao and Yu~\cite{LY}, studying the interaction between semidefinite programming and strongly regular graph counting. Starting from the positive semidefinite kernels furnished by Gegenbauer polynomials, we express weighted kernel sums and counting identities in the same labelled induced-subgraph counts. Eliminating the counting equations gives a semidefinite feasibility problem.
arxiv:2610.20259.authors: Zhen-Qi Liao, Jiaxin Wang, Wei-Hsuan Yu, Jianfeng Cai

arxiv:2610.20267.title: A new generalization of parking functions: $\rho$-Naples parking functions
arxiv:2610.20267.summary: We introduce a new model of parking functions, called $\rho$-Naples parking functions, in which each car has a certain number of spots to check preceding its preferred one before looking for available spots by moving forward. This notion, where each car has its own number of previous spots to check, generalizes that of Naples parking function, where this number is the same for all cars. We start by showing that, for a given sequence of preferences for each car, a successful parking strategy (that is, an assignment of how many backward spots each car is allowed to check) remains successful if we increase the number of backwards spots to check for some of the cars.

arxiv:2610.20300.title: Odd mapping cone Chern character
arxiv:2610.20300.summary: Our previous work established the mapping cone Chern character on the even-degree side, using the powers of the mapping cone curvature associated with the given mapping cone connection. In this paper, we carry out the odd-degree version using a trivial mapping cone connection and an automorphism on a trivial complex vector bundle. This version is based on the related odd-degree transgression.

arxiv:2610.20311.title: Quantitative lower bound for Pythagorean pairs in boxes of prime powers
arxiv:2610.20311.summary: For each positive integer $N$, let $p_i$ be the $i$-th prime for $i\in\{1,\ldots,N\}$, and set $$ \Phi_N=\left\{\prod_{i=1}^{N}p_i^{a_i}:a_i\in\{0,1,\ldots,N-1\}\right\}. $$ Write $f(N)$ for the largest cardinality of a subset of $\Phi_N$ containing no two distinct legs of an integral right triangle. We prove $$ N^{N-1}(\log\log\log N)\ll f(N).

arxiv:2610.20317.title: Power quotients of plactic-like monoids
arxiv:2610.20317.summary: In this paper we describe the quotients of several plactic-like monoids by the least congruences containing the relations $a^{\sigma(a)} = a$ for $\sigma(a) \geq 2$ for every generator $a$. The starting point of this paper is the recent paper of Reutenauer and the first author about the stylic monoid. This monoid is the quotient of the plactic monoid by the relations $a^2 = a$ for every generator $a$.
arxiv:2610.20317.authors: Antoine Abram, Florent Hivert, James D. Mitchell, Jean-Christophe Novelli, Maria Tsalakou

arxiv:2610.20358.title: On local minimality of Hausdorff dimension for round limit sets
arxiv:2610.20358.summary: We address a question of Canary--Taylor and Canary--Minsky--Taylor for sufficiently symmetric compact hyperbolic $3$-orbifolds with totally geodesic boundary. We give sufficient conditions on the symmetries of such an orbifold to show that, among the complete convex cocompact structures on the interior, the structure with Fuchsian ends is a critical point (respectively, a strict local minimum) for the critical exponent. We also provide an infinite family of non-rigid examples fulfilling these conditions.
arxiv:2610.20358.authors: Sami Douba, Andr\'es Sambarino, Franco Vargas Pallete

arxiv:2610.20364.title: A Unified Linear Programming Approach for Maximizing Vertex-Degree-Based Indices of Trees
arxiv:2610.20364.summary: The problem of maximizing vertex-degree-based topological indices over trees with a prescribed order and maximum degree $\Delta$ has traditionally relied on ad-hoc combinatorial arguments. In this paper, we establish a unified linear programming approach that systematically resolves these extremal problems. By formulating the optimization over degree-pair multiplicities, the search for an extremal tree reduces to minimizing a discrete dual penalty.

arxiv:2610.20368.title: Degeneracy graph determinants and higher-dimensional Young diagrams
arxiv:2610.20368.summary: Kemp and Ramgoolam proposed a basis of monomials for a commutative semisimple algebra with generators \(C_1,\ldots, C_L\), constructed from a degeneracy graph which records how the eigenspaces of \( C_1\) are successively split by \( C_2,\ldots, C_L\). They showed that the basis property is equivalent to the non-vanishing of the determinant of the matrix of values of these monomials on the projector basis, and conjectured a factorised formula for this determinant, as a product of powers of eigenvalue differences. We prove this formula for any number of generators.

arxiv:2610.20376.title: Discrete Morse Theory for Computing Filtered Cosheaf Homology
arxiv:2610.20376.summary: This paper addresses the computation of persistent homology for filtrations of cellular cosheaves over a fixed cell complex, where the algebraic data vary along the filtration while the underlying topological structure remains unchanged. We extend methods from discrete Morse theory to this setting, establishing conditions under which chain complexes can be reduced while preserving the associated persistence module. Building on these results, we introduce "FilteredScythe", an algorithm that identifies Morse matchings compatible with all stages of the filtration and performs reductions using Schur complements, based on the exist "Scythe" algorithm.

arxiv:2610.20379.title: GCD and ABC inequalities for abelian varieties over function fields
arxiv:2610.20379.summary: We prove two height inequalities for rational points on abelian varieties over function fields of characteristic 0. The first is the GCD inequality, which shows that the height with respect to a closed subscheme of an abelian variety of codimension at least 2 is much smaller than the usual height function. This can be viewed as a compact and geometric analogue of a theorem of Levin.

arxiv:2610.20386.title: The Kaplansky-Walker Lemma for additive categories
arxiv:2610.20386.summary: We establish a Kaplansky-Walker type lemma for idempotent complete additive categories with direct sums. It will be used in compactly generated triangulated categories to provide a version of Kaplansky's theorem on projective modules and an isomorphism-refinement result for direct sums of countable objects.

arxiv:2610.20391.title: Potatoes and Onions
arxiv:2610.20391.summary: The first major step in the theory of graph minors of Robertson and Seymour was the grid theorem, a fundamental duality result describing that any graph of sufficiently high treewidth must contain a large grid as a minor. Since this pioneering work, multiple grid theorems have been established in structural graph theory, linking various width parameters of combinatorial objects with the non-existence of grid-like obstructions. In particular, Kawarabayashi and Kreutzer [STOC'15] proved a variant of the grid theorem for directed graphs that links directed treewidth with the non-existence of topological minors of large cylindrical walls.
arxiv:2610.20391.authors: Marcin Bria\'nski, Meike Hatzel, Karolina Okrasa, Micha{\l} Pilipczuk

arxiv:2610.20404.title: On the Structure of Radical Towers and their Parametrizations
arxiv:2610.20404.summary: Radical parametrizations describe algebraic varieties by means of nested radicals of polynomials, and their theory relies on three varieties associated with a parametrization, namely, the incidence, tower and radical varieties. In this paper we revisit this framework from a computational point of view and show that it is governed by the radical tower rather than by the particular parametrization. We prove that the tower variety depends only on the tower and that the incidence variety is always irreducible, so that no prime decomposition is needed.
arxiv:2610.20404.authors: Javier Sendra-Arranz, Juan Rafael Sendra, Juana Sendra

arxiv:2610.20407.title: Treewidth and the Product of Tree-Independence and Tree-Chromatic Numbers
arxiv:2610.20407.summary: For a graph $G$, let $\mathrm{tw}(G)$, $\mathrm{tree}\text{-}\alpha(G)$, and $\mathrm{tree}\text{-}\chi(G)$ denote its treewidth, tree-independence number, and tree-chromatic number, respectively. We prove that every nonempty graph $G$ satisfies $\mathrm{tw}(G)+1\leq\mathrm{tree}\text{-}\alpha(G)\mathrm{tree}\text{-}\chi(G)(1+\lfloor\log_2(\mathrm{tree}\text{-}\alpha(G))\rfloor)$. This improves the quadratic bound of Koutsoutis, Krause, Liu, Redzic, and Ueckerdt.

arxiv:2610.20408.title: Two Perfect One-Factorizations of $K_{92}$
arxiv:2610.20408.summary: A perfect 1-factorization of the complete graph $K_{2t}$ is a partition of its edges into perfect matchings such that the union of any two of them is a Hamilton cycle. Kotzig conjectured in 1963 that $K_{2t}$ has a perfect 1-factorization for every $t \ge 2$, but apart from some infinite families and a list of sporadic orders the conjecture is open, and $92$ was one of the nine orders up to $100$ for which no perfect 1-factorization was known. In this paper we construct two non-isomorphic perfect 1-factorizations of $K_{92}$.

arxiv:2610.20414.title: The terminal leave in random greedy hypergraph matching
arxiv:2610.20414.summary: Let $G$ be the terminal graph of the random triangle-removal process started from $K_n$. We prove that $e(G)/n^{3/2}\to1/(2\sqrt2)$ in $L^2$. More generally, we obtain the analogous result for any fixed strictly $k$-balanced $k$-graph.

arxiv:2610.20428.title: The classical homotopy category is cartesian closed
arxiv:2610.20428.summary: The category of all topological spaces and homotopy classes of maps is cartesian closed. In fact, the $(\infty, 1)$-category of all topological spaces and continuous maps, localised at homotopy equivalences, is cartesian closed. We model the exponential object using a topological space whose points are continuous maps equipped with putative neighbourhood filters.

arxiv:2610.20430.title: Deformations of Holomorphic $p$-Contact Structures
arxiv:2610.20430.summary: We investigate the notion of holomorphic $p$-contact structure, that we introduced recently in the scalar case with H. Kasuya and L. Ugarte and in the line-bundle case with K.

arxiv:2610.20443.title: Intersecting families of loose spanning hypertrees
arxiv:2610.20443.summary: A loose hypertree is a hypergraph whose incidence graph is a tree. Let $b\ge3$, $n\equiv1\pmod{b-1}$, and $s:=(n-1)/(b-1)$. We determine the largest $t$-intersecting families of loose spanning $b$-uniform hypertrees on $[n]$, simultaneously for every $1\le t\le s$, provided $n$ exceeds an explicit constant depending only on $b$.

arxiv:2610.20464.title: Topological recursion for spin enumeration of hypermaps
arxiv:2610.20464.summary: We establish topological recursion for the spin enumeration of hypermaps, or, in the dual language, spin dessins d'enfants. This problem has remarkable features distinguishing it from other applications of topological recursion to enumerative combinatorics. First, the spectral curve is elliptic rather than rational, as in most cases studied before.
arxiv:2610.20464.authors: Alexander Alexandrov, Boris Bychkov, Petr Dunin-Barkowski, Maxim Kazarian, Sergey Shadrin

arxiv:2610.20466.title: A prismatic Riemann-Hilbert correspondence
arxiv:2610.20466.summary: We study the category of constructible $p$-Kummer-\'{e}tale sheaves on the log adic generic fiber $(\mathrm{X},\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{D}})_\eta$ for the stratification induced by a horizontal normal crossings divisor $\mathrm{D}$, showing that it is antiequivalent to a category of finitely generated unit Laurent crystals on the log prismatic site. We give a local description of finitely generated unit crystals on a framed log affine in terms of $(\varphi,\Gamma)$-modules, and show pushforward compatibility for strict log smooth proper morphisms.

arxiv:2610.20478.title: Crystallographic quotients of Artin braid groups and torus bundles over flat $3$-manifolds
arxiv:2610.20478.summary: For $n\geq3$, let $\overline B_n=B_n/[P_n,P_n]$ be the crystallographic quotient of the Artin braid group, with translation subgroup $\overline P_n=P_n/[P_n,P_n]\cong\mathbb Z^N$, where $N=\binom n2$. We prove that every compact connected flat $3$-manifold $M$, considered up to affine equivalence, is the base of a geometric torus bundle whose total space is a compact flat manifold with fundamental group a Bieberbach subgroup of some $\overline B_n$. More precisely, for every $n\geq n_M$, where $n_M\in\{3,4,5\}$ is an explicit optimal threshold depending on $M$, we construct a Bieberbach subgroup $\Gamma_n(M)\leq\overline B_n$ of dimension $N$ and a complete normal subgroup…

arxiv:2610.20496.title: Smoothness criterion for Fano orbifolds and bases of Lagrangian fibrations
arxiv:2610.20496.summary: We establish a smoothness criterion for Fano varieties with quotient singularities. As an application, we show that if $X\to B$ is a Lagrangian fibration from a compact hyper-K\"ahler manifold and $B$ has quotient singularities, then $B$ is a projective space.

arxiv:2610.20499.title: $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth approximation of mod $k$ integral cycles
arxiv:2610.20499.summary: We prove that every mod $k$ integral cycle $T$ of sufficiently high codimension in an oriented Riemannian manifold $\mathcal{M}$ can be approximated in flat norm by a cycle which is a $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth submanifold $\Sigma$ of nearly the same area, up to a singular set of codimension 5. If in addition $T$ belongs to a mod $k$ homology class admitting an embedded $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth manifold representative, then $\Sigma$ can be taken fully regular, up to the codimension one stratum of classical singularities. This extends the smooth approximation theory to cycles with coefficients in $\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$ in stable regimes.

arxiv:2610.20510.title: Claw-Free and Line Graph Edge Deletion on Block Graphs
arxiv:2610.20510.summary: Edge deletion problems ask for the fewest edges whose deletion gives a graph with a specified property. We study two such problems on block graphs. First making the graph claw-free, and second making it a line graph.

arxiv:2610.20513.title: Effective equidistribution of polynomial trajectories in $\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb R)/\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb Z)$
arxiv:2610.20513.summary: For a fixed matrix-polynomial trajectory in $\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb R)/\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb Z)$, we give a necessary and sufficient intrinsic Diophantine condition for its time averages to equidistribute at a power rate on its homogeneous orbit closure. The condition uses a lattice in the space of polynomial functions on the normalized orbit-closure group, each admitting a representative of total degree at most two in the matrix entries. These polynomial tests have a common degree bound of two, independent of the curve degree and optimal in general.

arxiv:2610.20545.title: The $k$-color poset Ramsey number of the diamond is $2k$
arxiv:2610.20545.summary: The $k$-color Ramsey number of a poset $P$ is the smallest dimension $d$ such that any $k$-coloring of the $d$-dimensional Boolean lattice contains a monochromatic induced copy of $P$. For $ j\ge 2$ the $j$-diamond is the poset that consists of a maximum element, a minimum element and an antichain of size $j$. We prove that the $k$-color Ramsey number of the $j$-diamond is at most $jk$.
arxiv:2610.20545.authors: Tom Bohman, Will Cong, Quentin Dubroff, Teresa Huang, Zheyuan Li, BangTam Ngo

arxiv:2610.20558.title: Minimal $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ Complexes of Rational Tangles via the Fukaya Category
arxiv:2610.20558.summary: We compute minimal $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ complexes for oriented rational tangles, denoted $[\![\tau_{u/v}^{O}]\!]_N$, in terms of the topological Fukaya category of the $3$-punctured disk. This demonstrates that the complexes stabilize, allowing us to define a HOMFLY-PT homology for rational tangles.

arxiv:2610.20562.title: Hypergraphs with the smallest Hall ratio are still hard to colour
arxiv:2610.20562.summary: For $H$ a hypergraph, the Hall ratio $\rho(H)=\text{max}_{X\subseteq V(H)}\frac{\lvert{X}\rvert}{\alpha(H[X])}$ is a natural lower bound for its chromatic number, and among non-empty $k$-uniform hypergraphs the smallest possible Hall ratio is $k/(k-1)$. For graphs ($k = 2$), having minimum Hall ratio $2$ forces chromatic number $2$. Ne\v{s}et\v{r}il, R\"{o}dl, and Sales asked whether a similar phenomenon holds at higher uniformities.
arxiv:2610.20562.authors: Veronica Bitonti, Freddie Illingworth, Pedram Noohi, Jane Tan

arxiv:2610.20565.title: Minimal Resolutions of $k$-divisible and $(k-1)$-dominant Ideals
arxiv:2610.20565.summary: We introduce invariants we call $k$-divisibility and $d$-dominance, which are combinatorial constraints on the minimal generators of monomial ideals. We then prove that $k$ (respectively, $d$) is an upper bound (respectively, lower bound) for the projective dimension of a $k$-divisible (respectively, $d$-dominant) monomial ideal. This leads us to an explicit minimal resolution of $k$-divisible, $d$-dominant ideals when $d=k-1$ via a Lyubeznik resolution.

arxiv:2610.20566.title: Completely parabolic surfaces are Veech
arxiv:2610.20566.summary: We prove that completely parabolic translation surfaces are Veech, answering a question of Smillie-Weiss.

arxiv:2610.20575.title: Arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula on the product of modular curves
arxiv:2610.20575.summary: We prove the full generating series arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula on the product of two modular curves, with arbitrarily singular coefficients. This is the case $\operatorname{GSpin}(2,2)$ in Kudla's program.

arxiv:2610.20577.title: Decay-Ramsey Sequences
arxiv:2610.20577.summary: Given a sequence $\mathbf{a}=(a_i)_{i\geq 1}$ of positive real numbers, we say that a colouring $c:E(K_n)\to \mathbb{N}$ is $\mathbf{a}$-bounded if the proportion of edges coloured $i$ is at most $a_i$, for all $i$. We write \[ \mathbf{a}\, \to\, K_k \] if, for all sufficiently large $n$, all $\mathbf{a}$-bounded colourings $c:E(K_n)\to \mathbb{N}$ contain a monochromatic $K_k$. We say that the sequence $\mathbf{a}$ is \emph{Decay-Ramsey} if $\mathbf{a}\to K_k$ for all $k\ge 2$.
arxiv:2610.20577.authors: Francesco Di Braccio, Simon Griffiths, Pedram Noohi, Leo Versteegen

arxiv:2610.20648.title: Connectivity and Diameter of Friends and Strangers Graphs Using Minimum Degree
arxiv:2610.20648.summary: Given graphs $X,Y$ on $n$ vertices, Defant and Kravitz defined the friends and strangers graph, denoted $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$. The vertices of $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$ are bijections $\sigma:V(X)\to V(Y)$, and two bijections $\sigma$ and $\sigma'$ are adjacent in $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$ if they differ by a transposition $(ab)$ such that $a$ and $b$ are adjacent in $X$ and $\sigma(a)$ and $\sigma(b)$ are adjacent in $Y$. Our main result resolves a conjecture of Bangachev that if $X,Y$ are connected graphs and $2\min\{\delta(X),\delta(Y)\}+3\max\{\delta(X),\delta(Y)\}\ge 3n$, then $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$ is connected.

arxiv:2610.20649.title: Cotangent cohomology and higher-order obstructions of matroids
arxiv:2610.20649.summary: We show that matroid Stanley-Reisner rings can have essential deformation obstructions of arbitrarily high order over every field, even at corank three. For every $m\ge3$, we construct a connected cosimple matroid with $m$ fine-homogeneous first-order deformation classes whose proper subcollections integrate jointly and whose pairwise primary cup products vanish. These classes define a joint flat family whose $(m-1)$-jet has no lift to order $m$, even without preserving the grading.

arxiv:2610.20657.title: A polylogarithmic bound for list replicability
arxiv:2610.20657.summary: Zhang [Zha26] recently posted a manuscript announcing that the list-replicability number of every class of $M\ge 2$ binary concepts on $N\ge 2$ domain points is $O(\log^2 M\log N)$, which would be the first polylogarithmic upper bound on this quantity. In this note, we present a short, self-contained proof of this bound, following the high-level approach of the manuscript but with considerably simpler arguments.
arxiv:2610.20657.authors: Ari Blondal, Hamed Hatami, Pooya Hatami, Chavdar Lalov, Sivan Tretiak

arxiv:2610.20663.title: Crystallization of the undertile
arxiv:2610.20663.summary: We classify all periodic tilings with a monotile known as $\mathbf{R1}$ and called here the undertile, which underlies several aperiodic monotiles such as the Taylor-Socolar one. The classification is done using deflation, through a study of fracture lines between zones where deflation can be performed. A full classification of fracture patterns is given, that also applies to non-periodic tilings with the undertile.

arxiv:2610.20688.title: The real Betti realization of very effective Hermitian K-theory
arxiv:2610.20688.summary: Real Betti realization is a symmetric monoidal functor from the category of motivic spectra to that of topological spectra, extending the functor that associates to a scheme over $\mathbb{R}$ the space of its real points. In this article, we identify the $\mathcal{E}_1$-ring structure on the real realization of $\mathsf{ko}$, the very effective cover of Hermitian K-theory $\mathsf{KO}$, by an explicit 2-local fracture square, as being equivalent to $\mathsf{L}(\mathbb{R})_{\geq 0}$, the connective L-theory spectrum of $\mathbb{R}$. Along the way, we also compute the real realization of other motivic ring spectra: motivic cohomology $\mathsf{H}\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathsf{H}\mathbb{Z}/2$, the…

arxiv:2610.20769.title: Eccentricity Shortest Path: the structural parameter landscape
arxiv:2610.20769.summary: The Eccentricity Shortest Path problem asks, given a connected graph and a nonnegative integer $R$, whether some shortest path is within distance $R$ of every vertex. We study its structural parameterized complexity. We give fixed-parameter algorithms for vertex-deletion distance to cographs, vertex-deletion distance to interval graphs, and bandwidth.
arxiv:2610.20769.authors: Anand Babu, Ashwin Jacob, Hitendra Kumar, R. B. Sandeep

arxiv:2610.20775.title: The Lov\'asz number is not alone: a continuum of R\'enyi points in the entanglement-assisted spectrum of graphs
arxiv:2610.20775.summary: Li and Zuiddam's entanglement-assisted asymptotic spectrum of graphs consists of the normalized graph parameters that are additive under disjoint unions, multiplicative under strong products and monotone under entanglement-assisted cohomomorphisms; the entanglement-assisted Shannon capacity is their pointwise minimum. To our knowledge, the Lov\'asz number $\vartheta$ was its only known element. We find a continuum of others.

arxiv:2610.20801.title: Nilpotent Deformation Theory via Ultrasolid Algebra
arxiv:2610.20801.summary: Deformation theory studies how varieties and other algebro-geometric objects vary in families. A central part of the subject is formal deformation theory, where one deforms over an Artinian base; such deformation problems are governed by Lie algebraic models. We pose the question of deforming varieties over nilpotent but not necessarily Artinian bases.

arxiv:2610.20802.title: Two Short Proofs of the $A^A$ Theorem
arxiv:2610.20802.summary: In 1984, D.~Duffus asked whether $A^A\cong B^B$ implies $A\cong B$ for finite, nonempty ordered sets $A$ and~$B$. J.\,D. Farley and the author proved that it does.

arxiv:2610.20817.title: The $A^A$ problem for finite ordered sets
arxiv:2610.20817.summary: For ordered sets $X$ and $Y$, let $Y^X$ denote the ordered set of order-preserving maps from $X$ to $Y$, ordered pointwise. In 1984, D. Duffus asked whether $A^A\cong B^B$ forces $A\cong B$ when $A$ and $B$ are finite ordered sets.

arxiv:2610.20825.title: Linear Independence of Polynomial Compositions with Bounded Input Degree
arxiv:2610.20825.summary: We prove the weak composition-independence conjectures of Kohn, Marchetti, Massarenti and Mella. The proof uses deformations of rational curves and a single kernel of the linearized equation. Riemann-Roch gives a contradiction from tangent fields with controlled poles.

arxiv:2610.20855.title: Perfect and peak state transfer on IBM quantum hardware
arxiv:2610.20855.summary: We run continuous-time quantum walks with perfect and peak state transfer on a present-day superconducting quantum processor, IBM Quantum's $156$-qubit Heron device ibm_kingston, deliberately without error correction or error mitigation. Perfect state transfer and its relaxations have been studied extensively in algebraic graph theory, where one can prove exactly which graphs move a quantum state from one vertex to another with probability one (or with the largest probability the graph allows, in the case of peak state transfer), and at what time.
